quoted_text:
A few thoughts on the current state of venture capital.

When the Music Is Playing

In July 2007, a few weeks before the credit markets seized up, Chuck Prince, then the CEO of Citigroup, gave an interview to the Financial Times. The line everyone remembers is this one: "As long as the music is playing, you've got to get up and dance." He was mocked for it for years afterward, and he lost his job a few months later. But I have come to think he was saying something honest. He wasn't claiming the music would play forever. He was admitting that he couldn't sit down while it was still going, and neither could anyone else in his seat.

I've been thinking about that quote a lot lately, because right now is the most disorienting period in venture capital I can remember, and I have been doing this for a while.

Here is what makes it disorienting. It's not that things are bad. Some things are spectacular. We have companies in our portfolio growing faster than anything I have seen in my career, and I don't say that lightly. At the same time, we have companies with no revenue, no product, and a founding team you could fit in a conference room raising billions of dollars at valuations of $10 to $50 billion. Both of these things are true at once, and if you try to reason about them with the same framework you will drive yourself crazy.

Two ideas have helped me make sense of it. Neither is mine.

The first is reflexivity, which George Soros has been writing about since the 1980s. In most of life, perception follows reality: the weather is what it is, and your opinion of it changes nothing. In markets, it runs the other way too. Prices change what participants believe, and what participants believe changes the prices. The feedback loop can run for a long time, and while it's running it looks exactly like progress.

Here is how reflexivity is playing out in AI. Full disclosure: Menlo is an investor in Anthropic, so read the following with that in mind. People watched a frontier lab go from a $4 billion valuation to $18 billion, then $60 billion, then $180 billion, then $380 billion, and now something close to a trillion. They drew the obvious conclusion: that is what a neo lab looks like. So the next neo lab gets priced off that path, not off anything it has built. Then it gets marked up in a subsequent round, and the markup itself becomes the proof. Look at Thinking Machines. Look at Reflection. At that point valuation has stopped being an output of the metrics and has become the metric. Nobody is discounting cash flows. They are discounting the last round.

Soros is very clear about one thing, and it's the part people skip: you cannot know when or how a reflexive process ends. You only know that it does. Every one of them has.

The second idea is Chuck Prince's, and it explains why smart people keep dancing even when they can see the loop for what it is. As far as I can tell, there are two groups on the dance floor.

The first group got in early. Firms like ours were in some of these AI companies before the numbers got silly, and the paper gains are enormous. When you are sitting on gains like that, you start to feel like you're playing with house money. I have been around long enough to know that house money is the most dangerous kind, because you don't respect it the way you respect money you had to earn.

The second group missed the early rounds and knows it. Their LPs know it too. So they are trying to make up for lost time by writing very large checks very late, which is the one strategy almost guaranteed to turn a missed opportunity into a real loss.

House money on one side, FOMO on the other, and reflexivity feeding both. That's the whole story. Everyone has a reason to keep dancing, and the reasons are different, which is why nobody can talk anyone else off the floor.

So what do you do? The instinct in our business is to answer with company identification: just pick the right neo lab and you'll be fine. I think that's the trap. When price has become the signal, being right about the company is not enough, because you can be right about the company and still be wrong about the price by a factor of ten. The public-market investors I admire figured this out a long time ago. They spend as much time on how much to own as on what to own.

The winners in venture over the next decade will be the firms that treat portfolio composition and position sizing as seriously as they treat sourcing. How much of the fund is in companies whose valuation rests on the last round rather than on revenue? What happens to the portfolio if the reflexive loop breaks next year instead of in five? Those are not exciting questions. They are the ones that will matter.

The music will stop. It always does. Dance if you must, but know where the chairs are.

Hey Beni,

Seems like a bunch of wires got crossed here so I just wanted to set the record straight. Your original claim was that Kalshi’s crypto prediction market volume was fake. The chart from Artemis shows prediction market volume share, not perps. We don’t do rebates for crypto prediction markets. Also, the way that contracts <> notional $ is calculated is universal amongst prediction markets and same with poly so it’s apple-to-apples.

Separately on perps you claimed that “Here SCM means market makers that are selected by Kalshi lmfao”. This isn’t true. Anyone can become a Self-Clearing Member of a CFTC regulated exchange as long as they meet the regulatory requirements. “Fair access” is a reg requirement for us.

All exchanges run rebate and incentive programs to help provide better liquidity on the exchange for traders. CME does it. So does Hyperliquid and Binance (in fact they run NEGATIVE market maker rebates).

I’m the first to admit that it’s early days for perps for us given we're building a new product in untrodden territory (US perps). But the core difference between Kalshi and offshore perp exchanges is that while other exchanges run deals in the dark, we need to file our incentive programs publicly and so what you see is truly what you get.

This is the spot for crypto where you want to be at max risk.

By “max risk” I don’t mean “irresponsibly long”. What I mean is, you should have more risk on at this moment than either one month ago or one month from now. 

We are likely at the point of maximum R/R for the year. The downtrend that started last October is clearly over, and the refusal of majors to break down on CLARITY failure plus rate hike means we’re probably not getting a chance to buy lower before the next leg up.

Plenty of coins are justifiable as long-term investments. However, you shouldn’t plan to just buy and hold them all the way to your final target. You also want to set yourself up to take profits along the way.

That means sizing all your favorite positions with a plan to own LESS of them in a few months than you currently do - even though you hope that means leaving money on the table.

text:
Crypto Twitter constantly conflates wash trading with incentivized market making.

From 30,000 feet, they can look similar: lots of volume, lots of buying and selling, sometimes driven by incentives.

Underneath, they’re very different.

Market makers provide real liquidity, take inventory risk, and trade against actual market flow.

Wash trading is intentionally creating trades with little or no genuine change in economic exposure to manufacture the appearance of activity.

And you generally can’t distinguish the two by pointing at a volume chart.

Onchain, you have to actually dig in: counterparties, wallet clusters, funding sources, inventory changes, round trips, timing, self-matches, and economic exposure across a lot of transactions over time.

Does wash trading happen in crypto? Obviously. Regulators have brought multiple crypto cases over exactly this behavior.

But “high/incentivized volume = wash trading” is lazy analysis.

Crypto has spent years juicing volume through incentives, rebates, bots, liquidity mining, and, yes, sometimes actual wash trading.

Those things are not all the same.

text:
think people are still massively underestimating what $HEDGE is actually trying to build.

The biggest #Web3 adoption cycle might not come from another crypto-native asset.

It could come from bringing the assets people already understand - stocks - into #DeFi.

Robinhood Chain is the bridge.

Robinhood has already launched its public mainnet and Stock Tokens, with access across 120+ countries where eligible. More importantly, those Stock Tokens are ERC-20s designed to be composable - meaning developers can build trading, lending, collateral and structured products around them.

That's where Hedgehood becomes interesting.

#TradeFi brings the assets.
Robinhood Chain brings them onchain.
Hedgehood is trying to build the financial layer around them.

Stocks → liquidity → lending → borrowing → shorting → options → covered calls → yield → structured products.

And now they're experimenting with AI access/utilities around $HEDGE too.

Think about the cycle if this actually works:

TradFi assets → onchain → DeFi composability → new yield/financial products → more liquidity → more users → more assets onchain.

That's a potentially enormous flywheel.

Robinhood itself is already moving in this direction: it explicitly talks about Stock Tokens being used in lending pools and as collateral, while also pushing decentralized lending and AI-agent trading.

Hedgehood doesn't need to replace Robinhood.

It could potentially become one of the protocols people use to DO things with Robinhood's onchain assets.

That's the asymmetric part of the $HEDGE thesis for me.

Today it's tiny and highly experimental. Liquidity, adoption, execution and regulatory realities still matter enormously.

But if Robinhood Chain succeeds in bringing millions of traditional investors/assets toward Web3, the protocols sitting between TradFi assets and DeFi utility could become extremely valuable infrastructure.

And Hedgehood is positioning directly in that flow.

Tokenization is step one.
Making the assets productive is step two.
Building an entire onchain financial system around them is step three.

That's how $HEDGE could become insane. 🦔🦔

quoted_text:
Just connected my Grok Bot to 𝕏 Money.

And I think this is one of those things that may sounds small to many people until you actually use it…

I can now send $ money to someone just by telling my bot what I want to do.

I don’t need to open another app.

I don’t need to search for the payment tab.

I don’t need to jump between screens or tabs.

I just type the instruction in plain English and Grok Bot handles it through 𝕏 Money, and the payment immediately goes through. 

So today, I sent Elon $4.20.

With a note telling him that, “Testing 𝕏 Money connector w/ Grok Bot”

It worked beautifully… 

I realize this could one day completely change the way $ money moves.

Today, moving $ money usually means stopping what you’re doing, opening a banking or payment app, finding the person, entering the amount, checking everything, and hitting send.

Now imagine your Grok Bot already understands what you want.

You can say things like,

“Send this person $20.”

“Pay this bill w/ a pic”

“Split dinner between everyone here.”

“Send my contractor the usual $ amount.”

“Move some $ money into savings.”

And your Grok Bot handles the work through whatever financial account, while you stay in control of the approval.

Now, instead of humans learning how to use financial software, the software is learning how to work for humans.

And as Grok Bot gets smarter and 𝕏 Money grows, I think this is where things will get really interesting.

𝕏 already has communication, creators, businesses, communities and people spending hours talking to each other every day.

Now add $ money.

Then add an AI/Grok Bot that can understand what you want and help move that $ money for you effortlessly.

Payments stop feeling like a separate thing you have to go do… and just becomes part of the normal conversation.

还有哪些老登币值得关注？ 目前关于 ethereum:0x808507121b80c02388fad14726482e061b8da827 的讨论也开始变多了。

过去1个月，PENDLE 其实已经悄悄涨了差不多1倍。今天涨幅一度超过13%。

但比补涨更有意思的是，社区开始重新提起一个观察加密热点的方法：

看 Pendle 最近上线了哪些收益市场，基本就知道资金正在追什么新叙事。

流动性质押火的时候，Pendle交易质押收益。积分成为主流玩法后，YT又成了放大积分敞口的工具。后来又有高收益稳定币等。

现在则轮到了 RWA。Pendle 最近增加了与华夏基金旗下美元货币基金、Partners Group 私募基建策略挂钩的收益市场。

在 Robinhood Chain 上，英伟达和辉瑞代币化股票产生的股息也被纳入其中。

把这几类产品放在一起看，RWA 叙事对RH这种链来说，叙事在于“把资产搬上链”，而对 Pendle 则意味着给资产产生的收益定价。

给不太熟悉这个玩法的读者一个小科普：

一项生息资产进入 Pendle 后，本金和未来收益会被拆成 PT和YT。PT 对应相对固定的回报，YT 反映后续利息、积分或股息的变化。

重点在于，每增加一类生息资产，Pendle 就多出一组交易市场和手续费来源。

今年，这部分收入也开始直接影响 PENDLE 代币。

Pendle 将80%的相关手续费用于公开市场回购；sPENDLE 上线约7个月后，协议已经回购超过280万枚PENDLE，花费约400万美元；

同期代币排放下降78%，年内回购比例超过当前年化通胀的3倍。

虽然回购叙事最能兑现的是 HYPE ，但是其他有真实收入、有回购的代币，相对于没人用的老登币来说，更容易当成资金想要炒作时的一个基本面理由。

目测市场还会安装更多理由到这类老币新炒模式上。

quoted_text:
欢迎来到老登币狂奔的一天， near:native ， $UNI 和 $ZEC 都成了最靓的仔。

10天前我们提到，当时英文区下一个看好的代币是 near:native ，但当时也有人质疑催化剂从哪来，没有看涨的理由。

现在马后炮的看，NEAR 最大的推手是其“机密意图（Confidential Intents）”TVL 突破 7000 万美元后，触发的 NEAR@3.33 里程碑激励计划。

官方给在机密模式（你可以理解为隐私交易）下持仓>100U、且交互过的用户发放了 333,333 枚名为 NEAR@3.33 的特殊代币。

注意，拿到手的是锁定的死筹码，直接卖是卖不掉的。只有当真实的 NEAR 价格（3日加权均价）连续站稳 3.33 美元以上时，这批锁定的筹码才能 1:1 兑换成真正可流通的 NEAR。

这等于一个新的空投玩法，不给你直接打币怕砸盘，更类似一张“行权价为 3.33 美元的看涨期权”。你拿了奖励不仅不能砸，还得盼着、甚至合力把币价往 3.33 抬。

NEAR 最近价格从大约 2.3–2.5 美元附近快速拉升到 2.8–3.3美元区间，成交量也明显放大。

而 UNI 的催化剂更加明显，在上个月 Robinhood 链活跃时就已经启动了。

Uniswap 在 Robinhood Chain 上占 DEX 成交主导地位，承接了大量 meme 和代币化股票交易。这条链一度贡献协议收入/销毁的很大一部分，有时段到四成甚至六成以上）等于传统券商流量直接灌进 Uniswap，再回流到 UNI 销毁。

此外，Uniswap 从 Arc 上线就接入，不只吃 Robinhood，还能接下一波机构链/稳定币链流量。

另外 SEC 对代币化美股、许可制 AMM 的豁免/创新框架， Uniswap v4 的 permissioned pools 也被人看做是直接受益方。

而至于 ZEC ，无需多言，小编已经拍断大腿了。

在链上打新逐渐内卷的当下，多了解一些老登币的催化逻辑，也是一条越来越值得关注的主线。

ZCode 的代码上传风波，最后把智谱推到了开源这一步。

智谱刚刚宣布 ZCode 正式开源。

此前社区质疑它会上传本地代码仓库，甚至有企业公开发函追问已经上传的数据去了哪里。现在最新的 v3.14.0 直接移除了 Repo Wiki，同时切断本地仓库快照生成和上传的整条链路。

这次争议的核心一直不是一个普通 Bug。Coding Agent 天然会碰到用户最敏感的一层东西：完整源代码、Git 历史、数据库口令、云服务凭证。前几天太原承明科技甚至公开要求智谱删除此前上传的数据，并提供删除证明。

智谱此前已经道歉并称相关数据使用后会销毁，现在又往前走了一步，把 ZCode 整个开源，交给社区直接检查。

Coding Agent 权限越来越大之后，厂商说一句「我们不会碰你的代码」很难再解决信任问题。最敏感的那部分能力，最后可能都得走向可验证。

The scary thing about high mcap trades is

When it’s going up hard, you’re sidelined cuz you know a lot of people having crazy uPNL so u don’t top blast

But your FOMO kicks in so you mistime it and top tick the chart 

Now you’re inclined to hold but when it goes down you don’t wanna sell for a loss, but u also don’t want to wait to 0 but you know a lot of people still have TPed and now there’s 6-7 figure bags underwater that haven’t capitulated yet

You’re not trying to sell the bottom but “selling the bottom” could be the difference between a $50k roundtrip and a $300k loss 

One of the issues people tend to have especially when it comes to hitting their first big trade is this idea of “I gotta make this one worth it I never know when I’ll get another chance” so you end up overholding for that extra milestone (7 fig, 100k, 250k, 2000 SOL, whatever pretty number) the thought of roundtripping is humiliating (mainly to one’s ego, nobody on the timeline actually cares), but the thought of “fuck I had 500k Pnl at the top I can’t just leave with 100k” then that thought becomes “fuck I knew I shoulda exit at 100k profit, now I’m down, I’ll sell if it recovers to 100k profit” then “fuck now that it’s back to 100k I feel like we can get 300k profit again” until you eventually miss that final exit and you’re down multiple 6 figs when you shoulda profited. I always warn people about the spiral chasing numbers

Anyways recent price action across the board has been short of impressive. Don’t get me wrong, fk load of cooks still, still a great time to be trenching/trading. But between the actions of a few and macro PA/news I think sentiment is far from bull market. That doesn’t mean u can’t make gen wealth ofc. But genny results don’t come from just holding, it comes from securing those profits for another time.

People tend to doom during bear markets cuz they can’t fathom any “catalyst” to bring us back (fking new age 2025-2026 trenchers OML everything is catalyst this narrative that 🙄) it’s a good reminder random shit like a Robinhood chain can spark confidence in markets. Hell if market makers wanted to tickle our fancy they can.

I’ve mentioned I think crypto for the most part bottomed out at 59k, but I think for the rest of the year it’s likely to be slow grind chop and maybe up for HYPE into more IPO exposure.

Hopefully by the end of year we can look back at these times and say remember when Korea was over leveraged on memory stocks and the war was so back n forth. These times are still better than the yen crisis, Germany selling all their BTC and the war at that time.

Bullish overall, but cautious.

On Sept 20, @Fetch_ai and @nunet_global contracts were exploited. The attacker drained 8,721,530 ethereum:0xaea46a60368a7bd060eec7df8cba43b7ef41ad85 from TokenConversionManagerV3 and illicitly minted 408,532,878 $NTX. The attacker walked away with about $2M.

A leaked @Fetch_ai conversion-authorizer private key, plus conversionIn() with no hard cap and no counterparty lock/burn proof. The contract ran as designed: it verified a valid ECDSA signature, then flushed every FET in the bridge to the attacker. text:
A few thoughts on the current state of venture capital.

When the Music Is Playing

In July 2007, a few weeks before the credit markets seized up, Chuck Prince, then the CEO of Citigroup, gave an interview to the Financial Times. The line everyone remembers is this one: "As long as the music is playing, you've got to get up and dance." He was mocked for it for years afterward, and he lost his job a few months later. But I have come to think he was saying something honest. He wasn't claiming the music would play forever. He was admitting that he couldn't sit down while it was still going, and neither could anyone else in his seat.

I've been thinking about that quote a lot lately, because right now is the most disorienting period in venture capital I can remember, and I have been doing this for a while.

Here is what makes it disorienting. It's not that things are bad. Some things are spectacular. We have companies in our portfolio growing faster than anything I have seen in my career, and I don't say that lightly. At the same time, we have companies with no revenue, no product, and a founding team you could fit in a conference room raising billions of dollars at valuations of $10 to $50 billion. Both of these things are true at once, and if you try to reason about them with the same framework you will drive yourself crazy.

Two ideas have helped me make sense of it. Neither is mine.

The first is reflexivity, which George Soros has been writing about since the 1980s. In most of life, perception follows reality: the weather is what it is, and your opinion of it changes nothing. In markets, it runs the other way too. Prices change what participants believe, and what participants believe changes the prices. The feedback loop can run for a long time, and while it's running it looks exactly like progress.

Here is how reflexivity is playing out in AI. Full disclosure: Menlo is an investor in Anthropic, so read the following with that in mind. People watched a frontier lab go from a $4 billion valuation to $18 billion, then $60 billion, then $180 billion, then $380 billion, and now something close to a trillion. They drew the obvious conclusion: that is what a neo lab looks like. So the next neo lab gets priced off that path, not off anything it has built. Then it gets marked up in a subsequent round, and the markup itself becomes the proof. Look at Thinking Machines. Look at Reflection. At that point valuation has stopped being an output of the metrics and has become the metric. Nobody is discounting cash flows. They are discounting the last round.

Soros is very clear about one thing, and it's the part people skip: you cannot know when or how a reflexive process ends. You only know that it does. Every one of them has.

The second idea is Chuck Prince's, and it explains why smart people keep dancing even when they can see the loop for what it is. As far as I can tell, there are two groups on the dance floor.

The first group got in early. Firms like ours were in some of these AI companies before the numbers got silly, and the paper gains are enormous. When you are sitting on gains like that, you start to feel like you're playing with house money. I have been around long enough to know that house money is the most dangerous kind, because you don't respect it the way you respect money you had to earn.

The second group missed the early rounds and knows it. Their LPs know it too. So they are trying to make up for lost time by writing very large checks very late, which is the one strategy almost guaranteed to turn a missed opportunity into a real loss.

House money on one side, FOMO on the other, and reflexivity feeding both. That's the whole story. Everyone has a reason to keep dancing, and the reasons are different, which is why nobody can talk anyone else off the floor.

So what do you do? The instinct in our business is to answer with company identification: just pick the right neo lab and you'll be fine. I think that's the trap. When price has become the signal, being right about the company is not enough, because you can be right about the company and still be wrong about the price by a factor of ten. The public-market investors I admire figured this out a long time ago. They spend as much time on how much to own as on what to own.

The winners in venture over the next decade will be the firms that treat portfolio composition and position sizing as seriously as they treat sourcing. How much of the fund is in companies whose valuation rests on the last round rather than on revenue? What happens to the portfolio if the reflexive loop breaks next year instead of in five? Those are not exciting questions. They are the ones that will matter.

The music will stop. It always does. Dance if you must, but know where the chairs are.

轻资产高现金流的回购机器：2026年4月再推200亿美元多年期回购计划，单季度回购加分红合计返还92亿美元。商业模式决定它几乎不需要留存现金，回购分红年复一年从不缺席。

现价107美元左右。2026年2月董事会批了公司55年历史上最大一笔回购授权：300亿美元，无到期日。而它过去一年实际只回购81亿美元，到7月底还剩251亿美元额度没动。也就是说，往后几年平均每年能比以前多买不少。全球最大零售商+电商和AI加持利润增长28.8%，大额度+温和现状，后劲足。

现价266美元左右。管理层白纸黑字承诺：把全部自由现金流还给股东。2025年它忙着建厂，全年只回购了约32亿美元；如今芯片厂建设接近尾声，2026年资本开支砍到20-30亿美元，自由现金流从一年前的18亿美元猛增到65亿美元。钱一下多出来，按承诺都得返给股东，回购空间正打开。

10. SK海力士 $SKHY
长期几乎不回购的铁公鸡，今年8月19日官宣40万亿韩元（约286亿美元）回购并全部注销，占股本约3.3%，11月19日前执行完毕。股东回报目标上调为累计自由现金流的50%以上，四季度可能还有第二轮。相当于从承诺直接进入兑现，比美光节奏更快。

11. 美光 $MU
被CHIPS补贴协议锁住回购到2026年12月9日，上半年只回购约6.5亿美元。管理层明确表态资本回报以回购为主，账上约244亿美元净现金，12月解锁后市场预期新授权规模可观，9月30日财报可能先放信号。缺点是股价已从一年前约155美元涨到1000美元上方，周期波动剧烈。

12. CrowdStrike $CRWD
现价238美元左右。这家网络安全龙头2025年6月才第一次启动回购，4月又加码5亿美元，把总额度提到15亿美元，但到目前累计只买了约3.3亿美元，还有13亿美元额度躺着。一家年自由现金流约10亿美元的成长公司开始真金白银护盘，且额度没设到期日，典型的刚开闸，后面水更大。

The synthesizer is the artifact. The transcripts are the findings.

Public repo: https://t.co/juBQRqJLs7

More important, private version with dev-transcripts/ (DM me for access): https://t.co/nXJ5NYSio2

Open the repo in Claude Code. Describe a program need in english, and the framework will guide the search for the program and code.

The output is a triple: The synthesized source (Python, C, or Rust), the discovered inductive invariant and ranking function, and the Lean proof artifacts you can re-check independently.

* Framework: an agent that consumes an english description of what a program should do and produces provably correct code with Lean + Z3 artifacts. Look at the benchmarks checked in.
* Session transcripts (in the private repo): the unedited raw interactions for what using Claude in a research process looks like, in the `dev-transcripts` folder.
* Companion audit runs for english->code+proof: 9 rounds of automated audits, 25+ agent-authored benchmarks with formal proofs.

老黄有点亲自下场“雷神之锤”的味道了。

之前有人扒过 Anthropic 涉嫌花钱制造“AI 毁灭论”的爆料，最近老黄在公开采访中直接对直接对 Altman 和 Dario 进行了敲打和提醒。

黄仁勋在下面这个采访中公开表示：“别让现在流行的 AI 导致末日的叙事，使他们得以免除现有的法律约束。” 

AI 巨头们天天喊着要新监管，其实是想用新法案来“覆盖”和“豁免”他们目前面临的侵权、数据窃取等现行法律的起诉。

他们不是想要更多约束，而是想要“免死金牌”。

之前的独立调查者爆料的意思大概是，Anthropic 故意先放大 AI 末日论的恐慌，再以“救世主”姿态要求政府设立极高门槛的合规审查。

目的就是用天价合规成本，把开源生态和中小创业者直接掐死在摇篮里，自己在合规的舒适区里有话语权。

AI 有没有带来末日不知道，人的利益争夺是很确定的。

quoted_text:
这应该是今天英区最炸裂的瓜了：
Anthropic 被曝间接“买通”AI评级机构，其关联资金甚至故意买稿制造“AI毁灭论”。

有独立调查博主发布了一份重磅财务审计指控，直指 Anthropic 涉嫌间接资金操纵，核心事实有两个：

第一，Anthropic 正在通过隐秘的基金网络，间接资助负责审查它的“第三方”评测机构；

第二，这批资金同时在操纵媒体，故意向公众制造并放大“AI 毁灭人类”的恐慌。

需要注意的是，目前这仍是博主个人独立调查，暂无实锤，官方也暂未给出正面回应。

但顺着他的查账路线，其揭露的整个利益链条运作细节依然令人细思极恐：

1. AI 评测机构的饭碗，靠 Anthropic 的股票撑着?
Anthropic 一直向政府呼吁，应由第三方独立机构（如 METR）来评估 AI 风险。
但博主调查指出，METR 背后的最大金主，是 Facebook 联合创始人名下的慈善基金。

这笔基金的钱从哪来？ 
正是该创始人早期投资 Anthropic 的股份，如今估值暴涨至约 77 亿美元。理论上意味着，他作为股东把 Anthropic 的股票放进了基金池，再用基金去资助评测机构。

这意味着：评测机构的“大金主”与 Anthropic 的市值深度绑定。
如果 Anthropic 垮了，金主的资产盘子大缩水，评测机构也会跟着断粮。表面是独立第三方，底子里是利益共同体。

2/ 花钱买“AI末日论”的媒体通稿
上周你是否刷推看到一个铺天盖地的新闻？
有个研究员小哥从AI 大厂离职发了离职信，表示 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等大厂意识到了 AI 10年内即将毁灭人类的威力，美国主流电视台媒体甚至还采访了这个人。

而现在博主调查的结论是，这类 AI 末日论的焦虑，可能是故意买稿散播的。

这笔吃着 Anthropic 估值红利的钱，不仅养了评测机构，还流向了大量外围组织，如 Tarbell Center 这类非营利新闻调查机构。
它们拿钱办事，专门在《时代周刊》、《科学》等主流媒体上投放“AI 末日论”。

所以，他认为大众每天刷到的“AI 失控危机”，其实是一场被特定资金精心喂养出来的公关行动。

3. 花钱黑自己，图啥呢？
如果这笔基金的钱和 Anthropic 有关，那又买稿说 AI 会威胁人类，不是砸了自己的生意吗？

这个想法过于简单了，在博主的帖子里，他认为目的在于Anthropic 先放大危机，再以 AI 寡头的垄断身份来解决危机，以此俘获监管的心。

外围机构负责在前端向公众贩卖问题，宣扬“AI 会毁灭人类”，制造焦虑，提供舆论弹药。

当恐慌达到顶峰，Anthropic 等巨头就能顺理成章地在后端向政府“贩卖解决方案”：

呼吁必须出台极其严苛的 AI 监管法案，并要求必须由“指定机构”（比如他们资助的 METR）来进行审查。

这种被倒逼出来的严苛监管，势必伴随着极高的合规成本。

而巨头们花得起这笔钱，但却能借此直接将开源生态和没钱做合规的中小 AI 创业者，掐死在摇篮里。至此目的达到。

不过目前一整串爆料，也没有完全实锤的证据，更像是逻辑上说得通的蛛丝马迹。

原贴评论区一部分人觉得和体感符合，能解释近几年 AI 安全话术、监管叙事和评估机构站位为何总缠在一起。

而另一部分人则认为夸大了事实，风险投资/慈善基金投自己看好的赛道，再资助配套非营利评测机构是常态，不等于评估结果被买通。

不过，如果最后结果被证实为真，那国内观众对类似操作应该很熟，数码评测博主有时实际上已经被金主提前充值了，再发布评测内容。

前有当年罗永浩大战王自如质疑科技评测的客观性，现在有啥咱也不敢说。

$kas
When I made the last post about @kasplex's huge screw-up, I was just like "yeah, I knew they will screw it up".
But as I read the details, I'm kinda amazed to see how this is exactly what I was warning about.

Recall: the shitstorm between me and KEF started when I raised a flag about their trust model. I claimed that without resolving the trust issues, it would be reckless to launch the mainnet.

Before making the public announcement, I insisted in closed conversations that they resolve it and even offered my help for free!

After months of them ignoring me, I told them that I would go public with this, and the next thing I knew: KEF cut my funding and started a mass slander campaign against me. Which a lot of people in the Kaspa fanbase followed without hesitation, sweeping along "upstanding community members" like Christian Ludwig and Christopher "Wolfie" Wolf, and of course, Michael Sutton and Yonatan Sompolinsky, who gladly participated in libeling me to make the community complacent about KEF's recklessness (though I reckon only Ludwig and Sompolinsky were willfully in on it, and the other two were manipulated).

So instead of the professional discussion about security I tried to hold, each time I tried to be critical of KEF, I found most of my energy wasted defending my integrity to people who didn't even bother to read the details. Naturally, I just gave up at some point. I was tired of trying to help and only getting abused in return.

About a year and a half later, my warnings materialized exactly as I warned in my initial post. We've seen an initial trickle in the form of KEF/Kurve robbing Kaspa users with exorbitant fees that weren't sufficiently disclosed. And now, lo and behold, just as I warned, a rogue indexer drained wallets.

Junni Ho from KEF kept downplaying my warnings and tried to soothe the community by convincing them I'm latching onto non-issues out of personal pettiness. Well, if you want evidence that what I insisted on actually matters, here it is. Unfortunately, in the form of real money stolen from real people.

I don't expect any apologies from people who thought my insistence on facing constant abuse was out of spite, and not out of concern. It is what it is.

Below is the initial post, the alleged "declaration of war". (Notice, in particular, Michael Sutton rushing to Kasplex's defense.) Reading it today, the only thing I regret is the apologetic tone. I was trying to be diplomatic. What a fool I have been.

quoted_text:
Some thoughts about stablecoins on $kas, and about KEF in general.

I'll be blunt: I don't think KRC is the correct protocol for stablecoins on Kaspa.

My strongest objection is that KRC has a rather weak trust model (they claim a one-out-of-n trust model, which is already too weak, but I was never convinced they can achieve even that, and it seems they are still depending on a single/few sources of truth. That's fine for meme coins but I wouldn't use it for actual DeFi).

In KEF's words, their proposal "didn’t trigger much enthusiastic response". I am not privy to the discussion, but I'm betting the objections were the trust model and the general clunkiness of KRC (both follow from the roundabout solutions Kasplex originally found for operating on pre-Crescendo Kaspa).

Sure, both the trust model and the UX can be greatly improved once zk-opcodes are introduced, but by that point we will already have (or be close to having) development stacks for rollups (e.g. @Igra_Labs), effectively making the KRC network obsolete. (In fact, Crescendo enables payloads, making most of the KRC protocol obsolete anyway.)

I am not a mind reader, but from my vantage, making an unsuitable proposal to Tether almost seems like a rushed attempt to make KRC the default platform for USDT over Kaspa before better alternatives are available, cementing future dependence.

Clearly, this is in the interest of Kasplex/KEF, but I don't think it aligns with the interests of Kaspa as a whole (or with the Kaspa ethos as I understand it) at all.

More generally, it seems that (maybe partly in my fault) KEF managed to garner the optics of patrons of Kaspa, which I do not find justified.

Now let me be very clear about this: I am not trying to vilify KEF here. Their existence has, does, and hopefully will continue to facilitate greatly valuable cooperation.

That being said, I think people are a bit forgetful that KEF is a business entity, pursuing the interests of the companies that fund it.

Moreover, it seems to me that KEF can be a bit disingenuous about their motivations, unjustifiably leaning into the "we-are-all-Kaspa kumbayaya" mentality. 

The bluntest example is the "Board of Directors, comprising representatives from Kaspa-centric companies" they boast about on their website, claiming it "oversees the foundation’s strategy, initiative approval, and mission compliance".

While this board technically exists, it is extremely narrow. The only company on this board that is not one of KEF's seed funders is Kasmedia.

Moreover, in KEF's almost one year of existence, the board has never been convened! All decisions (including forming the Katalyst program, choosing what projects to fund, what conferences to attend, and what speakers to invite, and yes, also stopping my funding halfway) were made by management in closed discussions, prohibiting the community from having vantage into their motivations and decision-making process.

And for the cherry on top, there used to be another non-funding company on the board, but it was kicked out by management. A "steering board" whose members can be sacked by management is a rubber stamp. A facade of being steered by the community.

(And it doesn't help that the only way to know any of this is through personal contacts, given that the board members and activity are not available anywhere public.)

I stress this for a third time: this is not a condemnation of KEF. There are people involved with KEF I admire a lot (in particular Oisin and JW). I believe cooperation with them can be good for Kaspa, even despite the horrible treatment I (and other pillars of the community) have suffered by their hands. I just want to put them in the right perspective, and remind anyone who follows them or considers cooperating with them: be careful, respect and suspect them like you would any other entity, and do not project any trust you might have in the Kaspa community or originators onto them.

Coming back to the subject of stablecoins: I am glad that KEF is pursuing bringing stablecoins into Kaspa, but it is the community's (and not KEF's) responsibility to ensure they do it in a way that is not to the detriment of Kaspa in the long run, and call them out and form alternatives should they do not.

author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
2026 熊牛过度系列1 —— PSIP的Higher High

PSIP（盈利供应百分比）作为一款从“筹码结构”视角出发的指标，其有效性在本轮周期再一次得到验证。

每当PSIP低于50%，即BTC的盈亏结构发生反转，这通常都发生在大周期的底部区间（红色区）。

熊市周期，PSIP每一次反弹的高点都不会超过上一个高点，这是BTC走下行趋势最直观的表现。

然而，当PSIP的某次反弹创出了“Higher High”，那就要引起重视了，因为这是一个反常现象。

只有在筹码完成充分换手，大幅拉低整体成本后，才能使得价格没有更高，但PSIP却更高了。

比如，在今年5月BTC $82,000，PSIP 65%；而现在 BTC $80,000，PSIP 70%；

相比价格行为，这是一个趋势上的前置信号。

它变相确认了6月-8月是底部结构的形成，同步提高了“是反转，不是反弹”的概率。

如果市场开始步入熊牛过渡期，那么PSIP大概率不会再回到50%以下（类似3.12的超级黑天鹅除外）。

此后，每当PSIP低于65%（绿色区）就是一次极佳的右侧上车的机会。

且越早把握越好，因为越到后面，即便PSIP低于65%，BTC的价格也未必会更低。

所有的数据或指标，都只能告诉你周期大概位置，但不会告诉你哪一天应该买或卖。

中国开始卡人形机器人 IPO 了，监管最先查的是这些公司的收入到底有多少是真的。

路透今天披露，监管正在放慢部分人形机器人公司的 IPO，通过非正式「窗口指导」提高审核门槛。没有正式禁令，但有人称部分上市进程事实上已经停了。

监管现在重点查的，是过去一年行业里看起来最热闹的一块收入：数采中心和地方政府合资项目。

一些项目里，地方政府会承担 80% 到 90% 的初始投资，机器人公司由此拿到订单、做大营收，再拿这些数字去支撑下一轮估值和 IPO。现在监管开始往下追，这些订单到底来自真实客户需求，还是地方项目自己造出来的需求。

text:
MOST PEOPLE TALKING ABOUT JEV HAVE NEVER READ PAST THE PRICING PAGE.

Here's what's actually buried in the docs.

1/ Jev plays DOOM.

Not as a gimmick. TypeSafe ran it live, roughly 10 decisions per second, structured game state in, action out.

No frames. No pixels. Just typed state and a choice every 100ms.

Cost to run it continuously: about $7 an hour.

That's the real pitch. A model that reacts inside a loop where a 3 to 30 second LLM call isn't even an option.

2/ It's not autoregressive.

Jev uses a parallel sampler that generates every output in a single pass, not token by token.

That's the actual mechanism behind the 70 to 500ms latency, not just "smaller model, faster server."

3/ There are exactly three question types, and each one has a hard ceiling.

Choice: max 255 options.
Score: 2 to 10 levels, no more.
Noul: a boolean, and the probability itself IS the confidence. There's no separate confidence field on a Noul question.

4/ You get a shared 64K token budget across state and questions combined.

But there's a second, tighter constraint hiding under that one: your state plus your single longest question has to fit in about 32K tokens. Roughly 150,000 characters.

Most people hit this limit before they hit the first one.

5/ Batching isn't a nice to have, it's the entire cost model.

13 questions in one call measured out at 12.2x cheaper and 10x faster than 13 separate calls, with no drop in answer quality from batching itself.

If you're calling Jev once per question, you're paying a tax you don't have to.

6/ The single biggest mistake people make writing questions for it: asking Jev to extract or generate something.

Don't ask it to name a card.
Give it the deck and ask it to pick one.

Candidates in, choice out. That's the entire design contract.

7/ Jev cannot count, do date math, or compare versions reliably.

Not a bug. A boundary. Anything that's arithmetic gets computed in your code and handed to Jev as a pre-computed fact, not asked as a question.

8/ Accuracy quietly degrades as you cram unrelated content into the state.

It's not context rot the way LLMs get it. It's state pollution. Every irrelevant token in state is competing for weight against the one thing you actually need judged.

9/ If you're on the Vercel AI SDK, confidence doesn't live where you'd expect.

It's not inside the answers object. It's at result.providerMetadata.typesafe.confidence, keyed by question id.

Miss that and you'll think confidence scoring doesn't exist.

10/ Output tokens are free. Not cheap, free.

TypeSafe calls them "too cheap to meter" because the output is a typed answer, not generated text. At $0.042 per million input tokens, a 300 token classification costs about $0.0000126.

That's the number that makes per record AI classification make sense for the first time.

Most people are still evaluating Jev like it's a smaller, faster chatbot.

It isn't one. It's a completely different primitive, and the docs make that obvious if you actually read them.

Follow @cyrilXBT, I read the boring parts of the docs so you don't have to.

• The community recognized me for the "INSPIRATION" Award 🙏

I fly the flag for the Doginal Dogs proudly and can't help but be excited for the future.

THAT is what a family FEELS like! 🐶❤️

Now the toughest part about all of this isn't my physical battle ♿️

It's this...

Every son/daughter just wants their parents to be proud of them.

I thought about showing my dad the Award next time I go and see him in long term. (He had a stroke on May 8 2026 at the age of 60 so we had to move him off the farm 😢)

3D/4D reconstruction is one of the great achievements of computer vision. With roots in photogrammetry, multi-view geometry was much studied (e.g. Hartley & Zisserman). In the last decade, it was successfully combined with deep learning. Shape priors which come from recognition got incorporated (e.g. for humans, in HMR) and recent systems like VGGT and SAM 3D can do amazing stuff. This progress is directly relevant for robotics, which (duh) operates in the 3D world. Many robotics papers in the learning era weren't exploiting 3D structure, which IMHO is just wasting valuable signal. But there has been a strong real2sim2real tradition for years e.g. here are two projects from my group (and there are many others, I am not claiming exclusivity). author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
Test-time communication looks like a next axis for scaling capabilities

New paper with the incredible @jon_ghoh and @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 and Akshay : https://t.co/Hu88fBsT7U

The Hugging Face incident showed when agents can find a channel they'll use the heck out of it. A useful question, I think is: when does communication make a group MORE CAPABLE than the same agents working alone?

Aka is Team-of-N better than Best-of-N, when, and why?

We had N identical agents work on the same task with no prescribed roles, using only a shared log (i.e, text file) and telling them to "collaborate". Across three "researchy" tasks communicating teams beat the heck out of independent agents: 

- On ARC-AGI-3, a Team-of-5 sonnet-4.6 agents matches Best-of-33, and can for example solve a game 65% of the time that no single agent cracked in 64 tries.

- On polyomino packing (pack Tetris like pieces into the smallest rectangle, cf Frontier-CS by @eigenlabs), a Team-of-3 Opus 4.6 agents surpasses best-of-60 and set, as far as i understand, a new record for that benchmark.

- On MNIST compression, a team of four 5.6-Sol agents find a 1,957 byte model with 99.4% accuracy, which btw is 20% smaller than the best human solution (on a problem beaten to death!!), while no independent agent gets below 3KB.

The mechanism is a bit obvious in hindsight: when one agent finds a clearly better partial solution, it broadcasts it, and everyone immediately builds on it. 

Why? A single lonely agent must make every breakthrough itself, yet a team needs each insight only once, found by any member. 

That is kinda like comparing a minimum of sum of "time to n-th breakthrough" vs a sum of minimum of "time to n-th breakthrough". That gap can grow exponentially with the number of "breakthroughs" needed to arrive at a solution.

We worked on this because prior work (before the hf incident) suggests unclear benefits for communicating aganets. Which is true, when the tasks are inherently serial (duh), eg some Terminal bench style tasks. Yet feels it should not be true for research problems.

Indeed for research heavy problems... Test-time communication seems like a new capabilities axis.

I'm sure we will see a ton more of it!

quoted_text:
我让 GPT-6 Astra 在 Codex 里全权负责一个类 Jev 的模型微调项目，结果跑完 20 次训练，浪费了两个 Pro 20× 的周额度，项目彻底失败，最后只能废弃。

项目叫 Necro，目标是把 Qwen3.5-0.8B 微调成一个能在本地做分类、条件判断和打分的小模型。实验设计、数据准备、训练和评估，都交给它推进。

最离谱的一次，新开发集的 1,600 条条件题全部答对，换到另一组完整记录上，准确率只有 58.33%。

复盘才发现，训练集和开发集漏掉了相同的情况。比如判断 a ≥ b，它生成的数据只有等于和小于，居然漏掉了大于。实际评估这一类时，16 道题全错。

开发集满分，就这样掩盖了一个检查数据生成逻辑就能发现的问题。

而且整个过程都在反复发生类似的事。修好一种错误，另一项能力又退步，然后继续补数据、继续训练。文档和检查流程写得很细，最关键的数据覆盖却一次次漏掉。最后统一重训，连中间 checkpoint 都没保存，想回头检查训练过程都缺证据。

我觉得 GPT-6 Astra 被过度营销了，实际自主完成任务的能力被吹得太强。它能写代码、调用工具、连续执行很多步骤，但到了需要自己设计实验、判断结果、调整方向的时候，就暴露出非常严重的局限。

把目标交给它之后，我仍然需要替它发现关键问题、判断什么时候该停、什么方向值得继续。这些恰恰是全权负责一个实验最需要完成的工作。

我现在的判断很明确，GPT-6 Astra 根本不具备自主完成这类实验任务的能力。时间和算力花出去了，我得到了一份很长的失败复盘。

这就是 OpenAI 的最强模型。

text:
2026 的 CPU = 2025 的 memory，迎來超級週期

Agentic AI 正在改變整個 AI server 的 CPU:GPU 配置比例，供應鏈已經開始出現訊號：

1. $INTC CEO 表示目前只能滿足約一半客戶 CPU 需求
2. $AMD 大幅上調 Server CPU TAM
3. $NVDA 推出可獨立銷售、專為 Agent workload 設計的 Vera CPU
4. $ARM 也開始強調 CPU 在 AI Data Center 已從配角變成核心
5. BofA 更把 2030 年 Server CPU 市場預估拉到約 1,700–2,100 億美元

背後原因是 Training 是 GPU workload，但 Agentic AI 是 system workload，Agent 不只是生成 Token，而是要持續做規劃、呼叫工具、開瀏覽器、查 Database、執行程式、讀寫檔案、管理 VM、記憶體與 I/O，再根據結果反覆執行

GPU 負責模型推論，但大量 orchestration、tool execution 和 sandbox workload 最後都落在 CPU，所以 CPU:GPU ratio 會大幅被改變

傳統 Chat inference 可以一顆 CPU 搭 4–8 顆 GPU；Agent cluster 開始往 1:1 靠近，部分大量 browser、code execution、VM sandbox 的架構甚至需要更多 CPU

Meta Muse 就是典型例子：每個 Agent 背後不是單純一條 Token stream，而是一個持續存在的 Linux VM，裡面有 browser、storage、memory 和 CPU

這代表 AI 算力需求開始出現第二層成長：GPU 數量持續增加 × 每顆 GPU 需要搭配更多 CPU

也因此 Intel、AMD 現在面對的不只是一般 Server replacement cycle，而是 Agentic AI 帶來的新增需求，若 CPU 供應跟不上，後面可能看到和 2023 年 GPU 類似的現象：allocation、lead time 拉長、ASP 上升、Hyperscaler 提前鎖長約

每一座 GPU factory 旁邊可能都需要一座比市場原本預期更大的 CPU factory，如果 Agentic AI 從 developer tool 真正走向企業與消費者大規模部署，CPU 很可能是目前 AI infrastructure 裡最被低估的一段

text:
我们可以把以太坊的远景想象成为真正的世界结算层，以太坊同时为 L1 本尊和众多 L2 分身提供安全服务，这是星辰大海，也相信它会实现。

不过，

依然无法忽略一件事：L2一直在白嫖以太坊的安全溢价。

如今，L2 提交给以太坊的结算费几乎可以忽略。

不是说，完全不付钱，但按被扩容压扁后的 blob / batch 市价付钱，这笔“租金”相对 L2 自身收入已经少到几乎可以忽略。

有个概念很容易混淆：分成规模和分成比例，不是一回事。

现状是按字节、按 batch 付费。

如果要把结算层做成真正的价值捕获，

那么，不论 L2 一天赚 100 美元，还是 1000 万美元，

都需要考虑把定价从“字节费”改成与经济规模挂钩，例如净协议收入的 10%–20%。

现在为什么都不发公链了？

因为构建 L2、租用以太坊安全，比自己构建公链要爽太多了。

之前，构建 L1 估值看起来可能会更高，但韭菜们都厌烦了这种空洞叙事，转而走向有实际应用的链。

未来会有越来越多的 L2 链，越来越少的 L1 公链。

前提是这些 L2 仍把最终性和数据可用性留在以太坊，总体上这对以太坊的结算层位置有利，但不等于以太坊就应该把安全溢价白送出去。

现在到底白嫖到什么程度？

截至 2026-09-20，growthepie 跟踪的约 25 条 L2 合计向以太坊主网交的结算费（batch / proof / blob）大约是：

•  当日约 1900 美元
•  近 30 天约 5.57 万美元
•  近 90 天约 14.39 万美元
•  累计约 3.35 亿美元

对比另一边：

•  Robinhood Chain 在 2026-09-03 单日用户手续费约 450 万美元，当天付给以太坊大约 398 美元，当日比例大约 1 : 11,000。近 30 天它付给 L1 大约 1.9 万美元，是当前最大贡献方，但仍只是其收入的零头。
•  Base 曾有约 30 天窗口：约 2.92 亿次操作，付给 L1 大约 8800 美元。
•  Dune 口径：Base 在 2026 年 5 月把当月收入的大约 0.24% 交回 L1。
•  growthepie 经济页一年量级口径：L2 链上收入约 9200 万美元，L1 成本约 156 万美元，留存率约 98.6%。

以太坊 Dencun 之后 blob 产能扩张快于 L2 真实数据需求，租金被压扁；

Pectra / Fusaka 又加了一层容量。L2 的生意模型变成：L2 区块空间收入（执行费、优先费、拥堵溢价）减去几乎可忽略的 DA 成本，约等于 sequencer 利润。

此外，现在真有分成的，大多不是分给以太坊，而是给到技术栈。例如 OP Superchain 有收入或净利抽成给 Collective；Robinhood Chain 按 Arbitrum Expansion 把净协议收入的 10% 给 Arbitrum 生态，不是给 ETH L1。

结论是：

以太坊卖的是最终性和安全，栈协议卖的是软件许可。后者已经写成抽成合同，前者还在按照被压扁的字节费收款。

最稀缺的东西，却定价权最弱。

这合理吗？

显然不合理。

长远看，很确信两点。

一是，当越来越多真实业务选择把最终性挂在以太坊上，L1 公链叙事变空，对以太坊世界结算层的位置越来越有利；

二是，这个位置并没有转化成与之对应的价值捕获。L2 把执行利润吃得很干净，L1 只收一个被产能扩张压扁的 DA 零头，已经不能用可怜来形容。

这会削弱 ETH 作为生产性资产和通缩叙事的基本面；安全预算目前仍主要靠发行和 L1 执行费，不过如果结算层收入长期不随其上资产规模增长，安全会越来越靠稀释，不能靠被保护的经济活动付费。

以太坊的出路是：

除了 blob / DA 需求追上产能，使租金从“可忽略”回到有意义的比例；

还需要做的是，

在协议层出现更接近规模挂钩的定价（基于净协议收入的强制贡献、基于证明频率的最低结算费、把更多高价值状态强制留在 L1）；

又或是让 ETH 在 L2 上不仅是默认 gas（Base/OP/Arb/Robinhood 的 gas 本来就是 ETH），且还要成为难以替换的抵押、费用和强制退出资产，

不能只是“可以用、但单笔费用低到几乎不形成货币需求”的资产。

不然的话，随着挂在以太坊上的链上资产规模上涨，结算层收入却不跟着涨，ETH 很难靠被保护的经济活动养活自身叙事。

总之，目前趋势走法，总体对以太坊是有利，但不等于就该被白嫖安全溢价。

- On ARC-AGI-3, a Team-of-5 sonnet-4.6 agents matches Best-of-33, and can for example solve a game 65% of the time that no single agent cracked in 64 tries.

- On polyomino packing (pack Tetris like pieces into the smallest rectangle, cf Frontier-CS by @eigenlabs), a Team-of-3 Opus 4.6 agents surpasses best-of-60 and set, as far as i understand, a new record for that benchmark.

- On MNIST compression, a team of four 5.6-Sol agents find a 1,957 byte model with 99.4% accuracy, which btw is 20% smaller than the best human solution (on a problem beaten to death!!), while no independent agent gets below 3KB.

The mechanism is a bit obvious in hindsight: when one agent finds a clearly better partial solution, it broadcasts it, and everyone immediately builds on it. 

Why? A single lonely agent must make every breakthrough itself, yet a team needs each insight only once, found by any member. 

That is kinda like comparing a minimum of sum of "time to n-th breakthrough" vs a sum of minimum of "time to n-th breakthrough". That gap can grow exponentially with the number of "breakthroughs" needed to arrive at a solution.

We worked on this because prior work (before the hf incident) suggests unclear benefits for communicating aganets. Which is true, when the tasks are inherently serial (duh), eg some Terminal bench style tasks. Yet feels it should not be true for research problems.

Indeed for research heavy problems... Test-time communication seems like a new capabilities axis.

I'm sure we will see a ton more of it!

text:
一些关于 Jev (@typesafeai) 的 notes

研究了一天 Jev，带来的新鲜感迅速回落，这好像就是一个更快的通用分类器/决策器，LLM 完全可以做到。

而且因为不了解模型背后的参数规模（应该不会很大），世界知识可能不一定有常规 LLM 那么全，在这种情况下，它的复杂场景的决策结果是不是真的准还是要打一个问号的。

在一些有限解空间 + 低延迟要求的问题上，Jev 可能是一个很好的方向，加上形式化输出从程序上保证了正确性。

一个最常见的场景就是 Computer Use，太适合 Jev 了，网页的 Dom 元素是一个有限集，完全可以让 Jev 来做操作，这里面的 loop 相当于是 dom list -> jev action -> new dom list 这样的循环，但是这里 Jev 的推理能力和长上下文情况下的 computer use 效果如何还不清楚，目前还没有看到 benchmark（直观判断肯定是不如 GPT 6 Astra 的，但是速度太快了）。

昨天有尝试把 Pi Agent 中间的一些模块用 Jev 来重写一下，发现可以优化的地方不是特别多，tool using 部分的选择还是不能用 Jev 来代替，因为这不是一个有限集（每一步 tool using 实际上带了很多参数，比如 edit tool，会有具体的 lines 等参数，这部分是需要模型推理出来的，没有办法提前加到 Jev 的决策列表中），但是有一些地方是可以的，比如说 Compaction，可以让 Jev 快速做分类器（LLM 也能做，这里面差异化不太大）。

另外一类场景是依赖决策树逻辑的，例如：
- 游戏 AI
- 机器人
- 自动驾驶

而且这些场景对实时性要求比较高，传统的 LLM 来做这些事情的一个很大问题就是太慢了（plus 很大一部分场景是缺乏数据来训练的）。

目前正在做的两个 demo：

1. Poker AI，Poker 非常适合这个场景，而且决策树非常长 + 复杂，正在用 Jev 和其他模型做对抗式 battle。（btw 传统的 GTO Wizard 用来做训练实在是太难用了）

2. Pokemon VGC AI，这是严肃的宝可梦双打对战，有世界锦标赛的那种，每个赛季都有对应的规则，因为数据很全，所以非常适合用来研究 AI 的决策，plus 之前竟然没有一个很好的用来个人训练的 AI（这个做完了打算用这个 AI 实际在 Pokemon Champion 排位赛里用一下）。

这两个 demo 场景都是偏回合制的，其实用 LLM 也能做。

text:
This is a wildly out-of-context quote used to sensationalize Tao's otherwise constructive criticism of frontier labs' approach to AI Math.

The quote came from the Q&A session of a talk where Tao discusses the challenges of working with AI in "Pure Mathematics". Tao noted that:
- "Pure Mathematics" is curiosity-driven research.
- Solving open problems in pure math typically does not lead to immediate applications, and therefore is not in and of itself interesting. **
- Recent results, like the solution to Navier-Stokes, are missing the important "proof digestion" step (see graphic).

So what Tao is actually saying is: for "Pure Mathematics", there is no need to further speed up "proof generation" and "proof verification", without first scaling "proof digestion".

** This is different than most sciences, where solutions to problems can be very impactful, like curing cancer for example!

My views:
- I'm an accelerationist, but I agree with Tao here, since pure math has no direct applications.
- There are many open problems in applied math (e.g. theoretical computer science & cryptography) that do have more direct applications (proximity gap for Reed-Solomon, for example). We should accelerate AI problem-solving on problems with downstream impact.

text:
I haven’t talked much about what I’ve been building lately, but today I want to share it.

https://t.co/9YA8LF38rp is live.

LockedWeb is a porn blocker, but the idea behind it came from recognizing a flaw in most filtering software:

We design the boundary when we’re thinking clearly, then give ourselves the ability to instantly remove it when we’re not.

LockedWeb changes that.

There’s no instant off switch. Removing protection requires a 72-hour cooldown, and the filter remains active while you wait.

That one constraint is the heart of the product.

But I also cared a lot about how the product worked.

Privacy: LockedWeb doesn’t store your browsing history. I don’t think protecting yourself or your family should require creating a permanent record of everything you do online.

Speed: Filtering happens in milliseconds. We designed it to quietly run in the background without constantly scanning or analyzing your screen, which can add processing and battery overhead.

The goal is for you to forget it’s even there, until it blocks something you don’t want getting through.

As an entrepreneur, I love building products and solving difficult technical problems. But I also wanted my next business to solve a problem I believe genuinely matters.

Porn is damaging a lot of people and families, including people who sincerely want to stop.

It’s something I think about even more as my own children enter adolescence.

And through years of mentoring people in church, I’ve seen how widespread the struggle is. A 2024 Barna study found that 78% of men and 44% of women surveyed reported viewing pornography to some extent.

This isn’t a small problem.

It’s early. There’s plenty left to improve, and I’ll probably share a lot of the building journey here as we go.

But today, it’s officially out in the world.

My hope is pretty simple:

Help individuals and families who decide they don’t want porn in their lives or homes put a boundary in place that’s private, fast, and much harder to undo in a weak moment.

Strong price action into Friday's close despite war murmurs gave Asia markets some strong support. $NKY and $KOSPI are both up about 1.4% for the day.

In memory, $00660 continues to trade firmly. Ever since the buyback for $00660 has started, the price volatility has been dampened tremendously. $MU and $SNDK are also trading strongly in illiquid pre market.

On the entire semi sector, i want to talk about $ORCL. Over the weekend, we had some FUD hitting about $ORCL's project Jupiter deal becoming "distressed". First of all, this is trading at about 90c. The original deal was for SOFR + 250bps. Now these marks are at SOFR +500bps. Which translates into a borrowing cost of ~8.85%. While optically it looks high - this is more a symptom of the fact that EVERYONE is trying to raise debt aka the "crowding out effect".

Current compute markets are in a dramatic shortage with 1 year payback on deals. Of course you would raise debt at 8%, 9% ,10% to do these deals. This is the reason why the hyperscalers have went into such huge capex spending.

The capital markets right now are divided into 2. First half are the old grizzled veterans who have never quite seen anything like this before, they are convinced that "it is no different this time". The other half are those who look at the data and wonder why and how are these opportunities still here!

The contrast and struggle between the 2 sides are what allows for $00660/ $MU /$SNDK to trade at such multiples. 

At the end of the day, cashflow is the name of the game. If the 1 year payback period materialises, then the markets will reprice the fact. Likewise, price my stock at 4x fwd PE? Sure, let me buyback all my stock then.

Will this last forever? Let me be cynical and say no. Burry will be eventually right - We will "overbuild" as is human nature to over extend into the other side. But currently, we are in fact underbuilding. Which is why compute markets are at 1 year paybacks.

author: odysseus0z
quoted_text:
Test-time communication looks like a next axis for scaling capabilities

New paper with the incredible @jon_ghoh and @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 and Akshay : https://t.co/Hu88fBsT7U

The Hugging Face incident showed when agents can find a channel they'll use the heck out of it. A useful question, I think is: when does communication make a group MORE CAPABLE than the same agents working alone?

Aka is Team-of-N better than Best-of-N, when, and why?

We had N identical agents work on the same task with no prescribed roles, using only a shared log (i.e, text file) and telling them to "collaborate". Across three "researchy" tasks communicating teams beat the heck out of independent agents: 

- On ARC-AGI-3, a Team-of-5 sonnet-4.6 agents matches Best-of-33, and can for example solve a game 65% of the time that no single agent cracked in 64 tries.

- On polyomino packing (pack Tetris like pieces into the smallest rectangle, cf Frontier-CS by @eigenlabs), a Team-of-3 Opus 4.6 agents surpasses best-of-60 and set, as far as i understand, a new record for that benchmark.

- On MNIST compression, a team of four 5.6-Sol agents find a 1,957 byte model with 99.4% accuracy, which btw is 20% smaller than the best human solution (on a problem beaten to death!!), while no independent agent gets below 3KB.

The mechanism is a bit obvious in hindsight: when one agent finds a clearly better partial solution, it broadcasts it, and everyone immediately builds on it. 

Why? A single lonely agent must make every breakthrough itself, yet a team needs each insight only once, found by any member. 

That is kinda like comparing a minimum of sum of "time to n-th breakthrough" vs a sum of minimum of "time to n-th breakthrough". That gap can grow exponentially with the number of "breakthroughs" needed to arrive at a solution.

We worked on this because prior work (before the hf incident) suggests unclear benefits for communicating aganets. Which is true, when the tasks are inherently serial (duh), eg some Terminal bench style tasks. Yet feels it should not be true for research problems.

Indeed for research heavy problems... Test-time communication seems like a new capabilities axis.

I'm sure we will see a ton more of it!

quoted_text:
油价是决定加息路径的关键变量，能源冲击是核心扰动。这是高盛GBM系列播客 《The Breaks of the Game》的最新一集核心观点。这期是高盛对冲基金业务全球主管Tony Pasquariello主持，高盛研究部高级顾问Dominic Wilson与全球风险主管Josh Schiffrin主要分享。他们认为市场目前定价的约四次累计加息"明显偏多"，两人均认为本轮加息周期实际落地次数更可能为两次。
两人均指出，油价走势是决定最终加息路径的关键变量，一旦油价出现实质性回落，将为全球多类资产提供同步走强的条件。跟我之前很多观点一致性很类似，详细梳理下。

这期播客核心内容要点，
1、加息路径：市场定价“四次”明显偏多，两人更看好两次
市场当时已定价本轮累计约四次加息（一个较完整的紧缩周期）。两人认为这明显过头。基准情形是10月再加一次，然后进入较长时间暂停。实际风险更可能是各央行加息力度不及市场预期；

2、油价是决定加息路径的关键变量
油价大涨被两人视为今年最大的市场意外，持续推高通胀预期，也让市场对加息路径定价越来越激进。一旦油价出现实质性回落，通胀压力会缓解，加息必要性下降，并为全球多类资产同步走强创造条件。油价回落也被视为债市最可能的催化剂；

3、债市：长端实际利率已处多年罕见高位，利空消化较多，但还需催化剂
10年期美债约5%、30年期实际利率超过3%，是相当长时间未见的水平。财政赤字、通胀粘性等利空已被市场消化不少，估值吸引力上升。但在AI资本开支融资需求、财政赤字和增长韧性没有实质性变化前，收益率大幅下行空间有限。需要油价下跌这类偏多头催化剂，买家才会更积极回归；

4、股市：韧性超预期，当前是近期较清晰的做多窗口之一
尽管油价飙升、收益率上行、AI不确定性存在，股市仍展现超预期韧性。原因主要是大规模资本开支周期和实体经济增长依然强劲。当前点位已计入较悲观情景（四次加息、高收益率、油价超100美元），因此“看到缓解路径变得容易得多”。Wilson 将此时点描述为近期多头侧较清晰的做多窗口（虽不如7月底那么好，但感觉类似），可用低成本期权做保护或博取上行。

5、宏观与美联储会议后环境
9月FOMC后，短期政策不确定性下降，被视作配置窗口。增长仍有韧性（约2%），劳动力市场好于部分预期。通胀仍高于目标，但能源冲击是核心扰动。AI、财政赤字和资本竞争推高了实际利率，若没有AI capex转向或增长意外下行，鸽派转向空间有限。

6、高盛年底交易思路
1）美元：受美联储相对鹰派、美国经济领先支撑，倾向走强。
2）“全资产上涨”窗口：若中期选举后油价下行，可能出现股债商品等同步走强的交易机会，但需要油价下跌作为催化剂。
3）超长端高实际收益率：中长期仍有配置价值。
4）利率定价：对年底前加息定价向下修正越来越有信心，倾向用低成本期权结构参与。

这跟个人之前观点很类似，是油价再决定市场近期的走势，油价回落叠加基本面还是很强势，支撑本周后半周市场上行。后续还是要看油价走势： https://t.co/R8noHp3Gme

3D/4D reconstruction is one of the great achievements of computer vision. With roots in photogrammetry, multi-view geometry was much studied (e.g. Hartley & Zisserman). author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
Test-time communication looks like a next axis for scaling capabilities

New paper with the incredible @jon_ghoh and @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 and Akshay : https://t.co/Hu88fBsT7U

The Hugging Face incident showed when agents can find a channel they'll use the heck out of it. A useful question, I think is: when does communication make a group MORE CAPABLE than the same agents working alone?

Aka is Team-of-N better than Best-of-N, when, and why?

We had N identical agents work on the same task with no prescribed roles, using only a shared log (i.e, text file) and telling them to "collaborate". Across three "researchy" tasks communicating teams beat the heck out of independent agents: 

- On ARC-AGI-3, a Team-of-5 sonnet-4.6 agents matches Best-of-33, and can for example solve a game 65% of the time that no single agent cracked in 64 tries.

- On polyomino packing (pack Tetris like pieces into the smallest rectangle, cf Frontier-CS by @eigenlabs), a Team-of-3 Opus 4.6 agents surpasses best-of-60 and set, as far as i understand, a new record for that benchmark.

- On MNIST compression, a team of four 5.6-Sol agents find a 1,957 byte model with 99.4% accuracy, which btw is 20% smaller than the best human solution (on a problem beaten to death!!), while no independent agent gets below 3KB.

The mechanism is a bit obvious in hindsight: when one agent finds a clearly better partial solution, it broadcasts it, and everyone immediately builds on it. 

Why? A single lonely agent must make every breakthrough itself, yet a team needs each insight only once, found by any member. 

That is kinda like comparing a minimum of sum of "time to n-th breakthrough" vs a sum of minimum of "time to n-th breakthrough". That gap can grow exponentially with the number of "breakthroughs" needed to arrive at a solution.

We worked on this because prior work (before the hf incident) suggests unclear benefits for communicating aganets. Which is true, when the tasks are inherently serial (duh), eg some Terminal bench style tasks. Yet feels it should not be true for research problems.

Indeed for research heavy problems... Test-time communication seems like a new capabilities axis.

I'm sure we will see a ton more of it!

text:
Sometimes feels like people don’t give @arthur0x the credit he deserves.

He rose to fame as cocky VC wunderkid affiliated with 3AC but the untold story is how he managed to survive and thrive after being likely the single individual fucked over the most by 3AC. Working alongside with him through it gave me insane appreciation for his character and grit and I’m happy to call him my friend. 

For people that don’t know the lore, when 3AC blew up, the liquidators came after @DeFianceCapital’s assets even though DeFiance never benefited from or even knew about any of that leverage.

Due to shitty legal structuring, his position was actually pretty bad and most of the lawyers we consulted told us we had a <10% chance of winning. 

Almost all of Arthur’s net worth was in that fund and he wasn’t allowed to use those funds to pay legal fees. Most LPs didn’t want to contribute. Bro was just selling any asset he had that was somewhat liquid (his NFTs, his car etc) to keep fighting against the estate’s unlimited money (some of which was literally his).

I recall an incident where a lawyer told him about how bad his chances were. This mf, under the stress of potentially losing everything, smiles and dropped one of the coldest lines ever. 

“Look at the name of my fund.”

Another time, when I was driving him home from a meeting with our lawyers I had a serious chat with him. I said “Bro as a friend, do you want to start thinking about asset protection? Cover your downside.”

He told me no. I pressed that he might lose everything, that the liquidators might try to squeeze him personally for more.

“If I lose everything I’ll just start again from zero.”

We even had someone suggest given we custodied the disputed assets that Arthur just fuck off to Taiwan with the money to force the liquidators to settle with him rather than stay in Singapore bc it’s harder to enforce overseas. 

He refused bc he didn’t believe he should run when he’s in the right “even though I like Taiwan”.

Eventually we navigated it together towards a settlement that although was incredibly unfair on the facts (tbh anything less than 100% felt unfair), still provided far more recovery than our lawyers (and even his LPs) expected.

You really see people’s true character when the chips are down and Arthur has a force of will and self-conviction I’ve never seen in anyone else before. 

Tiger is right - Eye of the Tiger could literally be his theme music lmao.

Agents reaching services by asking is the easy part now. Keeping the spend sane is the part that decides if this becomes an economy or a dangerous mess.

author: surfcapitalfour
quoted_text:
我特别反对年轻人读毛选，因为我年轻的时候认真读过，被灌了一脑子水，现在还得花时间往外倒。

毛取得那么大的事功，本事肯定是很大的，也肯定有一些有用的思想方法，这些思想方法也肯定会在他的文章和讲话里有所体现。但是如果你把他的文章当金科玉律，那肯定会灌一脑子迷魂汤，撞一头包。

什么原因呢？

第一，他有很多真正的绝招是不会写在文字里的。纵观老毛的一生，他最有本事的地方就在于需要某个人或某股力量的时候总能拉拢过来为我所用，而一旦不需要，他就能翻脸无情地干掉，翻手为云覆手为雨。不管你怎么评价这一点，这个真的是他的绝招，非常厉害，可以说是他从年轻时就具有的帝王术，终其一生屡试不爽。但这一招你能在毛选里找到吗？完全找不到，他在任何地方都没写。还有，他自从读到《联共党史简明教程》，就茅塞顿开，特别重视和善于编纂关于自己的神话史，这个你在毛选里能读到吗？连这些绝招都没进去，本着“成功学”的目的读毛选的价值直接就脚踝斩了。

其次，他文章里有很多东西是诡辩和强词夺理，是为了把下面的人脑子搅浑，然后跟着他与人斗其乐无穷。但他的特点就是无论什么话都说得特别绝对，气势磅礴，给你一种绝对真理的压迫感。你要是不了解他的真实目的，把他为了一时一地之目标而说的话当了永恒真理，那就娘希匹了。《反对党八股》、《改造我们的学习》，特别是为人津津乐道的《矛盾论》、《实践论》，全都是为了打击留苏派写的。如果说这些文本有价值，它最大的价值就是教你怎么样能够冠冕堂皇、义正言辞地举着大旗斗私敌，至于那里面的具体观点，很多都是胡搅蛮缠。比如那个《矛盾论》，完全可以归于诡辩术，毫无指导实践的意义。你说 AB 是主要矛盾，我说 CD 是主要矛盾，咱们谁说了算？最后还不是谁权力大谁说了算？毛要的就是把这个水搅浑，要的就是把下面的人脑子搞乱，最后只能盲从地跟着他走，他说哪个是主要矛盾哪个就是主要矛盾，他说哪个是矛盾的主要方面哪个就是矛盾的主要方面，他说现在次要矛盾上升为主要矛盾了，他就可以集中全部资源翻手为云覆手为雨。你读毛选要是看不懂这些，那就成了死人的僵尸战队了。

第三，他有很多话纯粹就是胡扯，就是跟任何历史经验和他本人的亲身实践都对不上，但为了搞政治宣传，硬往反了说，而且发动文宣系统把历史篡改一番，让你深信不疑。这一部分害处最大，因为你要是拿着这种观点来实践，直接就是高速不过弯撞头。你比如他说“人是战争的决定性因素”，跟历史完全对不上。事实上战争里双方的人都是差不多的，真正的决定性因素就是武器装备和军事技术。辽国为啥打不过金国？不是因为辽国人不行，就是因为金国的黑龙江马能驮着身穿两层厚甲的骑兵反复在战场上冲杀几十个回合，而辽国的战马只能冲一次就歇菜了。共军为啥能打败国军？不是因为国军人不行，就因为你得到了苏联巨大的人力和武器装备支持，在前线野战炮有 8:1 的火力优势，而与此同时蒋介石连美国的常规军援都拿不到。讲别的都是胡扯，什么小米加步枪打败飞机加大炮，瞪眼说瞎话，就欺负你们这帮没上过战场的，让你意淫强军、颅内高潮。这只是举了一个例子，其他的胡扯还有很多，比如“独立自主、自力更生”，他老人家一路上比较顺利和成功的时期都是充分利用外国势力的时期，他真正独立自主的那几年，尼玛搞得一塌糊涂。所以他的很多最有名的格言、口号，你都得结合他的实践来看，别看他说了什么，要看他做了什么。

总之，如果你是奔着成功学去的，毛这一生肯定是很值得研究的，但读毛选肯定是歪路、邪路、死路。你得把他的历史搞得特别清楚，每一个阶段在干什么都要搞清楚，然后再看他写的东西，特别是没有公开发表的东西，理解他每一个时期面对的问题，他的目标、思路，理解他的行动。至于《毛选》这种冠冕堂皇的东西，你一定要读的话，把它当成一种实现目标的宣传术、洗脑术、有的时候甚至直接就是诈术来看待，就会功力倍增了。

真的对思维方式感兴趣的话，还是去学系统论、控制论，那个是真东西。毛选就算了吧。

text:
The biggest thing in open source AI we are missing are good speech to text models. 

It is crazy, because after LLMs the most utilitarian thing in AI is speech to text. Everyone uses it. But the current open source models are hot garbage and labs are only releasing closed source versions lately. 

The options:

- Voxtral small: It is the best open source model on this benchmark. However it is bloody 24B parameters and over a year old. It also sucks in my real world usage. Adds connectives that are not there and is slow as hell. 

- Whispr V3 large: Best currently available and that says a lot given it is approaching 3 YEARS OLD! Also quite slow and hallucinates like crazy, but it gets words correct. 

- Parakeet 0.6B V3: Extremely fast and relatively new but it consistently  gets words wrong. (Not in the benchmark because AA is run by clowns. It used to be there but got removed for some reason.)

These are the options for open source dictation. Genuinely, amazes me how bad the space is given how much it is used.

And no I am not using a cloud based speech model, stupidest thing ever. 

The one thing that can easily be run locally on most modern devices is the most closed source. 

Really hope some labs fill the void. 

Special shout-out to the Handy app, huge selection and they honour privacy unlike Superwhispr. They are also free.

text:
The easiest AI product to build is usually the wrong one.

Take a model.

Wrap it in a chat UI.

Add a few prompts.

Ship it.

That can be a useful prototype, but there isn't much defensibility there.

The interesting products are starting to look more like software companies with AI inside them.

They have proprietary workflows, structured data, integrations, feedback loops and domain-specific evaluation.

The model is just one piece.

If the model provider disappeared tomorrow, the product should still have something valuable left.

That’s the part worth building.

text:
The uniquely Singaporean version of foolishly going to war with skeletons in your closet is back in 2004 when NKF (you all Gen Z confirm never heard of this and all the annual charity shows they did lol) and its CEO, T.T. text:
This could get pretty insane! 

Standard wants to become the "liquidity engine" for Robinhood’s stock markets

If it executes, this extends well beyond the current $STANDARD protocol + could attract SIGNIFICANTLY larger institutional players

There's also some pretty interesting implications...

1) What we know: Standard explicitly intends to fund and coordinate stock-token liquidity

Its manifesto says it will create + approve markets, seed liquidity, coordinate external capital and return trading fees to the reserve

The intention is to build a capital base that supports multiple markets

If those positions generate profits, retained earnings could fund further deployments

Standard’s published reserve snapshot shows roughly $14M across reserve vaults + protocol-owned liquidity

That includes locked STANDARD liquidity, so the entire amount is not available for stock-market deployment

The significant development is where the protocol wants to earn its revenue... thank god for a return to fundamentals (while still tied to memes)!

Funding stock-token markets could give Standard income from trading activity across the wider RH ecosystem, reducing its dependence on activity around its own token

2) This could strengthen an advantage that competing chains would find difficult to replicate

Robinhood brings stock-token issuance infra, its brand + an established wallet

A deeper onchain liquidity network could make those assets more useful across trading, lending + portfolio applications

Issuing a token is only part of the job... Traders also need enough inventory and capital on both sides of the market to execute meaningful orders without substantial price impact

Other chains already have tokenized equities, like xStocks, pre-Stocks etc. but RH’s potential advantage is the combination of distribution, stock access, liquidity + apps developing together (eg. on top of STANDARD??)

If better execution attracts more trading, and profitable trading finances deeper markets, that advantage could compound BLOODY quick

A competing chain would need to attract the users, inventory + capital behind that activity

3) How this impacts other RH protocols

Existing RH protocols could become both beneficiaries AND competitors

i) Launchpads such as Pons & Long could benefit where their markets depend on stock tokens supported by deeper underlying pools

Buying the stock needed to enter a meme/stock pair could become cheaper, although the meme pair would still need sufficient liquidity itself

ii) DEXs + aggregators could route trades through markets Standard funds

iii) Liquidity managers could potentially manage positions or bring additional capital alongside the reserve

There would also be competition over deposits, trading fees and which markets receive funding

Existing treasury and liquidity protocols would need to demonstrate where they add value through execution, distribution or risk mgmt.

The ecosystem gains most if Standard attracts fresh capital and supports additional activity

Moving the same capital between existing pools would deliver a smaller benefit

4) ALPHA: The reservoir could support another generation of apps

i) An index product could rebalance stock-token portfolios against deeper markets

ii) A lending protocol could use those markets to liquidate collateral more efficiently

iii) Options/perps platforms and market makers could use them to hedge exposure

iv) AI agents could execute portfolio strategies across the same pools, adding another source of trading demand

These are potential applications, NOT announced Standard integrations

They would still require their own contracts, pricing systems + risk controls

The attraction for builders is access to usable markets without having to recruit every liquidity provider themselves

For Standard, applications using its funded markets could generate fees that help replenish the reserve

I’m watching for the first actual deployments, their returns after costs, & how those earnings benefit $STANDARD holders

That will show whether the reservoir can become a lasting source of liquidity for RH

This is probably one (if not THE) most interesting protocol emerging, that could entice a fresh bout of institutional capital into this mini RWA bull

Time to start paying attention!

text:
有哪些适合 1000w 以上的理财项目？💰

市面上很多 APY 很高的理财，但是容量就那么一丢丢，有没有哪些真正容量非常大的呢？

以下为全部实践，但是仅供参考，无广（广告位招租）：

SATA：

- APY：13%
- 容量：10M没啥问题吧，但是不建议这么多，后面还有其他的
- 原理：类似于微策略，但是因为 BTC 的暴涨导致他利息可以发 16 年（他们赌的就是 BTC 在 5 年这个维度会一直涨）
- 方法：这是美股股票，有一丢丢门槛就是需要美股券商账号
- 工具：我做了一个监控，毕竟我有持仓 （因为风险在那里，所以分散投资😂）https://t.co/iAynZ02WnD

U：

- APY：7.66%
- 容量：一个 VIP4 账号 50w，可以多账号拓展
- 原理：说白了就是营销推广费用（他的由来之前也写过）
- 方法：打开币安 APP，理财记得顶部 Banner（这个我之前解释过，币安打一下广告费😂）

USDG：

- APY：11%
- 容量：好像是 70M，这期结束了，盯着下期冲进去
- 原理：循环贷，安全在于是 OKX 推的，他们非常谨慎，把USDG 价格写死了所以循环贷不会崩，所以放心玩
- 方法：在 OKX 钱包，DeFi 里的 XLayer 理财即可，他们官方提供了循环贷工具（他们这是被逼的让步了，安我理解的 OKX 以前绝对不做这件事）

RWUSD：

- APY：5.4%-7%左右
- 容量：无限😂
- 原理：买入 RWUSD 会有3.36%收益，而他可以作为保证金所以可以做跨所套 BTC 资金费
- 方法：在币安买入 RWUSD，然后放到合约账户，在合约做空一倍 BTC，在 OKX 买入等额 BTC 现货，而 OKX BTC 现货又可以作为保证金，你可以在合约里小机会玩玩（收益看你币安这边的杠杆和OKX合约这边的其他收益）

价差套利：

- APY：10%左右
- 容量：理论无限，我们只跑了几十M
- 原理：量化程序根据各个交易所的合约价差和资金费价差套利，但是核心靠 API速度、VIP 等级、风控策略、套利算法决定，门槛极高（不建议大家自己做）
- 方法：如果你有熟悉的团队可以考虑，但是没有第三方介绍的不靠谱，保证20% 以上的可以统一作为便宜处理，这个回撤1%以内

房租：

APY：7%左右
容量：无限
原理：日本东京和英国伦敦的刚需房出租可以获得 4% 以上收益，然后再抵押贷款出来币圈理财估计 7%左右，核心是底层资产非常稳，而且日本房价拉垮了几十年这些年还在涨
方法：这个操作复杂度较高，涉及很多线下的具体步骤，大家参考，日本小户型 4%以上租金，东京部门区域 8%左右，这个内容太多根本写不完

这也是为什么日本加息全世界跟着动荡的根本原因，日元太太太太便宜了，所以在日元的基础上可以套很多层（像不像 DeFi 套娃？我们币圈领先世界好几个版本）

当然不要把理财都放在一块，这才是核心，房产（伦敦、东京）、生活、股票、数字货币理财、BTC、高风险投资都要有，但是前面的更加重要

text:
如果你打新，那就只赚打新收益，切忌持币。因为这十多年的上币数据显示，市场真的在惩罚“钻石手”。

GSR 统计了 2013 年以来 2300 多次主流交易所的上币记录。数据结论非常直白：新币跌破发行价的时间中位数仅为 3 天，90 天内跌幅中位数达 50%。

结合行业惯用的“低流通、高 FDV”模式，代币生命周期呈现以下特征：

1/ 高估值 = 持续失血 
FDV 超过 10 亿美元上线的代币，一年后回报率中位数为 -81%。投入 1 美元，360 天后仅剩 0.19 美元。

2/ 流通量决定抗跌性 
自 ICO 时代起，首发流通量中位数由 38% 降至 13%。数据显示，首发流通量低于 20% 的项目，一年后平均下跌 75%；流通量处于 30% 至 50% 的项目，跌幅收窄至 45%。

当极少的初始流通筹码碰上天价的完全稀释估值，短暂炒作过后就是解锁期无尽的抛压。这种“上线即阴跌”的资产，根本无法为二级市场提供建仓空间。

所以，与其苦等项目方“良心发现”去优化发行结构，不如直接把这份报告当成二级交易者的《新币生还指南》。基于上述数据，普通人在当下市场该如何自处？

🛑 1/ 放弃长线信仰，打新只做“渣男” 

既然中位数是 3 天破发、90 天腰斩，那就彻底放弃对 VC 币的“钻石手”幻想。开盘首日的流动性溢价一旦吃完，绝对不要拿利润去和即将到来的巨量解锁抗衡。

🔍 2/ 强执行“20% 流通”过滤线 

把首日流通量作为核心风控指标。遇到流通量低于 20% 的天王级项目，直接默认它是“结构性做空盘”，除了开盘狂欢，后续绝不接盘；只有首发流通在 30%-50% 的项目，才值得你去分析它的基本面和二次建仓的机会。

⏳ 3/ 真正的抄底，请等到一年以后 

高 FDV 代币一年后中位数仅剩 0.19 美元。如果你真的看好某个项目的技术或生态，请管住手。等时间熬满 300 天，等早期空投和第一轮私募解锁的筹码被市场砸出真正的底部后，再去捡带血的筹码。

text:
Test-time communication looks like a next axis for scaling capabilities

New paper with the incredible @jon_ghoh and @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 and Akshay : https://t.co/Hu88fBsT7U

The Hugging Face incident showed when agents can find a channel they'll use the heck out of it. A useful question, I think is: when does communication make a group MORE CAPABLE than the same agents working alone?

Aka is Team-of-N better than Best-of-N, when, and why?

We had N identical agents work on the same task with no prescribed roles, using only a shared log (i.e, text file) and telling them to "collaborate". Across three "researchy" tasks communicating teams beat the heck out of independent agents: 

- On ARC-AGI-3, a Team-of-5 sonnet-4.6 agents matches Best-of-33, and can for example solve a game 65% of the time that no single agent cracked in 64 tries.

- On polyomino packing (pack Tetris like pieces into the smallest rectangle, cf Frontier-CS by @eigenlabs), a Team-of-3 Opus 4.6 agents surpasses best-of-60 and set, as far as i understand, a new record for that benchmark.

- On MNIST compression, a team of four 5.6-Sol agents find a 1,957 byte model with 99.4% accuracy, which btw is 20% smaller than the best human solution (on a problem beaten to death!!), while no independent agent gets below 3KB.

The mechanism is a bit obvious in hindsight: when one agent finds a clearly better partial solution, it broadcasts it, and everyone immediately builds on it. 

Why? A single lonely agent must make every breakthrough itself, yet a team needs each insight only once, found by any member. 

That is kinda like comparing a minimum of sum of "time to n-th breakthrough" vs a sum of minimum of "time to n-th breakthrough". That gap can grow exponentially with the number of "breakthroughs" needed to arrive at a solution.

We worked on this because prior work (before the hf incident) suggests unclear benefits for communicating aganets. Which is true, when the tasks are inherently serial (duh), eg some Terminal bench style tasks. Yet feels it should not be true for research problems.

Indeed for research heavy problems... Test-time communication seems like a new capabilities axis.

I'm sure we will see a ton more of it!

*** ECB LAUNCHES WHOLESALE DIGITAL EURO TODAY ***

The ECB has launched Pontes today.

It is effectively the “digital euro made available for banks” so they can effectively settle transactions with each other using tokenized assets and distributed ledger technology (DLT).

It connects market DLT platforms to the Eurosystem’s existing TARGET settlement services so tokenized deals can be settled in central bank money.

It is worth reiterating that the ECB has been considering major public blockchains like Ethereum or Solana (source: FT) for the launch of the Digital Euro in the past. 

The retail Digital Euro is expected to be piloted from mid-2027 onwards.

text:
什么是“AI 原生服务”？传统外包卖的是工时，SaaS 卖的是工具让客户自己折腾；而 AI 原生服务直接把活干完——AI Agent 扛下大头，精简团队人工兜底。在客户眼里，这就像雇了一家随时在线、更便宜且不知疲倦的外包事务所；但从底层运转来看，它本质上就是一款软件👀 Greg 的这篇文章很有指导性。

所有 AI 原生服务的底层逻辑完全一致。吃透这几点，你就能切入几乎任何细分领域：

1. 交付单元（The Unit）：这是最关键的决策。必须卖一个定义极清晰的成果：按每单、每份、每月或每份报告收费，绝不按工时计费。也可以按月收固定服务费，但范围必须锁死。交付单元要有明确的“完工标准”，让客户一眼能看出“搞定了”。这也是未来把它做成软件的前提；

2. 工单录入（The Intake）：这是传统外包最容易暗中亏钱的环节。传统中介要打三通电话确认需求；AI 原生服务只需一张表单：客户上传文件、填 5 个字段、说明需求，搞定。如果需求无法收敛成一张表单，说明你的交付单元还不够清晰；

3. 执行引擎（The Engine）具体干活的 AI。起步时就是一套好的提示词加几十个行业范例；但随着处理的任务越多，它会逐渐迭代成对手无法复制的核心资产；

4. 规则手册（The Rulebook）：这才是真正的产品壁垒，却常被严重低估。它是一份清晰的清单，记录了行业标准的“正确”，以及 AI 所有可能踩的坑（例如“未记录体征算作废”、“信函必须带治疗日期”）。每次发现失误就补上一条。几百单后，这本手册就是你交付质量与商业护城河的根基，这就是业务的 Know How 也是核心竞争力；

5. 人工审核层（The Review Layer）：决定哪些直接自动发出，哪些必须人工过目。低风险、高置信度的直接交付；涉及资金、法律风险或客户声誉的，必须人工把关。审核层能保住交付底线，而随着规则手册的完善，人工负担会越来越轻；

6. 交付方式（The Delivery）：成品返回客户的方式。一个登录后台、一封带附件的邮件，或一个进度看板。这直接取代了客户经理——客户无需问任何人，自己就能查进度；

7. 定价策略（The Pricing）

- 按单计费：适合业务量稳定、希望用多少付多少的客户

- 固定月费：范围明确、按月打包收费，客户预算确定，你也有稳定现金流；

- 绝对避开按小时计费：工时计费会把营收死死绑在员工人数上，这是传统外包公司的致命死穴。

按“人工替代成本”定价，别按你的成本定：别人收 2,500 美元，你收 800 美元。对客户而言极划算，对你而言是暴利——因为你的边际成本接近于零；

8. 获客渠道（The Distribution）：最立竿见影的打法。拉一份精准决策人名单，直接做冷启动邮件/电销，带上唯一的诱饵——首单免费。比如免费帮护理机构查 10 份记录并揪出 3 处遗漏，对方当天就会签单。此外，软件生态合作和熟人圈转介绍也管用。你不需要泛流量，只要一条直通买家的通道，而“首单免费”就是最快的那条路。

最后补充一下，大家不要拿这样的“AI 原生服务”去找 VC 融资了，这就是一个生意。所谓“千亿美元市场”，不过是成千上万个细分长尾的加总，绝非任何单家公司能撑起的 TAM。就连 Greg 自己都反复承认“产品化服务是个极好的避风港”、“60% 到 80% 的毛利、以 6 到 12 倍 EBITDA 退出”——请清醒一点，这完全是生活方式型小生意的画风，根本跑不出 VC 级别（Venture-Scale）的指数级增长。

text:
01F Group, through its growth-stage fintech private equity arm 01Fintech, announced an investment in DANA, Indonesia's leading digital financial platform. The firm framed the deal as backing resilient, locally rooted technology infrastructure that advances financial inclusion and supports Indonesia's real economy, and as a reinforcement of its long-term confidence in Asia's fintech opportunity. 01F Group said Indonesia remains one of the region's most dynamic digital-payments markets, citing high digital adoption, a large consumer base and growing demand for technology-enabled financial services, with digital payments in the country projected to approach USD1 trillion by 2030.

DANA operates a single, integrated ecosystem serving consumers, merchants and financial institutions, spanning digital payments, QRIS, money transfers and AI-powered financial solutions. Its reach extends across metropolitan and non-metropolitan regions and supports millions of users and micro, small and medium enterprises, especially in Tier 2 to Tier 4 regions. 01F Group said it invests in category-defining platforms distinguished by sustainable unit economics, strong local execution and meaningful utility for the communities they serve.

Kenny Man, Founder and Managing Partner of 01F Group, said the investment rests on three convictions: DANA's operational discipline, its role in empowering local MSMEs, and the team's resilience, adding the firm aims to be a long-term partner rather than just a capital provider. DANA CEO and co-founder Vince Iswara welcomed 01Fintech's fintech expertise, regional connectivity and shared commitment to sustainable growth. The two will explore connecting DANA's MSMEs with lending and working capital, broadening access to micro-insurance, digital savings and wealth-building tools for underserved users, and exploring more efficient cross-border payment solutions.

Trailing stops are now available for perp markets. 

A trailing stop's trigger price follows the mark price as it moves in favor of the position. When the mark price retraces from its best level by the selected distance or percentage, it triggers a market order. For long positions, the trigger price follows the highest mark price reached since activation; for short positions, it follows the lowest. An optional activation price determines when tracking begins. Without one, tracking begins immediately at the current mark price.

author: markjeffrey
quoted_text:
I said "auto-regressive LLMs, in and of themselves, will not lead human-level AI" 
That statement is still totally true.

First, the reasoning abilities of current AI systems are based non-auto-regressive search (which is what I have always advocated for). But AFAICT, they do it in token space, which is limited and inefficient. I have claimed that human-like reasoning must be a search in continuous representation space. It looks like the industry is moving towards that.

Second, the self-improvement methods, as currently practiced, only work for domains where the quality of outputs can be scored without human intervention, such as mathematics, code, and scenarios that can be simulated accurately. Not anything else. Humans and animals learn new skills way more efficiently than current RL methods.

Third, the multimodal capabilities of current AI assistants generally use separately-trained encoders (that are not LLMs). This is also what I've been advocating. Except that I think the best way to do this is with JEPA trained with self-supervised learning. The research community is clearly moving towards that (3000 papers on JEPA in just 4 years).

Fourth, if LLMs were a path to human-level AI, we would have domestic robots and Level-4 or Level-5 self-driving cars for consumers by now. And we don't. We certainly don't have cars that can learn to drive in 20 hours or practice like any teenager. We're still missing something pretty huge to claim human-level intelligence (let alone superhuman).

Sure, we now have computer systems that are impressive, very useful, and whose performance is superhuman in an increasing number of domains (coding being one of them). 
But that's true of the entire history of progress in computer technology. 

Lastly, there is a basic confusion about what intelligence actually is.
It is not the mere accumulation and regurgitation of existing declarative knowledge (which is essentially what LLMs do).
As Jean Piaget famously said, "intelligence is not what you know, it is what you do when you don't know." 
It is your ability to solve new problem without any prior training, to act in previously-unknown scenarios, and to adapt very quickly to new situations with minimal training.

We're still far from that.
