Tokenized equities today are exactly where stablecoins were in 2019.

the first pmf is here. bringing equities onchain is just as obvious, simple, yet genius as bringing dollars onchain was back then. we've already seen the first growth spurt push us to the first few billion in onchain supply.

but zoom out and it's painfully obvious we're still incredibly early. an easy 100x in growth still ahead over the next few years.

here's where it gets interesting though:

stablecoin growth was slower, because we spent years operating in a completely different environment. one that mocked crypto, treated it with deep skepticism, and forced us to fight regulatory headwinds the whole way. one of the biggest catalysts, the GENIUS Act, only came last year, many years after the first pmf, and accelerated stablecoin significantly.

tokenized equities are positioned completely differently.

there's already massive institutional interest and adoption, and tokenized equities are an obvious, compelling fit for exactly that crowd. and just days ago the SEC issued its Innovation Exemption, explicitly allowing tokenized stocks to trade onchain, actively pushing this development forward instead of fighting it.

so I think tokenized equities are equally obvious with equally asymmetric upside as stablecoins in 2019. except this time it's going to move much, much faster.

one of the biggest opportunities forming in this space right now.

text:
投资医药公司最难的，不是看市场有多大，而是判断这个市场最后有多少真的能变成收入。临床数据漂亮，不代表FDA一定同意；FDA同意，不代表医生一定买账；医生买账，也不代表患者长期使用。所以医药股最稀缺的东西，其实不是想象力，而是确定性。

这也是我看好Insmed这个公司的第一个原因，确定性正在快速提高。 核心产品BRINSUPRI已经跨过临床、审批和初期商业化三道大关，2026年Q2销售达到3.09亿美元，环比+49%。现在的问题已经从“这药到底行不行”，变成了“它到底能卖多大”。看起来只是换了一个问题，风险等级却完全不同。

第二，增长空间可能还没被完全看见。 BRINSUPRI峰值销售预期已经提高到70亿美元以上。更值得关注的是，支气管扩张症过去长期缺少针对性治疗，部分潜在患者甚至没有被发现。相信大家身边也有不少长期咳嗽、咳痰和反复呼吸道感染的人，当然这些症状并不代表就是支气管扩张症，但至少说明这类症状在人群中并不少见。现在有了有效的新药，医生主动筛查和确诊患者的动力也可能提高。所以BRINSUPRI不一定只是在占据一个蛋糕的份额，而是它可能顺手把蛋糕做大。

第三，TPIP又给了Insmed第二张牌。 公司预计TPIP峰值潜力超过60亿美元。这个数字我不会全部算进去，毕竟Phase 3还没毕业，医药行业最忌讳的就是把录取通知书当毕业证。 但换个角度，只要TPIP最终兑现其中一部分，Insmed就可能拥有第二个重磅产品。BRINSUPRI抬高下限，TPIP打开上限，这个组合我很喜欢。

现在最大的估值分歧也很简单：Insmed已经不便宜了，但市场给的到底是一款成功药的高估值，还是低估了一家平台型药企正在形成？ 我的判断更偏向后者。

当然风险也很明确：BRINSUPRI销售低于市场的高预期，或者TPIP Phase 3失败，都可能带来明显的估值压缩。所以我真正看好Insmed的，并不是“140亿美元峰值销售”这种漂亮的加法题，而是它少见地同时拥有：越来越高的确定性，以及仍然巨大的市场空间。

如果未来证明BRINSUPRI不是一次“中彩票”，而是Insmed具备持续推出重磅产品的能力，那么市场需要重新计算的，就不是BRINSUPRI值多少钱，而是Insmed从产品驱动型Biotech成长为平台型Biopharma后，应该值多少钱。

text:
La “tasa de usura” en Colombia tiene buenas intenciones, pero termina perjudicando precisamente a quienes busca proteger. La explicación es contraintuitiva. Prestar tiene riesgo de impago. Si una persona tiene poco historial crediticio, es más difícil evaluar ese riesgo. Cuando la tasa máxima permitida no alcanza para cubrirlo, el banco simplemente niega el préstamo.

El resultado para esa persona no es crédito más barato: es quedarse sin crédito. Y sin alternativas formales, termina en el “gota a gota”, pagando muchísimo más y exponiéndose a amenazas y violencia. El informe de ANIF y Colombia Fintech de 2025 cita que más del 65% de los adultos en Colombia no tenían crédito formal. Y estima tasas anuales promedio del “gota a gota” de alrededor del 382% para personas y del 666% para mipymes.

Esa es la paradoja: un límite diseñado para proteger al consumidor termina cerrándole la puerta del crédito formal y lo deja expuesto a préstamos mucho más caros.

¿Cual es la solución? Eliminar el tope de intereses Y aumentar la competencia, exigir transparencia en los costos y mantener una protección firme contra los abusos. Quitar el tope, por sí solo, no basta. Gracias a desarrollos tecnológicos, Colombia tiene una gran oportunidad para impulsar esa competencia:

• Bre-B puede facilitar que entidades digitales como Nu compitan con los grandes bancos sin necesitar una red de sucursales. Esto significa que pueden venir muchos mas competidores al sistema. Que gane el mejor!

• Los pagos digitales dejan un historial que, con autorización del cliente, ayude a evaluar a personas y negocios que antes eran invisibles para el crédito formal.

• El "Open Finance" permite que cada persona comparta su información con otras entidades para conseguir mejores ofertas.

¿Quién perdería con más alternativas formales? El “gota a gota”.

La “tasa de usura” no ha funcionado en ningún país del mundo, y tampoco ha funcionado en otras industrias donde el gobierno decide por decreto “el precio justo”. Desde las políticas de alquiler de apartamentos en Nueva York o Buenos Aires, que dejaron miles de personas fuera de sus apartamentos y, al mismo tiempo, miles de apartamentos vacíos, hasta la decisión de Venezuela hace décadas de fijar los precios de los alimentos en los supermercados, que dejó los estantes vacíos. A pesar de ser contraintuitivo, el libre mercado es muchísimo mejor para encontrar el precio adecuado de un producto que una política de gobierno.

text:
AI agents are going to make APIs feel very different.

Today, most APIs are designed for developers to call directly. An agent can discover a tool, understand its schema, decide when to use it, pass arguments, inspect the result and continue the workflow.
That changes what good API design looks like. Clear schemas matter more. Errors need to be useful. Actions need predictable side effects. Permissions need to be explicit. Tool responses need to contain enough context for the model to act on them.

We're slowly moving from software calling software to software deciding when to call software.

That shift is going to create a lot of interesting infrastructure work around APIs, permissions, observability and agent tooling.

author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
A few thoughts on the current state of venture capital.

When the Music Is Playing

In July 2007, a few weeks before the credit markets seized up, Chuck Prince, then the CEO of Citigroup, gave an interview to the Financial Times. The line everyone remembers is this one: "As long as the music is playing, you've got to get up and dance." He was mocked for it for years afterward, and he lost his job a few months later. But I have come to think he was saying something honest. He wasn't claiming the music would play forever. He was admitting that he couldn't sit down while it was still going, and neither could anyone else in his seat.

I've been thinking about that quote a lot lately, because right now is the most disorienting period in venture capital I can remember, and I have been doing this for a while.

Here is what makes it disorienting. It's not that things are bad. Some things are spectacular. We have companies in our portfolio growing faster than anything I have seen in my career, and I don't say that lightly. At the same time, we have companies with no revenue, no product, and a founding team you could fit in a conference room raising billions of dollars at valuations of $10 to $50 billion. Both of these things are true at once, and if you try to reason about them with the same framework you will drive yourself crazy.

Two ideas have helped me make sense of it. Neither is mine.

The first is reflexivity, which George Soros has been writing about since the 1980s. In most of life, perception follows reality: the weather is what it is, and your opinion of it changes nothing. In markets, it runs the other way too. Prices change what participants believe, and what participants believe changes the prices. The feedback loop can run for a long time, and while it's running it looks exactly like progress.

Here is how reflexivity is playing out in AI. Full disclosure: Menlo is an investor in Anthropic, so read the following with that in mind. People watched a frontier lab go from a $4 billion valuation to $18 billion, then $60 billion, then $180 billion, then $380 billion, and now something close to a trillion. They drew the obvious conclusion: that is what a neo lab looks like. So the next neo lab gets priced off that path, not off anything it has built. Then it gets marked up in a subsequent round, and the markup itself becomes the proof. Look at Thinking Machines. Look at Reflection. At that point valuation has stopped being an output of the metrics and has become the metric. Nobody is discounting cash flows. They are discounting the last round.

Soros is very clear about one thing, and it's the part people skip: you cannot know when or how a reflexive process ends. You only know that it does. Every one of them has.

The second idea is Chuck Prince's, and it explains why smart people keep dancing even when they can see the loop for what it is. As far as I can tell, there are two groups on the dance floor.

The first group got in early. Firms like ours were in some of these AI companies before the numbers got silly, and the paper gains are enormous. When you are sitting on gains like that, you start to feel like you're playing with house money. I have been around long enough to know that house money is the most dangerous kind, because you don't respect it the way you respect money you had to earn.

The second group missed the early rounds and knows it. Their LPs know it too. So they are trying to make up for lost time by writing very large checks very late, which is the one strategy almost guaranteed to turn a missed opportunity into a real loss.

House money on one side, FOMO on the other, and reflexivity feeding both. That's the whole story. Everyone has a reason to keep dancing, and the reasons are different, which is why nobody can talk anyone else off the floor.

So what do you do? The instinct in our business is to answer with company identification: just pick the right neo lab and you'll be fine. I think that's the trap. When price has become the signal, being right about the company is not enough, because you can be right about the company and still be wrong about the price by a factor of ten. The public-market investors I admire figured this out a long time ago. They spend as much time on how much to own as on what to own.

The winners in venture over the next decade will be the firms that treat portfolio composition and position sizing as seriously as they treat sourcing. How much of the fund is in companies whose valuation rests on the last round rather than on revenue? What happens to the portfolio if the reflexive loop breaks next year instead of in five? Those are not exciting questions. They are the ones that will matter.

The music will stop. It always does. Dance if you must, but know where the chairs are.

An AI experiment project called Truman World.

It turns the movie The Truman Show into an AI-simulated world that runs continuously.

The main character, Truman, doesn't know he's living in a simulation. The people around him are independent AI characters with memories, capable of interaction, and their relationships gradually change over time.

Viewers can pay to send prompts that alter the people, events, and objects around him. These AI characters then decide for themselves what happens next.

The livestream starts with an 8-hour countdown. Every $5 spent adds 1 minute to the stream. Even if the stream ends, the simulated world doesn't stop. Truman will continue to "live" on.

This is described as the first experiment with a "persistent social world engine." The goal is to see how this world evolves on its own after viewer intervention, and whether Truman will one day discover he's an AI.

StonkFun just released its latest data:

Revenue: $1,100,719
Buyback: $660,554
Burned: 2.35M $STONK

In other words, the platform generated around $1.1M in revenue that day, with roughly 60% of it used to buy back STONK, and the repurchased tokens were then permanently burned.

This means STONK’s logic is not simply “Launchpad grows → platform earns fees.” It is:StonkFun Trading Volume ↑ → Platform Revenue ↑ → 60% of Revenue Used for STONK Buybacks → STONK Buying Pressure ↑ → Repurchased STONK Gets Burned → Circulating Supply ↓

So the variables that really matter for STONK are not simply price, but:StonkFun Revenue × Buyback Rate × Burn Rate

More importantly, the $660K buyback represents actual capital that has already been deployed, rather than the project simply announcing that it will conduct buybacks in the future.

Based on the roughly $0.36 price shown in the screenshot that day, 2.35M STONK had a nominal value of around $846K, while the actual buyback cost was $660,554, implying an average buyback cost of approximately $0.281 per STONK.

Therefore, the difference between STONK and a typical Meme or Launchpad Token is that it is attempting to directly convert the platform’s real economic activity into continuous token buying pressure and supply contraction.

But what really needs to be validated is not “how much was burned today,” but whether this flywheel can continue.

If, in the future:

Revenue remains at a high level
Trading Volume remains sustainable
Buybacks continue
Burns continue

Then StonkFun’s platform growth will continuously translate into STONK buy pressure and declining supply.

On the other hand, if STONK’s price continues to rise while StonkFun’s Revenue and Volume begin to decline consistently, the market may be pricing in future buybacks ahead of time rather than the platform itself continuing to create value.

So, STONK is attempting to directly convert Launchpad revenue into continuous token buybacks + supply contraction.

text:
GM CT

Most people looking at @axisrobotics see the contributor side first: open the Hub, control a robot, complete tasks, generate trajectories, earn Points.

I've been digging into the other side of the equation:

Who actually pays for all this robot data?

That's where the Axis business model gets interesting.

Axis describes it as B2B2C.

The community sits on the front end producing physical-action data at scale. On the back end, Axis turns that network into data + model infrastructure for robotics companies.

And the commercial product isn't simply "here are a million trajectories."

Axis packages data around what a customer actually needs:

→ Scenario: where the robot needs to operate
→ Skills: grasp, place, push, rotate, etc.
→ Randomization: different layouts, objects and physical conditions
→ Trajectories: the actual volume of usable training data

Put those together and you get what Axis calls a Task Package.

So a hardware company with a robot that needs better manipulation data doesn't have to build an entire collection pipeline from scratch.

Axis can generate the tasks, distribute them across contributors, collect the trajectories, verify/process the data and deliver something designed around that specific use case.

The customer side is already broader than just robot manufacturers too:

→ Robotics hardware
→ Foundation models + AI infrastructure
→ Industrial automation

And @FeagineRobotics is a good recent example of what this looks like commercially.

Axis is building customized simulation/data pipelines around Feagine's flexible manipulators and supplying training data for its Fi0 cross-embodiment model.

That's when Axis starts looking less like a browser robot game with Points and more like an actual data business.

Community on the front end.

Robotics companies on the back.

Axis is the infrastructure connecting the two.

text:
美国 SEC “创新豁免” 监管框架推出，后续政策正如何影响 Web3 产业走向？

9 月 16 日，美国参议院就《CLARITY Act》进行程序性表决，由于未能达到继续推进审议所需的 60 票门槛，该法案未能进入下一阶段。由于该法案一直被视为美国建立数字资产市场结构监管框架的重要立法，因此，其推进受阻也意味着市场期待已久的联邦层面监管仍将面临着较大的不确定性。

过去几年，美国 Web3 行业一直围绕着几个问题持续展开争论：

链上资产如何定性？
不同类型的链上资产由谁监管？
美国证券交易委员会（SEC）和商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）的监管界限在哪里？

在现行法律框架下，SEC 主要负责证券市场监管，而 CFTC 则主要负责商品期货、期权、掉期等衍生品市场。但 Web3 行业的发展又产生了大量介于传统证券和商品监管边界之间的新型资产与交易模式，由此产生了监管归属上的模糊地带。原本有望通过《CLARITY Act》明确的 SEC 与 CFTC 职能范围，也因法案推进受阻，至今未能得到解决。因此，SEC 与 CFTC 开始在现有法律授权范围内，通过监管解释、规则制定以及豁免机制等方式，逐步处理数字资产市场已经出现的现实问题。

此前，外捕研究（Web3Caff Research）曾追踪点评过 SEC 于 8 月中旬提出的《Regulation Crypto Assets》（即链上资产监管条例）。在该条例中，SEC 提出了两种证券注册豁免路径，分别为 Startup Exemption（初创豁免）和 Fundraising Exemption（募资豁免）。其中：

text:
The Manhattan Project and NASA proved that tightly-run, state-funded institutions can deliver radical breakthroughs, largely by the state borrowing private-sector talent.
If frontier models are the threat to national security their own builders say they are, why is their development left to a handful of labs, accountable to no one but their investors? Shouldn’t the state attempt to steward radical breakthroughs?

Taiwan seeded TSMC, Malaysia owned Petronas, Europe funded Airbus. Public capital, private-sector talent and market discipline enabled these companies to catch up to their incumbents.

If the frontier AI race is constrained by key infrastructure that requires public subsidy (power, grid connections, fabs), surely it’s in the state’s interest to build its own expertise?

Good stewardship could point research at the public interest, and give government expertise of its own, so regulators aren’t taking instructions from the firms they oversee.

This could get pretty insane! 

Standard wants to become the "liquidity engine" for Robinhood’s stock markets

If it executes, this extends well beyond the current $STANDARD protocol + could attract SIGNIFICANTLY larger institutional players

There's also some pretty interesting implications...

1) What we know: Standard explicitly intends to fund and coordinate stock-token liquidity

Its manifesto says it will create + approve markets, seed liquidity, coordinate external capital and return trading fees to the reserve

The intention is to build a capital base that supports multiple markets

If those positions generate profits, retained earnings could fund further deployments

Standard’s published reserve snapshot shows roughly $14M across reserve vaults + protocol-owned liquidity

That includes locked STANDARD liquidity, so the entire amount is not available for stock-market deployment

The significant development is where the protocol wants to earn its revenue... thank god for a return to fundamentals (while still tied to memes)!

Funding stock-token markets could give Standard income from trading activity across the wider RH ecosystem, reducing its dependence on activity around its own token

2) This could strengthen an advantage that competing chains would find difficult to replicate

Robinhood brings stock-token issuance infra, its brand + an established wallet

A deeper onchain liquidity network could make those assets more useful across trading, lending + portfolio applications

Issuing a token is only part of the job... Traders also need enough inventory and capital on both sides of the market to execute meaningful orders without substantial price impact

Other chains already have tokenized equities, like xStocks, pre-Stocks etc. but RH’s potential advantage is the combination of distribution, stock access, liquidity + apps developing together (eg. on top of STANDARD??)

If better execution attracts more trading, and profitable trading finances deeper markets, that advantage could compound BLOODY quick

A competing chain would need to attract the users, inventory + capital behind that activity

3) How this impacts other RH protocols

Existing RH protocols could become both beneficiaries AND competitors

i) Launchpads such as Pons & Long could benefit where their markets depend on stock tokens supported by deeper underlying pools

Buying the stock needed to enter a meme/stock pair could become cheaper, although the meme pair would still need sufficient liquidity itself

ii) DEXs + aggregators could route trades through markets Standard funds

iii) Liquidity managers could potentially manage positions or bring additional capital alongside the reserve

There would also be competition over deposits, trading fees and which markets receive funding

Existing treasury and liquidity protocols would need to demonstrate where they add value through execution, distribution or risk mgmt.

The ecosystem gains most if Standard attracts fresh capital and supports additional activity

Moving the same capital between existing pools would deliver a smaller benefit

4) ALPHA: The reservoir could support another generation of apps

i) An index product could rebalance stock-token portfolios against deeper markets

ii) A lending protocol could use those markets to liquidate collateral more efficiently

iii) Options/perps platforms and market makers could use them to hedge exposure

iv) AI agents could execute portfolio strategies across the same pools, adding another source of trading demand

These are potential applications, NOT announced Standard integrations

They would still require their own contracts, pricing systems + risk controls

The attraction for builders is access to usable markets without having to recruit every liquidity provider themselves

For Standard, applications using its funded markets could generate fees that help replenish the reserve

I’m watching for the first actual deployments, their returns after costs, & how those earnings benefit $STANDARD holders

That will show whether the reservoir can become a lasting source of liquidity for RH

This is probably one (if not THE) most interesting protocol emerging, that could entice a fresh bout of institutional capital into this mini RWA bull

Time to start paying attention!

text:
I was there Friday night in San Francisco for the @REK event, and this is something you had be in the room to get it, but I’ll try to describe it.

It hit completely differently from robot-versus-robot fights. Those are entertaining, sure, but after a while they start to feel strange. You’re empathizing with machines that aren’t conscious, don’t feel pain, and don’t feel anything. Robot versus human hits different and raw, it was an emotional rollercoaster. I felt real fear for the human fighter, and real excitement, mostly fear, and when it ended there was a huge wave of relief.

The robots were remote-controlled, of course, but the kicks were genuinely powerful. We know how power-dense those actuators are, and the human fighter took real hits to his body. The kicks from the six-foot-tall EngineAI T800 seemed nearly impossible to dodge when they were hurled in the right direction. The Unitree H1 was even harder to deal with because its dynamic balance is so good that it just refused to go down.

This could be the start of a genuinely new entertainment genre. But I can tell you this: if someone wants to fight a robot with a real AI brain and real perception, you’d need robots that are far less powerful, throttled down, and compliant. Otherwise it ends in serious injury or worse.

This is the beginning of something different in robotics and entertainment, and we need to think seriously about it before regulators use moments like this as fearmongering fodder to throttle the entire humanoid frontier. https://t.co/ry0goqg7Oa

text:
ZEROBASE WEEKLY 9.14-9.20

ZBT traded in a $0.074–$0.083 range this week. It opened near $0.080 on September 14, slipped with the broader mid-week risk-off move to a low around $0.0744–$0.0746 on September 16, then recovered with the Friday–weekend bid and closed near $0.081–$0.082. Trading volumes remained decent through the dip and liquidity conditions stayed relatively stable, with bid-ask spreads holding at reasonable levels.

Crypto markets produced a two-act week: a sharp mid-week flush driven by policy and geopolitics, then a powerful late-week squeeze that reversed most of the damage. Total cryptocurrency market capitalization started the period near $2.65T–$2.69T, compressed during the Tuesday–Wednesday selloff, then expanded again as Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000, finishing closer to the $2.78T–$2.91T area by Sunday depending on the aggregator.

Bitcoin opened the week near $76,800–$76,840 on September 14 (Sunday close around $76,838), pushed to an early-week high near $79,500–$79,590, then sold off hard on September 15 to a weekly low around $74,940–$75,025. It baselined in the mid-$76,000s through the Fed decision, then accelerated on September 18, printing a high near $81,390–$81,925 and closing the week around $81,160–$81,270. That was a net gain of roughly 5.5–6% from the September 13 close and more than 8% from the weekly low.

Ethereum moved in parallel but with a deeper mid-week drawdown and a comparable rebound. It started around $2,477–$2,515, dipped toward $2,360–$2,372 on September 15–16, then rallied with a September 18 close near $2,608–$2,612 and finished the week around $2,630–$2,650 — a gain of approximately 6–7% from the weekly low and about 5–6% from the prior Sunday close.

Derivatives metrics reflected the same sequence. Liquidations clustered around the Tuesday flush (roughly $278 million in a single 24-hour window early in the week, with longs accounting for the larger share), funding rates on major pairs reset from mildly positive toward neutral during the drawdown, then flipped back as shorts were squeezed through $80,000. Open interest rebuilt into the Friday advance rather than collapsing, which is consistent with a squeeze-and-repositioning tape rather than a structural unwind.

Macro and geopolitical developments set the tone. Escalating Middle East supply risk — including disruption to a Saudi pipeline used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz — pushed crude sharply higher. Brent traded from about $105.85 on September 14 toward $109.20 on September 15 before easing to the $103–$104 area by September 20; WTI moved from about $101.50 to a mid-week peak near $106.37 and finished the weekend closer to $99.70–$100. 

The oil spike transmitted directly into rates: the 10-year Treasury yield briefly broke above 5.00–5.04%, its highest print since 2007 on an intraday basis and the first sustained test of 5% since late 2023.

Policy delivered the second shock. On September 16 the FOMC, in a 12–0 vote under Chair Kevin Warsh, raised the federal funds target by 25 basis points to 3.75–4.00% — the first hike since 2023. The statement was terse and hawkish on inflation. The Summary of Economic Projections lifted 2026 PCE inflation to a 3.7% median, held unemployment near 4.1%, and put the year-end funds-rate median at 4.1%, implying at least one additional hike is the committee’s base case. Sixteen of 18 participants penciled in further tightening this year.

Crypto-specific politics compounded the mid-week risk-off. On September 15 the Senate rejected cloture on the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act by a 49–50 vote, removing a near-term path to federal market-structure rules. That session produced the week’s largest Bitcoin ETF outflow ($450 million) and a heavy Ethereum ETF redemption day as well.

U.S. equity markets finished mixed, masking a violent internal rotation. For the September 14–18 cash week the S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,650.50, essentially unchanged to down about 0.1% from the prior Friday’s 7,656.98 after an intraweek low of 7,507.77 on September 16. 

The Nasdaq Composite finished higher by roughly 0.7% at 26,522.55, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped about 1.7% to 51,682.64 — a third consecutive losing week for the Dow. Chip and AI-hardware names led Monday’s decline after major AI lab leaders publicly called for a slower development cadence; Coinbase jumped 11.7% on Friday as crypto beta reasserted itself.

Institutional flows told the same two-act story. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $160 million on September 14, then lost $450 million on September 15 and another $296 million on September 16. Thursday recovered $160 million and Friday added $433 million — the largest daily creation since September 3 — leaving the complex barely positive on the week at roughly $6 million. 

BlackRock’s IBIT led the weekly net (+$121 million), while Fidelity’s FBTC supplied $311 million of Friday’s print. Spot Ethereum ETFs opened with +$121 million on Monday, then posted three consecutive outflow sessions (including −$224 million on Wednesday) before a $144 million Friday rebound; the week still closed at about −$141 million, snapping a four-week inflow streak. Combined U.S. spot crypto ETF products finished slightly negative on the week.

Crypto Fear & Greed Index started Monday around 57 (greed), jumped to 69 on September 15 even as prices broke, collapsed to 50–51 through the Fed session, then recovered with the squeeze to 56 on Friday and 70–71 by the weekend.

On-chain and positioning data were more constructive than the Tuesday tape suggested. The mid-week dump was absorbed without a breakdown of the $75,000 area on a closing basis; exchange-traded product creations flipped back positive as soon as price reclaimed $80,000; and Bitcoin dominance held in the high-50s (roughly 57–59%) even as ether outperformed on the bounce. 

Long-term holder distribution did not accelerate through the $75,000 test, and the Friday advance was accompanied by rising spot volume rather than purely derivative covering. Stablecoin capitalization remained near the $290–$305 billion zone, indicating dry powder was still in the system.

In summary, the September 14–20 period was a classic policy-and-oil shock followed by a positioning squeeze. The CLARITY Act failure and the first Fed hike in three years, layered on $105–$109 crude and a 5% 10-year, produced the week’s low. Once those events were digested, ETF demand returned, shorts covered, and Bitcoin closed the week above $81,000 with ether back above $2,600. 

Higher energy prices remain an upside risk to inflation and therefore to the Warsh Fed’s rate path; the market is now trading that tension rather than a one-way risk-off regime. With ETF flows stabilizing, Fear & Greed back in greed, and on-chain holders not capitulating at the $75,000 test, the tape looks like consolidation at a higher range — still hostage to oil, yields, and the next Washington headline.

如果你打新，那就只赚打新收益，切忌持币。因为这十多年的上币数据显示，市场真的在惩罚“钻石手”。

GSR 统计了 2013 年以来 2300 多次主流交易所的上币记录。数据结论非常直白：新币跌破发行价的时间中位数仅为 3 天，90 天内跌幅中位数达 50%。

结合行业惯用的“低流通、高 FDV”模式，代币生命周期呈现以下特征：

1/ 高估值 = 持续失血 
FDV 超过 10 亿美元上线的代币，一年后回报率中位数为 -81%。投入 1 美元，360 天后仅剩 0.19 美元。

2/ 流通量决定抗跌性 
自 ICO 时代起，首发流通量中位数由 38% 降至 13%。数据显示，首发流通量低于 20% 的项目，一年后平均下跌 75%；流通量处于 30% 至 50% 的项目，跌幅收窄至 45%。

当极少的初始流通筹码碰上天价的完全稀释估值，短暂炒作过后就是解锁期无尽的抛压。这种“上线即阴跌”的资产，根本无法为二级市场提供建仓空间。

所以，与其苦等项目方“良心发现”去优化发行结构，不如直接把这份报告当成二级交易者的《新币生还指南》。基于上述数据，普通人在当下市场该如何自处？

🛑 1/ 放弃长线信仰，打新只做“渣男” 

既然中位数是 3 天破发、90 天腰斩，那就彻底放弃对 VC 币的“钻石手”幻想。开盘首日的流动性溢价一旦吃完，绝对不要拿利润去和即将到来的巨量解锁抗衡。

🔍 2/ 强执行“20% 流通”过滤线 

把首日流通量作为核心风控指标。遇到流通量低于 20% 的天王级项目，直接默认它是“结构性做空盘”，除了开盘狂欢，后续绝不接盘；只有首发流通在 30%-50% 的项目，才值得你去分析它的基本面和二次建仓的机会。

⏳ 3/ 真正的抄底，请等到一年以后 

高 FDV 代币一年后中位数仅剩 0.19 美元。如果你真的看好某个项目的技术或生态，请管住手。等时间熬满 300 天，等早期空投和第一轮私募解锁的筹码被市场砸出真正的底部后，再去捡带血的筹码。

quoted_text:
@0xbeyondlee 我的 25 年人生经历过两次锥心刺骨的时刻，一次是今晚，一次是 2023 年 5 月 8 号

那一天，我的妈妈被诊断为甲状腺右叶 C-TIRADS 5 类低回声结节，用更直白的话讲 —— 甲状腺癌

说来好笑，那晚我才知道电影里的歇斯底里、声嘶力竭都是骗人的，绝望的人根本留不出眼泪

那晚我向所知的一切神明祈祷，祈祷患癌的是我而不是我妈妈有多好

此后三年治疗路上的满满坎坷，我不愿回忆，也从未提起

可以吐露的是，天下无癌，是我此生最大的愿望，这样的痛苦真的不愿再看到任何一个家庭承受了

尽我所能帮助与我有缘、被我知晓且罹患癌症的家庭

其中两次我公开在了 X 上，只为像子路受牛般带动更多人行善

詹臻便是其中之一，只可惜她已不幸离世
https://t.co/UjORyRmBWe

另一次便是今年 9 月 9 日的 王*悦，因为癌症，不得不放弃一路苦读才考取的博士学位，谁见了不为之动容

因此我再次捐款 1 万元

原本是发自内心的善举，却无意间差点酿成最不堪的祸事

这次事件，被人发上链铸成了 Meme 币，当时我正在机上，落地第一时间有人提醒我可以领取税收作为善款，我只看到了好的一面却忽略了另一面

事实证明，人类的理性经不起短时反复的捶打，税收成为了无尽噩梦的开始

人在国外，给她转账只能使用电子方式，最担心的是如果在出金过程遇到不明资金，进而影响到她救命钱的使用，那真是我最不愿看到的事情，而我当时又没有足够资金垫付

迫不得已，只能向她解释原因，等一个月后再想办法，并且在推特发布

这之后，无边的困扰遍袭来了，对我本人的攻击和狐疑我可以承受，但对受捐对象 王*悦 的无休止打扰真的令我无比愧怍，最难以接受的是有人胁迫她发布 Meme 相关内容

就让这一切就此停止吧，我们已经心力憔悴了，就在刚刚已经把这个 Meme 的税收权限转入黑洞，并且永不提及，永不关注

已经获得的税收仍在链上从未动过，未来也不会再碰触，这个钱包未来动作将交由律师及相关人士妥善处理

但是为了让她尽早得到救助，我已按照今日价格 1u/6.66r 转给了 王*悦，钱是我连夜拆借垫付来的，这期间的种种痛苦就到此为止吧

最后想说我正如之前所说的我们从未引导、许诺关于这个 Meme 的任何信息，完全与我们无关，盈亏自负

所有相关信息我已全部取证保存，并且会持续取证所有提及此代币的人，我已与委托律师取得联系，确保我和 王*悦 的权益可以得到保障

感谢事件中的一切正义之士，尽管你们有些对我产生误解

最后，愿天下无癌 🙏

作者吐槽在公司新岗位的经历：所有规格、代码、测试、PRD 和单元均由 Claude 生成，团队成员被迫快速交付却无人真正理解内容，每天工作 12-13 小时，仅仅只是“按回车”😆 导致了严重的思考缺失和强烈灵魂枯竭感 ... 

这种"只管 ship"的开发模式撑不了太久！它的代价有滞后性，但一定会以事故、安全漏洞和核心人才流失的形式集中兑现。真正会拉开差距的，是那些把 AI 省下的时间重新投资到理解上的公司。生成越便宜，判断越贵，这条规律在代码上和在内容上是一样的🤔
author: indigox
quoted_text: I am done with this shit. It is over. The state of engineering right now is horrible. It has been half a month since I started a new role at a big company. Nobody knows anything here. The specs, code, tests, PRDs, tickets, resolution of those tickets, reports, etc., everything is made by Claude Code. Nobody on my team likes this. They are being forced to ship as much as they can. I have heard multiple times from higher management that pushing code is not a bottleneck, so why are we slow? People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter. Nobody is reading anything. Humans in corporate are doing nothing on their own. Everyone, literally everyone, from an L1 to an L7 engineer here is doing the same thing. Talk to Claude. There is no sense of victory. Nobody is resolving bugs. In reality, nobody is thinking anymore. Everything is done by LLMs. It is so soul-sucking. I would not mind it, to be honest, if we were at least given the time to check out the code and see what is going where. But no, the goal is to just ship. No matter what happens.

A different kind of weekly update 🌍

On Sep 19, an attempt to exploit a VM-level issue caused invalid state changes, and network progression was paused to protect users.

What happened:
🔍 An actor exploited a VM-level atomicity issue; a fix was prepared the same day
🧩 The root cause: an order-of-operations mistake in edge cases, contained fast thanks to the validators' rapid response

Where things stand:
🛡 The incident is contained; the attacker's accounts have been identified and frozen with major exchanges, and law enforcement is engaged
🔧 Recovery will be a coordinated hard fork from a known-good checkpoint, rehearsed on Testnet and Devnet with validators first
⚙️ The code is ready and public, and testing is ongoing

⏸️ Until the all-clear: don't submit or rebroadcast transactions, and don't use EGLD/ESDT deposit and withdrawal routes on exchanges or bridges. Exchanges and bridges will reopen in stages after the restart.

A full technical incident report will follow.
Thank you to the validators, partners and everyone who stood with the network this week. Our regular recap returns once the network is back, with two weeks of building to catch up on.

author: 0x_ultra
quoted_text:
The Kalshi drama is a good window into human nature.

Specifically, as it relates to the vice of pride.

Not just pride at the surface level definition, but all the underlying emotions that makeup what we commonly refer to as “pride.”

The drive not just for money, but to have more money than your neighbors.

The need not only to be successful, but more successful than college friends.

The drive to not only be good looking, but better looking than that other guy.

Pride is what causes people to knowingly (or in some cases unknowingly) use others for their own gain, and to dispose of them as soon as they don’t see any future gains to be derived from them. 

I have no idea who is right or wrong in this volume debate. I am not smart enough to figure that out.

But I do know that many of the comments on that original post from Beni are filled with people taking delight in the takedown. 

Here is where the pride comes in. 

For over a year I have seen MANY if not MOST of these same people kissing the Kalshi teams’ ass and clout chasing them on the timeline. 

But they were mostly doing that because they thought they could gain something from doing it.

Quietly, they envied the individuals.

They hated their perceived success. 

They never liked or even cared about them; they were simply trying to gain something from them.

Many such cases.

Anyways, I don’t really care what the outcome is.

Have a great day.

Verifiability is imo the most underrated property of truly public blockchain networks.

On Ethereum, you can permissionlessly run a small machine and convince yourself that billions/trillions of dollars of transaction value (payment, swaps, credit etc) were settled according to committed rules. Not only for L1 but also for L2s.

It’s the ultimate security backstop, and it gives the Ethereum network a herd immunity and “eyes on the street” that are hard to beat in the class of fully programmable environments.

深度参与Saturn 已经快半年了，越参与越觉得它的前景和实力比我想象中的还要厉害

关于Saturn 的分享大部分是参与空投的角度，但深度参与后真有点低估了 STRC 这条线。

周五的 AMA 里 联创 Kevin 也提到现在STRC 的链上入口更简单了

以前想拿 STRC 敞口，基本要走传统券商体系。现在通过 Saturn，稳定币就可以获得 STRC 敞口，不需要美国券商账户。

Kevin 提到“100 万美元资金进出的成本大约只有 6 到 8bp，其他渠道大约在 15 到 20bp。”

循环策略理论上可以做到 3 倍以上，传统券商差不多是 2 倍。所以Saturn 不仅是把 STRC 搬到链上，还提高了资金效率，成本同时更低。

比如 srUSDat的策略
目前 srUSDat 目标年化 7.8%左右，Junior 部分优先承担亏损，相当于给 Senior 提供一层风险缓冲。到目前为止，这层保护依然没被打破。

还有Pendle 的玩法，把原本浮动的收益拆开，通过 PT 把未来收益锁定成固定收益。

所以 ，Saturn 满足大家对于Defi 项目的向往，一方面有空投预期，另一方面也有更实际的 STRC 收益和一些 DeFi 可组合策略。

如果后续 STRC 的链上规模能继续扩大，Saturn 还是有机会成为这类数字信用资产进入 DeFi 的核心入口

上周五的Saturn 中文 AMA 有很多干货，错过的可以看看👇joejoe老师的总结

以上仅为个人项目记录与信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。内容主要面向非美国受众，请自行研究，DYOR。

Benmo x Ondo x YZiLabs x Saturn
AMA 文字精华整理 

YZiLabs  在筛选项目方面更看重什么？哪些信号被认为有潜力？
为什么Ondo认为 RWA的流动性比传统金融的流动性更“贵”？
既然STRC能链上买卖了，要Saturn何用？
......

全是行业价值干货，可以看看开拓视野
已尽量精简了，但内容还是较长，舍不得继续删减

1️⃣ 第一部分：RWA 走到哪一步了?

🔸Matt @fullportmatt （ @Ondo DeFi Leader）：
🔹代币化股票才刚刚开始，目前 @Ondo 上线这类业务一年时间，TVL已经达到 $1B，证明了它很受市场欢迎。
🔹用户选择代币化股票原因有3点：
代币化股票费用更便宜、购买门槛更低、摆脱中心化环境不稳定风险
🔹代币化股票比传统股票资产更‘有用’，通过DeFi组合，更有创新性和创造力

🔸Haley @Hui_Huangg (Investment Director, @YZiLabs )：
🔹RWA领域正在从标准化RWA资产（例如美债等）向非标准化RWA资产发展（例如从最初始的代币化国债，发展到现在的代币化骨跑）
🔹过去行业更多是在搭建、完善RWA基础设施层（路径合规等层面），让用户和机构入场。在此之后市场会更看重应用层，例如RWA资产的质押、借贷等等

🔸Kevin @kevinlhr88  (Co-Founder @saturn_credit  )：
🔹STRC 的推出，我认为这是比特币的“iPhone 时刻”
🔹比特币大规模普及的核心障碍是波动性。STRC 首次在大规模下降低波动、保留比特币敞口，并真正进入固定收益市场。
🔹DeFi 缺可持续、可规模化的收益来源；STRC 的优势在于上市公司融资能力，以及持续把资本配置到比特币
🔹Strategy 以约 12% 股息率发行 STRC 并买比特币。只要回报高于资金成本，模式就能持续，并有机会做到数百亿乃至数千亿美元规模。它在比特币、传统信用市场和链上收益之间，建起了可大规模扩展的桥梁。

2️⃣ STRC 进入DeFi 带来哪些思考

🔸Kevin:
🔹用户们 为什么选择 STRC
・STRC 的收益是建立在一个大家更能够理解的资产和商业模式之上的：Strategy 通过支付资金成本来融资，然后把这些资金继续部署到比特币上。
・流动性强以及固定收益产品的收益特征，这非常适合 DeFi。
・更容易被理解、定价，也更容易真正实现链上规模化
🔹Saturn的价值主张
・全球无许可入口 + 低成本
用户可用稳定币直接买 STRC，无需美国券商账户。
100 万美元仓位进出成本约 6–8bp，低于其他渠道的 15–20bp。
・DeFi 可组合性，做出传统券商做不到的产品  
循环杠杆可将敞口做到 3 倍以上（传统通常约 2 倍）；  
分层成 senior / junior 不同风险收益结构  ；
通过 Pendle 交易收益率，把浮动收益锁成固定收益
🔹关于STRC 风险管理
管理风险最好的办法是正面讲清产品与用户真实承担的风险。
sUSDat 从一开始就向用户坦承风险：
承担的是 STRC 价格波动和市场风险。从产品设计到市场推广层面，风险方面一直保持透明，所以STRC 波动时 Saturn 已有准备。
当前 STRC 风险已改善：Strategy 约有 60 亿美元现金和 20 亿美元回购计划，下行保护更强，但波动仍在。过去三个月，senior 产品 PMF 很强：想拿 STRC 收益、少承担价格波动的用户，可通过 senior tranche 获约 7.8% 收益，由 junior 先亏。junior 保护尚未击穿。
这体现了把 STRC 带上 DeFi 的价值：同一资产，链上可重组为不同风险收益结构

🔸Matt：
🔹Ondo 不只是RWA资产买卖入口。还有资产的使用（应用于DeFi）、资产的build (创立你想要的DeFi)
🔹种优先股固收类资产正在变得越来越重要，这在DeFi领域非常有吸引力。
Saturn是一个优秀的例子， @OndoPerps 也是一个很好的例子，用户可以用STRC做抵押品，一边可以交易，然一边赚抵押品的收益
🔹优先股、固守类RWA与普通股票上链的不同
・分红的处理，技术上和法律上都要解决好
・普通股票上链，主要是投资者感兴趣；优先股、固守类RWA则主要是DeFi开发者和用户感兴趣
🔹关于STRC 风险管理
很认同Kevin的观点，风险方面最重要的是对用户保持透明，让所有用户都知道自己的资产暴露在什么样的风险之下

🔸Haley：
🔹STRC 这类资产是很大的 BTC-yield 机会。此前在BTC-yield staking 上，用户资产安全、托管和灵活性都缺少像 STRC 这样的方案。
🔹STRC 与比特币高度相关，它有月度分红，同时自带信用风险并捕捉价格波动，这种“混合结构”此前较少见。
🔹资产上链后还能进一步释放链上优势，给资产和用户带来更多玩法。
🔹主要挑战：传统资产有交易时段，链上则 24/7，定价、赎回和流动性管理更依赖运营能力；底层比特币波动也需关注。
🔹总结：赛道仍早、成长性高，后续会有更多优质资产与链上结合，带来新机会

3️⃣ Ondo × Saturn × Pendle，这几层接在一起能做什么

🔸Kevin：
🔹sUSDat 最难的是管理链下与链上流动性：出入金成本、结算、执行风险。
因此与 Ondo 合作——Ondo 负责投研运营和传统资产上链，Saturn 专注分发与结构化设计。
🔹分层产品最难、也是长期护城河：匹配不同风险偏好的资金。
Senior 与 Junior 互相依赖，缺一边结构就跑不起来。目标是做成两端资金网络，高效撮合资本。Saturn 的长期价值不在“把 STRC 搬上链”，而在把流动性、分发和资本匹配结合起来，做出传统券商难以获得、甚至不存在的结构化产品与衍生品。

🔸Matt：
🔹对Ondo来说最难的也是流动性
这也是RWA整个行业的最大问题。例如有人想买代币化STRC，那么我们必须在链下有足够的现金买链下的STRC股票；反之如果有人想卖，我们又要有足够的链上稳定币进行支付
许多人说代币化就代表有更好的流动性，我反而觉得是相反，RWA的流动性一定会比传统金融的流动性更“贵”
🔹Saturn也解决了Ondo的问题：创造力和创新

🔸JoeJoe @joejoedefi ：
Saturn吸引我的地方在于
🔹收益丰厚，玩法多样
收益标的STRC 能够提供相对稳定的 11%+ Apr的收益，在DeFi中并不常见，而且资金规模基本没有限制，不存在基数扩大、收益被稀释的情况。
然后再通过Saturn提供的DeFi组合，衍生出丰富的参与策略，适合不同投资喜好的玩家
🔹收益来源独特
BTC信贷依托于Crypto的根本信条之一BTC，诞生于现实世界金融，现在又通过Saturn回馈于Crypto，这个叙事天生政治正确，很吸引我这样的加密原生用户。

4️⃣ 下一步与未来

🔸Kevin：
两大长期方向：
🔹数字货币
按 Saylor 的构想，做最终由比特币支撑、更可用的“钱”。比特币变货币的核心障碍是波动。
分两步去波动：先用 STRC 去掉大部分波动、保留 BTC 经济敞口；再用分层进一步削剩余波动。目标是做出相对稳定、约 7% 收益的数字货币，把比特币触达几乎所有资金。
🔹数字信用扩张
STRC、SATA 只是开始，会有更多发行方和产品。Saturn 要帮这类资产上链、全球分发，并做结构化产品。长期希望 sUSDat 从单一底层变成多元化数字信用指数。

🔸Matt：
🔹代币化股票未来的突破在于 使用性
大部分用户买代币化的股票是因为买不到现实股票，或者觉得他们买到的地方太贵了。那下一步是让这些资产真正的能用，做抵押品，做结构化的产品，还有24小时的交易
🔹代币化股票的挖掘方向
・Pre-IPO股票
・美股之外的全球化股票

🔸Haley：
未来看两大方向：更多新资产，以及更强的可组合性。
🔹新资产方面：
除现有 credit 外，关注 private credit、公司层债权、高收益债、信用利差，以及代币化股票等股权类资产。
🔹组合性方面：
随代币化股票 AUM 增长，把稳定收益资产当抵押品，打开借贷、衍生品和杠杆。早期/pre-IPO 缺定价确定性，会有更多链上验证。交易场所与发射平台会覆盖股票、指数篮子、大宗商品等，公共市场或从单纯持有收益转向交易、分红、杠杆的 hybrid 模式——这才是 TradFi 做不到的可组合价值。
🔹项目筛选上更看重：是否有真实现金流（激励补贴不可持续）、用户粘性，以及 AUM 稳定性。

Every electron in the universe might be the same electron.

In 1940, John Wheeler called Richard Feynman and suggested that the reason every electron has exactly the same mass and charge, to a precision we cannot even measure a deviation from, is that there is only one of them.

A single electron, weaving forwards and backwards through time, threading through every moment of cosmic history, appearing as matter when it moves one way and as its antiparticle when it moves the other.

The idea was never proven, but it was never quite killed either. The math allows it.

An electron going backwards in time is mathematically identical to a positron going forwards, and the equations do not care which description you pick.

If Wheeler was right, then the particle in your retina reading this sentence is the same particle burning in the heart of a star ten billion light years away.

You are not made of many things. You are made of one thing, seen from many angles at once.

text:
Jev Engineering is the term for what turns an agent stack into an actual control system.

It moves the expensive model out of every decision loop.

Up to 193x faster. 444x cheaper. Measured, not theoretical.

The core idea:

The model shouldn't decide everything.

Here's the actual shape of the loop:

request
→ structured state
→ Jev router
→ cheapest capable model
→ worker
→ relevance / approval checks
→ execution gate
→ tool

The important part isn't the diagram, it's this.

The decision layers don't generate prose.

They route. Score. Block. Approve.

Nothing in that layer writes a sentence.

So the expensive model only gets called when the task actually requires reasoning, not for every checkpoint along the way.

That's the whole point of Jev Engineering:

Separate reasoning from decision-making.

Then make the decision layer measurable, cheap, and fast.

Full breakdown in the article below.

Follow @cyrilXBT, this is the architecture pattern most agent builders haven't caught up to yet.

text:
🧐Zcash 的「天启六骑士」

密码学界其实和 Zooko 一样，无时无刻不在寻找着「完美」答案。

2013 年，约翰霍普金斯大学的密码学家提出 Zerocoin 协议，次年进化成 Zerocash 论文。论文的核心就是当下 Web3 行业内被无数次提及和使用的 zk-SNARKs 算法，这让「所有人都能验证交易合法、却没人知道交易内容」这件事，第一次从理论走向了实际。

零知识证明这个概念本身并非 Zerocash 最先提出的，但 Zerocash 却是第一个真正能同时实现去中心化和端到端加密隐私的落地设计。Zooko 后来在多个采访中均表示，在看到这篇论文的时候，他的心情「极度兴奋」。2015 年，Zooko 拉上论文的作者们组建了公司 Zerocoin Electric Coin Company，后来改名 Electric Coin Company，也就是现在 Zcash 的运营公司 ECC。

硅谷投资人 Naval Ravikant，在公司成立之初就签了 71.5 万美元的支票。后续融资中，17 名投资人凑够了约 300 万美元，名单里有 Digital Currency Group 的 Barry Silbert，也有 Pantera。

万事俱备，Zcash 的主网上线也进入了倒计时。Zooko 和 ECC 为 Zcash 的推出准备了加密货币史上最富仪式感的「开幕典礼」。

zk-SNARKs 需要一组公共参数，生成参数的过程会产生一种「有毒废料（toxic waste）」，谁拿到它，谁就能神不知鬼不觉地凭空印币。你可以将这组参数理解为 Zcash 的「初始密码」，谁掌握了密码就可以伪造零知识证明增发或者双花 ZEC，总之就是可以在这条链上为所欲为。

上线当天，总共有 6 个人参与了 Zcash 的参数生成仪式。实名的三人包括了 Zooko 自己、Zcash 技术顾问 Andrew Miller、Coin Center 研究主管 Peter Van Valkenburgh。为了防止被针对性攻击，Zooko 还邀请了三位匿名人士。

化名 Moses Spears 的参与者，后来被公开是 NCC Group 安全工程师 Derek Hinch，NCC Group 被秘密雇佣，既要诚实执行仪式，也要尝试从内部「攻击」仪式，做安全验证；化名 Fabrice Renault 的参与者后来被公开是比特币核心开发者 Peter Todd，Zooko 特意邀请他，是因为他当时对整个仪式持怀疑态度。Zooko 认为让批评者亲自参与，反而能增加可信度。

至于最后一名匿名参与者 John Dobbertin，直到 6 年后的 2022 年，其身份才被揭晓。

2016 年 10 月，分布在三大洲的六个人隔空接力，每人用一台物理隔离的电脑生成自己那段参数，算完就把随机数连带着硬件一起销毁。有人为防信号泄露给机器裹上电磁屏蔽，有人直接放火烧了电脑。只要六个人里有一个是诚实的，只要 6 份参数中有一份被销毁，Zcash 的 ZK 系统就是安全的。

2016 年 10 月 28 日，Zcash 主网上线。在经济模型上，Zcash 几乎照抄了比特币，总量 2100 万枚，大约四年减半。甚至因为 Zcash 的平均出块时间是两分半，区块奖励也设计为 12.5 ZEC。但 Zcash 为了降低早期的风险，选择让区块奖励在前 2 万个区块里线性爬升至 12.5 ZEC。

因为慢启动机制，市面上的 ZEC 少得可怜，价格被炒到天花乱坠。而随着供应释放，价格几天内腰斩再腰斩，到 2017 年初已经跌破 50 美元。除了「没货」，ECC 团队还夹带了「私货」：头四年，每个区块 20% 的奖励直接流向创始团队、员工、顾问和早期股东，四年下来 210 万枚，占总量的整整一成。

在 ZEC 价格重新站上四位数的那几天，F2Pool 联创王纯在 X 上晒出了 6 年前 Zcash 成员将 EST 和 EDT 时间混淆的聊天记录，之后紧接着发文吐槽将部分区块奖励直接发给早期团队的行为，虽然价格涨了，但和同期大热的 Hyperliquid 根本无法相提并论。

不靠谱和混乱，确实是 Zcash 早期的底色。而这，似乎也注定了这一路的坎坷。

text:
Recently, a lot of people have been discussing robinhood:0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3, but I think the core of this rally is no longer simply the AI Narrative. The market is starting to reprice a new asset category: AI Inference Marketplace + Tradable AI Credits + Tokenized Revenue.

0xaa07a0e9209e16ac99708c3ec70159c6ef3128a3 

When we first looked at ORBIO, the logic was actually very simple: trading ORBIO generates a 1.5% fee, with a portion converted into OpenRouter Credits and distributed to qualifying holders according to the rules.

So the market was initially betting on:ORBIO → Trading Fees → AI Credits

In other words, “hold a token while receiving real AI usage credits.”

But what really started accelerating ORBIO was the emergence of CREDIT.

Around September 15, CREDIT + Staking went live, turning the AI credits that previously existed inside user accounts into on-chain assets.

Now:1 CREDIT = $1 of AI usage

CREDIT can be generated through staking, traded, transferred, or activated into API balance for actually calling AI models. Unused CREDIT can also be sold at a discount through the on-chain Order Book and Uniswap.

This fundamentally changed ORBIO’s product logic:

Before:ORBIO → Earn AI Credits

Now:ORBIO → Stake → CREDIT → Trade / Transfer / Consume

So ORBIO is no longer simply a “hold the token and earn credits” Token. It is attempting to build a secondary market for AI Inference Credits.

The entire system can be understood as two layers:

ORBIO = Staking Layer + Fee Engine

CREDIT = AI Inference Consumption Asset

ORBIO generates incentives and fees, while CREDIT is what actually enters the AI usage layer.

As a result, what the market is betting on has also changed.

Initially, people were betting:“Holding ORBIO gives you AI usage credits.”

Now they are betting:“Can Orbio turn AI Inference into an on-chain commodity that can be traded, transferred, and consumed?”

If this logic works, the flywheel becomes:ORBIO Trading Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → CREDIT Supply ↑ → Discounted AI Credits ↑ → AI Users / Agents ↑ → Inference Demand ↑ → Platform Revenue ↑ → ORBIO Utility ↑

This is fundamentally different from the valuation logic of a typical AI Meme, because the ultimate value is not simply that “people believe in ORBIO,” but that people actually need CREDIT to use AI.

Orbio already has some real product usage data, including a significant number of API Requests, Tokens Served, and Credits Distributed. The Gateway also supports hundreds of models and provides an OpenAI-compatible API that can be connected directly to Cursor, Claude Code, or self-built applications.

So the market is now effectively assigning several Narratives to ORBIO:

AI Infrastructure

AI Inference Marketplace

Tokenized AI Credits

AI Agent Economy

Revenue-linked Token

Robinhood Chain

Tokenized Assets

But I think the most important factor is not RH Chain or NVDA. It is whether CREDIT can actually become an AI Consumption Asset with real buyer demand.

That is also the most important validation point for the next stage of the rally.

First, can CREDIT trading volume continue to grow?

The existence of CREDIT does not mean the Marketplace has already succeeded. What really matters is how much CREDIT is traded every day, how many buyers and sellers there are, and what the average discount is.

Second, can real AI Revenue continue to grow?

Crypto trading volume can be driven by speculation, but real users paying to call AI models is a completely different signal.

Third, will AI Agents start actively using CREDIT?

If Agents can eventually purchase CREDIT through their own wallets, transfer CREDIT, and call models, then CREDIT is no longer just an “AI API Coupon.” It could become the Fuel of the Agent Economy.

Fourth, can CREDIT Supply and Demand form a sustainable market?

Stakers provide CREDIT Supply, while AI Users provide CREDIT Demand.

If there are only large numbers of ORBIO Holders but not enough real AI users, the outcome could eventually become:Holder receives CREDIT → Holder wants to sell → Not enough buyers → CREDIT discount gets deeper

On the other hand, if AI users continue to grow:Holder provides CREDIT → AI User buys discounted credits → CREDIT gets consumed → Marketplace forms

That would be the real Product-Market Fit.

Fifth, can ORBIO Staking continue to grow?

Staking turns ORBIO from a purely tradable asset into a yield layer while continuously generating CREDIT. If the amount of staked ORBIO continues to grow, the connection between ORBIO and CREDIT becomes stronger.

But one of the biggest risks for ORBIO right now is that it still has strong Volume Reflexivity.

ORBIO rises → More people trade → Fees ↑ → CREDIT ↑ → Staking yield ↑ → More people hold ORBIO → ORBIO becomes easier to push higher

When this cycle works, it is very powerful.

But the reverse is also true:ORBIO falls → Trading Volume ↓ → Fees ↓ → CREDIT ↓ → Staking yield falls → Holding ORBIO becomes less attractive → Further weakness

So the real question is:Is Orbio building a real AI Marketplace, or is it using ORBIO’s own trading volume to subsidize the AI Marketplace?

These two scenarios imply completely different long-term value.

There is also another very important risk: although CREDIT is defined as 1 CREDIT = $1 of AI Usage, it is not $1 USDC, nor is it an asset that can be directly redeemed for cash.

It essentially represents AI consumption capacity. Once activated, it becomes API Balance and cannot be redeemed back into cash.

So:CREDIT = AI Consumption Right

Not:CREDIT = $1 Cash

ORBIO’s valuation is also no longer operating under the same logic as when it was at a few million dollars in market cap. As the market gradually prices in the product, CREDIT, Staking, AI Usage, and Marketplace narratives, what needs to grow next is the underlying fundamental data, rather than simply the Narrative.

So the key things to watch going forward are:

Retail AI Revenue ↑

Gateway Usage ↑

CREDIT Volume ↑

CREDIT Buyers ↑

Agent Usage ↑

Staked ORBIO ↑

CREDIT Discount remains healthy

Revenue / Buyback / CREDIT Funding mechanisms remain transparent

Conversely, if we see:

ORBIO Volume ↓

Insufficient CREDIT Buyers

AI Revenue stagnates

CREDIT discounts become increasingly deep

Staking yield declines

New mechanisms fail to operate sustainably

Then the current AI Infrastructure Premium will come under pressure.

So my current core view of ORBIO can be condensed into one sentence:

ORBIO started as “hold the Token to receive AI Credits,” and is now attempting to evolve into “ORBIO as the economic layer, with CREDIT as the tradable fuel for AI Inference.”

What the market is really betting on is no longer:“Is ORBIO a good AI Token?”

It is:“Can Orbio become the trading and settlement market for AI Inference?”

If CREDIT can eventually evolve from “a reward given to ORBIO Holders” into “a product that AI users actively want to purchase,” then ORBIO’s story will have truly moved from Token Incentive to Product-Market Fit.

On the other hand, if CREDIT remains highly dependent on ORBIO’s own trading volume and crypto liquidity, then a large part of the current valuation is still trading the Narrative, rather than a mature AI infrastructure business.

尽我所能帮助与我有缘、被我知晓且罹患癌症的家庭

其中两次我公开在了 X 上，只为像子路受牛般带动更多人行善

詹臻便是其中之一，只可惜她已不幸离世
https://t.co/UjORyRmBWe

另一次便是今年 9 月 9 日的 王*悦，因为癌症，不得不放弃一路苦读才考取的博士学位，谁见了不为之动容

因此我再次捐款 1 万元

原本是发自内心的善举，却无意间差点酿成最不堪的祸事

这次事件，被人发上链铸成了 Meme 币，当时我正在机上，落地第一时间有人提醒我可以领取税收作为善款，我只看到了好的一面却忽略了另一面

事实证明，人类的理性经不起短时反复的捶打，税收成为了无尽噩梦的开始

人在国外，给她转账只能使用电子方式，最担心的是如果在出金过程遇到不明资金，进而影响到她救命钱的使用，那真是我最不愿看到的事情，而我当时又没有足够资金垫付

迫不得已，只能向她解释原因，等一个月后再想办法，并且在推特发布

这之后，无边的困扰遍袭来了，对我本人的攻击和狐疑我可以承受，但对受捐对象 王*悦 的无休止打扰真的令我无比愧怍，最难以接受的是有人胁迫她发布 Meme 相关内容

就让这一切就此停止吧，我们已经心力憔悴了，就在刚刚已经把这个 Meme 的税收权限转入黑洞，并且永不提及，永不关注

已经获得的税收仍在链上从未动过，未来也不会再碰触，这个钱包未来动作将交由律师及相关人士妥善处理

但是为了让她尽早得到救助，我已按照今日价格 1u/6.66r 转给了 王*悦，钱是我连夜拆借垫付来的，这期间的种种痛苦就到此为止吧

最后想说我正如之前所说的我们从未引导、许诺关于这个 Meme 的任何信息，完全与我们无关，盈亏自负

所有相关信息我已全部取证保存，并且会持续取证所有提及此代币的人，我已与委托律师取得联系，确保我和 王*悦 的权益可以得到保障

感谢事件中的一切正义之士，尽管你们有些对我产生误解

最后，愿天下无癌 🙏

Foundations: Market Structure, Volatility Targeting, Pod Shops & Other Gremlins 

What this says is that the market is picking itself up more day-to-day than ever before. In fact, 40 years ago, the market just randomly walked through one day to the next. Now, there is a mean reversion, a walk back to the starting point.

In fact, within and especially across days, this market increasingly reverses itself.

The 1985-2000 market was 1.02, a coin flip, a random walk day to day.

Not anymore. 0.881, nope.

Again for the academics, the two-day variance ratio today is 0.881 with a z-statistic of −2.56 across 3,774 sessions. That’s walking back.

How the Market Works Today, Yesterday, and the Decades before THAT.

text:
A useful AI career path for backend developers is becoming much clearer.

AI infrastructure engineer.
You don't have to become a machine learning researcher.
Your existing backend skills already transfer.
APIs → model serving
queues → async inference
caching → KV/prompt caching
databases → AI state and retrieval
observability → agent tracing
Docker/Kubernetes → model deployment
distributed systems → scalable inference

Then add the AI-specific layer
PyTorch basics
GPU fundamentals
LLM inference
embeddings
RAG
model serving
quantization
evaluation

This is interesting because every company adding AI eventually runs into infrastructure problems.
Latency.
GPU utilization.
Inference cost.
Reliability.
Scaling.
Data movement.

The models may change constantly.
But those engineering problems aren't going away.
You don't need to start from zero to move into AI.
Sometimes the fastest path is adding AI infrastructure skills to what you already know.

text:
**This is the 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3 running at ~30 tok/s on 16× NVIDIA DGX Spark.**

Not a synthetic “it boots” test.

👇 **Actually generating. Usable speed.**

A few weeks ago, the question was:

*Can a model this big even run properly on a cluster of Sparks?*

Then:

*Can we make it fast enough to actually use? What about for agentic frameworks?*

I think we're well past that question now.

With the new **V5**, we're seeing roughly another **20% speed-up**, plus a big improvement in concurrency:

⚡ **C1: 29.8 tok/s**
⚡ **C2: 42 tok/s aggregate**
⚡ **C4: 58 tok/s aggregate**
⚡ **C8: 87.1 tok/s aggregate**
⚡ **136 tok/s peak at C8**

And long context remains usable:

→ ~20 tok/s @ 300K context

So **Kimi K3 on DGX Spark is no longer a “yes, it boots” experiment.**

It's becoming a genuinely usable platform for **agentic coding, long-running agents and concurrent workloads**.

Getting here required work across almost the entire stack:

→ GB10 / SM121-specific vLLM work
→ Kimi-specific fixes and patches
→ optimized MLA / CuTe kernels
→ DSpark speculative decoding nst  3/6 fusioning
→ FlashInfer / Triton / CUDA work
→ KV-cache/ DCP + long-context fixes
→ NCCL / RoCE tuning
→ MoE fusion + nopad — projection-transport  fusion + per-rank slice legality (VLLM_K3_MARLIN_NOPAD=1) and many other small fixes, from open source community and from us.

There wasn't one magic flag.

It was dozens of improvements stacked together until a **2.8 trillion parameter model on 16 tiny GB10 boxes became something I actually want to use.**

Code, image, recipes and patches:

https://t.co/HkMfJYLqhF

**Pull it. Run it. Break it. Improve it.**

I'm pretty sure we still haven't found the ceiling.

If somebody tells you Kimi K3 on DGX Spark is just a proof of concept…

**show them this video. 🙂**

https://t.co/oIf2z4v4W6

text:
Trailing stops are now available for perp markets. 

A trailing stop's trigger price follows the mark price as it moves in favor of the position. When the mark price retraces from its best level by the selected distance or percentage, it triggers a market order. For long positions, the trigger price follows the highest mark price reached since activation; for short positions, it follows the lowest. An optional activation price determines when tracking begins. Without one, tracking begins immediately at the current mark price.

- 原理：买入 RWUSD 会有3.36%收益，而他可以作为保证金所以可以做跨所套 BTC 资金费

author: Foresight_News
quoted_text:
🧐Zcash 的「天启六骑士」

密码学界其实和 Zooko 一样，无时无刻不在寻找着「完美」答案。

2013 年，约翰霍普金斯大学的密码学家提出 Zerocoin 协议，次年进化成 Zerocash 论文。论文的核心就是当下 Web3 行业内被无数次提及和使用的 zk-SNARKs 算法，这让「所有人都能验证交易合法、却没人知道交易内容」这件事，第一次从理论走向了实际。

零知识证明这个概念本身并非 Zerocash 最先提出的，但 Zerocash 却是第一个真正能同时实现去中心化和端到端加密隐私的落地设计。Zooko 后来在多个采访中均表示，在看到这篇论文的时候，他的心情「极度兴奋」。2015 年，Zooko 拉上论文的作者们组建了公司 Zerocoin Electric Coin Company，后来改名 Electric Coin Company，也就是现在 Zcash 的运营公司 ECC。

硅谷投资人 Naval Ravikant，在公司成立之初就签了 71.5 万美元的支票。后续融资中，17 名投资人凑够了约 300 万美元，名单里有 Digital Currency Group 的 Barry Silbert，也有 Pantera。

万事俱备，Zcash 的主网上线也进入了倒计时。Zooko 和 ECC 为 Zcash 的推出准备了加密货币史上最富仪式感的「开幕典礼」。

zk-SNARKs 需要一组公共参数，生成参数的过程会产生一种「有毒废料（toxic waste）」，谁拿到它，谁就能神不知鬼不觉地凭空印币。你可以将这组参数理解为 Zcash 的「初始密码」，谁掌握了密码就可以伪造零知识证明增发或者双花 ZEC，总之就是可以在这条链上为所欲为。

上线当天，总共有 6 个人参与了 Zcash 的参数生成仪式。实名的三人包括了 Zooko 自己、Zcash 技术顾问 Andrew Miller、Coin Center 研究主管 Peter Van Valkenburgh。为了防止被针对性攻击，Zooko 还邀请了三位匿名人士。

化名 Moses Spears 的参与者，后来被公开是 NCC Group 安全工程师 Derek Hinch，NCC Group 被秘密雇佣，既要诚实执行仪式，也要尝试从内部「攻击」仪式，做安全验证；化名 Fabrice Renault 的参与者后来被公开是比特币核心开发者 Peter Todd，Zooko 特意邀请他，是因为他当时对整个仪式持怀疑态度。Zooko 认为让批评者亲自参与，反而能增加可信度。

至于最后一名匿名参与者 John Dobbertin，直到 6 年后的 2022 年，其身份才被揭晓。

2016 年 10 月，分布在三大洲的六个人隔空接力，每人用一台物理隔离的电脑生成自己那段参数，算完就把随机数连带着硬件一起销毁。有人为防信号泄露给机器裹上电磁屏蔽，有人直接放火烧了电脑。只要六个人里有一个是诚实的，只要 6 份参数中有一份被销毁，Zcash 的 ZK 系统就是安全的。

2016 年 10 月 28 日，Zcash 主网上线。在经济模型上，Zcash 几乎照抄了比特币，总量 2100 万枚，大约四年减半。甚至因为 Zcash 的平均出块时间是两分半，区块奖励也设计为 12.5 ZEC。但 Zcash 为了降低早期的风险，选择让区块奖励在前 2 万个区块里线性爬升至 12.5 ZEC。

因为慢启动机制，市面上的 ZEC 少得可怜，价格被炒到天花乱坠。而随着供应释放，价格几天内腰斩再腰斩，到 2017 年初已经跌破 50 美元。除了「没货」，ECC 团队还夹带了「私货」：头四年，每个区块 20% 的奖励直接流向创始团队、员工、顾问和早期股东，四年下来 210 万枚，占总量的整整一成。

在 ZEC 价格重新站上四位数的那几天，F2Pool 联创王纯在 X 上晒出了 6 年前 Zcash 成员将 EST 和 EDT 时间混淆的聊天记录，之后紧接着发文吐槽将部分区块奖励直接发给早期团队的行为，虽然价格涨了，但和同期大热的 Hyperliquid 根本无法相提并论。

不靠谱和混乱，确实是 Zcash 早期的底色。而这，似乎也注定了这一路的坎坷。

黄仁勋：2030年前AI毁灭世界的可能性为零

黄仁勋在接受CBS采访时表示，完全不同意“AI将在2030年前毁灭人类”的说法，并称这一事件发生的可能性为“0%”。

他认为，相关末日论是在制造恐慌，背后可能存在政治或吸引关注等动机。

此前，Anthropic前安全研究负责人Evan Hubinger曾表示，未来十年AI毁灭人类的概率超过10%，并称目前行业尚未找到解决超级智能对齐问题的方案。

黄仁勋主张AI开发应尽可能加速，认为现有监管已足够，政府无需新增规则。但他同时强调，企业不应在产品尚未准备好或存在安全风险时将其推出。

A trailing stop's trigger price follows the mark price as it moves in favor of the position. 上线当天，总共有 6 个人参与了 Zcash 的参数生成仪式。实名的三人包括了 Zooko 自己、Zcash 技术顾问 Andrew Miller、Coin Center 研究主管 Peter Van Valkenburgh。为了防止被针对性攻击，Zooko 还邀请了三位匿名人士。

化名 Moses Spears 的参与者，后来被公开是 NCC Group 安全工程师 Derek Hinch，NCC Group 被秘密雇佣，既要诚实执行仪式，也要尝试从内部「攻击」仪式，做安全验证；化名 Fabrice Renault 的参与者后来被公开是比特币核心开发者 Peter Todd，Zooko 特意邀请他，是因为他当时对整个仪式持怀疑态度。Zooko 认为让批评者亲自参与，反而能增加可信度。

至于最后一名匿名参与者 John Dobbertin，直到 6 年后的 2022 年，其身份才被揭晓。

2016 年 10 月，分布在三大洲的六个人隔空接力，每人用一台物理隔离的电脑生成自己那段参数，算完就把随机数连带着硬件一起销毁。有人为防信号泄露给机器裹上电磁屏蔽，有人直接放火烧了电脑。只要六个人里有一个是诚实的，只要 6 份参数中有一份被销毁，Zcash 的 ZK 系统就是安全的。

2016 年 10 月 28 日，Zcash 主网上线。在经济模型上，Zcash 几乎照抄了比特币，总量 2100 万枚，大约四年减半。甚至因为 Zcash 的平均出块时间是两分半，区块奖励也设计为 12.5 ZEC。但 Zcash 为了降低早期的风险，选择让区块奖励在前 2 万个区块里线性爬升至 12.5 ZEC。

因为慢启动机制，市面上的 ZEC 少得可怜，价格被炒到天花乱坠。而随着供应释放，价格几天内腰斩再腰斩，到 2017 年初已经跌破 50 美元。除了「没货」，ECC 团队还夹带了「私货」：头四年，每个区块 20% 的奖励直接流向创始团队、员工、顾问和早期股东，四年下来 210 万枚，占总量的整整一成。

在 ZEC 价格重新站上四位数的那几天，F2Pool 联创王纯在 X 上晒出了 6 年前 Zcash 成员将 EST 和 EDT 时间混淆的聊天记录，之后紧接着发文吐槽将部分区块奖励直接发给早期团队的行为，虽然价格涨了，但和同期大热的 Hyperliquid 根本无法相提并论。

不靠谱和混乱，确实是 Zcash 早期的底色。而这，似乎也注定了这一路的坎坷。

quoted_text:
Scammers found a way to make people drain their own wallets without sending them a phishing link.

They uploaded YouTube tutorials showing people how to build an AI crypto trading bot with Claude.

People followed the tutorial themselves.

Copied the code.

Deployed the smart contract themselves.

Funded it from their own wallets.

And approved every transaction themselves.

Except the “trading bot” had no trading logic.

It was built to send their ETH straight to the scammers.

224 wallets lost 274.6 ETH, worth about $517,000 when it was stolen.

The median victim lost 1 ETH.

Some victims even got an error after getting drained telling them to deposit another 50% to fix the bot.

They literally got people to build, fund and approve their own wallet drainer.

You've got to be very careful this days

🧐Zcash 的「天启六骑士」

密码学界其实和 Zooko 一样，无时无刻不在寻找着「完美」答案。

2013 年，约翰霍普金斯大学的密码学家提出 Zerocoin 协议，次年进化成 Zerocash 论文。论文的核心就是当下 Web3 行业内被无数次提及和使用的 zk-SNARKs 算法，这让「所有人都能验证交易合法、却没人知道交易内容」这件事，第一次从理论走向了实际。

零知识证明这个概念本身并非 Zerocash 最先提出的，但 Zerocash 却是第一个真正能同时实现去中心化和端到端加密隐私的落地设计。Zooko 后来在多个采访中均表示，在看到这篇论文的时候，他的心情「极度兴奋」。2015 年，Zooko 拉上论文的作者们组建了公司 Zerocoin Electric Coin Company，后来改名 Electric Coin Company，也就是现在 Zcash 的运营公司 ECC。

硅谷投资人 Naval Ravikant，在公司成立之初就签了 71.5 万美元的支票。后续融资中，17 名投资人凑够了约 300 万美元，名单里有 Digital Currency Group 的 Barry Silbert，也有 Pantera。

万事俱备，Zcash 的主网上线也进入了倒计时。Zooko 和 ECC 为 Zcash 的推出准备了加密货币史上最富仪式感的「开幕典礼」。

zk-SNARKs 需要一组公共参数，生成参数的过程会产生一种「有毒废料（toxic waste）」，谁拿到它，谁就能神不知鬼不觉地凭空印币。你可以将这组参数理解为 Zcash 的「初始密码」，谁掌握了密码就可以伪造零知识证明增发或者双花 ZEC，总之就是可以在这条链上为所欲为。

上线当天，总共有 6 个人参与了 Zcash 的参数生成仪式。实名的三人包括了 Zooko 自己、Zcash 技术顾问 Andrew Miller、Coin Center 研究主管 Peter Van Valkenburgh。为了防止被针对性攻击，Zooko 还邀请了三位匿名人士。

化名 Moses Spears 的参与者，后来被公开是 NCC Group 安全工程师 Derek Hinch，NCC Group 被秘密雇佣，既要诚实执行仪式，也要尝试从内部「攻击」仪式，做安全验证；化名 Fabrice Renault 的参与者后来被公开是比特币核心开发者 Peter Todd，Zooko 特意邀请他，是因为他当时对整个仪式持怀疑态度。Zooko 认为让批评者亲自参与，反而能增加可信度。

至于最后一名匿名参与者 John Dobbertin，直到 6 年后的 2022 年，其身份才被揭晓。

2016 年 10 月，分布在三大洲的六个人隔空接力，每人用一台物理隔离的电脑生成自己那段参数，算完就把随机数连带着硬件一起销毁。有人为防信号泄露给机器裹上电磁屏蔽，有人直接放火烧了电脑。只要六个人里有一个是诚实的，只要 6 份参数中有一份被销毁，Zcash 的 ZK 系统就是安全的。

2016 年 10 月 28 日，Zcash 主网上线。在经济模型上，Zcash 几乎照抄了比特币，总量 2100 万枚，大约四年减半。甚至因为 Zcash 的平均出块时间是两分半，区块奖励也设计为 12.5 ZEC。但 Zcash 为了降低早期的风险，选择让区块奖励在前 2 万个区块里线性爬升至 12.5 ZEC。

因为慢启动机制，市面上的 ZEC 少得可怜，价格被炒到天花乱坠。而随着供应释放，价格几天内腰斩再腰斩，到 2017 年初已经跌破 50 美元。除了「没货」，ECC 团队还夹带了「私货」：头四年，每个区块 20% 的奖励直接流向创始团队、员工、顾问和早期股东，四年下来 210 万枚，占总量的整整一成。

在 ZEC 价格重新站上四位数的那几天，F2Pool 联创王纯在 X 上晒出了 6 年前 Zcash 成员将 EST 和 EDT 时间混淆的聊天记录，之后紧接着发文吐槽将部分区块奖励直接发给早期团队的行为，虽然价格涨了，但和同期大热的 Hyperliquid 根本无法相提并论。

不靠谱和混乱，确实是 Zcash 早期的底色。而这，似乎也注定了这一路的坎坷。

quoted_text:
从fomopeek 被盗事件看web3钱包的巨大安全隐患

1️⃣  为啥ios不安全？
app store 审核没有发现问题 +ios自己漏洞，总之是苹果的锅

2️⃣ 为啥私钥会泄漏？
黑客app 突破沙盒，读取了keychain文件和钱包文件，然后离线破解；还有可能是直接读取了内存里面的明文密钥

3️⃣ 哪些钱包受影响？
只要是自托管的钱包全部有隐患（因为私钥凭证就在本地），包括okx wallet，gate wallet， metamask等

4️⃣ 交易所app受影响吗？
目前看风险比较小，因为交易所的凭证在服务器和用户输入密码；即使密码存在了keychain，交易所还有双重验证，比如生物识别的通行密钥，这个是存在Secure Enclave，黑客后门目前无法触及

5️⃣ 为啥币安web3钱包没有在攻击列表？
因为币安web3钱包大部分是mpc的，也就是说私钥分片，本地没有全部私钥，而获取其他私钥，对于fomopeek攻击成本很高。不得不说，作为第一大所，币安web3钱包的安全设计理念是超过其他交易所的。

6️⃣ 解决自托管的钱包安全问题的终极方案是什么？
如果私钥在手机电脑的内存或者文件里面，一直是最大的风险；所以终极方案就是把私钥转到外部的硬件芯片，这就是硬件钱包比如 @OneKeyHQ  的作用，建议大家重要资产全部用硬件钱包

Claude 已经开始帮 Anthropic 造下一代 Claude 了，而且现在 26% 的研发任务，主要是它自己在做。

这个数字 2 月还不到 1%。

Anthropic 最近做了一次内部测量，现在超过 90% 的研发任务里都有 AI 参与，其中 26% 已经到了「AI leads」的程度，人只给一个高层目标，Claude 自己往下拆任务、执行，再把结果交回来审核。

配套的基础设施规模也已经很夸张。Anthropic 内部同时有大约 3 万个 agent 持续运行，8 月一个月，监控系统审查了超过 10 亿次 agent 决策。

在线系统真正拦下来的比例只有 0.002%。离线系统每周还会另外筛出约 10 万条记录，最后大约 50 条会进入人工审查。

所以 Anthropic 现在内部发生的事情，比「程序员开始用 Claude 写代码」往前走了很多。

它已经在搭一套机器研发机器的流水线，几万个 agent 同时工作，模型负责越来越多研发，人类逐渐往目标制定、审核和异常处理的位置退。

26% 如果继续按照过去半年的速度往上爬，接下来真正值得盯的，就是这个数字什么时候过 50%。

text:
从fomopeek 被盗事件看web3钱包的巨大安全隐患

1️⃣  为啥ios不安全？
app store 审核没有发现问题 +ios自己漏洞，总之是苹果的锅

2️⃣ 为啥私钥会泄漏？
黑客app 突破沙盒，读取了keychain文件和钱包文件，然后离线破解；还有可能是直接读取了内存里面的明文密钥

3️⃣ 哪些钱包受影响？
只要是自托管的钱包全部有隐患（因为私钥凭证就在本地），包括okx wallet，gate wallet， metamask等

4️⃣ 交易所app受影响吗？
目前看风险比较小，因为交易所的凭证在服务器和用户输入密码；即使密码存在了keychain，交易所还有双重验证，比如生物识别的通行密钥，这个是存在Secure Enclave，黑客后门目前无法触及

5️⃣ 为啥币安web3钱包没有在攻击列表？
因为币安web3钱包大部分是mpc的，也就是说私钥分片，本地没有全部私钥，而获取其他私钥，对于fomopeek攻击成本很高。不得不说，作为第一大所，币安web3钱包的安全设计理念是超过其他交易所的。

6️⃣ 解决自托管的钱包安全问题的终极方案是什么？
如果私钥在手机电脑的内存或者文件里面，一直是最大的风险；所以终极方案就是把私钥转到外部的硬件芯片，这就是硬件钱包比如 @OneKeyHQ  的作用，建议大家重要资产全部用硬件钱包

text:
You have only a few minutes to remember and interpret the meanings of a dream after waking. Visions are much the same: intensely clear in the first five minutes after being downloaded from the Akashic records, then rapidly blurring. The receptor must act fast: writing it down to materialize it, initiating implementation as soon as possible. As days pass, the dreamer gets lost; the vision reduces to a narrow idea, far removed from its formless, original nature.

Back in 2016, I had a vivid vision of what AI and Big Data would mean for society in 2025, 2030, 2050. It felt like a somnambulist experience, navigating two superposed futures: one deeply dystopic, echoing the bleakest sci-fi paradigms like Gattaca, yet anchored in Isaac Asimov's seminal work, Foundation (I still keep an Italian edition of the complete quadrilogy spanning 1953 to 1983). This uncertainty about the future gave me the strength to act, but I initially got lost, mistaking the initial revelation for a mere technical challenge to solve, as engineers often do. But that time, it wasn't just an idea. However, I followed a path that would teach me invaluable lessons: from my involvement in developing an AI solution for HR to my efforts building portfolio management tools for Mubadala. These were projects, products, and ideas, but not the true essence of the mission.

Datachain Rope and all its components like the Datawallet+, Datachain Nova, and the Databox are the true materialization of the vision I had a decade ago: DDMI.

At the core of this physical and digital architecture is the Databox, a high-performance, edge-computing micro data management unit designed to bring decentralized intelligence directly into local communities. Engineered to orchestrate heavy local workloads, the Databox operates alongside Datachain Rope, and Datachain Nova, the intelligent orchestration layer design to powers local AI model execution, storage indexing, and secure cryptographic validation across the ecosystem. Together, this triad bridges the gap between raw compute power and human proximity.

By shifting data processing away from monolithic cloud monopolies and bringing it physically closer to where life happens, proximity computing unlocks transformational benefits across every level of society:

1. For Individuals: Everyday citizens gain access to ultra-low-latency AI services, private personal vaults, and autonomous digital agents running locally, without exposing their private life to centralized corporate trackers.

2. For Local Businesses: Regional enterprises can run advanced predictive analytics, local inventory automation, and customer AI models directly on neighborhood nodes, drastically reducing bandwidth costs and eliminating cloud vendor lock-in.

3. For Public Administrations: Cities, municipalities, and local government districts can process sensitive public records, traffic data, and municipal analytics locally, guaranteeing strict compliance with data sovereignty regulations while modernizing public infrastructure.
Deploying a global decentralized network does not mean building from scratch; it means intelligent integration. The Datachain Foundation intends to empower individuals, leverage existing telecommunication towers, central offices, fiber distribution hubs, and local energy substations as host anchor sites for Databox nodes. By tapping into existing power grids and high-speed backbones, we will deploy decentralized data management nodes rapidly and sustainably, transforming passive utility footprints into active hubs of neighborhood intelligence.

To ensure widespread adoption, the network is built on a mutually rewarding economic framework:
Node Owners & Hosting Partners: Individuals, local businesses, or infrastructure operators who purchase and/or host a Databox hardware node earn recurring yield.

Localized Revenue Streams: As residents, shops, municipal offices, and enterprises within a specific quartier, arrondissement, village, or city subscribe to local AI, storage, and computing services, a direct portion of those subscription fees is automatically distributed to the node owners powering that local area.
This aligns the interests of node operators and local users, fostering a self-sustaining micro-economy around proximity computing.

Centralized AI platforms rely on harvesting massive amounts of personal data into single, vulnerable silos. The proximity data center model flips this paradigm on its head. By running AI models locally on decentralized proximity nodes, user data never leaves its immediate geographic zone. Advanced cryptographic proofs, zero-knowledge architectures, and auditable open-source protocols ensure that AI interactions remain secure, fully transparent, and strictly anonymous.

This is the true decentralized internet we are talking about for the last two decades. An infrastructure where advanced artificial intelligence becomes a public utility, accessible, private, and empowering for the many, rather than an instrument of control for the few.

QUOTE 1 - Love for life and rationality are essential for life to become a source of joy and flourishing.
: Love for life and rationality are not optional extras. They are the essential foundation that turns mere existence into a source of genuine joy and flourishing.
Love for life brings warmth, gratitude, and a deep appreciation for the gift of being alive. It fuels curiosity, resilience, and the desire to protect and nurture what is beautiful. Rationality, in turn, provides clarity, honesty, and the ability to navigate reality without illusion. Together, they create a powerful synergy: a heart that cherishes life guided by a mind that understands it.
Without love for life, rationality can become cold and empty. Without rationality, love for life can become blind or fragile. When both are present and balanced, life stops being a struggle to endure and becomes something worth celebrating every day.
This combination allows us to face difficulties with courage, find meaning in ordinary moments, and build a future worth living in. It is the quiet secret to a flourishing existence.
QUOTE 2 - Love is the only force that turns millions of individuals into a nation, and nations into humanity.
: Love is the only force powerful enough to turn millions of separate individuals into a genuine nation, and nations into a united humanity.
Laws can regulate behavior, shared interests can create alliances, and culture can foster identity, but only love creates the deep emotional bond of belonging and mutual care. It transforms “them” into “us.” It makes people willing to sacrifice, to protect, to build together rather than merely coexist.
On a larger scale, the same principle applies. When love extends beyond national borders, it turns competing states into parts of a single human family. Without this connecting force, unity remains fragile, easily broken by fear or self-interest. With it, differences become complementary rather than divisive.
Love is the invisible thread that holds humanity together. It is what makes a nation more than a territory, and humanity more than a collection of nations. In the end, the strength and future of both depend not on power or wealth, but on our capacity to love one another.

author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
I said "auto-regressive LLMs, in and of themselves, will not lead human-level AI" 
That statement is still totally true.

First, the reasoning abilities of current AI systems are based non-auto-regressive search (which is what I have always advocated for). But AFAICT, they do it in token space, which is limited and inefficient. I have claimed that human-like reasoning must be a search in continuous representation space. It looks like the industry is moving towards that.

Second, the self-improvement methods, as currently practiced, only work for domains where the quality of outputs can be scored without human intervention, such as mathematics, code, and scenarios that can be simulated accurately. Not anything else. Humans and animals learn new skills way more efficiently than current RL methods.

Third, the multimodal capabilities of current AI assistants generally use separately-trained encoders (that are not LLMs). This is also what I've been advocating. Except that I think the best way to do this is with JEPA trained with self-supervised learning. The research community is clearly moving towards that (3000 papers on JEPA in just 4 years).

Fourth, if LLMs were a path to human-level AI, we would have domestic robots and Level-4 or Level-5 self-driving cars for consumers by now. And we don't. We certainly don't have cars that can learn to drive in 20 hours or practice like any teenager. We're still missing something pretty huge to claim human-level intelligence (let alone superhuman).

Sure, we now have computer systems that are impressive, very useful, and whose performance is superhuman in an increasing number of domains (coding being one of them). 
But that's true of the entire history of progress in computer technology. 

Lastly, there is a basic confusion about what intelligence actually is.
It is not the mere accumulation and regurgitation of existing declarative knowledge (which is essentially what LLMs do).
As Jean Piaget famously said, "intelligence is not what you know, it is what you do when you don't know." 
It is your ability to solve new problem without any prior training, to act in previously-unknown scenarios, and to adapt very quickly to new situations with minimal training.

We're still far from that.

quoted_text:
There has been very little coverage of how much money Chinese AI labs, specifically Zhipu, Moonshot, and DeepSeek, have raised since June 2026.

They have raised around $35B in the last 4-5 months, which is 7x higher than what they have raised before May
Kimi and DeepSeek will likely raise another $10B each from their IPO, and Zhipu will likely raise another $5B by January 2027
The 3 Chinese labs will raise around $60B from May 2026 to January 2027
I personally believe that this much money is enough for them to remain competitive with the frontier, especially if they continue focusing on efficiency 
v4.1 Flash enables the whale to generate a loooot more RL rollouts for training compared to what the other labs can achieve with their models. A more efficient model at inference also improves the economics of training ur next gen model

Do I think China may agree to "pacing AI development"??
I certainly expect that Xi-Trump meeting will lead to a
testing agreement. I expect that Chinese labs will start publishing safety testing reports as well, and there will be greater scrutiny towards the cybersecurity capabilities of Chinese models. They will likely lobotomize their models in those domains, just like Fable/Opus/Astra/Sol.

Agreeing to a pacing agreement doesn't really impact Chinese AI developers in the next 9-15 months. Deploying $60B and buying compute takes time. It will probably take them around 9 months to burn through all the cash and convert it into compute, and the next big capabilities jump from the Chinese side will probably occur in Q2-Q3 2027. They may agree to a pacing agreement (training models on lots of compute) but continue building their compute capacity, and once their big data centers are ready, or they are close to releasing their "dangerous model," they can withdraw from the agreement. 
China can't/won't have much of an impact in the near term (next 9-15 months) as it takes time to convert the capital they have raised into usable compute. Now, if a breakthrough like test-time parametric continual learning is achieved (DeepSeek is working on it), then things will change. The real "pacing the frontier" basically means an agreement on limiting the amount of training compute. I don't think China will agree to that.

text:
I’ve known @jumperapp for a long time, but honestly I always had it in a pretty simple box in my head

basically, somewhere I could use when I needed a bridge

but today I spent a lot more time actually going through the app, and where I place Jumper in my head changed a bit

because I don’t think Jumper’s main thing is being a bridge aggregator

bridge is just where Jumper first meets the user

but after looking through the app, I realized something:

if capital is already moving through Jumper, why should the user need to go to another app for the next financial action?

I first noticed this in a normal bridge flow

when Jumper found me a route to bridge from Arbitrum to Base, it even noticed I was low on gas on Base and added the option to get destination gas inside the same flow

up to this point, you can still say it’s just a really good bridge aggregator

but the part where it really clicked for me was Earn

I was looking at a Morpho $USDC vault on Monad

my capital was sitting on Arbitrum as $ARB

naturally, a bunch of different steps formed in my head

but on Jumper, I selected the $ARB on Arbitrum and the system built a route directly into that Morpho position for me

so the bridge aggregation doesn’t stop at the bridge screen

the routing layer starts getting embedded into the financial action itself

that was the point where the super-app thesis started to feel real to me

then I looked at Advanced and the same pattern was there again

they’re putting different execution intents like Limit, TWAP and Multi-swap on top of the same aggregation engine

so the user’s intent changes, but what the infrastructure is doing stays the same:

what are you trying to do, and how do I get you there with the least friction?

the idea gets even broader on the RWA side

when I looked at $NVIDIA, it didn’t just show me one $NVDA token

I could see different issuer and chain options from xStocks, Ondo, Robinhood, Backpack Securities, Coinbase Tokenized Stocks and bStocks

you can also compare things like fees, redemption, dividends and other differences between the issuers

so I don’t think what’s being aggregated here is just liquidity or bridge routes anymore

the decision itself is starting to get aggregated too

and I think that part is really important

that’s why I don’t think the right way to read Jumper’s super-app thesis is:

“they added Earn next to bridge, added RWA, and Perps is coming too.”

if you actually dig into the product, it feels more like:

it’s trying to aggregate what users do before, during and after capital moves

being a super-app doesn’t just mean having a lot of features

it means reducing the number of times a user has to leave for another app every time their financial intent changes

and this isn’t an app starting from zero and still looking for distribution

Jumper is already at $40B+ lifetime volume and 100K+ monthly active users

because what I saw today wasn’t a bunch of independent features

it was the same aggregation/routing logic being reused across more and more financial intents

Make the JUMP

text:
先说结论：Jev 非常有用。

它保证格式是对的。选没选对，要自己 eval。

我们实测，用它替换链路里的 Gemini Flash / GPT Luna 这类判断，成本大概能降 20–60 倍，端到端也快一个数量级。

别想着用它超越 Flash 或 Luna 的生成能力。看置信度，低于 80% 再丢给它们。大头走 Jev，吃不准的再走小生成模型，成本还能再削一截。前提是 online / offline eval 做好。

比如：Model Router、进模型前的预处理、出模型后的检查、自定义打标。

Jev 不聊天，也不会写字。你把一段状态丢给它，再问几个事先定好的问题，它一次答完，每个答案带着概率。

和 BERT 的差别就一句：BERT 要标注再训练，标签一改就重来。固定标签可以继续微调小模型；标签老变的，改 Jev 那句规则当天就能用。

它适合的都是「在几个选项里选一个」：这条该便宜模型还是贵模型，工单算哪类，内容打哪些标签，进大模型前要不要拦、要不要检索，出来之后能不能发、有没有答上问题。

这些现在很多团队会丢给小模型，甚至为了省钱去微调。还是慢，格式一炸就只能重试。改写、压缩、生成回复，留给会写字的 LLM。
