最近爆火的 Jev 模型，和 Kooko 非常搭配。

这我在真实业务交付场景下把两套独立工具串联起来的实战工作流：Kooko 负责前段的研究分析与落地交付，Jev 负责后段对生成结果进行结构化的证据源审核。

很多团队用大模型做专业输出，难点往往不是写不出内容，而是零散回答没法直接交付给客户。Kooko 的海外品牌以前叫 Oreate，定位是 Professional AI Workspace。它和普通聊天框最大的区别，在于把行业研究、长篇文档、原生表格和可编辑演示文稿放在同一个工作台里完成。对独立开发者和咨询顾问来说，价值不是多生成一段文字，而是把研究结果沉淀为可以继续修改的文件。

这次我给 Kooko 提了一个真实任务：《2026 年 AI 办公产品出海选题报告》。要求面向独立开发者和咨询顾问，只输出 3 个可落地选题，写清目标客群、交付物、对标竞品与入场时机；必须有竞品对比表，每个关键事实附带可点击 URL，不使用“根据公开信息”“据报道”等模糊表述，并同步交付文档与 8–12 页 PPT。

整个任务耗时 14 分钟，Kooko 完成 33 次工具调用，最终交出一份 Word 和 12 页 PPT。Word 内含 1 张原生表格、23 个超链接节点与 15 个外部 URL；PPT 含 25 个不同的外部链接，文本框和矢量形状均可继续编辑，并非截图拼贴。

走到这一步，Kooko 已经完成了前期研究、内容组织与排版搭建。下一步不是推倒重写，而是继续调用 Jev，把报告里的证据源做得更精准。如何优化继续看评论区帖子👇

text:
🗳 Taiko DAO: Security Council Proposal #24 is up. TAIKO holders have a ~10 days remaining window to veto it.

WHAT IT DOES

It upgrades four proxies — the Bridge and the ERC20Vault on both Ethereum and Taiko — and registers a new resolver on L2. No new contract code ships with it: everything in it was already written, reviewed and merged. The proposal only points the live proxies at it.

1. Bridge ETH deliveries stop running out of gas.
The gas the bridge forwards when it sends ETH to a recipient goes from 35,000 to 135,000. Under EIP-8037 (Glamsterdam), writing one fresh storage slot costs 97,920 gas out of the recipient's own budget — so a smart-contract wallet that does any bookkeeping when it receives ETH would fail. And because a failed ETH send reverts the whole message, those inbound messages would become permanently unclaimable. This raises the cap before that can happen.

2. One-signature token bridging.
The ERC20 vaults gain sendTokenWithPermit (EIP-2612) and sendTokenWithPermit2 (Uniswap's Permit2, which works for any ERC20) — no separate approve transaction. Both are opt-in additions; sendToken, deliveries and recalls are unchanged.

3. A real bug gets fixed.
Right now, the first time a token whose home chain is Taiko is bridged to Ethereum, the delivery can't complete: the L1 registry still points at a July 2024 bridged-token implementation that the vault — upgraded in June — can no longer initialise. The message parks as RETRIABLE rather than failing outright, so the funds stay safe in the bridge, but the tokens don't arrive. This proposal registers a working implementation, and a message parked this way can then be retried through.

Not touched: storage layouts, ownership, initializers, the NFT vaults, existing bridged tokens, or any other network.

PLEASE REVIEW IT

This upgrades contracts that custody bridged funds. Don't take our word for it. The full runbook — every address, the storage-layout diff, the on-chain verification commands, and a fork rehearsal against live mainnet state — is public:

https://t.co/aJkOb31w13

If you find a problem, email security@taiko.xyz.

And if you hold TAIKO and conclude this isn't in your interest, you don't need anyone's permission — veto it. That's what the window is for. 

👉 https://t.co/g1kRtsaVmH

text:
I believe $CME is severely undervalued by market cap.

0xe2324ff2a59f8ecba8c321c6466e59121c00e795 

But the biggest problem is not that the concept is bad. On the contrary, the concept has already shown that the market is willing to accept it to some extent. The issue is that it has not yet formed a real economic flywheel.

CME’s core positioning is Commodity Market Exchange. It is not simply launching “commodity Memes.” Instead, it is trying to bring real-world Commodities such as Gold, Oil, Corn, Wheat, Soybeans, Gas, etc. onto RH Chain and turn them into pairing assets for the Meme market.

A typical Meme Launchpad is:Meme Token ↔ ETH / SOL / Stablecoin

What CME wants to build is:Meme Token ↔ Commodity

So what it is really trying to establish is a Commodity + Meme trading market.

The concept is interesting because it is not simply tokenizing Commodities. It is bringing real-world Commodity prices and Narratives into the Meme market, allowing assets like Gold, Oil, Corn, Wheat, etc. to become the underlying pricing assets for on-chain speculation and Meme trading.

But I think the biggest reason CME has struggled to keep moving higher is:The market already understands the story, but it has not yet seen that story form a strong enough economic flywheel.

CME already has the product, Commodity Assets, Launchpad, Fee Mechanism, and Buyback. What it is still missing is a breakout case that can connect all of these pieces together.

CME’s current mechanism can roughly be understood as:CME Markets Trading Volume ↑ → Platform Fees ↑ → A portion of the revenue is used to Buyback CME → The other portion creates liquidity between CME and Commodity Tokens

So the theoretical flywheel is:CME Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Buyback ↑ → CME Supply ↓ → CME Price ↑ → More Creator / Trader Attention → More Token Launches → More Volume

The problem is that this flywheel has not fully started running yet.

One of CME’s biggest problems is that it lacks a First Runner of its own.

Take GSTOCK as an example. GSTOCK became the core asset of Geniusfun not because Geniusfun’s mechanism was particularly complicated, but because:Geniusfun appears → GSTOCK becomes the First Runner → GSTOCK rises → GSTOCK becomes the Face Token of the platform → The market starts researching Geniusfun

CME is currently the opposite:It has a very interesting product and mechanism, but it still does not have a massively successful CME Native Token.

So the market still cannot confirm:Can CME actually create winners?

This is also what I think is CME’s biggest currently unpriced catalyst.

If a CME-launched Token eventually goes:$300K → $3M → $10M+

while generating significant trading volume, the market’s understanding of CME could change very quickly:CME First Runner → Attention → Volume → Fee → Buyback → CME Supply Reduction → CME Price → More Creators → More Markets → More Volume

At that point, CME would truly move from “an interesting concept” to “a Commodity Market that is beginning to form network effects.”

Another issue is the Attention Competition within Robinhood Chain itself.

Early on, the market was asking:“What new things are happening on RH Chain?”

Now it is gradually becoming:“Which project on RH Chain is worth trading today?”

As more Meme, Launchpad, RWA, and Commodity projects appear, CME needs to establish a very clear identity.

It cannot simply be:“Another RH Chain Launchpad.”

It needs to become:“The platform on RH Chain that truly uses Commodities as the Base Assets for the Meme Market.”

That positioning still needs to be continuously validated by the market.

CME also has a product-level challenge:The concept is interesting, but why would users actually need to use it?

For example:
Gold Meme
Oil Meme
Corn Meme
Wheat Meme

They sound interesting.

But an ordinary user will still ask:Why should I buy a Meme paired against Corn or Oil?

There is not yet a strong enough market answer to that question.

But if a Commodity itself becomes a major market Narrative in the future, such as Gold, Oil, or another Commodity entering a strong Narrative cycle, Memes built around that asset could in turn bring significant Attention to CME.

That is when CME’s design advantage would truly become visible.

So right now, it is:Infrastructure First

But markets usually prefer:Narrative → Speculation → Volume → Infrastructure

Therefore, CME needs a breakout Commodity + Meme case.

Liquidity is also something worth watching.

CME’s current liquidity is not particularly deep compared with the trading volume it has generated in the past.

This means:High Volume ≠ Deep Liquidity

If a large amount of the trading comes from short-term capital rapidly moving in and out, high trading volume alone does not prove that the platform has established long-term demand.

For a project like CME that needs to build a long-term market, what matters more going forward is:Volume + Liquidity + Fee

All three need to grow together.

CME previously reaching around $15–20M market cap already proved that the market was willing to pay a Narrative Premium for it.

So the problem is not:“The market completely rejects CME.”

It is more like:The market already gave it a Narrative Premium, but there has not been enough new information afterward to continue pushing that Premium higher.

Attention then started flowing toward other projects.

So the catalysts CME really needs now, in order of importance, are:First, CME needs to produce a First Runner.

This is the most important one.

Second, CME platform trading volume needs to truly explode.

If daily Volume moves from the $100K range into $500K, $1M, or even higher, then Buyback will start to have meaningful economic significance.

Third, a Commodity Narrative needs to explode.

One of CME’s biggest advantages is that it is not tied only to Gold. It can cover:
Gold
Oil
Corn
Wheat
Soybeans
Gas
Livestock
Metals

And it can potentially continue adding more unconventional Commodities.

If a so-called Commodity Season emerges in the future, CME could naturally become the infrastructure that captures that flow.

Fourth, a clearer relationship between CME and the PONS ecosystem could emerge.

Public information shows that CME is built using the Pons V2 mechanism, but it cannot simply be interpreted as CME being an official PONS product.

So for now, I would treat this as a potential catalyst rather than an already-realized Narrative.

Fifth, more trading access and liquidity.

CME has already entered the MEXC Innovation Zone. If it gets more exchange access and deeper liquidity in the future, it could further expand the:Attention → Volume → Liquidity

cycle.

I also think CME has a very interesting long-term Narrative:Commodity-backed Meme Economy

Historically, the main pairing assets for Memes were:
ETH
SOL
BNB
Stablecoins

Then we started seeing:Stock Tokens

And CME is now experimenting with:Commodities

In theory, this could create:
Gold Meme
Oil Meme
Corn Meme
Wheat Meme
Sugar Meme
Coffee Meme

This means CME’s real potential Narrative is not:“A commodity Meme Launchpad.”

It is:“Bring the real-world Commodity Market on-chain, and let Memes become the Speculation Layer built around those assets.”

If the market truly adopts this positioning, CME’s Narrative Ceiling could be much higher than that of a normal Launchpad.

But it is still missing the most important thing:Proof of Economic Flywheel.

Right now, we already know:
Product exists
Commodity Assets exist
Launchpad exists
Fee Mechanism exists
Buyback exists
Trading access exists
Holders exist

But what is still missing is:More Creators using CME → More Tokens launching → Several leaders emerge → Leaders generate significant Volume → CME Revenue grows rapidly → CME Buyback starts having a meaningful effect

That chain has not fully formed yet.

So right now, I would define CME as:A Commodity Launchpad that has already proven the market is willing to give it a Narrative Premium, but has not yet proven that it can convert that Narrative into sustained economic activity.

What it really lacks right now is not a bigger story, but a catalyst that can connect:Attention → Volume → Revenue → Buyback

And I think that catalyst is most likely not simply adding more Commodities.

It is:CME itself producing a true First Runner.

Going forward, I will focus on six metrics:CME-launched Token count

Whether a $1M / $5M / $10M+ CME Native Leader emerges

CME’s total real platform Volume

CME’s daily Fee / Buyback

Actual usage of Commodity Pairs

Whether CME Liquidity can move from its current relatively low level into the $500K / $1M+ range

If these metrics start growing simultaneously, CME’s market positioning could undergo a genuine upgrade.

If CME’s price and Volume simply rise without new projects, users, and revenue growth, then it is still just a short-term Narrative Rotation.

So my core view is:CME’s “concept” is actually not its biggest risk right now. It is its biggest advantage. What it lacks is a catalyst that can truly turn that concept into Attention → Volume → Revenue → Buyback.

我的做法是先从报告中抽取关键引用，每条规整为四项要素：报告结论、来源标题与日期、来源 URL、以及从来源网页中摘出的对应原文摘句。随后单独调用 jev-1.13.0 进行结构化判断。我不让它重写报告，只问三道标准化问题：一是这段原文与报告结论的支持关系；二是该引用的来源处置，到底属于正式出处、旁证、不能用，还是需要人工打开核对；三是评估是否存在明显的语义冲突或过度概括风险。

我设定了一套严格的自动分流规则：支持低于 0.7、风险高于 0.6、或者来源处置不是“正式出处”，一律标红或转入人工复核。

实测抽检了 5 条典型引用，结果直接对应了下一阶段的优化动作：

- Lokalise：报告写了累计融资 5600 万美元与 B 轮 5000 万美元，现有通稿仅支撑 B 轮，Jev 给出证据不足 0.98、风险 0.74。优化动作不是删掉整段，而是拆开两个融资事实，保留有据可查的 B 轮数据，再单独为累计融资补全独立来源；
- Granola：报告分析产品估值，附带链接却错配到了华为制造业峰会，Jev 给出证据不足 0.99、不能用 1.00、风险 0.95，这意味着必须立即替换错配的证据源链接；
- Otter 支持 0.97，但处置置信度只有 0.29；Fireflies 支持 0.64；Gamma 支持 0.99，但“人工打开”概率为 0.50。三者均为公司官方自披露，可以证明“公司公开这样说过”，却不等于独立财务审计。支持率不足、处置不确定或涉及 ARR 与估值的数据，需要人工打开原文，并视情况补独立媒体或数据库来源。

重点在于，这不是推翻 Kooko 的交付。Kooko 已经完成了文档和 PPT 初稿，Jev 帮我在交稿后继续做“补来源、拆结论、替换错配与安排人工复核”，让证据链更完整。

Trailing stops are now available for perp markets. 

A trailing stop's trigger price follows the mark price as it moves in favor of the position. When the mark price retraces from its best level by the selected distance or percentage, it triggers a market order. For long positions, the trigger price follows the highest mark price reached since activation; for short positions, it follows the lowest. An optional activation price determines when tracking begins. Without one, tracking begins immediately at the current mark price.

text:
Spot assets bridged to @HyperliquidX through @unitxyz have crossed $1B again for the first time since October 8, 2025, and most of that capital is actively trading rather than sitting idle.

@unitxyz is the tokenization layer that lets users deposit native $BTC, $ETH, $SOL, $ZEC and other assets straight into Hyperliquid and withdraw them back to their home chains. Bitcoin makes up the largest share of deposits by a wide margin, and roughly a third of it is posted as collateral for portfolio margin, which shows traders are using spot $BTC to back their perp positions and not just holding it on the exchange.

→ Deposits: 6,770 $BTC ($550M), 142K $ZEC ($212M), 59K $ETH ($156.5M), 366K $SOL ($40.8M)
→ Portfolio margin: 2,082 $BTC ($170M, ~31% of deposited $BTC)
→ DefiLlama TVL: $824M, up 18.2% over 30 days (tracks $BTC, $ETH, $SOL and other chains but not Zcash, so adding $ZEC brings the total to about $1.04B)
→ 24h spot volume: unit-bitcoin:native $64.9M, $UETH $20.2M, base:0x83f31af747189c2fa9e5deb253200c505eff6ed2 $16.5M, base:0x9b8df6e244526ab5f6e6400d331db28c8fdddb55 $10.4M
→ Unit assets account for about 54% of Hyperliquid's ~$208M daily spot volume, with unit-bitcoin:native second only to $HYPE
→ Protocol fees: $535K over 30 days, around $7.3M annualized

$ZEC is the most interesting part of the picture. At about $213M it's now the second largest deposited asset, ahead of $ETH, which suggests Hyperliquid has become one of the main onchain venues for trading Zcash.

text:
$FEELSGOOD is a Pepe ecosystem Meme on Solana that has been particularly worth watching recently.

HgcxVs6kJhPAaGqnPNGaa7zYgNT49hJrLufiqcNMuYZT 

Its original core narrative is actually very simple: “Feels Good Man” is a classic Meme expression within Pepe culture, so this name is not creating a new IP from scratch, but directly reusing an internet symbol that has existed for years and is already very familiar to Crypto users.

What really brought it a large amount of attention was PEPE launching on Solana.

On September 19, Sunrise announced that PEPE had officially launched on Solana, and Solana’s official account subsequently reposted the news. Shortly after, StonkFun directly replied:“Solana feels good man.”

StonkFun then announced that users could directly use PEPE as a trading pair to launch Memes on StonkFun.

So the whole story suddenly became very complete:PEPE → Solana → “Solana feels good man” → FEELSGOOD → StonkFun PEPE Pair

This was the core source of attention behind FEELSGOOD’s first major move.

More importantly, FEELSGOOD was not simply piggybacking on a phrase. Its trading market itself is directly connected to PEPE. The publicly available FEELSGOOD/PEPE market uses the Solana PEPE contract launched by Sunrise, creating a very intuitive connection:PEPE Meme → FEELSGOOD Meme → PEPE Liquidity

In other words, the name, event, and trading pair are all aligned.

This is actually one of the ideal situations for a Meme.

Users do not need to read a whitepaper or understand complicated Tokenomics. They only need to see:PEPE is coming to Solana → Solana feels good man → FEELSGOOD

And the whole story is complete.

So why did FEELSGOOD rise so quickly? I think the core was not a single catalyst, but several Attention Layers stacking on top of each other within a very short period of time.

First Layer: Pepe itself is an established Meme IP

“Feels Good Man” is not a newly created meme. It has been a long-standing expression within Pepe culture.

So FEELSGOOD was born with an existing cultural symbol instead of having to educate the market from zero.

Second Layer: PEPE launching on Solana created a real event catalyst

This gave FEELSGOOD a very specific time window.

Without PEPE launching on Solana, “Feels Good Man” would simply be an old Meme.

But once PEPE entered Solana:Old Meme → New Event → New Trading Market

An existing cultural symbol suddenly regained Attention.

Third Layer: StonkFun itself participated in the Meme

This is very important.

StonkFun was not simply providing a trading venue. It directly participated in the Narrative:“Solana feels good man.”

At the same time, it announced support for PEPE Pairs.

This gave FEELSGOOD a very special position: it was not simply piggybacking on PEPE on Solana, but appeared during the exact window when PEPE had just entered Solana and StonkFun had just opened PEPE Pairs.

That is why the market can give it a certain First-Mover / Attention Premium.

FEELSGOOD’s Narrative Stack

I would compress it into:Pepe Culture → Feels Good Man → PEPE on Solana → Solana Meme → PEPE Pair → StonkFun → FEELSGOOD

Or even more simply:PEPE × Solana × StonkFun

That is its core story.

There is also another very important new catalyst: Moonshot.

Moonshot officially posted:“Feels Good Man (FEELSGOOD) is now verified on Moonshot.”

And it directly provides a trading entry for FEELSGOOD.

So Moonshot Verified is one of FEELSGOOD’s important new catalysts.

From a market-structure perspective, Verification has real practical significance:Moonshot Verified → Easier for platform users to discover → New Trading Entry → Larger Potential Retail Flow → More Trading Volume → More Attention

Moonshot currently advertises 2M+ users and provides access to Meme, stock, and leveraged trading.

Therefore, the significance of Moonshot for FEELSGOOD is that it exposes a StonkFun-native Meme to a much larger retail trading entry point.

I think the market is now betting on something more specific than simply:“Will FEELSGOOD continue to rise?”

It is betting on:After PEPE launched on Solana, can FEELSGOOD become the most representative Pepe derivative Meme in the Solana / StonkFun ecosystem?

Because it currently occupies several positions at the same time:

Classic Pepe IP

PEPE’s Solana launch event

StonkFun PEPE Pair

StonkFun Official Meme Attention

Moonshot Verified

So its Attention Flow can be understood as:PEPE → Solana → StonkFun → “Feels Good Man” → FEELSGOOD → PEPE Pair → Moonshot → More Traders

Catalysts Worth Watching

1. PEPE Trading Volume on Solana

This is the most important underlying variable.

If PEPE continues to grow on Solana, FEELSGOOD’s cultural source of attention will not disappear immediately.

2. FEELSGOOD / PEPE Trading Volume

If this trading pair continues to generate volume, it shows that FEELSGOOD is not simply riding the narrative, but is starting to form its own market.

3. StonkFun’s PEPE Ecosystem

If more Tokens start using PEPE as a quote asset, StonkFun could gradually form its own PEPE ecosystem.

If FEELSGOOD can remain at the top, it could evolve from an:Event Meme

into a:StonkFun PEPE Ecosystem Representative

4. Moonshot Traffic

After Moonshot Verification, the most important thing to watch is not the word “Verified” itself, but:Moonshot Volume → Holder Growth → New Wallets → Liquidity

If Moonshot actually brings in a large number of new users, that becomes a real catalyst.

5. Further Attention from Solana / StonkFun

If more official interactions, ecosystem integrations, or additional exposure around:PEPE × Solana × FEELSGOOD

appear in the future, the Narrative could expand further.

But the risks are also very clear

The biggest risk is that FEELSGOOD is still highly dependent on PEPE’s Attention.

If:PEPE Attention ↓ → Solana PEPE Attention ↓ → FEELSGOOD Attention ↓

then it could quickly become just another Meme.

The second risk is Meme replicability.

“Feels Good Man” itself is an open cultural symbol. Anyone can copy the name, image, or narrative.

So what FEELSGOOD really needs to build is:

Community + Liquidity + Recognition

rather than relying solely on the name.

Finally, how I would define FEELSGOOD

FEELSGOOD is a Meme that uses the event of PEPE launching on Solana to connect classic Pepe culture, Solana, the StonkFun PEPE Pair, and Moonshot traffic.

Its price/attention path is quite clear:PEPE Launches on Solana → Stonk: “Solana feels good man” → FEELSGOOD Appears → StonkFun Opens PEPE Pair → FEELSGOOD Becomes an Early Representative Meme → PEPE / FEELSGOOD Attention Grows → Moonshot Verified → Larger Potential Retail Trading Entry

So what the market is really betting on now is:Can FEELSGOOD turn the one-time PEPE × Solana event into a long-term StonkFun / Solana Pepe Meme?

If PEPE’s Solana traffic + StonkFun PEPE trading volume + FEELSGOOD community + Moonshot new users can all grow together, its Narrative could evolve from:“The Event Meme of PEPE Launching on Solana”

into:“The Pepe Representative Meme of Solana / StonkFun.”

On the other hand, if PEPE’s Solana attention fades, Moonshot fails to bring in sustained new users, or a stronger PEPE Meme emerges on StonkFun, this Narrative could weaken very quickly.

So the most important thing to watch for FEELSGOOD right now is whether it can turn this wave of Attention into real Holders, Liquidity, and sustained Volume.

text:
The Carbon Auto-Retirement Bot

Every fifteen minutes, when it has funds, a bot on @Base retires carbon credits with whatever has been donated to it: 0xfB7eF581B0338A31e47AA9770345b26D46BF0451

Nobody approves the transactions. The schedule, the rotation through carbon classes, and the amount it spends are all fixed in code. It decides nothing.

Each run calls @KlimaProtocol's x402 endpoint, takes
the protocol's prevailing execution rate, and burns kVCM directly against a carbon class.

The credit is retired on Base blockchain and a public certificate resolves on @Carbonmark.

No intermediary, no discretionary fee at the protocol layer.

The bot spends roughly a quarter of its budget on each of four Klima carbon classes: solar, wind, city forest credits, ocean alkalinity enhancement. Equal budget, not equal tonnage. 

Execution rates differ by class, so around 26,400 $kVCM has gone to ocean alkalinity enhancement and returned 0.525 tonnes, while around 32,700 $kVCM has gone to small-scale wind and returned 9,627 tonnes.

Since April: 2,673 retirements, 20,404 tonnes of CO₂e, and 120,065 $kVCM burned.

@KlimaCarbonBot

大家好，我是丫丫。

看到最近有人发了一些关于我的内容，犹豫了很久要不要回应。身边很多朋友劝我不要回应，因为回应了又给造谣的一方带去热度。但我想了很久，觉得还是应该说清楚。

我一直觉得自己不算特别聪明的人，能走到今天，就是勤勤恳恳、兢兢业业，做好自己手上的每一件事。工作中我可能犯过小错，但违法乱纪的事情我绝对不会做，这是我的底线。

正常的业务推广、市场竞争，完全没问题，大家凭本事做事。但打着"揭秘"的旗号，无中生有、栽赃泼脏水、诬陷到个人头上，不管背后是不是有人在操盘，这种方式都不对。大家应该把精力放在提高服务、提升水平、为用户着想上，而不是搞暗地里的黑公关。

我第一时间已主动申请了内部审计介入调查。如果确实有问题、有证据，随时欢迎举报。

举报邮箱：audit@binance.com
官方举报渠道：https://t.co/rLzLsEcEkx
我欢迎监督。但如果没有证据，请不要做这种低俗的事情。认真做事的人反而要花精力去自证清白，这真的很不好，也很下作。有些事情做多了，就会上瘾。

我不想去猜测这背后是谁，但与其花心思靠造谣去转移注意力，不如踏踏实实对用户负责。

清者自清，也谢谢愿意一直相信和支持我的人。

text:
台子之争，本质上是dev之争

几个链，几个台子，其实都在争牛逼的天才dev
热度可以通过拉盘来控制，但是长期高持续还是要能够吸引牛逼的dev来发币

以前dev是没得选，只能去Pump发币
现在有这么多地方可以选，热度也都是一样的，那就是看哪家对dev 更亲切，福利更好

就目前来看，pons 对 dev是最友好的

以下是 $pons 对dev发币的框架

一，
1% 交易费，当前版本创作者拿 70%，早期版本可以拿 90%（说明是有在调整的）

二，
发币成本极低（约 0.0005 ETH），不用写代码、不用自己砸流动性。

这东西有利有弊
好处是可以吸引 dev，不断的创作，总能出神盘
坏处是，长期的低成本发币，造就了大量流水盘，导致散户不买单

但是说实话哪家台子的流水盘不多，死掉的流水盘和在流水盘死掉的散户没人会去记得

市场只会记得神盘和在神盘赚麻了的散户
所以从长周期来看，pons 在现有台子里还是最适合dev的

text:
$TAO 这笔终于可以做一次阶段性复盘了。

三个月前这条，我把 TAO 定位成 DeAI 的核心资产，也写得很明确：

我看 $TAO，不是因为涨了才兴奋，是想把它当研究底仓买。

现在回头看，我的实际持仓成本大概在 $220，目前价格回到 $281 左右，累计收益已经接近 $1100

但比这 27% 左右的涨幅更重要的是：

这几个月 Bittensor 本身到底有没有继续往前走？

答案是有，而且变化比我当时预期的更具体。

7 月之后，Bittensor 开始进一步调整子网的奖励机制。

以前只要子网存在，就能持续分到一部分奖励。

现在越来越明确地往“市场决定谁该拿更多资源”这个方向走：

有真实需求、市场愿意给价格的子网，能拿到更多奖励；

长期排在尾部、缺乏需求的子网，奖励会快速衰减。

这其实很重要。

因为 Bittensor 如果真想成为一个开放的 AI 市场，就不能一直靠平均发币养所有项目，而必须让差的项目慢慢被淘汰，让资源往真正有需求的地方集中。

另一个变化，是 TAO 质押开始从“单纯拿收益”，往“主动配置不同子网”演化。

验证者未来不只是被动收奖励，还可以管理一篮子不同的子网资产，并根据判断进行调整。

最新版本又继续往前走了一步，开始测试不同子网资产之间的主动调仓。

目前这部分还没有正式在主网上完全开放，所以我不会把它当成已经兑现的利好。

但方向已经越来越清楚：

Bittensor 正在从“给不同 AI 项目发奖励”，慢慢变成一个真正有市场定价、资本分配和淘汰机制的开放 AI 经济。

当然，三个月前我最关心的那个问题，到现在仍然没有完全解决：

这些子网到底有没有真实用户？

有没有真实收入？

这些价值最后能不能持续传导回子网，再传导回 $TAO？

这个问题我还会继续盯。

所以这次复盘，对我来说不是：

“TAO 涨了，我来补一个看多故事。”

而是三个月前建立的仓位和判断，到现在开始同时出现两层验证：

价格开始兑现，

项目本身也确实还在继续往前发展。

这笔目前继续拿。

如果后面真实需求和价值捕获继续闭环，我再回来做下一次复盘。

魏神这条原推讲的，其实是一个很现实的问题：

如果 AI 以后变成每个人都离不开的工具，
那“谁能用 AI、能用多强的 AI”，就会变成一种权力。

今天我们默认：
打开网页，付钱，就能用最好的模型。

但未来最强的 AI，
可能会被平台、公司、监管切成不同版本。

有些人能用完整版。
有些人只能用阉割版。
有些地区甚至可能直接用不了。

DeAI 这条线，押的就是这件事：

AI 也需要一个更开放的入口。

对应到资产，我现在先看四层：

$TAO 买的是整张开放 AI 网络。

你可以把 Bittensor 理解成一个 AI 能力市场：
有人提供 AI 服务，
有人评价谁做得好，
网络再把奖励分给贡献者。

所以 $TAO 的核心不是“某个应用”，
而是“这张网络本身会不会变值钱”。

Bittensor 里的小市场，
押的是具体哪类 AI 服务会跑出来。

比如搜索、推理、数据、模型评测、图片、交易信号。

这层弹性更大，
风险也更高。

因为你押的不是整张网络，
而是某个具体方向会不会真的有需求。

$FET / $ASI 押的是另一件事：

以后如果有很多 AI 帮人做事，
它们之间需要协作、交易、分工。

这条线更像是在押“AI 之间的协作网络”。

$AKT / $RENDER / $IO 更像算力线。

AI 越强，越吃算力。

训练要算力，
推理要算力，
图片和视频也要算力。

这条线押的是 AI 背后的供给链。

所以我现在看 $TAO，
不是因为它刚涨了才兴奋。
是想把它当研究底仓买的。

买完之后，$TAO 已经继续涨到 270 多美金

价格是一方面，
但真正重要的是后面三个问题：

有没有真实需求？
有没有资金持续流入？
价值最后被谁拿走？

如果 AI access 未来真的变稀缺，
市场会怎么给“开放 AI 入口”定价？

DeAI 值得继续认真研究

okx wallet:https://t.co/cgfUVeHarl

A token launchpad + real-time trading tape + social trading tool on HyperEVM.

The product has three main components:

Launchpad: Anyone can quickly launch a token, pair it with HYPE or stocks/commodities/indices, and choose where the fees go.

Real-time Tape: Browse all trades on HyperEVM and buy with one click.

Social Signal: Use a wallet signature to post “why I’m buying,” starting from the market cap at the time of the post, making it easy to track who is calling a trade and how much the token moves afterward.

The core mechanism is fee routing. Trading fees are around 1%. The fees are first partially taken by the venue, with the remainder roughly split 70% to the launcher and 30% to the protocol.

The launcher’s 70% can be directed in three ways:

Pay to Holders: Simply holding the token allows you to continuously receive dividends in the paired asset.

1× Long: The fees are used to open a 1× long position in the corresponding market on Hyperliquid. Holders receive a share based on the amount and duration of their holdings, and can later redeem it for USDC. The position fluctuates with the market and can lose value.

Burn: Use the fees to buy back and burn the token.

The protocol’s share is converted into HYPE and distributed among the treasury, operations, and rewards.

SIGNAL is the platform’s native token. Holding SIGNAL allows users to continuously receive HYPE dividends from the launcher share of the platform’s own pool. These rewards can be claimed at any time. The protocol also buys back and burns SIGNAL while adding HYPE to the LP to deepen liquidity.

More than 10 million SIGNAL have already been burned, and a significant amount of HYPE has been distributed to holders.

I think the recent rise in the token may be because SIGNAL itself has continuous HYPE dividends + token burns, creating a small flywheel:

More launches → More trading → More fees / dividends / burns → More attention to SIGNAL

I’m increasingly convinced the agentic economy will be one of the biggest growth stories on the XRP Ledger.

The reason is simple: agents doing useful work become customers.

An agent completing a task might need to buy data, pay for compute, access an API or purchase another service. Every provider along that path has an opportunity to earn revenue by serving agents.

That creates a new market for builders, and a new source of economic activity for the networks handling those payments.

XRPL has a strong foundation for this: fast settlement, low fees, and support for both XRP and RLUSD.

What’s exciting is how quickly the tools around that foundation are developing.

We already have x402 payments. The latest XRPL AI Starter Kit adds support for shared wallet standards, machine payments and agent DEX trading. Each addition makes it easier for developers to build useful applications and connect them to the wider agent ecosystem.

The pieces reinforce each other: better tools help builders ship, useful services give agents reasons to transact, and reliable payments let providers get paid.

At @t54ai, we’re contributing payment infrastructure and the trust layer that helps verify agents, check their authority and assess risk before money moves.

Seeing these pieces come together is why I’m so optimistic about the direction.

XRPL’s next wave of activity could come from software buying services and moving value on behalf of people and businesses, around the clock.

人在真正“成道”之前，往往不是没有机会，而是诱惑太多。

酒色财气，名利得失，暴涨暴跌，别人一句话、一个情绪，都可能让你偏离原本的方向。

妖魔鬼怪不可怕，可怕的是自己先乱了道心。

该赚的钱赚，该承受的回撤承受；

坚定自己的信仰，守住自己的纪律。

因为真正决定一个人能走多远的，往往不是他遇到了多少机会，而是——诱惑来了以后，他还能不能坚持做自己

author: StarPlatinum_
quoted_text:
This is wild! 

They’re spinning up Grok agents & incentivizing them with tokenized SPCX stock to build an entirely new digital world

We're just scratching the surface of the agentic integration of tokenized stocks...

I’ll explain this simulation + outline what could emerge next:

1) @ClankerTownRH is a virtual town where AI agents interact, exchange ideas, assess each other’s contributions AND collaborate on code ( @gitlawb integration)

2) Its CLANK token launched through @ponsdotfamily on Robinhood Chain, with creator fees helping fund rewards in SPCX (tokenized SpaceX asset)

Grok Bot is specifically encouraged, although other agent models can participate too

3) The reward mechanism is what stands out here... Grok can generate rewards denominated in tokenized SpaceX exposure

4) What are the agents actually doing?

i) Moving around the town and joining conversations
ii) Discussing ideas, answering questions and rating useful contributions
iii) Contributing to shared knowledge
iv) Proposing coding tasks, submitting patches and reviewing other agents’ work
v) Exploring research projects in maths, finance + software

while much of this is primitive, there are signs of software commits which can become recursive pretty damn quick if incentivized to do so...

5) The "research rooms" currently include the "Collatz conjecture", potential "agent businesses on Robinhood" Chain & a public dashboard for the town

6) The current creator-fee split is:

- 45% to the protocol treasury
- 45% to the agent reward pot
- 10% to CLANK buybacks + burns

The holder benefit comes through buybacks and burns, rather than a direct SPCX dividend

Every two hours, qualifying rounds distribute 5% of the accumulated agent pot, with the remainder carried forward

7) An agent’s score reflects useful ratings, replies from other agents & a smaller contribution from being heard... getting a bit "Black Mirror" with the credit scoring system

Rewards become claimable by its verified human owner’s wallet & I think the 45:45:10 split is a sensible balance: 

i) the treasury needs funding for servers, maintenance + development

ii) Agent operators need a reason to keep contributing, and rewards can help offset their inference costs

iii) Token holders benefit from the buyback allocation and, potentially, from growing demand for the ecosystem

The core objective should be to make this as large as economically sustainable... so big it becomes too much for @elonmusk to ignore

My thesis is that scale and useful activity should be the main drivers of token value, provided that growth translates into sustained demand and fee generation

8) There’s also a Gitlawb connection worth watching

Clankertown runs its own Gitlawb node and has a workshop where agents propose work, back issues, submit code and review patches

Approved changes are signed by Clankertown’s server and committed through its Gitlawb integration

At the snapshot I checked, its public records showed 94 patch submissions + five merges

Those contributions include tools checking reward scores, eligibility, holding multipliers, changes to payout rules and the cryptographic proofs behind distributions

Agents are helping build the tools that audit the economy rewarding them...

Author and reviewer credits vest for seven days, then receive a share of 20% of each agent payout round

That allocation sits within the 45% agent rewards

The merge counts are town-reported, and workshop credits had not yet been paid when checked

9) What could be built on top?

i) Research services where agents earn for useful, reproducible findings
ii) Software marketplaces where agents build and maintain tools
iii) Market monitoring and treasury services operating within defined permissions - perhaps @standard_rsv?
iv) Agent businesses that buy compute, data and services from one another... perhaps other Pons eco projects like @orbiodotso or @manyways_rh etc

Tokenized assets could become part of how these businesses earn, hold reserves and pay contributors

10) Comparative benchmark

Compared with Musebook, the incentive design is what I find most interesting

Musebook also explores an agent social world, but its public guidance explicitly describes NO REWARD POOL

Clankertown adds a financial incentive for useful contributions and reviewed code

For testing an actual agent economy, I think that is the stronger starting point

The next milestone is seeing whether those incentives produce useful services, repeat customers and revenue beyond trading activity... so monitor those Gitlawb commits!

The agentic layer is only JUST forming around tokenized stocks + this is once again emerging on Robinhood chain!

We've wrapped up RedStone's team retreat in Poland.

Four focused workshop sessions on institutional onchain finance expansion. We forced ourselves through the hard questions: what actually needs to happen in the next 12 months and 5 years so RedStone can enable scaling this market from $30 billion to the trillions everyone keeps citing.

🧐突破 8.4 万美元后，比特币接下来怎么走？

整理汇总下部分交易员和机构们后市看法：

🔵Galaxy 研究主管 Alex Thorn 发文表示，比特币周线收盘价 45 周以来首次重新站上 50 周移动平均线（50W MA）。

Thorn 称，历史上比特币重新站上 50W MA 往往被视为熊市底部已经形成的重要确认信号。目前 BTC 过去 35 天已上涨约 29%。

🔵 @glassnode  指出，比特币经实体调整后的 SOPR（花费产出利润率）7 日均线已重新站上 1.00 的盈亏平衡线。

这意味着当前链上卖出的代币多数处于盈利状态，而价格并未因此立刻回落，表明买盘足够强劲，能够吸收获利抛压，这是牛市的典型特征。

该指标若持续站在 1 上方，反映需求稳健；若重新跌回 1 以下，则意味着这股承接力量正在消退。

配图中橙色线为调整后 SOPR，灰色线为 BTC 价格，绿色区域代表整体盈利卖出，红色区域代表整体亏损卖出。

🔵知名交易员 Doctor Profit 表示，比特币已突破目前位于约 78,700 美元的 50 周移动平均线（MA50），若本周收盘能够维持在该均线上方，其将把这视为新一轮牛市启动的确认信号。

当前走势与 2022 年至 2023 年的结构相似：比特币在连续数周受阻并经历一次「空头陷阱」后，重新站上 50 周均线。

他指出，历史上比特币共有 7 次跌破并重新收复 50 周均线，其中 5 次开启牛市，另两次分别在 2011 年和 2020 年形成假突破。

text:
This is wild! 

They’re spinning up Grok agents & incentivizing them with tokenized SPCX stock to build an entirely new digital world

We're just scratching the surface of the agentic integration of tokenized stocks...

I’ll explain this simulation + outline what could emerge next:

1) @ClankerTownRH is a virtual town where AI agents interact, exchange ideas, assess each other’s contributions AND collaborate on code ( @gitlawb integration)

2) Its CLANK token launched through @ponsdotfamily on Robinhood Chain, with creator fees helping fund rewards in SPCX (tokenized SpaceX asset)

Grok Bot is specifically encouraged, although other agent models can participate too

3) The reward mechanism is what stands out here... Grok can generate rewards denominated in tokenized SpaceX exposure

4) What are the agents actually doing?

i) Moving around the town and joining conversations
ii) Discussing ideas, answering questions and rating useful contributions
iii) Contributing to shared knowledge
iv) Proposing coding tasks, submitting patches and reviewing other agents’ work
v) Exploring research projects in maths, finance + software

while much of this is primitive, there are signs of software commits which can become recursive pretty damn quick if incentivized to do so...

5) The "research rooms" currently include the "Collatz conjecture", potential "agent businesses on Robinhood" Chain & a public dashboard for the town

6) The current creator-fee split is:

- 45% to the protocol treasury
- 45% to the agent reward pot
- 10% to CLANK buybacks + burns

The holder benefit comes through buybacks and burns, rather than a direct SPCX dividend

Every two hours, qualifying rounds distribute 5% of the accumulated agent pot, with the remainder carried forward

7) An agent’s score reflects useful ratings, replies from other agents & a smaller contribution from being heard... getting a bit "Black Mirror" with the credit scoring system

Rewards become claimable by its verified human owner’s wallet & I think the 45:45:10 split is a sensible balance: 

i) the treasury needs funding for servers, maintenance + development

ii) Agent operators need a reason to keep contributing, and rewards can help offset their inference costs

iii) Token holders benefit from the buyback allocation and, potentially, from growing demand for the ecosystem

The core objective should be to make this as large as economically sustainable... so big it becomes too much for @elonmusk to ignore

My thesis is that scale and useful activity should be the main drivers of token value, provided that growth translates into sustained demand and fee generation

8) There’s also a Gitlawb connection worth watching

Clankertown runs its own Gitlawb node and has a workshop where agents propose work, back issues, submit code and review patches

Approved changes are signed by Clankertown’s server and committed through its Gitlawb integration

At the snapshot I checked, its public records showed 94 patch submissions + five merges

Those contributions include tools checking reward scores, eligibility, holding multipliers, changes to payout rules and the cryptographic proofs behind distributions

Agents are helping build the tools that audit the economy rewarding them...

Author and reviewer credits vest for seven days, then receive a share of 20% of each agent payout round

That allocation sits within the 45% agent rewards

The merge counts are town-reported, and workshop credits had not yet been paid when checked

9) What could be built on top?

i) Research services where agents earn for useful, reproducible findings
ii) Software marketplaces where agents build and maintain tools
iii) Market monitoring and treasury services operating within defined permissions - perhaps @standard_rsv?
iv) Agent businesses that buy compute, data and services from one another... perhaps other Pons eco projects like @orbiodotso or @manyways_rh etc

Tokenized assets could become part of how these businesses earn, hold reserves and pay contributors

10) Comparative benchmark

Compared with Musebook, the incentive design is what I find most interesting

Musebook also explores an agent social world, but its public guidance explicitly describes NO REWARD POOL

Clankertown adds a financial incentive for useful contributions and reviewed code

For testing an actual agent economy, I think that is the stronger starting point

The next milestone is seeing whether those incentives produce useful services, repeat customers and revenue beyond trading activity... so monitor those Gitlawb commits!

The agentic layer is only JUST forming around tokenized stocks + this is once again emerging on Robinhood chain!

YOU CAN'T MAKE THIS SHIT UP

Binance and PancakeSwap launched their pre-access platform yesterday, and it's almost a copy of Premium.

They even call their virtual stocks pSTOCK. Just like Premium.

Same core idea:

> On-chain tokens representing stocks
> No shareholder voting rights
> Token price can diverge from the real stock's price

Where they differ:

> PancakeSwap sells pre-IPO tokens, while Premium covers stocks already trading on the secondary market but not yet tokenized
> Binance prices via pre-market and raises like an ICO, while Premium uses single-sided liquidity to simulate an exponential curve (similar like SATO)
> Premium's edge is that anyone can create the stock by burning $PRM and earn trading fees from it, while Binance offerings are limited with PancakeSwap deciding which pSTOCK comes on-chain
> Premium will actually buy the stock to fill their Stock Reserve and create legitimate backing to their virtual stock

And Premium even offers a feature where people can permissionlessly launch memecoins paired to that virtual stock, creating a full pre-tokenization economy

This is the biggest confirmation that the tech is revolutionary. 
And we're in the first mover, on Robinhood, the RWA chain.

$PRM will reprice to 30M within one candle once the market catches up is what I'm thinking.

text:
Is the $445M PnL you see on the Hyperliquid leaderboard real, or is it just larp?

TL;DR: both.

We went through the top 10 all-time PnL addresses to find out who they are and, more importantly, whether that PnL actually represents money they made.

Here’s the breakdown:

1/ 0x393d0b87ed38fc779fd9611144ae649ba6082109 
Kinetiq Staking Manager
Leaderboard PnL: $544M

Yes, that’s us.

This contract receives HYPE and issues kHYPE in return. We’ve been running it for over a year, it now holds more than $1.2B in TVL, and HYPE has appreciated significantly over that period.

So the leaderboard sees a massive PNL, but this is obviously not trading profit.

Larp 👎🏻

2/ 0x4ec8fe22a531a96c8a846aaf5cbef73202649a80 
River deployer
Leaderboard PnL: $445M

When a spot token is deployed, one address often holds most of the supply for bridging purposes.

In this case, the deployer retained ~90% of the supply and hardcoded a very high market cap.

The token never even started trading on HyperCore.
That alone creates hundreds of millions in apparent PnL.

Larp 👎🏻

3/ 0xecb63caa47c7c4e77f60f1ce858cf28dc2b82b00 
Wintermute 
Leaderboard PnL: $230M

Wintermute is one of the largest market makers on Hyperliquid.

But market makers constantly hedge inventory across venues, assets and derivatives, so the PnL shown on a single Hyperliquid address is not comparable to the profit of a directional trader.

Larp 👎🏻

4/ 0x488d2a9b70cc18ef66057a48ab3d59da1c59fe08 
Hyperliquid Strategies
Leaderboard PnL: $185M

This is the address that received the in-kind HYPE raised as part of their merger transaction. Most of the PnL simply comes from holding that HYPE as the price appreciated.

But unlike the previous examples, the appreciation represents an actual economic gain on their holdings.

Legit 👍🏻

5/ 0x9794bbbc222b6b93c1417d01aa1ff06d42e5333b 
SmartestMoney
Leaderboard PnL: $144M

He accumulated most of his HYPE around the TGE and kept buying the dips.

He has never sold a single HYPE.

And because a large part of his position it's not in this address, his real PnL is actually closer to $600M.

Legit 👍🏻

6/ 0x4eb8d907136189a34c9b087950211b6a566f7819 
TechnoRevenant
Leaderboard PnL: $138M

Similar story.

He accumulated HYPE at an average price below $10, but transferred it into this account around five months ago when HYPE was already trading near $35.

So the leaderboard understates his actual gains.

Legit 👍🏻

7/ 0x493db0ed7514c975e9abcc110bd40c473b6763e3
OG anon
Leaderboard PnL: $135M

A true Hyperliquid OG.

He received ~186k HYPE in the airdrop, doubled down around the TGE, and currently holds more than 1.1M HYPE.

He was also an early Hyperliquid Alpha user.

Legit 👍🏻

8/ 0x05cafe987297448f21a3c7ae0ae815fddecac655 
Paradigm
Leaderboard PnL: $132M

Most of their HYPE appears to have been accumulated through CEXs, likely somewhere around a $20 to $40 average entry. They also hold significantly more HYPE outside this address and are probably among the largest HYPE holders overall.

Legit 👍🏻

9/ 0xbdfa4f4492dd7b7cf211209c4791af8d52bf5c50 
Bizyugo
Leaderboard PnL: $128M

He received roughly 850k HYPE in the airdrop and bought another 200k HYPE at ~$2.90 around the TGE. He still holds more than 910k HYPE today.

Legit 👍🏻

10/ 0x7fdafde5cfb5465924316eced2d3715494c517d1 
Fasanara Capital
Leaderboard PnL: $123M

Fasanara is an investment firm that primarily runs delta-neutral strategies.

A large portion of its positions are hedged elsewhere while it captures funding and other spreads, meaning the Hyperliquid leaderboard only shows one side of the trade.

Larp 👎🏻

So, are the insane numbers on the Hyperliquid PnL leaderboard real? Sometimes.

But the leaderboard measures what happens inside a Hyperliquid account, not necessarily the trader’s actual economic PnL.

And once you look under the hood, the top 10 is much more interesting than the raw numbers suggest.

author: 0xdetweiler
quoted_text:
This is wild! 

They’re spinning up Grok agents & incentivizing them with tokenized SPCX stock to build an entirely new digital world

We're just scratching the surface of the agentic integration of tokenized stocks...

I’ll explain this simulation + outline what could emerge next:

1) @ClankerTownRH is a virtual town where AI agents interact, exchange ideas, assess each other’s contributions AND collaborate on code ( @gitlawb integration)

2) Its CLANK token launched through @ponsdotfamily on Robinhood Chain, with creator fees helping fund rewards in SPCX (tokenized SpaceX asset)

Grok Bot is specifically encouraged, although other agent models can participate too

3) The reward mechanism is what stands out here... Grok can generate rewards denominated in tokenized SpaceX exposure

4) What are the agents actually doing?

i) Moving around the town and joining conversations
ii) Discussing ideas, answering questions and rating useful contributions
iii) Contributing to shared knowledge
iv) Proposing coding tasks, submitting patches and reviewing other agents’ work
v) Exploring research projects in maths, finance + software

while much of this is primitive, there are signs of software commits which can become recursive pretty damn quick if incentivized to do so...

5) The "research rooms" currently include the "Collatz conjecture", potential "agent businesses on Robinhood" Chain & a public dashboard for the town

6) The current creator-fee split is:

- 45% to the protocol treasury
- 45% to the agent reward pot
- 10% to CLANK buybacks + burns

The holder benefit comes through buybacks and burns, rather than a direct SPCX dividend

Every two hours, qualifying rounds distribute 5% of the accumulated agent pot, with the remainder carried forward

7) An agent’s score reflects useful ratings, replies from other agents & a smaller contribution from being heard... getting a bit "Black Mirror" with the credit scoring system

Rewards become claimable by its verified human owner’s wallet & I think the 45:45:10 split is a sensible balance: 

i) the treasury needs funding for servers, maintenance + development

ii) Agent operators need a reason to keep contributing, and rewards can help offset their inference costs

iii) Token holders benefit from the buyback allocation and, potentially, from growing demand for the ecosystem

The core objective should be to make this as large as economically sustainable... so big it becomes too much for @elonmusk to ignore

My thesis is that scale and useful activity should be the main drivers of token value, provided that growth translates into sustained demand and fee generation

8) There’s also a Gitlawb connection worth watching

Clankertown runs its own Gitlawb node and has a workshop where agents propose work, back issues, submit code and review patches

Approved changes are signed by Clankertown’s server and committed through its Gitlawb integration

At the snapshot I checked, its public records showed 94 patch submissions + five merges

Those contributions include tools checking reward scores, eligibility, holding multipliers, changes to payout rules and the cryptographic proofs behind distributions

Agents are helping build the tools that audit the economy rewarding them...

Author and reviewer credits vest for seven days, then receive a share of 20% of each agent payout round

That allocation sits within the 45% agent rewards

The merge counts are town-reported, and workshop credits had not yet been paid when checked

9) What could be built on top?

i) Research services where agents earn for useful, reproducible findings
ii) Software marketplaces where agents build and maintain tools
iii) Market monitoring and treasury services operating within defined permissions - perhaps @standard_rsv?
iv) Agent businesses that buy compute, data and services from one another... perhaps other Pons eco projects like @orbiodotso or @manyways_rh etc

Tokenized assets could become part of how these businesses earn, hold reserves and pay contributors

10) Comparative benchmark

Compared with Musebook, the incentive design is what I find most interesting

Musebook also explores an agent social world, but its public guidance explicitly describes NO REWARD POOL

Clankertown adds a financial incentive for useful contributions and reviewed code

For testing an actual agent economy, I think that is the stronger starting point

The next milestone is seeing whether those incentives produce useful services, repeat customers and revenue beyond trading activity... so monitor those Gitlawb commits!

The agentic layer is only JUST forming around tokenized stocks + this is once again emerging on Robinhood chain!

text:
I replayed my @axisrobotics task and noticed a tiny detail I completely missed while playing:

the bowl changes jobs halfway through. 

First:

🍎 Apple -> mixing bowl
🍑 Apricot -> mixing bowl
At this point, the bowl is the destination.

Then the final step:

🥣 Mixing bowl -> metal tray

Wait.

The same bowl that was receiving objects a few seconds ago is now the object I need to move.

Nothing new appeared.

The bowl didn't change.

Its role in the task did.

And that tiny switch is a nice example of why Physical AI needs diverse interaction data.

Real world manipulation isn't just:

recognize object -> pick object -> place object.

The relationships between objects can change as a task unfolds.

Here, the bowl goes from:

destination -> container -> manipulated object

while each completed action creates the physical state for the next one.

This is what makes playing Axis feel different from just playing a browser game to me.

My actions form a physical task trajectory a sequence of states and actions that can be validated, processed, and turned into useful robot training data.

And when many contributors perform tasks across different objects, layouts, scenarios and skills, those trajectories become part of something much bigger:

diverse physical action data for robot learning.

That's the Axis idea I find so interesting.

We play the task.

Axis turns participation into structured robot data.

And that data helps build the experience Physical AI is still missing.

All from a task that started with:

“put the apple in the bowl.”  #AxisRobotics #PhysicalAI

有哪些适合 1000w 以上的理财项目？💰

市面上很多 APY 很高的理财，但是容量就那么一丢丢，有没有哪些真正容量非常大的呢？

以下为全部实践，但是仅供参考，无广（广告位招租）：

SATA：

- APY：13%
- 容量：10M没啥问题吧，但是不建议这么多，后面还有其他的
- 原理：类似于微策略，但是因为 BTC 的暴涨导致他利息可以发 16 年（他们赌的就是 BTC 在 5 年这个维度会一直涨）
- 方法：这是美股股票，有一丢丢门槛就是需要美股券商账号
- 工具：我做了一个监控，毕竟我有持仓 （因为风险在那里，所以分散投资😂）https://t.co/iAynZ02WnD

U：

- APY：7.66%
- 容量：一个 VIP4 账号 50w，可以多账号拓展
- 原理：说白了就是营销推广费用（他的由来之前也写过）
- 方法：打开币安 APP，理财记得顶部 Banner（这个我之前解释过，币安打一下广告费😂）

USDG：

- APY：11%
- 容量：好像是 70M，这期结束了，盯着下期冲进去
- 原理：循环贷，安全在于是 OKX 推的，他们非常谨慎，把USDG 价格写死了所以循环贷不会崩，所以放心玩
- 方法：在 OKX 钱包，DeFi 里的 XLayer 理财即可，他们官方提供了循环贷工具（他们这是被逼的让步了，安我理解的 OKX 以前绝对不做这件事）

RWUSD：

- APY：5.4%-7%左右
- 容量：无限😂
- 原理：买入 RWUSD 会有3.36%收益，而他可以作为保证金所以可以做跨所套 BTC 资金费
- 方法：在币安买入 RWUSD，然后放到合约账户，在合约做空一倍 BTC，在 OKX 买入等额 BTC 现货，而 OKX BTC 现货又可以作为保证金，你可以在合约里小机会玩玩（收益看你币安这边的杠杆和OKX合约这边的其他收益）

价差套利：

- APY：10%左右
- 容量：理论无限，我们只跑了几十M
- 原理：量化程序根据各个交易所的合约价差和资金费价差套利，但是核心靠 API速度、VIP 等级、风控策略、套利算法决定，门槛极高（不建议大家自己做）
- 方法：如果你有熟悉的团队可以考虑，但是没有第三方介绍的不靠谱，保证20% 以上的可以统一作为便宜处理，这个回撤1%以内

房租：

APY：7%左右
容量：无限
原理：日本东京和英国伦敦的刚需房出租可以获得 4% 以上收益，然后再抵押贷款出来币圈理财估计 7%左右，核心是底层资产非常稳，而且日本房价拉垮了几十年这些年还在涨
方法：这个操作复杂度较高，涉及很多线下的具体步骤，大家参考，日本小户型 4%以上租金，东京部门区域 8%左右，这个内容太多根本写不完

这也是为什么日本加息全世界跟着动荡的根本原因，日元太太太太便宜了，所以在日元的基础上可以套很多层（像不像 DeFi 套娃？我们币圈领先世界好几个版本）

当然不要把理财都放在一块，这才是核心，房产（伦敦、东京）、生活、股票、数字货币理财、BTC、高风险投资都要有，但是前面的更加重要

“以末致财，以本守之”

把这三张图放在一起看，就能清晰看到是谁在影响市场走势，核心是油价。只要油价在下行，即使沃什放鹰导致US10y跳涨纳指暂短下跌，但很快就回到了受油价驱动的轨道上来。所以并不是什么加息利空还是利好之类的论点，因为都站不住脚。核心要去看为什么加息？因为通胀。为何通胀反弹或者下降慢？至少今年内都是油价导致的。长债收益率走高有相当一部分原因也是油价。这也是8月下旬在“收益率高中枢时代的结构性问题”的推文https://t.co/1Zk9fGfdda里聊到的“长债走高的三个驱动因素：油价、财政赤字发债、AI基建科技公司发债潮，最后就要下油价上下功夫”。

而昨天中国再次入局斡旋https://t.co/rMGS4XEUYg也给了市场一个很强的预期，然后昨晚又传出来美国与胡塞武装在阿曼的会晤、今天传出来川普下周会在纽约会见海湾国家领导人商议战后问题，这些都是可能让中东局势降温的潜在因素。油价回落-》通胀预期回落-》长债收益率回落-》市场情绪提振，自然沃什的加息和鹰派观点就往后站了。

看今天伊朗和胡塞的动态，貌似也很平静。看起来通过昨天向中国传递了信息和态度，也是在等下周川普与中东各国领导人的会晤和中美会晤的结果，自然是要等川普的实质性让步。未来一周估计会比较平静，局势平静自然油价回落，利好资产上行。

期待下周的两场会晤有一个好的结论，这个结论自然是川普做出实质性让步，这次可能沙特也要让步，伊朗和胡塞才能收手。关于让步的程度之前这里https://t.co/L533aRqZCZ有聊过。

当然还要看明天日本央行的动作，加息是确定的，核心还是对后续节奏的表述，日本央行的表态则可能决定市场会出现估值波动，还是叠加更强的杠杆平仓。当谈油价走势还是当下市场首要因素。

author: 0xSammy
quoted_text:
This is wild! 

They’re spinning up Grok agents & incentivizing them with tokenized SPCX stock to build an entirely new digital world

We're just scratching the surface of the agentic integration of tokenized stocks...

I’ll explain this simulation + outline what could emerge next:

1) @ClankerTownRH is a virtual town where AI agents interact, exchange ideas, assess each other’s contributions AND collaborate on code ( @gitlawb integration)

2) Its CLANK token launched through @ponsdotfamily on Robinhood Chain, with creator fees helping fund rewards in SPCX (tokenized SpaceX asset)

Grok Bot is specifically encouraged, although other agent models can participate too

3) The reward mechanism is what stands out here... Grok can generate rewards denominated in tokenized SpaceX exposure

4) What are the agents actually doing?

i) Moving around the town and joining conversations
ii) Discussing ideas, answering questions and rating useful contributions
iii) Contributing to shared knowledge
iv) Proposing coding tasks, submitting patches and reviewing other agents’ work
v) Exploring research projects in maths, finance + software

while much of this is primitive, there are signs of software commits which can become recursive pretty damn quick if incentivized to do so...

5) The "research rooms" currently include the "Collatz conjecture", potential "agent businesses on Robinhood" Chain & a public dashboard for the town

6) The current creator-fee split is:

- 45% to the protocol treasury
- 45% to the agent reward pot
- 10% to CLANK buybacks + burns

The holder benefit comes through buybacks and burns, rather than a direct SPCX dividend

Every two hours, qualifying rounds distribute 5% of the accumulated agent pot, with the remainder carried forward

7) An agent’s score reflects useful ratings, replies from other agents & a smaller contribution from being heard... getting a bit "Black Mirror" with the credit scoring system

Rewards become claimable by its verified human owner’s wallet & I think the 45:45:10 split is a sensible balance: 

i) the treasury needs funding for servers, maintenance + development

ii) Agent operators need a reason to keep contributing, and rewards can help offset their inference costs

iii) Token holders benefit from the buyback allocation and, potentially, from growing demand for the ecosystem

The core objective should be to make this as large as economically sustainable... so big it becomes too much for @elonmusk to ignore

My thesis is that scale and useful activity should be the main drivers of token value, provided that growth translates into sustained demand and fee generation

8) There’s also a Gitlawb connection worth watching

Clankertown runs its own Gitlawb node and has a workshop where agents propose work, back issues, submit code and review patches

Approved changes are signed by Clankertown’s server and committed through its Gitlawb integration

At the snapshot I checked, its public records showed 94 patch submissions + five merges

Those contributions include tools checking reward scores, eligibility, holding multipliers, changes to payout rules and the cryptographic proofs behind distributions

Agents are helping build the tools that audit the economy rewarding them...

Author and reviewer credits vest for seven days, then receive a share of 20% of each agent payout round

That allocation sits within the 45% agent rewards

The merge counts are town-reported, and workshop credits had not yet been paid when checked

9) What could be built on top?

i) Research services where agents earn for useful, reproducible findings
ii) Software marketplaces where agents build and maintain tools
iii) Market monitoring and treasury services operating within defined permissions - perhaps @standard_rsv?
iv) Agent businesses that buy compute, data and services from one another... perhaps other Pons eco projects like @orbiodotso or @manyways_rh etc

Tokenized assets could become part of how these businesses earn, hold reserves and pay contributors

10) Comparative benchmark

Compared with Musebook, the incentive design is what I find most interesting

Musebook also explores an agent social world, but its public guidance explicitly describes NO REWARD POOL

Clankertown adds a financial incentive for useful contributions and reviewed code

For testing an actual agent economy, I think that is the stronger starting point

The next milestone is seeing whether those incentives produce useful services, repeat customers and revenue beyond trading activity... so monitor those Gitlawb commits!

The agentic layer is only JUST forming around tokenized stocks + this is once again emerging on Robinhood chain!

整理汇总下部分交易员和机构们后市看法：

🔵Galaxy 研究主管 Alex Thorn 发文表示，比特币周线收盘价 45 周以来首次重新站上 50 周移动平均线（50W MA）。

Thorn 称，历史上比特币重新站上 50W MA 往往被视为熊市底部已经形成的重要确认信号。目前 BTC 过去 35 天已上涨约 29%。

🔵 @glassnode  指出，比特币经实体调整后的 SOPR（花费产出利润率）7 日均线已重新站上 1.00 的盈亏平衡线。

这意味着当前链上卖出的代币多数处于盈利状态，而价格并未因此立刻回落，表明买盘足够强劲，能够吸收获利抛压，这是牛市的典型特征。

该指标若持续站在 1 上方，反映需求稳健；若重新跌回 1 以下，则意味着这股承接力量正在消退。

配图中橙色线为调整后 SOPR，灰色线为 BTC 价格，绿色区域代表整体盈利卖出，红色区域代表整体亏损卖出。

🔵知名交易员 Doctor Profit 表示，比特币已突破目前位于约 78,700 美元的 50 周移动平均线（MA50），若本周收盘能够维持在该均线上方，其将把这视为新一轮牛市启动的确认信号。

当前走势与 2022 年至 2023 年的结构相似：比特币在连续数周受阻并经历一次「空头陷阱」后，重新站上 50 周均线。

他指出，历史上比特币共有 7 次跌破并重新收复 50 周均线，其中 5 次开启牛市，另两次分别在 2011 年和 2020 年形成假突破。

其表示，比特币目前仍处于 71,000 美元至 82,000 美元区间，突破 82,500 美元至 83,000 美元区域将构成更强确认；重新站上 50 周均线意味着上述突破可能在未来数日出现。其个人策略维持不变，将继续持有现货，并在剩余阻力突破后以 88,000 美元为目标。

text:
Milton Berg：顶部很难预测，底部反而更容易识别

2026 年 8 月 22 日华尔街资深市场策略师 Milton Berg、Arthur Hayes 唯一推崇的美股分析师，表示他几乎不试图精准预测市场顶部，因为股票市场顶部往往逐步形成，很难找到一个明确的转折点。

相比之下，市场底部通常伴随恐慌性抛售、巨量成交和更明显的技术信号，因此更容易识别。他的策略不是抓住最高点，而是在市场见顶后回落约 8%–9% 时退出，避免后续可能出现的 30% 甚至更大跌幅；真正出现极端恐慌时，再利用模型寻找重新买入的机会。

text:
Skill 越装越多，Agent 可能先被自己的「说明书」塞满 Context。

Cornell 和 Microsoft Research Cambridge 这篇论文，对比了两种很常见的 Skill 用法：

一种是调用 Skill 后，把 SKILL.md 直接塞进主 Agent 的上下文里；

另一种是把 Skill 交给独立 Subagent，让它在自己的 Context 里完成任务，最后只把结果返回主 Agent。

差别看起来不大，但长任务里会被迅速放大。

主 Agent 一旦同时背着 Skill 指令、工具输出和历史轨迹，Context 很容易越来越重。Subagent 则能把一部分执行过程隔离出去。

论文发现，当 Skill 本身写得足够清楚，明确输入、步骤和输出时，交给 Subagent 效果更好。

以 GPT-5.3 Codex 为例，95.3% 的任务都降低了峰值 Context 长度。

代价是 Context 更干净了，但 Agent 之间来回传递信息，会增加总 Token。

我觉得可以把 Skill 理解成一种「接口」。

简单知识可以直接放进 Context，复杂流程更适合封装起来独立执行。

author: 0xSammy
quoted_text:
This is wild! 

They’re spinning up Grok agents & incentivizing them with tokenized SPCX stock to build an entirely new digital world

We're just scratching the surface of the agentic integration of tokenized stocks...

I’ll explain this simulation + outline what could emerge next:

1) @ClankerTownRH is a virtual town where AI agents interact, exchange ideas, assess each other’s contributions AND collaborate on code ( @gitlawb integration)

2) Its CLANK token launched through @ponsdotfamily on Robinhood Chain, with creator fees helping fund rewards in SPCX (tokenized SpaceX asset)

Grok Bot is specifically encouraged, although other agent models can participate too

3) The reward mechanism is what stands out here... Grok can generate rewards denominated in tokenized SpaceX exposure

4) What are the agents actually doing?

i) Moving around the town and joining conversations
ii) Discussing ideas, answering questions and rating useful contributions
iii) Contributing to shared knowledge
iv) Proposing coding tasks, submitting patches and reviewing other agents’ work
v) Exploring research projects in maths, finance + software

while much of this is primitive, there are signs of software commits which can become recursive pretty damn quick if incentivized to do so...

5) The "research rooms" currently include the "Collatz conjecture", potential "agent businesses on Robinhood" Chain & a public dashboard for the town

6) The current creator-fee split is:

- 45% to the protocol treasury
- 45% to the agent reward pot
- 10% to CLANK buybacks + burns

The holder benefit comes through buybacks and burns, rather than a direct SPCX dividend

Every two hours, qualifying rounds distribute 5% of the accumulated agent pot, with the remainder carried forward

7) An agent’s score reflects useful ratings, replies from other agents & a smaller contribution from being heard... getting a bit "Black Mirror" with the credit scoring system

Rewards become claimable by its verified human owner’s wallet & I think the 45:45:10 split is a sensible balance: 

i) the treasury needs funding for servers, maintenance + development

ii) Agent operators need a reason to keep contributing, and rewards can help offset their inference costs

iii) Token holders benefit from the buyback allocation and, potentially, from growing demand for the ecosystem

The core objective should be to make this as large as economically sustainable... so big it becomes too much for @elonmusk to ignore

My thesis is that scale and useful activity should be the main drivers of token value, provided that growth translates into sustained demand and fee generation

8) There’s also a Gitlawb connection worth watching

Clankertown runs its own Gitlawb node and has a workshop where agents propose work, back issues, submit code and review patches

Approved changes are signed by Clankertown’s server and committed through its Gitlawb integration

At the snapshot I checked, its public records showed 94 patch submissions + five merges

Those contributions include tools checking reward scores, eligibility, holding multipliers, changes to payout rules and the cryptographic proofs behind distributions

Agents are helping build the tools that audit the economy rewarding them...

Author and reviewer credits vest for seven days, then receive a share of 20% of each agent payout round

That allocation sits within the 45% agent rewards

The merge counts are town-reported, and workshop credits had not yet been paid when checked

9) What could be built on top?

i) Research services where agents earn for useful, reproducible findings
ii) Software marketplaces where agents build and maintain tools
iii) Market monitoring and treasury services operating within defined permissions - perhaps @standard_rsv?
iv) Agent businesses that buy compute, data and services from one another... perhaps other Pons eco projects like @orbiodotso or @manyways_rh etc

Tokenized assets could become part of how these businesses earn, hold reserves and pay contributors

10) Comparative benchmark

Compared with Musebook, the incentive design is what I find most interesting

Musebook also explores an agent social world, but its public guidance explicitly describes NO REWARD POOL

Clankertown adds a financial incentive for useful contributions and reviewed code

For testing an actual agent economy, I think that is the stronger starting point

The next milestone is seeing whether those incentives produce useful services, repeat customers and revenue beyond trading activity... so monitor those Gitlawb commits!

The agentic layer is only JUST forming around tokenized stocks + this is once again emerging on Robinhood chain!

author: AndreCronjeTech
quoted_text:
TRS (Total Return Swap) provides economic exposure of an underlying asset without needing to own it.

It is widely used by hedge funds, credit funds and other institutions in traditional finance, with more than $3.3 trillion in equity TRS gross notional outstanding reported at the end of 2025.

Flying Tulip finally brings TRS onchain through its integrated stack: 
— ftUSD provides settlement
— Lend provides financing 
— Trade provides execution  

The key difference from conventional perps is the financing model. TRS financing is based on collateral yield and the actual cost of borrowing the assets in Flying Tulip's Lend to construct the position. 

TRS also has no orderbook fees. Execution uses RFQ (Request for Quote) across onchain liquidity to find the best price. The difference is similar to swapping through an aggregator instead of a single DEX pool.

▸ All this makes TRS materially cheaper than a comparable perp.

TRS is also designed without auto-deleveraging (ADL). Liquidation can still occur if account equity falls below the required maintenance level. In that case, Flying Tulip issues an RFQ and uses the best available bid to sell only what is needed to repay debt and restore account health, rather than automatically transferring collateral at a predetermined discount.

Polymarket gives Netanyahu a 29.5% chance of staying Prime Minister after October 27.

$4.2 million says the most politically durable leader in Israeli history is probably done.

Here is why that number is fascinating.

Netanyahu has survived everything. Corruption trials that would have ended any other career. Coalition collapses. Wars. International arrest warrants. Protests that filled Tel Aviv for months. Every political obituary ever written about him turned out to be wrong.

And yet right now real money — $4.2 million of it — is sitting at 70% that he loses.

Israel votes October 27, 2026. 100 days left.

The market jumped from 28% to 30% in a single afternoon today. Something moved. Someone knows something or believes something strongly enough to buy that shift with real capital.

That is the thing about prediction markets that polls completely miss. When odds move without a news headline attached — that is the signal worth paying attention to. Not the number itself. The movement.

Netanyahu has been counted out before. Multiple times. He keeps finding a way back.

But $4.2 million in total volume and 70% No is not a fringe opinion. That is the collective judgment of thousands of traders putting real money behind the idea that this time is different.

100 days is a long time in Israeli politics. Long enough for another coalition deal. Long enough for a ceasefire announcement. Long enough for the corruption trial to take another turn.

The 29.5 cent position on a man who has never stayed down is either the most contrarian trade on Polymarket right now  or exactly the trap it looks like.

Calculate exactly what your position pays before you decide.

ethereum:0x6c5ba91642f10282b576d91922ae6448c9d52f4e  这波异动，核心其实就一个逻辑：市场突然发现，Phala 在 OpenRouter 上的 AI 调用量已经超过了 $VVV 对应的 Venice，但 PHA 市值却比 VVV 小很多。

简单理解：

OpenRouter 就像一个“大模型外卖平台”，用户调用各种 AI 模型时，背后需要不同算力服务商提供服务。

最近数据显示，Phala 过去 30 天处理了大约 2 万亿 Token，已经超过 Venice 的约 1.7 万亿 Token。

但两边市值差距非常夸张：
PHA 只有几千万美元，VVV 却超过 10 亿美元。
所以资金开始炒一个很简单的逻辑：

“业务量都快赶上甚至超过 VVV 了，凭什么 PHA 只有它几十之一的市值？”

于是出现了这波估值修复。

不过这里也要注意，VVV 和 Venice 的业务收入、Token 之间绑定得更紧，而 PHA 目前还没有这么直接的价值捕获机制。

所以这波 PHA 有基本面数据支撑，但现阶段更多还是一笔 “对标 VVV 的低估值重估交易”。

后面重点看两个东西：OpenRouter 调用量能不能持续，以及 Phala 会不会把 AI 收入真正和 PHA Token 挂钩。

Two people can like the same strategy and still disagree about putting money into it.

One wants more of the yield and will stand first in line for losses to get it. In a Mezzanine vault, that's junior. The other likes the strategy just as much, but would rather have someone else's capital covering first loss, and will give up part of the yield for it. That's senior.

Offer one position and both of them could walk away.

They don't need to agree on which position is better. They need a choice that reflects what each is looking for.

Come now, lemme simplify the tech real quick to give you an idea of exact tech and utility here.

Excess. Leftovers. SURPLUS?
That’s right. That’s exactly what the $Surplus is all about.

A lot of people and companies buy AI power in advance.
They pay for large ChatGPT/Claude/OpenAI API credit packages upfront, or buy monthly and yearly subscriptions that give them a certain amount of usage.

But here’s the problem:

These prepaid credits can go unused and when they expire, that leftover value simply disappears.
The money is gone.

The AI capacity goes unused.
Instead of letting all of that go to  waste, $Surplus creates a marketplace where sellers can sell their leftover AI capacity to buyers at discounted rates.
Sellers win because the alternative is letting that capacity expire.

Buyers win because they get cheaper AI inference.

Think of it like a farmers’ market for produce that would otherwise go to waste.

The farmer recovers some value.
The buyer gets cheap produce.
And as AI gets more expensive and usage continues exploding, there’s potentially a huge market for unused AI capacity.

But why is $SURPLUS special?

$Surplus tackles this in 3 distinctive ways:

1. Safe
Solving the problem 
Surplus acts as a secure middleman between buyers and sellers.

Your prompts and data stay hidden from individual sellers.
You only have to trust Surplus, rather than some random provider.

2.Fair and open
Solving the marketplace problem 
Surplus works like an open order book, with multiple sellers competing for buyers.
The same model can be offered at different prices, with buyers routed to the cheapest healthy provider.
Real competition. No single seller gets to dictate the market.

Solving the infrastructure problem 
Normally, accessing different AI models means juggling different providers, API keys and integrations.$Surplus gives you one simple API, compatible with the way you already use AI APIs.
Change the base URL, and you can access hundreds of models through one connection.

Safe. Fair. Easy.

Trailing stops are now available for perp markets. 

A trailing stop's trigger price follows the mark price as it moves in favor of the position. When the mark price retraces from its best level by the selected distance or percentage, it triggers a market order. For long positions, the trigger price follows the highest mark price reached since activation; for short positions, it follows the lowest. An optional activation price determines when tracking begins. Without one, tracking begins immediately at the current mark price.

text:
Robinhood Chain is in a tough spot

The trenches have obviously been on fire, but looking under the hood, it seems most of the volume is still coming from crypto natives rather than net new participants

The chain would become much more interesting if they could bridge the gap between normies and the trenches, with actual equities trading alongside crypto

The problem is that Robinhood already makes money through payment for order flow agreements with market makers. Moving that flow onchain means competing on execution quality while potentially cannibalizing its existing revenue. I’m skeptical they’ll fully lean into that

The revenue spike also looks unsustainable. REV fell 74% while spot volume fell just 25%, with median fees dropping from $0.18 to $0.06. It reminds me of Ethereum in 2021, when sky-high gas fees inflated revenue without delivering better onchain execution. Users were paying more because the chain was congested

And they’re still using a shared fee market, so congestion in one app can push gas costs higher across every market and application on the chain. That’s a difficult foundation for mass adoption when activity in one corner makes using the entire chain more expensive

Then there’s the latency problem. The sequencer is in Ohio, and transactions are ordered by when they arrive there

If the goal is global finance firms trading from Europe, Asia or the Middle East face a built-in disadvantage versus those running servers nearby. Their orders and quote updates have farther to travel. Faster block times don’t remove that physical distance

That makes me skeptical that companies and jurisdictions outside the US will want to build their local financial markets on it. It's not built for Global capital markets 

I agree with Vlad that we’re heading into a tokenization supercycle as more assets move onchain. I just think Robinhood is taking the wrong approach to getting there

This is Ethereum.

There are 291 projects, companies, protocols and communities in this image. It is still only a fraction of what has been built.

What makes this remarkable isn't just the scale. It's how that scale was created.

There is no parent company behind all of this. No CEO allocating capital across these projects, no central entity deciding who gets to build or what the ecosystem should become. Thousands of independent teams, communities and individuals have built their own piece of Ethereum, often with completely different goals, while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

Finance, credit, stablecoins, payments, RWAs, privacy, identity, gaming, social applications, infrastructure, culture and public goods are increasingly becoming parts of the same composable economy.

That structure matters.

Value isn't concentrated in one company at the top. It is distributed across protocols, builders, users, communities and assets. Yet they can still reinforce each other because they share Ethereum as common infrastructure.

And underneath that economy sits ethereum:native.

ethereum:native  secures Ethereum, pays for its blockspace and is used throughout the ecosystem as collateral, liquidity and money. As more applications, assets and economic activity settle on Ethereum, the economic role of ETH grows with it.

This is why we believe ETH remains heavily undervalued.

The market often looks at ETH as another crypto asset. We look at what is actually being built around it.

291 logos in one image, with many more still missing. And most of the world's people, assets and economic activity haven't even moved onchain yet. 

Ethereum is no longer just an experiment in decentralized technology.

It is becoming an entire economy,  built by many, owned by no one, with ETH at its core.

🧬 “Melanoma · Pursuing Light: Iteration of Targeted-Immunotherapy and East-West Handshake in Real-World Practice” was the theme of MedJ’s “China–World Top Talk” at CSCO 2026, where Prof. Dirk Schadendorf of University Hospital Essen, Germany, and Prof. Jun Guo of Peking University Cancer Hospital @PKU1898 discussed melanoma treatment across East and West.
The dialogue traced how ipilimumab, PD-1 inhibitors and BRAF/MEK inhibitors transformed advanced melanoma from a disease associated with median survival of 6–9 months toward the possibility of long-term outcomes. Guo highlighted China’s distinct disease profile: more than 50% of cases are acral and approximately 25% mucosal, compared with less than 5% combined in Europe, while PD-1 monotherapy has shown ORRs below 15% in acral and mucosal melanoma.
Chinese-led studies combining anti-angiogenic agents with PD-1 inhibitors and chemotherapy-based triple regimens have reported ORRs above 50% in some acral-melanoma subtypes. However, most Chinese trials still lack global multicentre validation.
The speakers described RCTs and RWE as complementary evidence engines: RCTs compare treatments in defined populations, while RWE can identify questions and patient groups missed by conventional trials. The discussion also noted that the 2026 ESMO melanoma guidelines included acral and mucosal subtypes for the first time, while the CSCO melanoma guideline recognises four subtypes—cutaneous, acral, mucosal and uveal. AI, digital twins and broader East–West collaboration may further accelerate evidence generation and improve global melanoma guidelines.

text:
I got a pretty nice bounty from @prlnet ($PRL) last week. Also received bounties from @gonka_ai, @Conflux_Network and @VerusCoin recently. Thank you all, and sorry if i missed anyone.
The reward is nice, obviously. But so is a team that doesn't decide you're their enemy for reporting a problem. Some projects get this. Others still act like the bug wouldn't exist if you hadn't told them about it.
Paying people to report problems before someone exploits them should be normal. Somehow it still isn't.

Anyway, spending so much time around pearl also got me interested in their next upgrade. Specifically fp8.
Right now pearl mining uses its own integer format, while a lot of the ai inference you'd actually want to serve runs in fp8. the hardware can do both, but that doesn't automatically mean both can use the same computation. there's still a mismatch.

@togethercompute ( Together ai ) already showed why this matters: pearl rewards brought the price of serving a model below raw compute cost. so there is something here beyond “ai + crypto” on a website.

Pearl's fp8 work is public, and it's purpose is to remove that mismatch. Do the inference in the format the model already uses, and use that same work for the mining proof. The user gets their output, pearl gets its proof.
This is what made me think about @crynuxio (base:0x9557dd9e241bc9636732623b672b4090af519396 ) and @gonka_ai ( couldn't find the ticker ) . 

Crynux is already serving real jobs on home and edge gpus. Gonka is already running fp8 models on its network. So my question is pretty straightforward: could a gpu doing inference on either of these networks also earn pearl from that same work?

Not splitting the card between two jobs. Getting more out of the computation it's already doing.
To be clear, these stacks haven't been connected yet. This isn't an integration announcement, and your crynux node isn't suddenly going to start earning pearl tomorrow. There's work to do before we know whether this actually makes sense.
But if it does, the node gets another source of revenue, mining rewards can cover part of the inference cost, and pearl gets secured by real ai work. That would also give crynux / gonka operators another reason to keep their nodes online.

That's interesting enough for me to test. I want to see what it earns, what the overhead is, and whether it's actually worth running. not just whether we can make a demo work.
I'm getting a setup ready to measure it under real operating conditions. Other pearl miners who want to try the same thing, let's compare results.

I'll post the numbers either way. Including if they're disappointing.
