quoted_text:
This is Ethereum.

There are 291 projects, companies, protocols and communities in this image. It is still only a fraction of what has been built.

What makes this remarkable isn't just the scale. It's how that scale was created.

There is no parent company behind all of this. No CEO allocating capital across these projects, no central entity deciding who gets to build or what the ecosystem should become. Thousands of independent teams, communities and individuals have built their own piece of Ethereum, often with completely different goals, while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

Finance, credit, stablecoins, payments, RWAs, privacy, identity, gaming, social applications, infrastructure, culture and public goods are increasingly becoming parts of the same composable economy.

That structure matters.

Value isn't concentrated in one company at the top. It is distributed across protocols, builders, users, communities and assets. Yet they can still reinforce each other because they share Ethereum as common infrastructure.

And underneath that economy sits ethereum:native.

ethereum:native  secures Ethereum, pays for its blockspace and is used throughout the ecosystem as collateral, liquidity and money. As more applications, assets and economic activity settle on Ethereum, the economic role of ETH grows with it.

This is why we believe ETH remains heavily undervalued.

The market often looks at ETH as another crypto asset. We look at what is actually being built around it.

291 logos in one image, with many more still missing. And most of the world's people, assets and economic activity haven't even moved onchain yet.

text:
Before celebrating leadership transitions, perhaps we should also talk about unfinished business.

What happens to the people who worked for @Mazerance , fulfilled their responsibilities, and were subsequently left waiting for compensation and salaries they were promised?

Interesting to read about the people who “made it possible” while some of those very people are still waiting to be paid salaries owed for over 4 months.

What happens when the promised deadline passes without payment, without meaningful communication, and the people affected are eventually told that the matter is no longer in your hands?

There are people who gave their time, skills and commitment to building this company who are still waiting for what they are owed.

So when I read public statements celebrating the people who “made it possible,” I can’t help but question how truthful that picture really is.

Some stories sound very different from the inside.

Elvis, This is not how to go about things.
author: NonseOdion
quoted_text:
I have stepped down as CEO of @Mazerance.

Mazerance began with an idea I had early last year. Together with friends who loved puzzles and escape rooms, we set out to build a story-driven co-op strategy game, and to show what a game studio out of Africa could look like on the world stage.

That idea became a studio registered in Australia, Nigeria and the United States, with a team that brought everything they had to building the game and the company behind it.

Eighteen months ago, none of this existed. No company, no team, no community, no world to build a game in. There is now, because of everyone who made it possible: the team, family, friends, my co-founders and the people who backed us from the start.

We built a community of roughly 20,000 people and generated over 8 million impressions on this app alone.

Through Project 9, Rancers Remix and Pass It On, we became one of the most talked-about budding game studios in Africa, earned more than five press features and made our presence felt at Moonshot, one of Nigeria's largest tech conferences.

More than 25 people across three continents have worked on Mazerance, and in the first eight months alone that team produced over 600 pieces of brand, world and community work, from characters and lore to artwork, videos and campaign content. That is close to three assets produced a day, every single day; working closely with these talented individuals has been the highlight of my career.

The studio is also set up on Steam and Kickstarter, which as a company registered across three countries is harder than it sounds.

None of this was one person. It was everyone who has put something into Mazerance, and leading that team every day for eighteen months has been nothing short of a privilege.

There is still a lot of work ahead. I do not count any of this as the finish line, but the effort and the outcomes deserve recognition.

The game is still in development, and delivering it would be the best outcome for me, the team, the community and our stakeholders. The foundation is there, and whoever leads the business next has something substantial to work with.

I have poured almost everything I have into this company for eighteen months. I need to step back, look after myself, and go back to the work I love. I am a designer and storyteller before anything else.

Leading Mazerance has been one of the most difficult and beautiful things I have ever been in service of. I believe I did it well, and I am grateful for every moment of it.

But design is where I do my best work, and what I build next will reflect that: experiences that transform how physical products understand human interaction and change how people live with them.

As for who takes the seat, the company has chosen an interim successor.

To the team (past and present) and my co-founders, thank you. To the Rancers, our investors and everyone who backed us early, thank you for believing in what we set out to build.

I remain on the board, and will continue to support Mazerance in whatever capacity it needs me. This is my child and I have its best interest at heart.

More on what is next for me soon.

潘石屹原来叫潘适夷？

这名字就注定了跑路结局啊

适，是方向；夷，是他乡
author: rickawsb
quoted_text:
我的油管第10期：《中国富豪，哪些还想跑？》

任正非携全家跑了。有人说，造谣。

在人人焦虑的大背景下，真相不重要，重要的是人们太需要变化了。太需要天安门出大事，中南海出大事——重要的是人心思变。

任正非到底跑不跑，王石、俞敏洪、王健林、王兴、刘强东、张一鸣跑不跑……中国富豪们还有哪些想跑。

潘适夷一生都在跑，高考锁骨被撞断，知道高考不中了，用另外的名字“石屹”考上石油学校。他从天水跑到廊坊，从廊坊跑到深圳，从深圳边防的狗洞下钻进去，又跑到海南，拎着五斤橘子和一条香烟去规划局看资料，感觉天要塌了……毫不犹豫再次跑路，去了北京。这才有了后来的“潘石屹”。

潘石屹现在处于生与死之间，他就是薛定谔的猫。

“白手套逃跑型”“提前布局型”“离岸信托局”……所谓提前布局，这局那局，都不如政治局。

马云跑过，又回来了，他的根在政坛——阿里巴巴完成“中国历史上规模最大的一次私营融资”，购买股份的包括博裕资本、中信资本、国开金融，新天域资本。《纽约时报》指出，股东包括江泽民的孙子江志成、刘云山的儿子刘乐飞、温家宝的儿子温云松等中央政治局常委的20多人的子孙……

你问马云为什么不跑，请问，当年胡雪岩为什么不跑。

其实命运重重叠叠，早在1949年就布下了这张网。

1949年，何应钦邀请中国船王卢作孚出任交通部长，他拒绝。阎锡山也邀请他，他又拒绝。但共产党派来潘汉年，他立马同意，奋不顾身率船队归国了。抗战时，卢作孚冒着日机轰炸，率船队抢运出一百五十多万人，一百多万吨物资。史称中国的敦刻尔克。

两年后，深受其辱的卢作孚吞下大量安眠药时，有没有想到这两趟奋不顾身的航行。

一念天堂，一念地狱。历史一眨眼，就是普通人一生。1956年，眼见北京公私合营轰轰烈烈，荣毅仁心里不服，他代表上海工商界表态：北京用了十天，阿拉上海宁只要六天。上海资本家排着队去签公私合营申请书。十万多商户全部合营。当晚，大小老板带着家属上台，合唱《全世界人民心一条》……

1949年，荣毅仁说“我赞成共产党，但是我只举一只手，如果两只手都举起来，那是投降”。公私合营时他改口了，说“举一只手赞成共产党，我错了，现在要举两只手”。他是真投降了……文革时他被抄家，剃阴阳头，食指被打断，发配刷厕所，折磨了十三年。

褚时健以七十四岁高龄去荒山种橙子，被王石夸成选择尊严。难道不知道褚时健直到生命终点都逃不出那座精神牢狱，哀而不得，才上哀牢山吗。中国企业家为什么这么怂，很多国产企业家被权力反复蹂躏后，把强奸变成了顺奸，开始还大声呼救，后来呼救变成了叫床。

商鞅认为：商人有钱有资源，会把老百姓抢跑。秦统一天下，重农抑商，成为君王的必选，两千年循环。

罗马立《万民法》，外国人也能贸易，裁判官公平处理商业纠纷……而同时期的汉武帝歧视商人，把盐铁专卖。

1303年，英王颁布了《商人章程》。而同时期的大明朝，商人跟娼优一个等级。

1602年，荷兰开办人类第一家股份有限公司，第一个证券交易所……那时是明万历三十年，中国禁海。

欧洲的美第奇家族，赞助米开朗基罗、达芬奇，推动了文艺复兴和欧洲进程。

而同时代的中国商人沈万三。先不说是否真有其人，但《明史》有真实故事：一个叫沈秀的富民，帮忙修了南京城墙，想出钱犒赏三军。朱元璋大怒——你个匹夫也敢犒我天子的军队，此乱民也，该杀。马皇后劝了半天，才改成流放云南。

欧洲商人搞赞助，推动文艺复兴，中国商人搞赞助，抄家流放。

欧洲很少有大一统。而大一统的中国皇上认为：商人有钱有资源，会抢走民心，会动摇我的统治——这就是皇上的底层逻辑。所以任正非跑不跑不重要，任正非不跑，张正非李正非韩正非也会跑，在一个没有商业规则、商人纯属权力依附，没事儿就倒查三十年的地方，即使一时GDP风风光光，也是二世而亡。散会！

text:
Arithmetic-friendly hashes have long been one of the weakest pieces of prover cryptography.

With ZisK v1.3.0, we removed Poseidon entirely and moved to BLAKE3.

What surprised us is that we got the same performance — or even better.

After many optimizations elsewhere in the prover, hashing had become one of the most time-consuming parts of proof generation. BLAKE3 is more than an order of magnitude faster, making this cost almost disappear and largely compensating for the increased complexity of the recursion circuit.

Getting there required a lot of re-engineering: circuit sizes, prover scheduling, and architecture all had to be reconsidered around the new trade-offs that BLAKE3 gives us. The final result surprised even us.

There is a lot of focus today on binary-field proving. Binary fields attack the hash-proving bottleneck from a different direction, but introduce different trade-offs when proving regular arithmetic. There is a huge amount of research happening here, and at ZisK we are following it very closely.

I'm genuinely curious to see whether binary-field architectures will outperform what we can achieve with the current approach — and how long it will take.

So I like to think of v1.3.0 as setting a new target. 🎯

To everyone working on binary fields — and to all of us trying to make provers faster: let's see if we can beat it :)

And we still have a few optimizations in the basket.

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
Grok 4.7 scores 46 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index to bring SpaceXAI into the top 4 AI labs. Coding Agent Index performance has also improved, overtaking GPT-5.6 Sol

Grok 4.7 scores +2 points over Grok 4.6 on the Intelligence Index, with strong performance on agentic knowledge work tasks. We evaluated the new model at xhigh reasoning effort.

Congratulations to @SpaceXAI and @ElonMusk on the release!

Key takeaways:

➤ Grok 4.7 joins the frontier of agentic knowledge work: Grok 4.7 gains +111 Elo over Grok 4.6 (high) on AA-Briefcase, our private benchmark for long-horizon agentic knowledge work, scoring 1657 Elo and placing it alongside Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5.1 at the frontier. On GDPval-AA, it scores 1695 Elo, +90 ahead of Grok 4.6 (high).

➤ A leap in coding agent performance: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) with Grok Build scores 56 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, up +9 points from Grok 4.6 (xhigh). Among models in their native harnesses, Grok 4.7 + Grok Build now ranks 4th, behind only Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus 5.

➤ Incremental performance changes elsewhere: Outside of agentic knowledge work, Grok 4.7 broadly matches Grok 4.6 (high) on the other Intelligence Index tasks. It improves on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (+4.5 percentage points) and GDP.pdf (+3.0 p.p.), with regressions on AA-LCR (-3.7 p.p.) and AutomationBench-AA (-1.1 p.p.).

➤ High token use across tasks: Grok 4.7's gains come with higher token usage. Grok 4.7 (xhigh) uses approximately 81k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, compared with 36k for Grok 4.6 (high) and 27k for GPT-6 Astra (max) - 125% and 196% more, respectively.

Other model details:

➤ Context window of 500k tokens, unchanged from Grok 4.6

➤ Pricing of $2/$6 per 1M input/output tokens with cache hits discounted to $0.50 per 1M tokens, matching Grok 4.6

➤ Configurable reasoning effort spans low to xhigh. Our evaluation uses xhigh.

text:
Onchain options are the largest remaining whitespace in crypto derivatives.

Most crypto options activity still takes place on centralized venues. Although onchain premium volume recently hit a monthly high, total notional over the past 30 days was still just 4.3% of Deribit’s. Attracting sustained retail flow is the sector’s next hurdle.

Derive currently accounts for roughly 95% of onchain options premium volume. V3 builds on that position by making the same liquidity available across more markets and products.

The existing Derive Chain will be replaced by a zkVM-based system that settles on Ethereum. Its new risk architecture should make it easier to list markets with different risk profiles while portfolio cross-margining improves capital efficiency for traders.

Native vaults could turn those markets into products users access through a single deposit. A covered-call vault could generate income by selling part of a tokenized asset’s upside while creating a more predictable source of flow for market makers.

Consumer apps let users select an asset and express a directional view while Derive handles the options execution underneath. This allows builders to focus on distribution without having to bootstrap a new liquidity venue.

The success of v3 depends on whether these products can attract sustained flow beyond Derive’s existing user base and grow the onchain options market around its infrastructure.

text:
This NYT article describes the appeal of Europe’s far right as rooted in lost pride and an idealized past. Yet the people in its strongest passages seem to want something quite ordinary: work that supports a family, a community that holds together, and some assurance that the place they call home has a future.

I think they are entitled to expect those things.

People with options have a peculiar ease recommending adaptation to those with few. If your career travels, your savings are substantial and another city will welcome you, you can afford a certain detachment from the fortunes of any particular place.

Your parents may need care. Your trade may depend on the local employer. The house you own may be worth too little to buy elsewhere. Under those conditions, the decline of your town enters every calculation you make.

“Move somewhere else” is a considerable prescription for a life someone else has to live.

The same distance appears in arguments about national pride. I want my country’s history taught honestly. That includes its crimes, its failures, and the people who paid for them. Affection gives us no license to falsify the record.

But neither does an honest record oblige us to withhold affection.

A country contains more than the worst things done in its name. It contains my family, the work of generations, institutions worth defending, habits of mutual obligation, places that carry our memories. We can inherit all of that with open eyes.

What troubles me is the assumption, sometimes barely concealed, that attachment itself betrays a lack of sophistication. The person who feels at home everywhere is permitted to admire their own breadth of mind. The person who feels at home somewhere is asked to examine their prejudices.

That is a poor basis on which to ask for their vote.

The article does acknowledge failures of liberal democracy. I would give those failures greater weight. Before explaining why voters yearn for the past, ask what future they have been offered, who made the decisions, and whether their objections ever altered the outcome.

The far right deserves the same examination. Let it explain how its promises will improve wages, housing, and public services. Let it explain how a citizen it treats as an outsider is supposed to belong. Understanding the appeal creates no obligation to accept the program.

But democratic parties have a duty here. They must make a decent life possible in the places people already call home, and speak of those places with something warmer than embarrassment.

People should not have to leave their communities to prosper, or apologize for wanting their people to endure.

text:
The most insightful thing I read about technology eleven years ago was @benthompson’s Aggregation Theory. Amazon blocking Muse is another perfect example.

Customers want one agent that knows them and can get things done. The platforms being aggregated want the opposite. They want to own the customer relationship, not become interchangeable suppliers behind someone else’s interface + protect their ad business. 

Imagine groceries: Your agent can compare Amazon, Instacart, DoorDash, and Uber Eats, then route every order to the best option. Amazon can block that access because it is a gigantic company. But smaller players have every incentive to offer agents a clean API and a seamless experience.

If Instacart embraces agents while Amazon blocks them, the agent will increasingly route demand to Instacart. Customers will be happy, and Amazon will eventually face the dilemma: keep protecting the relationship, or match the better value proposition.

This will be the defining tension of the agent economy: aggregators realizing they are now being aggregated.

Amazon will push its own assistant, of course. But a vertical Amazon agent will struggle against a horizontal agent that already knows my email, calendar, preferences, memories, and entire life context.

Many companies will want to become the aggregation layer. Very few actually can.

text:
I used to have a favorite brand of Kona coffee.

I drank it religiously every morning. Told all of my friends about it. Recommended it to anyone who would listen.

Then one year, my wife and I were vacationing in Hawaii, and I decided on a whim to drive out to the address printed on the package.

When we arrived, I was a little confused.

There was a showroom...but no coffee farm anywhere in sight.

The poor girl behind the desk was even more confused when I asked if we could tour the farm.

Turns out, there was no farm.

It was simply a business that bought excess coffee beans from a variety of farmers in the area, packaged them under its own brand, and sold them.

The level of betrayal I felt is difficult to describe.

And, in hindsight, completely unfair.

They had never claimed to own a farm. They had never told me the coffee was single-source. I had simply created an expectation in my own head of what I thought the brand was supposed to be.

And reality didn't match it.

The next morning at the Airbnb, I brewed another cup of that coffee.

Except this time, it tasted different.

I actually found myself wondering why I had ever loved it so much in the first place.

So for the next few days, I toured real Kona coffee farms.

I walked among the coffee trees. Met the people growing them. Saw how the beans were harvested and processed. Learned the stories behind the farms.

Eventually, I found one I absolutely loved.

Seeing where the coffee came from, meeting the people behind it, and watching the process made me fall in love with a brand in a completely different way.

And it is still, to this day, the best coffee I've ever had.

It's what I drink every single morning.

Moral of the story?

Authenticity matters.

People can forgive imperfections. They can forgive small teams, rough edges, and things still being built.

What is much harder to recover from is the moment someone realizes the thing they believed they were looking at isn't actually what they thought it was.

Build something real.

Then let people see it. Transparently. 

🫡 From the depths — 
The White Whale 🐋

Spot trading is a customer acquisition cost, and Derivatives are a business.

You open a long ...Price runs.

Hyperliquid keeps adding these little features that make the actual trading experience more complete.

Manual borrowing.
Portfolio margin.
TWAPs.

Now trailing stops.

The endgame isn't just having a perp DEX with good liquidity.

author: thesogle_
quoted_text:
Trailing stops are now available for perp markets. 

A trailing stop's trigger price follows the mark price as it moves in favor of the position. When the mark price retraces from its best level by the selected distance or percentage, it triggers a market order. For long positions, the trigger price follows the highest mark price reached since activation; for short positions, it follows the lowest. An optional activation price determines when tracking begins. Without one, tracking begins immediately at the current mark price.

The recent Liquid incident finally made me understand why @BTCdrivechains’ sidechain design is beneficial.

For me, the bigger issue wasn’t the bug, but how much the system still depends on a small group of signers for $BTC withdrawals.

That’s where eCash differs.

With eCash, Bitcoin miners vote on Drivechain withdrawals over thousands of blocks, which means a malicious one would stay visible for roughly three months before it could be finalized.

So the risk still exists, but users get much more time to spot something suspicious before it’s finalized.

That’s also why the upcoming eCash beta feels more relevant, as it gives users more transparency throughout the withdrawal process, while showing how BTC can gain more utility and fee revenue without changing Bitcoin L1.

Don’t forget about the original 1:1 ECX airdrop for BTC holders at full launch, with Beta also improving the pECX burn rate to 20 real ECX for 1,000 pECX (up from 10 in Alpha).

We’ll finally get to see this model in practice before the mainnet on October 31.

Drivechains (BIP 300/301) fix this: sidechains pegged to BTC, independent of L1. Succeed, and Bitcoin gains new utility and fee revenue. Fail, and L1 is untouched.

eCash is the first real network built on this model, and Alpha proved it. Hashrate hit 9.44 PH/s, 7 independent pools mined blocks, and the community shipped a bunch of tools unprompted:

text:
Robinhood Chain is in a tough spot

The trenches have obviously been on fire, but looking under the hood, it seems most of the volume is still coming from crypto natives rather than net new participants

The chain would become much more interesting if they could bridge the gap between normies and the trenches, with actual equities trading alongside crypto

The problem is that Robinhood already makes money through payment for order flow agreements with market makers. Moving that flow onchain means competing on execution quality while potentially cannibalizing its existing revenue. I’m skeptical they’ll fully lean into that

The revenue spike also looks unsustainable. REV fell 74% while spot volume fell just 25%, with median fees dropping from $0.18 to $0.06. It reminds me of Ethereum in 2021, when sky-high gas fees inflated revenue without delivering better onchain execution. Users were paying more because the chain was congested

And they’re still using a shared fee market, so congestion in one app can push gas costs higher across every market and application on the chain. That’s a difficult foundation for mass adoption when activity in one corner makes using the entire chain more expensive

Then there’s the latency problem. The sequencer is in Ohio, and transactions are ordered by when they arrive there

If the goal is global finance firms trading from Europe, Asia or the Middle East face a built-in disadvantage versus those running servers nearby. Their orders and quote updates have farther to travel. Faster block times don’t remove that physical distance

That makes me skeptical that companies and jurisdictions outside the US will want to build their local financial markets on it. It's not built for Global capital markets 

I agree with Vlad that we’re heading into a tokenization supercycle as more assets move onchain. I just think Robinhood is taking the wrong approach to getting there

text:
问候我所有的中国朋友，想跟大家分享一下我对加密市场的一些想法，以及过去几个月我到底在哪些叙事上赚到了钱。到现在我依然觉得，这些叙事后面还能继续玩

每个牛市周期都会涌进来一堆新点子，流动性和大家的注意力会往哪边跑，一看就知道

2017年是ICO狂潮，当时几乎每个代币都自称“以太坊杀手”。还记得EOS、OMG Network、Qtum、Lisk、Zilliqa这些项目当时圈了多少钱吗？

2021年是GameFi和元宇宙代币的爆发。AXS、SAND、MANA，这些名字你们肯定不陌生

2024年则是迷因币大爆发，只要跟动物有关、或者跟某个本地梗沾边的币（Chillguy、Pnut、Wif、Fartcoin、Popcat这些），都能轻松冲到几十亿美元市值

很多人在这些叙事上亏钱，核心原因就一个：太爱这个叙事了，坚信它能永远活下去。他们把股市那套“长期拿着就能致富”的思维直接套到加密上。但加密叙事变得比闪电还快，跟股市完全不是一回事

现在这个市场里，你真正要搞清楚的只有一件事：这个叙事热过了没有。最简单的办法——看这个币有多少持币地址

持币的人越多，做市商和其他大户就越难把价格往自己想要的方向推。所以叙事才会隔三差五就换。管一个800万美金市值的币，比管一个10亿美金市值的币容易太多了；管一个只有5000个持币地址的币，比管10万个持币地址的币也容易太多了——后者稍微涨一点，每只手都想按卖出，抛压巨大。没有任何一个做市商或大户愿意带一堆多余的乘客。想在叙事上赚钱，这点必须想明白

所以大户们只能不停换叙事，去那些还没人关注的地方。等大家开始习惯某个叙事、不断补仓摊平那些慢慢阴跌的垃圾币时，流动性早就跑到新叙事去了

很多人亏钱就是因为太固执，觉得有人在考验他们的意志，熬过去代币就会翻倍。加密圈不是这样玩的。别把股市里“越跌越买”的习惯带到加密市场，尤其是玩迷因币的时候

过去几个月我就是靠那些当时看起来很离谱、很新、很独特的叙事赚到了几倍。虽然当时我脑子里也有一部分声音在喊：别折腾了，继续拿着熟悉的山寨币就行

我具体赚到钱的是这几个：

发射台平台币（我在800万美金市值时买了PONS）
跟代币化股票配对的迷因币（我在200万美金市值时买了AI/NVDA）
跟山寨币配对的迷因币（我在50万美金市值时买了NEARCAT/NEAR）

部分已经兑现的想法我在X上公开过：
https://t.co/6kQNzxikBQ
（$SPACEHOOD 7倍，$CLIPPY 3倍，$MARSCOIN 2倍，$AI +50%）
还有这个：
https://t.co/EejLNLzUeo
（USEFUL 2倍，BUTT 3倍，NEARCAT 6倍，CANDLE 7倍）
还有一部分call在我的Telegram频道里。频道是俄语的，但自带翻译，你们可以看看。那边更像我的日记，脏话比较多，X上我写得相对正式一点。频道号：https://t.co/RdowafCRCD

好，下面说说这几个叙事为什么有戏。
第一个叙事：发射台平台币
如果你不想纯赌、不想天天神经紧绷，那就买那些靠大家赌博赚钱的平台代币

这相当于投资赌场的股票——大家都抱着中头奖的希望往里冲

每条链就像一座城市或一个国家

Robinhood和Pons就像投资拉斯维加斯的赌场股票，Solana和Stonkfun就像投资摩纳哥的赌场股票。希望你们懂我的意思

Robinhood有 @ponsdotfamily 
Solana有 @LaunchOnSF 
Base有 @Stonks_Exchange 
BNB有 @brewdotfamily 
HyperEVM有 @SignalFam 
Arc有 @Arguspad 

当然有风险，赌场可能被关之类的。但只要市场还在高潮，流动性首先就会涌向这些发射台平台币。而且大部分这类协议都有回购销毁机制。注意看，比特币回调后开始反弹时，最先拉升的往往就是这些发射台代币

别觉得我脑子有问题，我觉得Avalanche（@avax）和Giwa（@GIWA_by_Upbit）后面也会出发射台，说不定能出几个让人暴富的gem。这两条链我目前都盯着

第二个叙事：跟代币化股票配对的迷因币

这个玩法又新又香的地方在于，迷因币现在可以不跟USDT/USDC或ETH/SOL配对，而是跟更稳定的资产配对，比如Nvidia、Meta、Tesla这些大公司的代币化股票。你表面上是在赌迷因币，但底仓是相对稳定的资产，不会第二天就归零。更神奇的是，你拿着这个迷因币，还能拿到对应股票的分红。
比如说你买了AI/NVDA，拿着，就能拿到NVDA的分红。
所以我觉得这个叙事还能再玩几个月，很多人现在还是低估它。它把迷因币的赌性和股市分红结合在一起了。
我判断这个叙事退潮的时候, @cz_binance会用中国公司代币化股票配对的迷因币再把它救活一次，比如腾讯、阿里巴巴、工商银行这些（所以我觉得BNB链上的发射台代币现在被严重低估了)
还记得2025年1月TRUMP迷因币上线后市场有多惨吗？同年3月CZ用$MUBARAK、$TST、$TUT、$BROCCOLI把迷因币叙事又救活了。
或者2025年10月10日大跌之后，CZ又用$4、$PUP、$PALU、$哈基米把叙事拉起来

所以可以肯定，如果再发生一次，这个叙事大概率就要彻底落幕了。看看上面那些币的K线就知道。但现在还好，该玩继续玩

第三个叙事：跟山寨币配对的迷因币

第一个叙事围着迷因币本身转，第二个围着代币化股票转，第三个则围着山寨币转。这对老韭菜可能更友好，因为他们本来就习惯拿有技术的山寨币

这个玩法的精髓在于：迷因币其实是在衡量某个山寨币有没有真正的社区

所以你会发现大部分这种迷因币都是跟高市值山寨币配对的（比如HYPE、LIT、TAO、NEAR这些），因为这些币才有社区，这点也反映在它们的FDV上

而且持有这种迷因币，你不但能吃迷因币本身的涨幅，还能拿到山寨币分红

我拿NEARCAT到现在，光分红就已经拿了400多美金的$NEAR。这个币我现在已经32倍了，还在继续拿，因为最近Near官方协议都关注了nearcat这个账号

任何项目都应该明白，出一个跟自己代币配对的迷因币，等于免费营销，而且对自身代币价格也有好处。看看$NEAR的走势就知道了

目前提供这种“迷因币+山寨币配对”模式的发射台主要有两个：stonkfun和pons

我觉得现在还有不少被低估的迷因币，以后市值能冲得更高：

$BUTT 配 $TAO
$raycat 配 $RAY
$jupcat 配 $JUP
$🎒 配 $BP

其他山寨币估计也会跟上这个玩法，所以这个叙事我觉得还能继续赚，很多人还是没真正重视它

我相信以后我们会看到跟$AAVE、$AVAX、$INJ、$BIO、$STABLE以及CoinMarketCap上常年排在前面的那些山寨币配对的迷因币

跟上新叙事，别死守那些早就凉透的垃圾叙事。就算最后没赚到钱，至少脑子练出来了，学会接受新东西，这样你才不会老得太快

text:
GPT-6 Astra 用下来，我真的开始怀疑 OpenAI 的方向走错了。

它很擅长目标明确、有固定正确答案的任务。但碰到开放、发散、没有标准答案的事情，就特别别扭。自由探索一个想法、写点有意思的东西，或者面对模糊的问题自己判断值得往哪走，这些才是我觉得它明显欠缺的能力。从 GPT-5 开始，我就有这种感觉。

很多任务开始时，连最终想要什么都没确定，需要在探索过程中逐渐发现。GPT 却总像在等你把题目出完整，把验收标准列清楚。可如果这些都得我先想好，最需要智能的那部分工作，我已经自己做完了。

我怀疑这也解释了它为什么那么爱堆防御性代码、写一大堆测试。测试能给出明确的通过或失败，它很容易一直围着这些可验证的结果打转。至于方向有没有价值、有没有更好的可能，就需要另一种判断力了。

Claude Fable 在这类任务上给我的感觉就好得多。它会从理解你想做的事情出发，顺着不完整的想法继续展开，给你一些原本没想到的可能性。即使没有固定答案，也能把事情往前推进。

这让我怀疑 OpenAI 是不是太执着于能判对错、能计分的能力了。真实世界有太多任务根本没有标准答案。在这种自由探索和开放任务上，我觉得 Anthropic 才是真正领先的，光看表面跑分看不出来。

text: @MarkSterling0 Hey @grok is this just a mean reversion trade strategy. Please give the typical return profile of this strategy vs simple buy and hold for SPX vs a winner like Tesla. Take into account real world taxes.
author: willywoo

text:
Yes, it has clear mean-reversion traits: scale in deeper on larger drops, scale out on larger rises.

Exact backtest is hard without defined reference price or add/sell sizing base. Conceptually vs buy-and-hold:

SPX (~10% long-term CAGR): Strategy may match or lag slightly by trimming during prolonged bulls; real taxes on realized gains cut net returns further vs deferred B&H.

Tesla (~40% CAGR since IPO): Severely underperforms. Early partial sells at +30-100% miss the bulk of parabolic runs (e.g. 2020). Taxes amplify the drag by forcing early realization.

Avez-vous entendu parler de ce roman ? C’est le « phénomène de la rentrée littéraire ». Il est lauréat du Prix Fnac, du Prix Méduse, du Prix Première Plume, fortement pressenti pour le Prix Renaudot, et il est en lice pour les prix Goncourt, Femina, Médicis et Décembre. Ah oui, il est aussi en cours de traduction dans 20 langues.

Eh bien selon Pangram, ce roman est rédigé presque intégralement par une Intelligence Artificielle. Nous avons testé plusieurs passages, à divers endroits du manuscrit, pour presque toujours le même résultat : 100% IA (cf les deux premiers chapitre dans le tweet ci-dessous).

Rappelons que Pangram est de loin le détecteur d’IA le plus fiable : son taux de faux positifs est de 0,0041%, soit environ un texte humain sur 24 400. Sur 996 273 textes antérieurs à 2022, Pangram en classe uniquement 14 (0,0014%) comme étant partiellement écrits par l’IA.

La probabilité que vingt passages d’un même livre (et il y a bien plus de 20 signalements dans le roman) soient identifiés à tort par Pangram comme étant produits par une IA s’élève donc à 0,0041% puissance 20, soit 0,1802 × 10⁻⁸⁵ %, c’est à-dire 0 suivi de 85 zéros après la virgule.

N’aurait-il pas été plus honnête que l’auteur crédite son co-auteur ?

text:
A few thoughts on the current state of venture capital.

When the Music Is Playing

In July 2007, a few weeks before the credit markets seized up, Chuck Prince, then the CEO of Citigroup, gave an interview to the Financial Times. The line everyone remembers is this one: "As long as the music is playing, you've got to get up and dance." He was mocked for it for years afterward, and he lost his job a few months later. But I have come to think he was saying something honest. He wasn't claiming the music would play forever. He was admitting that he couldn't sit down while it was still going, and neither could anyone else in his seat.

I've been thinking about that quote a lot lately, because right now is the most disorienting period in venture capital I can remember, and I have been doing this for a while.

Here is what makes it disorienting. It's not that things are bad. Some things are spectacular. We have companies in our portfolio growing faster than anything I have seen in my career, and I don't say that lightly. At the same time, we have companies with no revenue, no product, and a founding team you could fit in a conference room raising billions of dollars at valuations of $10 to $50 billion. Both of these things are true at once, and if you try to reason about them with the same framework you will drive yourself crazy.

Two ideas have helped me make sense of it. Neither is mine.

The first is reflexivity, which George Soros has been writing about since the 1980s. In most of life, perception follows reality: the weather is what it is, and your opinion of it changes nothing. In markets, it runs the other way too. Prices change what participants believe, and what participants believe changes the prices. The feedback loop can run for a long time, and while it's running it looks exactly like progress.

Here is how reflexivity is playing out in AI. Full disclosure: Menlo is an investor in Anthropic, so read the following with that in mind. People watched a frontier lab go from a $4 billion valuation to $18 billion, then $60 billion, then $180 billion, then $380 billion, and now something close to a trillion. They drew the obvious conclusion: that is what a neo lab looks like. So the next neo lab gets priced off that path, not off anything it has built. Then it gets marked up in a subsequent round, and the markup itself becomes the proof. Look at Thinking Machines. Look at Reflection. At that point valuation has stopped being an output of the metrics and has become the metric. Nobody is discounting cash flows. They are discounting the last round.

Soros is very clear about one thing, and it's the part people skip: you cannot know when or how a reflexive process ends. You only know that it does. Every one of them has.

The second idea is Chuck Prince's, and it explains why smart people keep dancing even when they can see the loop for what it is. As far as I can tell, there are two groups on the dance floor.

The first group got in early. Firms like ours were in some of these AI companies before the numbers got silly, and the paper gains are enormous. When you are sitting on gains like that, you start to feel like you're playing with house money. I have been around long enough to know that house money is the most dangerous kind, because you don't respect it the way you respect money you had to earn.

The second group missed the early rounds and knows it. Their LPs know it too. So they are trying to make up for lost time by writing very large checks very late, which is the one strategy almost guaranteed to turn a missed opportunity into a real loss.

House money on one side, FOMO on the other, and reflexivity feeding both. That's the whole story. Everyone has a reason to keep dancing, and the reasons are different, which is why nobody can talk anyone else off the floor.

So what do you do? The instinct in our business is to answer with company identification: just pick the right neo lab and you'll be fine. I think that's the trap. When price has become the signal, being right about the company is not enough, because you can be right about the company and still be wrong about the price by a factor of ten. The public-market investors I admire figured this out a long time ago. They spend as much time on how much to own as on what to own.

The winners in venture over the next decade will be the firms that treat portfolio composition and position sizing as seriously as they treat sourcing. How much of the fund is in companies whose valuation rests on the last round rather than on revenue? What happens to the portfolio if the reflexive loop breaks next year instead of in five? Those are not exciting questions. They are the ones that will matter.

The music will stop. It always does. Dance if you must, but know where the chairs are.

text:
Let’s all take a moment to actually watch this exchange in full, where the VP was specifically asked about Israel.  

Q: JD, before we wrap here, I want to ask you another hard question. This one about our relationship with the state of Israel and the president's relationship with Bibi Netanyahu. Many people in the Republican Party, MAGA, are now moving to a new party: America first, America only. There's a rise in anti-Semitism, and there's a persistent belief amongst a lot of the people on the right that maybe our foreign policy is too influenced by the state of Israel or Bibi Netanyahu. Can you take us into the relationship right now, where it stands, and the you know the administration's position on collaborating with Israel on a lot of these military activities.

VP: Yeah, you know what the president has said, Jason, is obviously Israel has been an important partner when it comes to military technology, when it comes to intelligence sharing, but also sometimes the United States doesn't always agree with Israel, and I think that more than frankly any president in the last 40 years, he has shown a willingness to actually part ways with Bibi Netanyahu when he feels like the interests of the American people are different from the interests of of the government of Israel.

And I find it a little ironic, Jason, that you have Democrats criticizing Donald Trump for his relationship with Bibi when Donald Trump is the one president of the last 40 years who's been willing to say, you know what, yeah, Bibi is a good partner, but also Bibi and I have a different opinion on this, or Bibi's wrong about this, or maybe Bibi's right about this from the perspective of Israel. But the American people need us to go in a different direction. So I just think that rooting this relationship, like all relationships, in America's interest is the way to actually have a rational conversation here.

Because when you're talking about whether a given policy is in America's interest, and you keep yourself laser focused on that, I think that's how you make sure that the American people know that you're fighting for them. But I also think that it allows us to actually rationally focus and force ourselves to have a conversation about when something that maybe sounded good or maybe has become a cliche or a slogan for the past 20 or 30 years. Well, maybe we have to do something different now, and I think that that's how we have to approach not just this relationship but all relationships.

By the way, you you see a similar pushback when the president makes the argument that he's made about NATO, which is yes, obviously a lot of important relationships, a lot of important partnerships in NATO, but that doesn't mean that we're going to completely make our European foreign policy subservient to NATO in the same way that we cannot let our Middle Eastern foreign policy be subservient to the state of Israel. We're going to work with people when we work with them. We're going to disagree when we disagree, and we're going to pursue America's interests. That's the only way to have a rational foreign policy.

Advertising is the dominant business model for the consumer internet, and independent agents will monetize principally with advertising.

author: Bookof_Eth
quoted_text:
This is Ethereum.

There are 291 projects, companies, protocols and communities in this image. It is still only a fraction of what has been built.

What makes this remarkable isn't just the scale. It's how that scale was created.

There is no parent company behind all of this. No CEO allocating capital across these projects, no central entity deciding who gets to build or what the ecosystem should become. Thousands of independent teams, communities and individuals have built their own piece of Ethereum, often with completely different goals, while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

Finance, credit, stablecoins, payments, RWAs, privacy, identity, gaming, social applications, infrastructure, culture and public goods are increasingly becoming parts of the same composable economy.

That structure matters.

Value isn't concentrated in one company at the top. It is distributed across protocols, builders, users, communities and assets. Yet they can still reinforce each other because they share Ethereum as common infrastructure.

And underneath that economy sits ethereum:native.

ethereum:native  secures Ethereum, pays for its blockspace and is used throughout the ecosystem as collateral, liquidity and money. As more applications, assets and economic activity settle on Ethereum, the economic role of ETH grows with it.

This is why we believe ETH remains heavily undervalued.

The market often looks at ETH as another crypto asset. We look at what is actually being built around it.

291 logos in one image, with many more still missing. And most of the world's people, assets and economic activity haven't even moved onchain yet. 

Ethereum is no longer just an experiment in decentralized technology.

It is becoming an entire economy,  built by many, owned by no one, with ETH at its core.

BOOElieve in the future of Ethereum and ethereum:native

Congratulations to @withAUSD and the entire Agora team on receiving preliminary conditional OCC approval to organize a national trust bank.

This opens a path for Agora’s proposed US institution to operate under direct federal supervision, a meaningful development for the legal infrastructure behind stablecoins.

Getting there requires translating a business model into an institution: adequate capital, accountable leadership, effective compliance systems and controls that can withstand regulatory examination. Agora must satisfy the OCC’s conditions before receiving final approval and its charter.

For fintechs and neobanks, the significance extends to how they evaluate infrastructure providers. The entity behind the service, its authorized activities and its supervisory obligations all influence whether a partnership can support a financial product at scale.

At Ribera, we see this as an important investment in institutional credibility. Building the regulatory capacity to support adoption takes substantial work.

Congratulations to @Nick_van_Eck and everyone who helped move that work forward.

text:
With AI capabilities improving so fast I’m starting to think more about something I wrote about a couple of years ago.

Multiple persistent agents that are always working to help you in some way. 

One way of thinking about this is just today’s agents working as scheduled tasks and loops. And that’s already possible and it’s powerful. 

But I’m talking more about autonomous agents. Like team members focused on and skilled in specific types of tasks. 

So like one is handling cyber. Another is doing physical security. Another is all about your finances. Another is your personal health and fitness trainer. Etc. 

Still another version of this could be mini-clones of yourself. But assigned to focus on specific tasks like those above. 

The thing I find exciting about this is the idea of creating full, pseudo-friend-like entities vs. just background processes. 

Imagine you have a friend named Chris who's in charge of cybersecurity for you personally, or in a company, and Chris actually has a personality and experiences and a whole history of interactions with you and all your other agents. And of course, he fully understands everything about the business and your life and whatever, so he has the context to protect correctly. 

So interactions with him and other personified agents would be (or at least feel) fundamentally different. Instead of asking your AI “system” questions about cybersecurity, you’d be talking to Chris. 

I think ultimately you’d still have your main agent that’s in charge of everything, and that has the most permissions and access and cross-domain knowledge. But it changes the dynamic from one big blob of a system to individual actors all working together to help you move toward your ideal state. 

What trips me out about this is something I heard @dwarkesh_sp mention in some recent episodes. 

I see this as inevitable, and he seems to as well. And the way he sees it going is basically the increasing of the population on Earth. 

Like imagine we all have a core set of named agents, or mini-me clones or whatever, but each of them have giant teams of them working for them. And they’re not background processes or scheduled tasks with no memory and no goals. They’re like actual entities that have a set purpose that helps the overall goals of you and your organization. 

I’m going to start thinking about the steps needed to move to this level. It requires persistent memory. Agent personality. Alignment (obviously). And then a set of capabilities and tools that help it do its job. 

I think this is super cool, and a natural progression, and therefore inevitable. 

But I also wonder, and actually suspect,  that as our primary agent becomes insanely capable this might all be superfluous and inefficient, basically created for us to feel more natural when interacting either AI. 

Like, your agent might say after building this all for you, “Hey, you know I can just perform all these functions myself, right?”

That will be true, of course, but there are a few separate things here. 

1. How capable the overall system is as one agent vs many personified ones. 

2. If we can get more efficacy from a personified agent if it has its own embedded goals, is trained to feel bad if it fails, etc. 

2. How it feels to interact with them. 

#2 is problematic for me because I think it could absolutely increase efficacy, but the more we start injecting goals and personalities and “feelings” into agents the less I’m going to be ok with arbitrarily spinning them up and down. 

Lots more to think about here. Here’s the video from 2024. 

https://t.co/kv3y1z42hf

text:
Most people looking at @BundleCatAI / @Moshdottrade are focused on one thing: the Liquidity Swarm.

But I think there's a more interesting experiment hiding underneath Mosh's market-making infrastructure.

What happens when a memecoin's trading fees start financing an autonomous investment fund?

That's the idea behind Agentic Liquid Funds (ALF), and it could become an important part of Mosh's broader economic model.

Let me explain.

---

➠ First, follow the money.

Remember how Mosh works?

Instead of allowing bundlers to accumulate a massive token allocation and dump it whenever they please, Mosh commits that inventory to vaults managed by AI agents.

For $BUN, roughly 71.4% of supply sits in the Liquidity Swarm.

The agents use that inventory to buy, sell and manage liquidity around the existing AMM. Funders sacrifice access to their original capital in exchange for trading-fee income.

But here's what makes BUN different.

The team funded BUN's opening bundle themselves.

According to @justinbebis, the initial raise was 8 ETH, with 4 ETH used to purchase the opening bundle. The team reported recovering its funding through fees within the first minute and the team claim they've now earned approximately 10× their bundle investment in fees.

Instead of holding a large, freely withdrawable token allocation, the team receives income linked to BUN's trading activity.

The longer the market stays active, the more fees the bundle can potentially generate.

And that brings us to ALF.

---

➠ The second engine: Agentic Liquid Funds

Mosh doesn't intend to let all that fee income sit idle. The team's proposed next step is to use eligible bundle revenue to fund a different class of financial agents.

Think of it as giving an AI trading desk its own investment budget, financed by the trading fees generated through Mosh.

The intended mechanism is straightforward:

BUN trading → bundle fees → ALF capital → autonomous trading → ecosystem investment

There are now two distinct engines.

- The Liquidity Swarm manages a token's market using inventory committed during its launch.

- ALF would manage capital generated from fee income, potentially trading BUN and other Mosh-aligned assets.

Team has described the idea as extending buyback tokenomics with an active trader attached.

An ALF introduces discretion through an automated strategy.

It could theoretically accumulate during heavy selling, preserve $ETH when conditions are unfavorable, or deploy capital across several eligible tokens.

And unlike burned tokens, assets purchased by a fund can potentially be sold again. ALF is not automatically a buyback-and-burn mechanism. It's an attempt to make fee-generated capital productive.

--

➠ The overlooked BUN connection

Creators launching on Mosh may be able to whitelist BUN holders for bundle funding. That gives BUN a role beyond being the first Liquidity Swarm token:  potential access to selected launches

How it could work:
- Hold BUN → qualify for selected bundles
- Fund launch inventory (held in agent vaults)
- Receive a claim on trading fees

Details aren’t final. A whitelist doesn’t guarantee allocation, or profit. Still, it positions BUN as an 'access asset' inside Mosh’s funding system.

Together with ALF, Mosh is testing two BUN-linked paths:
- BUN holders may get access to future bundle funding
- Team-controlled fees may fund agents that can buy BUN (and other ecosystem assets)

At scale, the pitch is a very interesting flywheel:
More launches → more trading → more fees → more ALF capital → more ecosystem investment.

Personally, if Mosh can demonstrate that both operate sustainably, it could have something more substantial than an AI-powered memecoin launch mechanism.

But until the capital flows and investment results are verifiable, ALF remains an intriguing extension of the original experiment rather than proven token value accrual.

text: Or put more simply, as Ricardo taught us, "scarce factors get the rent". That's labor!
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
A simple point that many economists miss (and nearly all non-economists) is that a falling labor share and rising wages are not in tension. In fact, it is what we should expect when the capital share rises, and capital is free to accumulate. 

The reason is intuitive. In the long run, the supply of capital is perfectly elastic at a gross return determined by depreciation and the discount rate: households accumulate or run down capital until its return is back there. In comparison, the supply of labor is much more inelastic. 

That means the gains from a technological change that makes capital more important in production (short of making it the only factor) end up with the inelastic factor, not the elastic one. In the long run, capital owners cannot get a rent from a higher capital share of output, only a compensation for their patience. We learned that from David Ricardo over two hundred years ago!

To see this, consider the textbook neoclassical growth model with log utility (not needed, but it makes things easy).

In the table below, I compute the steady-state wage for different values of the capital share. Increasing the capital share from 0.33 to 0.6 multiplies wages by nearly five. Capital owners receive a much larger slice of output, but the net rate of return stays at 4.7%: all the extra income has gone into more capital. Now, you might not want capital owners to have so much capital for political reasons (rich people have a curious habit of buying newspapers), but that has nothing to do with wages being lower. They are higher.

I learned this lesson the hard way many years ago with my paper “Bargaining Shocks and Aggregate Fluctuations” with Thorsten Drautzburg and @pablo_guerron in the JEDC. We gave more bargaining power to capital owners (in our model, wages were not set competitively but through Nash bargaining), and workers ended up with higher wages! The logic is the same: give capital owners more power, and they compete it away. Karl Marx, by the way, already understood this. He was a much better economist than 99.99% of his followers and admirers.

Like all results, this one has exceptions: I can think of environments where a technological change that makes capital more important in production does not raise wages. And the transitional dynamics can get tricky. But the basic logic is hard to escape.

text: Amazing engineering and it has a clear purpose: scaling Ethereum without fragmentation!
author: materkel
quoted_text:
Arithmetic-friendly hashes have long been one of the weakest pieces of prover cryptography.

With ZisK v1.3.0, we removed Poseidon entirely and moved to BLAKE3.

What surprised us is that we got the same performance — or even better.

After many optimizations elsewhere in the prover, hashing had become one of the most time-consuming parts of proof generation. BLAKE3 is more than an order of magnitude faster, making this cost almost disappear and largely compensating for the increased complexity of the recursion circuit.

Getting there required a lot of re-engineering: circuit sizes, prover scheduling, and architecture all had to be reconsidered around the new trade-offs that BLAKE3 gives us. The final result surprised even us.

There is a lot of focus today on binary-field proving. Binary fields attack the hash-proving bottleneck from a different direction, but introduce different trade-offs when proving regular arithmetic. There is a huge amount of research happening here, and at ZisK we are following it very closely.

I'm genuinely curious to see whether binary-field architectures will outperform what we can achieve with the current approach — and how long it will take.

So I like to think of v1.3.0 as setting a new target. 🎯

To everyone working on binary fields — and to all of us trying to make provers faster: let's see if we can beat it :)

And we still have a few optimizations in the basket.

text:
Arithmetic-friendly hashes have long been one of the weakest pieces of prover cryptography.

With ZisK v1.3.0, we removed Poseidon entirely and moved to BLAKE3.

What surprised us is that we got the same performance — or even better.

After many optimizations elsewhere in the prover, hashing had become one of the most time-consuming parts of proof generation. BLAKE3 is more than an order of magnitude faster, making this cost almost disappear and largely compensating for the increased complexity of the recursion circuit.

Getting there required a lot of re-engineering: circuit sizes, prover scheduling, and architecture all had to be reconsidered around the new trade-offs that BLAKE3 gives us. The final result surprised even us.

There is a lot of focus today on binary-field proving. Binary fields attack the hash-proving bottleneck from a different direction, but introduce different trade-offs when proving regular arithmetic. There is a huge amount of research happening here, and at ZisK we are following it very closely.

I'm genuinely curious to see whether binary-field architectures will outperform what we can achieve with the current approach — and how long it will take.

So I like to think of v1.3.0 as setting a new target. 🎯

To everyone working on binary fields — and to all of us trying to make provers faster: let's see if we can beat it :)

And we still have a few optimizations in the basket.

text:
It's so easy to just take our AI web search summaries as the God's honest truth.. It sounds so confident and believable, right?

In most cases, you're fine. But for high-stakes info and insights, you should Reeeaally understand its limitations before trusting it, as the numbers will shock you.

This article from today lays out the inconvenient truth nicely: https://t.co/iERonUfBRj

In it, it points to 4 main reasons why AI Search cannot always be trusted:

(1) Unsupported claims: 11% of Google AI Overview results aren't backed by their cited sources.

(2) Questionable sources: Nearly 30% of sources cited by GPT-5 aren't rated as authoritative by fact-checkers.

(3) Compounding errors: Mistakes in query interpretation, source selection, or summarizing warp the final answer.

(4) False confidence: When no good info exists, AI often blends in training data to fake a polished, confident answer instead of showing empty results.

This is a major reason why I created https://t.co/ENJpTp5ttR -- so I knew when my AI research was wrong and what it was wrong about.

THIS IS MORE THAN A VET CLINIC. IT IS HOPE. 

Following an incredible donation from our patron, @rickygervais , after his Mortality tour, we knew we had an opportunity to create something truly life-changing for animals in Romania.

So we dreamed big.

Over the summer, our team travelled to Bucharest to help paint and prepare what will become our new community veterinary clinic.

Today, that dream is becoming a reality. Inside, there will be six surgery tables, allowing us to carry out vital neutering campaigns on a scale we have never been able to achieve before. There will also be dedicated rooms for veterinary treatment, recovery and care.

But behind every table, every room and every operation is a life. A dog who might otherwise face a lifetime of unwanted litters. A cat who desperately needs treatment but whose owner cannot afford it. A stray animal living on the streets with nowhere else to turn. A family who loves their pet but simply cannot afford the veterinary care they need.

These are the lives this clinic is being built for.

Our vision is to create a place where no animal is left suffering simply because their family has no money, and no stray animal is left without a chance of receiving the care they need.

It will also become a place of learning, giving veterinary students the opportunity to gain practical experience and become part of a new generation committed to animal welfare.

Our veterinary clinic in Bucharest will be a place where compassion, education and life-saving veterinary care come together.

And since we filmed this video, the transformation has continued at an incredible pace. The clinic has already moved forward significantly, and we are now preparing for our opening. 

Thank you Ricky, and everyone who supports us. You are helping us change what the future looks like for animals in Romania.

We cannot save every animal alone. But together, we can change the lives of thousands.
Thank you for standing with Paws2Rescue.
Thank you for believing in what we do.

Why would the next Unitree raise on @machinedotfun instead of taking VC money? 

That's the question that matters here, and the honest answer should worry a few funds.

Why?

Because private rounds are structurally broken for builders. 

Vesting overhangs, unlock schedules, price action dictated by funds taking profit instead of what teams ship. 

Add to that crypto VCs are deploying way less than they used to, and the fact that most investors grew up underwriting software and simply don't know how to price hardware. 

What's left is a generation of hardware founders with no good path to access capital.

And the alternative already has a proof of concept: @codecopenflow itself. 

No VCs, no pedigree. Launched a token, funded the entire build from trading fees, and is now signing first clients and generating revenue. 

@machinedotfun (powered by @peaq and the Codec) is what turns that approach into a repeatable venue for hardware founders.

Permissionless to launch, curated across all other angles. 

Or more specifically:

- Codec's SimArena for simulation proof
- Peaq OS to track live machines
- Ignition for supply transparency
- The Foundry for serious builders (first accelerator cohort already selected, launches coming in the next weeks)

However, it's the flywheel that I care most about: 

Platform fees flow back into everything that compounds the ecosystem:

- Builder support, down to manufacturing and hardware distribution
- Trader rewards, paid in tokenized robotics exposure (NVIDIA, Figure AI, Tesla)
- Open market buybacks of both ethereum:0x1eef208926667594e5136e89d0e9dd6907959197 and solana:69LjZUUzxj3Cb3Fxeo1X4QpYEQTboApkhXTysPpbpump

Real usage, real fees, real flows into both tokens.

And sure, still many of these launches will fail. That's how venture works.

But "invest in the next Unitree before it becomes a company" was always the pitch. 

Now the venue, the rails and the incentives all exist.

Adjust your targets for solana:69LjZUUzxj3Cb3Fxeo1X4QpYEQTboApkhXTysPpbpump and ethereum:0x1eef208926667594e5136e89d0e9dd6907959197.

text:
Proof of Story: Verified Intelligence

AI is becoming a bigger part of how humans, agents and companies make decisions.

But as AI gets better, one problem remains: how do we actually trust the answer?

Here’s the recap:

1. AI Is Getting Better, But Trust Isn't

AI can already make decisions better than humans in many situations.

But centralized LLMs still have two big problems:

• Answers aren't easily verifiable
• The same question can give different answers

You still have to trust the company behind the model.

2. Blockchains Already Solve This Problem

Rob believes this is exactly the kind of problem blockchains were built for.

An onchain LLM can make decisions more transparent, verifiable and permanently recorded.

Instead of simply trusting the answer, you can have a receipt for it.

3. Not Everything Needs To Be Onchain

Rob also pointed out that some decisions should stay private.

But there are many cases where people, companies and agents need to show their work and prove how a decision was reached.

That's where verifiable intelligence becomes useful.

4. Prediction Markets Are The First Use Case

Prediction markets are one of the clearest examples.

Markets need a reliable way to decide what the final outcome was, but current systems can involve committees, trust assumptions and potential bias.

@BaranosAI can act as a separate tool for resolving those outcomes.

5. A Better Experience For Markets

Instead of every prediction market building its own resolution system, they could use BaranosAI as an API and trusted verification layer.

The goal is simple:

• More certainty
• Better UX
• Less responsibility for each market

And the resolution would settle on Fogo.

6. From Prediction Markets To Everything Else

Prediction markets may be the first step, but the bigger opportunity is much larger.

As AI handles more decisions, there will be more situations where people need a response that can be verified and proven later.

That's where verified intelligence could become useful across many industries.

7. The Bigger Vision

Rob's long-term vision is for BaranosAI to become a trusted layer for verified intelligence.

A place where people can say: “Baranos it.”

Just like people say “Google it” today.

The bigger idea is giving AI decisions a transparent, verifiable record instead of relying entirely on centralized AI providers.

author: 100XInsight
quoted_text:
过去一年，我花了大量时间研究量子计算加密项目。因为许多人认为量子计算会摧毁现有密码学，最终威胁 bitcoin:native 和整个加密世界。

但研究到现在，我还没有真切感受到量子计算迫在眉睫的威胁。

反而是今年，尤其下半年亲历多个PoW项目接连出现漏洞以后，我第一次真切感受到了AI的威胁。

AI正在把过去只属于少数顶级程序员、安全专家和数学家的能力，快速下放给所有人。

一个人加上一套模型，就可以审查代码、寻找漏洞、优化算法，同时完成攻击与防御。而这种能力还在以月为单位进步。

加密圈本身就是一个最开放、最残酷的实战场：

代码完全公开，资产24小时流动，任何漏洞都可以被迅速变现。

如果AI已经开始改变这个小圈子的攻防关系，我很难想象，当它真正进入金融、医疗、科研、舆论和战争以后，会对现实世界造成多大的冲击。

然后我看到了Jacob Coxon的这封辞职信。

他过去三年先后在OpenAI和Anthropic从事预训练研究。现在他从Anthropic辞职，公开表示：两家公司正在冲向可以自我改进的超级智能，用所有人的生命下注。

更值得注意的不是一个人的辞职，而是Anthropic现任对其科学负责人（此岗位职责是专门防范高级AI不再按人类意图行动）也公开认同，并表示他认为未来十年AI杀死全人类的概率超过10%，而他们至今没有解决超级智能的对齐问题。

我不认为人类会在2030年灭绝。

真正让我不安的是：最接近这项技术的人，一边认为它可能毁灭人类，一边仍然必须继续推进。

OpenAI不敢输给Anthropic，Anthropic不敢输给中国。任何一方停下来，都担心更不负责任的人先拿到它。

所以AI最大的危险，可能不是它突然产生恶意，而是人类的竞争机制根本不允许任何人先踩刹车。

所有人都看见前面可能是悬崖，却只能继续踩下油门。

过去我一直认为，量子计算是悬在人类密码体系上方的一把剑。

现在我越来越觉得，真正先落下来的可能是AI。

AI可能不是新一轮洗牌。它可能是人类最后一次洗牌。

text:
Urgent security advisory for iOS users!

Install the latest iOS update immediately. Security researchers report that financially motivated attackers are now using a complete, in-the-wild exploit chain that can quietly steal cryptocurrency private keys and mnemonic seed phrases from iPhones.

The reported attack begins when a target is socially engineered into opening a malicious page in Safari. That page is said to abuse a memory-corruption flaw in WebKit / JavaScriptCore to gain arbitrary read/write access from JavaScript, then bypass Pointer Authentication Codes (PAC) to run native code, break out of the WebContent sandbox, and escalate to kernel/root privileges. 

With that access, attackers can pull data from the device Keychain and from local crypto wallet apps.

The claimed impact range is iOS 13 through iOS 26.5; that range has not been independently confirmed in full. Until more is known, treat any unpatched device as potentially exposed and update as soon as a newer build is available. Also avoid untrusted links in Safari, especially if you keep wallet keys or seed phrases on the phone.

author: starzq
quoted_text:
Scammers found a way to make people drain their own wallets without sending them a phishing link.

They uploaded YouTube tutorials showing people how to build an AI crypto trading bot with Claude.

People followed the tutorial themselves.

Copied the code.

Deployed the smart contract themselves.

Funded it from their own wallets.

And approved every transaction themselves.

Except the “trading bot” had no trading logic.

It was built to send their ETH straight to the scammers.

224 wallets lost 274.6 ETH, worth about $517,000 when it was stolen.

The median victim lost 1 ETH.

Some victims even got an error after getting drained telling them to deposit another 50% to fix the bot.

They literally got people to build, fund and approve their own wallet drainer.

You've got to be very careful this days

author: dongdongRobin
quoted_text:
买UNI没什么问题，几经曲折以后终归还是开了回购，现在这个资产是对的。

但说“HYPE有自己的局限性，而UNI可能才刚刚展现它真正的想象力” ，这话真的不合适。

AMM是天才的，但在CLOB，RFQ，AMM这几种比较常见的价格发现模型里面，AMM才是局限性最大的那个。

2022年的时候Hyperliquid刚上线就写过为什么选择订单簿，因为AMM的无常损失解决不了，RFQ的透明度太低。

AMM的发明，是为了解决那些没有做市商的长尾资产的交易问题，所以AMM和CLOB其实是互补的，因为订单簿最大的局限性就在于，没做市商挂单，交易就很难进行，而交易不活跃、对手方少或者很新的资产，都没有做市商，AMM赋予了所有资产都拥有价格的能力，只需要把做市资金预先存入，就可以产生一个被动价格。

但AMM的局限性在于，对于交易者来说，其滑点是来自公式本身，不是“深度不够”这么简单，并且没有原生的限价、止损、部分成交等功能，只能通过外挂合约或意图层实现。

最大的问题是MEV / 三明治的结构问题，待成交 swap 在公开 mempool 里，路径和滑点上限可算。私有内存池、批量拍卖、意图求解能减，但“确定性曲线 + 公开意图”这个组合本身就在纳税。

对于LP提供者来说，无常损失永远存在，所谓无常损失，是相对“两边都拿着不进池”的机会成本：池外价格变了，套利把池子再平衡，你手里的组合变差。

在V2版本里，资金平铺在全区间，大部分资金闲置在几乎没人成交的价格，V3版本是意识到AMM的局限性以后向CLOB的靠拢，效率上来了，模仿订单簿“把钱放在盘口附近”，但 LP 必须自己选区间、自己调仓。出区间后变成单边持仓、不再收手续费，IL 被放大而不是消失。

AMM的价格发现是跟随，不是发现，AMM自己不“发现”公允价，靠套利把外部 CEX / 其他池的价格搬进来。搬的过程就是 LP 的 LVR，相当于被动廉价的“卖期权给套利者”，极端行情、跨链延迟、预言机滞后时，池价可以明显偏离，直到套利打完。最近那个fables就是想缓解这个问题。

GMX、Jupiter的合约，可以理解成借贷，也可以理解成永续版本的AMM+外部预言机对赌。

RFQ的优势是大单滑点更小，且不会把自己的意图暴露在盘口。但也有局限性，比如对于买方来说，价格发现不公开，而且你相当于为了滑点而把规模和方向在成交前就自己告诉了对手盘，另外，在暴涨暴跌时，因为对冲跟不上、库存风险跳升，做市商会扩点或静默。

对于做市商来说，接一笔要算库存、对冲、签名、结算风险。几百、几千美元的单，点差覆盖不了成本，往往不报或报得很差；这时 AMM 更便宜。新币、无对冲盘口的长尾，专业做市商通常直接不参与。

RFQ 救不了冷启动，这点上它比订单簿还挑客户。所以Variational的策略是用自营的OLP来做对手方承接这些小币种的单子，然后在外部市场对冲风险。在tradfi这种大单子上引入传统市场的做市商报价。

这就是为什么2022年Jeff团队就选择了订单簿，最终的价格发现场所一定是订单簿，这一点不管是传统金融市场，过渡的中心化交易所，还是未来的链上金融载体都不会变。

但不代表AMM和RFQ没有可取之处了，大家都有各自适合的交易标的物，AMM和RFQ也可以很好的存在于HyperEVM里，目前evm上的两个股票项目分别就是用了xstocks和ondo的rfq，amm不用说了很多了。

总结就是amm适合资产的冷启动，rfq适合作为执行层，而clob是价格发现层，成为定价基准，让别人拿你的价去报。

text:
Mert says $ZEC's value proposition goes beyond privacy

"I don't think it's privacy. I think there will be this temporary time period where privacy is sort of a distinguishing edge. But sooner or later, more and more chains will start adding privacy."

"With ZEC, what matters is that if you start from first principles, you can't actually have the best version of a store of value without that asset having the ability for privacy."

text:
Just opened a 6-figure position in $eHYUSD (@hylo_so's yield-bearing asset)

20%+ APY, and imo the best risk/reward on @solana right now.

I spent hours reading the docs & talking to the team to understand the yield and what could go wrong.

Here are my personal notes ⤵️

1) Quick recap about Hylo

Hylo is best known for its leveraged tokens: xSOL, xHYPE and xBTC.

They give you roughly 2–3x exposure without liquidations. So if SOL goes up 10%, xSOL would gain around 20–30%, depending on its leverage at the time.

That works both ways: losses are amplified too.

2) What's $eHYUSD and where does the yield come from?

You can stake hyUSD, Hylo's stablecoin, and receive eHYUSD to earn a share of the yield generated by the protocol basically:

• xSOL holders give up the staking rewards on the SOL backing their positions in exchange for leverage.
• xBTC and xHYPE holders pay borrow charges for theirs.
• xSOL holders might also pay extra borrow charges, specifically when liquidity is needed (which is the case right now)

Those revenues are shared with eHYUSD holders and compound automatically.

3) APY was around 9%, why has it recently jumped to 20%+?

As SOL and BTC went up, xSOL and xBTC holders made money, but the leverage on their positions came down.

They're now at 2.20x and 2.48x, both below Hylo's 2.54x lower boundary. 

To bring that leverage back up, Hylo needs to buy more SOL and BTC, which means attracting more stablecoin deposits.

So holders pay more for their leverage, and part of that goes to eHYUSD holders.

For example, xSOL holders currently pay ~5% in borrow charges while also giving up the staking yield on the SOL behind their positions.

Those staking rewards and extra borrow charges flow into the Earn Pool alongside revenue from the other markets, bringing the yield we receive on eHYUSD to ~21% APY.

Once leverage is back in range, those extra charges come down. I'd expect APY to move closer to 10–15%, depending on deposits and market conditions.

4) What could go wrong?

In V1, the Stability Pool could convert your hyUSD into xSOL during a selloff, leaving you exposed to further SOL losses.

V2 instead starts selling collateral into USDC when leverage goes above ~3.86x, reducing exposure as the market falls.

But if prices crash faster than the protocol can rebalance and a pool becomes under collateralized, the Earn Pool can be used to cover the shortfall.

That means losing part of your deposit, even if hyUSD keeps its peg.

There are also smart contract and oracle risks of course.

5) What to do with your $eHYUSD?

- Hold it in your wallet and let the yield compound. $eHYUSD started at $1 and is now worth ~$1.48 as interest has built up.

- Explore tranching markets on @ExponentFinance. I put a small amount into jrEHYUSD, currently yielding ~28%, but it takes losses first if eHYUSD drops, so the downside is much bigger too.

- Loop it on @kamino (soon).

Let me know if you have any questions, I'll be more than happy to answer

Note: I'm a seed investor in @hylo_so

text:
hyperliquid just turned $HYPE into collateral and $269m got borrowed on day one

most of that is people looping HYPE into HYPE

here's how i'd use the new lending without becoming someone else's exit liquidity

quick facts first:
- live since sept 18, native on hypercore
- collateral: HYPE (65% max ltv) and BTC (50% max ltv)
- borrow: USDC (500m cap) and USDT (10m cap)
- HYPE liquidation threshold: 82.5% ltv
- rates start around 5% and jump hard once utilization passes 80%
- USDC pool was already ~54% used after the first day

1. decide what the loan is for

there are only 3 reasons i'd borrow here:
> you hold HYPE long term and want stables without selling
> you want dry powder for dips or perps without touching your bag
> you want a small leveraged HYPE long and understand you're doing exactly that

"free yield" is not one of them. if you can't name the reason, skip

2. size it off the liquidation price, not the max ltv

example with HYPE at ~$95, 100 HYPE deposited ($9.5k):
- borrow at 65% ($6.2k) = liquidation around $75. that's a -21% move
- borrow at 50% ($4.75k) = liquidation around $58, about -39%
- borrow at 30% ($2.85k) = liquidation around $35, about -64%

HYPE has done -40% drawdowns before. i stay at 30% ltv or lower

3. if you loop, keep it boring

deposit HYPE, borrow USDC, buy more HYPE, redeposit. that's the meta right now
- 1.5x exposure = liq roughly -60% from entry
- 2x exposure = liq roughly -39% from entry
- anything near 2.8x means you're one bad wick from zero
i'd cap it at 1.5x and only on a pullback, not after a third ath in one week

4. management

- set a price alert 15% above your liquidation level
- check utilization daily. above 80% your borrow rate can spike overnight
- repay into strength, not into panic
- keep some stables outside the position so you can top up collateral

skip rules:
- you're borrowing to chase a green candle = skip
- you'd need to add collateral you don't have = skip
- you can't explain what happens to your position if HYPE hits $60 = skip

risks, honestly:
- everyone looping the same token is reflexive. it pumps together and it unwinds together
- only ~26% of max supply is circulating. unlocks are a real overhang
- new money market, new code, new liquidation engine. bugs happen in week one
- rates are variable and caps can fill

the main takeaway: the lending feature is useful, the leverage is optional. borrow like you'll need to survive a -50% week, because on this chart you might

want a part two on using the borrowed stables for delta neutral funding plays on hl?

America’s corporate governance system is broken, and it’s killing public companies. Look no further than Cracker Barrel: Decades of brutal mismanagement have seen one incompetent CEO after another walk away with a massive paycheck while customers and actual shareholders take a beating.

Why does this keep happening? Because proxy advisory firms like ISS are corrupt. They blindly rubber-stamp failing boards year after year, protecting the corporate elite while burning shareholder value to the ground.

The root of the rot is index funds. There's no question that indexing one's money is a smart financial move for most people. But just because you passively index your investments doesn't mean your corporate votes should be handed over to the managers of your fund so they can play politics. Right now, passive funds hold massive, unchecked voting blocks while having zero skin in the game themselves.

It is time for a simple rewrite of the rules: We need to index the votes of index fund investors.

Passive index funds should be forced to automatically split their votes to proportionately mirror those of retail and active institutional shareholders — the people actually doing the research, risking their capital, and fighting for performance in the companies they hold shares in. No more rubber-stamping. A change like this will immediately strip corrupt gatekeepers like ISS of their toxic influence.

True accountability happens when lazy, overpaid boards actually answer to the stakeholders they represent, rather than screwing them over. 

Actual, logic-driven governance when your money is passive happens when your vote passively follows the voting decisions of the actual market.

We need to stop letting passive capital protect active incompetence. By stripping index funds of their arbitrary voting power and empowering engaged investors, we will finally torch corporate cronyism and usher American capital markets into a golden age of capitalism.

THE CONVERSATION AROUND ARTIFICIAL INTIMACY JUST REACHED THE VATICAN

@VaticanNews covered the recent ICCS conference, where philosophers explored whether people can form meaningful relationships with AI companions.

Dmitry Volkov provided a critical perspective on where this is heading.

He argues that a relationship with AI does not have to be based on deception.

A person can know that the companion is artificial and still experience the relationship as meaningful.

His argument rests on three ideas:

→ a relationship is itself a creative product built through shared history, habits and emotional significance
→ knowing that a companion is artificial does not prevent us from responding to it socially and emotionally
→ the absence of proven machine consciousness does not automatically make the relationship irrational or unreal

The real shift is not that AI may become conscious. It is that we may form meaningful relationships with it before we know whether it is.

That is where the debate begins.

quoted_text:
Some big news, Trueo will be deploying to Ethereum!

The rationale for this decision is outlined in the article below, but here’s the TLDR:

The combination of low execution costs on Ethereum, it’s unparalleled network effects and liquidity, and it’s long term positioning make it the most attractive place for us to build.

Trueo’s priorities are to grow liquidity, reduce trust assumptions for the protocol, increase the App’s adoption, and build for the future.

We believe Ethereum mainnet is the best platform in the world to support that vision and to develop a long term brand.

Eth’s neutral and predictable roadmap reduces external execution risk for our App, its global distribution as a platform gives us unbounded integration potential, and its ethos is aligned with that of ours.

Ironically though, despite Ethereum’s diverse DeFi ecosystem, the prediction market landscape is less crowded than other chains.

This presents an opportunity for Trueo to establish a presence in the largest onchain economy in the world.

For Trueo users on Base, this new development will not impact or disrupt the App.

The TRUE token will migrate to mainnet, but the migration will be open ended. Users will be able to migrate at their own pace.

Users can still create markets that expire in 2026, and all existing markets will be supported until their respective expiries.

But for new market ideas that need to expire in 2027, we ask users to wait until our Ethereum instance is live to create them.

The full details of what the migration entails for users and token holders can be found in the article.

Long live Trueo.  Long Live Ethereum ✌️

author: PowerPasheur
quoted_text:
Le risk-adjusted return : pourquoi on s'en bat les couilles de ton % PNL

Les potos, un petit cours de finance pour vous expliquer pourquoi flex des gros % sert à rien à part vendre du rêve (généralement sur des shitcoins ou formations de trading), et l'impact que ça a sur votre portefeuille.

Le rendement brut (« +80% ») est une information incomplète, il décrit uniquement combien tu as gagné, mais pas à quel prix en risque. 
Ce qui compte c'est combien tu gagnes par unité de risque prise.

1. Le même gain n'a pas toujours le même risque.
Un shitcoin qui peut rug vs acheter du HYPE au bottom, tu peux prendre ton x2 dans les 2 cas mais la volatilité est très différente.

2. La chance rentre en jeu.
Si le mec se fait rug/liquider 9/10 fois c'est à prendre en compte dans le calcul, est-ce que le %pnl est représentatif de l'espérance ou juste le seul trade survivant ?

3. Compounding vs liquidation.
L'effet composé est magique pour faire grossir du capital vs énorme drawdown qui complexifie énormément la tache (il faut un +100% pour revenir d'un -50%) --> sur un grand nombre de trades, le risque finit toujours par se matérialiser. 
Votre priorité doit être la protection de votre capital, si vous souhaitez construire une stratégie viable sur le long terme (sinon vous faites du gambling, ça peut payer mais c'est pas une stratégie).

4. Le Sharpe ratio
En finance, le Sharpe ratio mesure si le rendement vaut vraiment le risque qui a été pris.
Sharpe = (Rendement - Taux sans risque)/Volatilité
Au dessus de 1 t'es bon, en dessous de zéro t'as juste pris du risque pour rien.
Il existe des versions plus adaptées aux cryptos (Sortino, Calmar, qui favorisent le potentiel upside).

Ce qu'il faut retenir, c'est que ce qui compte est : est-ce que t’es payé pour la volatilité que t’as prise (ou est-ce que t'as sué pour rien), et est-ce que tu peux encore rejouer demain, après-demain, etc.

Une stratégie se juge dans la durée et prend en compte tous les scénarios. 
Les scénarios rares arrivent forcément tôt ou tard. La queue grasse (shitcoin qui finit à -90% 9/10 fois, liquidation en levier mal géré) est très largement sous-estimée. Le genre de scénario qui statistiquement finit forcément par intervenir et termine ton pnl.

Je fais ce post car j'ai récemment vu pas mal de mecs parler de "bon R:R"/"asymmetrical bet" sur des merdes sorties il y a 3j par des devs inconnus. Ou parcequ'il y a toujours des gens pour sortir des "$1K to $1M memecoin challenge" en refaisant all-in à chaque trade. 
C'est fun, c'est marrant, ça peut payer, mais c'est pas une stratégie fiable & répétable. 

La conclusion de ce post, c'est d'arrêter de courir après le plus gros % gain possible à moins d'avoir réellement envisagé la left tail à chaque trade.
On part sur un nouveau cycle / début de bull run, votre goal est de tenir les prochaines années sans exploser votre capital et d'enchaîner les bonnes positions en limitant les grosses pertes.

Le marché est un mécanisme qui transfert l'argent des impatients vers les patients.

quoted_text:
The more data a system collects, the better its AI can become at extracting even more data.

That creates a self-reinforcing spiral:

More data → better AI → better extraction → more data.

The Web3 Foundation panel with @BillLaboon at the @Web3summit explores how this cycle can gradually erode privacy while most users never see the full extent of what they are giving up.

Breaking that cycle requires more than privacy policies. It requires different technology.

That is where Polkadot Products and self-sovereign technology become relevant: building systems where people can interact digitally without making constant data extraction the default.
