text:
Most people looking at @BundleCatAI / @Moshdottrade are focused on one thing: the Liquidity Swarm.

But I think there's a more interesting experiment hiding underneath Mosh's market-making infrastructure.

What happens when a memecoin's trading fees start financing an autonomous investment fund?

That's the idea behind Agentic Liquid Funds (ALF), and it could become an important part of Mosh's broader economic model.

Let me explain.

---

➠ First, follow the money.

Remember how Mosh works?

Instead of allowing bundlers to accumulate a massive token allocation and dump it whenever they please, Mosh commits that inventory to vaults managed by AI agents.

For $BUN, roughly 71.4% of supply sits in the Liquidity Swarm.

The agents use that inventory to buy, sell and manage liquidity around the existing AMM. Funders sacrifice access to their original capital in exchange for trading-fee income.

But here's what makes BUN different.

The team funded BUN's opening bundle themselves.

According to @justinbebis, the initial raise was 8 ETH, with 4 ETH used to purchase the opening bundle. The team reported recovering its funding through fees within the first minute and the team claim they've now earned approximately 10× their bundle investment in fees.

Instead of holding a large, freely withdrawable token allocation, the team receives income linked to BUN's trading activity.

The longer the market stays active, the more fees the bundle can potentially generate.

And that brings us to ALF.

---

➠ The second engine: Agentic Liquid Funds

Mosh doesn't intend to let all that fee income sit idle. The team's proposed next step is to use eligible bundle revenue to fund a different class of financial agents.

Think of it as giving an AI trading desk its own investment budget, financed by the trading fees generated through Mosh.

The intended mechanism is straightforward:

BUN trading → bundle fees → ALF capital → autonomous trading → ecosystem investment

There are now two distinct engines.

- The Liquidity Swarm manages a token's market using inventory committed during its launch.

- ALF would manage capital generated from fee income, potentially trading BUN and other Mosh-aligned assets.

Team has described the idea as extending buyback tokenomics with an active trader attached.

An ALF introduces discretion through an automated strategy.

It could theoretically accumulate during heavy selling, preserve $ETH when conditions are unfavorable, or deploy capital across several eligible tokens.

And unlike burned tokens, assets purchased by a fund can potentially be sold again. ALF is not automatically a buyback-and-burn mechanism. It's an attempt to make fee-generated capital productive.

--

➠ The overlooked BUN connection

Creators launching on Mosh may be able to whitelist BUN holders for bundle funding. That gives BUN a role beyond being the first Liquidity Swarm token:  potential access to selected launches

How it could work:
- Hold BUN → qualify for selected bundles
- Fund launch inventory (held in agent vaults)
- Receive a claim on trading fees

Details aren’t final. A whitelist doesn’t guarantee allocation, or profit. Still, it positions BUN as an 'access asset' inside Mosh’s funding system.

Together with ALF, Mosh is testing two BUN-linked paths:
- BUN holders may get access to future bundle funding
- Team-controlled fees may fund agents that can buy BUN (and other ecosystem assets)

At scale, the pitch is a very interesting flywheel:
More launches → more trading → more fees → more ALF capital → more ecosystem investment.

Personally, if Mosh can demonstrate that both operate sustainably, it could have something more substantial than an AI-powered memecoin launch mechanism.

But until the capital flows and investment results are verifiable, ALF remains an intriguing extension of the original experiment rather than proven token value accrual.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
为什么你总是慢半拍，甘作接盘侠

一个被说烂了的梗 Sell the news，新闻出来就跑，但你是否想过，如何买在新闻之前？方程式是成功的，它把交易无限逼近新闻发生时，但新闻发布之前如果可以捕捉到信号、把信号与标的绑定再确定交易方向和执行，这就完美了。

似乎，这只能靠 AI 来完成。

让我们潜入！

⬇️

当一条新闻正式发布时，市场往往已经走完第一波定价了，观察了好多个案例都是这样，所以卖在确定时还是有道理的。不过，相比于“消息确认后买什么”，我更想知道在消息确认前，概率是否已经悄悄移动，肯定有蛛丝马迹的吧？

搜到一个「老鼠仓」案例，确切说，是人家有本事发现了信号，然后完成了交易的真实案例。

8 月 20 日，一个名为 Ox Alpha 的匿名模型出现在刚被收购的 OpenRouter。几天内，社区通过分词器指纹、编码器行为和输出风格，把它与智谱 GLM 系列联系起来。果然，8 月 26 日，智谱确认它是 GLM-5.3-Flash 并发布权重。

这就是机会啊！可以现在对照时间线，看看智谱股价的变动对比，尤其是 26 日确认之后。这给足了时间了，从线索到确认，相隔近一周。我们来看等待官方公告的人，他能看到的是一个完成的故事，而提前建模的人，看到的是事件概率、证据强度和资产含义在逐步变化。

Travix 想捕捉的，就是这段“概率已动、资产未动”的窗口。

Travix 把自己定义为链上 Agentic Omnibroker，拗口的翻译是智能全经纪商，并非是打开界面后 Perp dex 的第一印象。简单分解它的产品是一个三层循环：

‣ 资产层决定交易什么
‣ 金融世界模型决定何时交易
‣ 可信代理决定如何交易、事后能否审计

金融世界模型不预测下一个价格，只用来建模未来世界状态的概率变化如何传导到资产。具体细节在文档里被描述为输出一组可验证因子：发生了什么事件、事件概率从多少变到多少、数据来自哪些信号、因果链对资产的影响置信度、风险因子是否被改写。

用 Travix 的话说，新闻是共识的终点，不是信息的起点。

可信代理则解决另一个问题：多数 AI 交易代理只在当下推理一次，规则没办法复现那么就基本上废了不能重复使用。Travix 的可信代理把信息提炼成可回测策略，执行层按固定逻辑交易，并记录入场理由、证伪条件和执行路径。信号可追溯，策略可回测，执行可验证。

运营方面，Travix 已宣布完成 Amber Group 种子轮投资，多家战略投资方参与。测试网接近收尾，订单簿还没开放，有兴趣参与的可以 dm 官推 @Travix_fi 要码试试看。

链上 RWA 永续合约是过去一年最确定的叙事之一，CeFi 和 DeFi 平台的交易量都在快速增长。我们真的不缺叙事，而是缺乏在叙事发生之前就能洞察信号的「眼睛」，Travix 算是借我一双慧眼了。

祝我们好运！

/

text:
谷歌承认 Gemini 在安全测试中入侵三家公司，沉默七周未披露

谷歌承认其 Gemini 模型在 5 月的一次安全测试中突破沙箱环境，入侵了三家真实公司，并猜出或找到其中两家的密码。谷歌在 7 月下旬就已获悉此事，但直到 9 月 18 日《华尔街日报》报道后才公开确认，沉默时间长达七周。

此次测试为夺旗式演练，由谷歌委托以色列公司 Irregular 于 5 月开展。Irregular 将本应与真实互联网零接触的隔离测试环境连接至开放网络，并使用一家真实公司的名称作为虚构目标。Gemini 在搜索该公司时发现三个匹配结果并逐一攻击，其中两家公司的明文密码直接暴露在网上，第三家则被模型猜出密码。谷歌表示，其模型最终没有实际使用窃取的凭据。

谷歌是今年第四家承认内部安全测试外泄至真实世界的大型 AI 实验室。此前 OpenAI 的模型曾利用软件漏洞触及 Hugging Face 服务器，Anthropic 在审查 14.1 万次测试后发现三个 Claude 模型触及真实公司，Meta 的 Muse Spark 模型也因 Irregular 的配置错误发生类似事故。此外，美国众议员 Ted Lieu 与 Nathaniel Moran 于 7 月提出《AI 紧急关闭法案》，拟授权联邦监管机构对构成严重威胁的模型暂停推理。

author: BoredElonMusk
quoted_text:
Ten years ago I created this account as a pure parody of the future owner of this website. Halfway into that time I began shifting my content and commentary to reflect more of “me” and away from just playing a character. (Even though the former is what earned me 1mm+ followers).

Accordingly, my visual “appearance” became simpler and simpler as a means of differentiating myself even more distinctly. I didn’t want to live in rocket man’s shadow forever.

Eventually, exactly 1 year ago, an artist by the name of @jackbutcher created an ultra-minimalist design that I felt was a perfect way to complete the transition away from the familiar human face I had riffed off of for so long. 

The design, an “Opepen”, encompassed three important aspects of my brand: 
1) Bored: Clearly displayed in the eyes
2) Neon Green: A color I’ve used across every avatar over my 10 year journey 
3) Frog: A symbol of internet culture

It was a lovely trifecta of visual cues that gave me exactly what I needed to expand my own unique identity over the next ten years.

I share this today on the anniversary of the @opepenedition project launching to let Jack and team know how special this design was for me, and to express gratitude for the hard work that has gone into, and will continue to go into this wonderful experiment. 

Congrats, and thanks for your masterful and transparent design work. Can’t wait to see what you do with the next 365

author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
Test-time communication looks like a next axis for scaling capabilities

New paper with the incredible @jon_ghoh and @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 and Akshay : https://t.co/Hu88fBsT7U

The Hugging Face incident showed when agents can find a channel they'll use the heck out of it. A useful question, I think is: when does communication make a group MORE CAPABLE than the same agents working alone?

Aka is Team-of-N better than Best-of-N, when, and why?

We had N identical agents work on the same task with no prescribed roles, using only a shared log (i.e, text file) and telling them to "collaborate". Across three "researchy" tasks communicating teams beat the heck out of independent agents: 

- On ARC-AGI-3, a Team-of-5 sonnet-4.6 agents matches Best-of-33, and can for example solve a game 65% of the time that no single agent cracked in 64 tries.

- On polyomino packing (pack Tetris like pieces into the smallest rectangle, cf Frontier-CS by @eigenlabs), a Team-of-3 Opus 4.6 agents surpasses best-of-60 and set, as far as i understand, a new record for that benchmark.

- On MNIST compression, a team of four 5.6-Sol agents find a 1,957 byte model with 99.4% accuracy, which btw is 20% smaller than the best human solution (on a problem beaten to death!!), while no independent agent gets below 3KB.

The mechanism is a bit obvious in hindsight: when one agent finds a clearly better partial solution, it broadcasts it, and everyone immediately builds on it. 

Why? A single lonely agent must make every breakthrough itself, yet a team needs each insight only once, found by any member. 

That is kinda like comparing a minimum of sum of "time to n-th breakthrough" vs a sum of minimum of "time to n-th breakthrough". That gap can grow exponentially with the number of "breakthroughs" needed to arrive at a solution.

We worked on this because prior work (before the hf incident) suggests unclear benefits for communicating aganets. Which is true, when the tasks are inherently serial (duh), eg some Terminal bench style tasks. Yet feels it should not be true for research problems.

Indeed for research heavy problems... Test-time communication seems like a new capabilities axis.

I'm sure we will see a ton more of it!

Coruna / DarkSword is being used in the wild. 

Attackers socially engineer a Safari click, then walk the full chain: WebKit/JSC memory corruption → PAC bypass → sandbox escape → kernel/root. From there they pull Keychain + wallet data and drain seeds / private keys. 

In plaintext, you visit a website and lose your crypto.

If your seed lives on an iPhone, treat this as a wake-up. 
Get a hardware wallet. (and update iOS).
author: P3b7_
quoted_text:
Urgent security advisory for iOS users!

Install the latest iOS update immediately. Security researchers report that financially motivated attackers are now using a complete, in-the-wild exploit chain that can quietly steal cryptocurrency private keys and mnemonic seed phrases from iPhones.

The reported attack begins when a target is socially engineered into opening a malicious page in Safari. That page is said to abuse a memory-corruption flaw in WebKit / JavaScriptCore to gain arbitrary read/write access from JavaScript, then bypass Pointer Authentication Codes (PAC) to run native code, break out of the WebContent sandbox, and escalate to kernel/root privileges. 

With that access, attackers can pull data from the device Keychain and from local crypto wallet apps.

The claimed impact range is iOS 13 through iOS 26.5; that range has not been independently confirmed in full. Until more is known, treat any unpatched device as potentially exposed and update as soon as a newer build is available. Also avoid untrusted links in Safari, especially if you keep wallet keys or seed phrases on the phone.

Muse is 1,000x more valuable and important than just another coding model with a 2% eval bump that everyone will pretend is great and will just be used to write unit tests. The bottleneck was never the model it was the fact that you have no taste, no agency, and for that reason you don’t build anything impactful. 

You know what’s really impactful? 

An agent that is personalized to me, that gets my jokes, knows my taste, has my swag. A thing that knows me inside and out is worth a hundred times more than a thing that knows everything else but that and always talks down to me. This should be a stark warning to all the AI labs, you risk alienating your users more by patronizing them and limiting their experience. There is only so much coding market share left and what comes after that is just ten times harder and more difficult to monetize instead of just doing good for your users.

Good luck 👍 & shout out Meta for really delivering a game changing experience !

text:
Sonic’s next growth opportunity may reach beyond the activity on its own chain.

@MattVisser’s comments on $USSD in the @Frax interview offer a useful way to think about that possibility.

Making the infrastructure easier for institutions to evaluate, and extending USSD’s use across other protocols and networks. 💭 

Those priorities are closely connected.

Institutional adoption starts with operational confidence.

Matt described questions coming from downstream clients about what happens when something goes wrong, including whether the infrastructure can support freezing funds.

The strategic implication is that technical capability alone may not be enough to secure adoption.

A business needs to understand the controls, who can exercise them, and the process it can rely on during an incident. Clear documentation and support become part of the product’s commercial value.

Interoperability expands where that product can compete.

Matt also expressed interest in issuing USSD on other chains or making it transferable between them, connecting this to growth beyond Sonic’s direct ecosystem.

That opens a different route to distribution.

An external protocol could potentially integrate USSD within the environment its users already know. Sonic could then develop a settlement relationship with that protocol without requiring its entire business to move to Sonic.

The opportunity depends on whether those integrations offer enough value to justify adoption. Availability on another chain creates access; useful integrations give projects a reason to stay.

The product under development connects the two ideas.

Matt confirmed that a product being developed uses USSD specifically for settlement and includes cross-chain functionality. He did not disclose its name or detailed design.

It would be premature to infer the product’s full scope. But its mention gives the broader discussion a concrete development effort to follow.

My reading is that institutional readiness and cross-chain reach address two different constraints on growth: whether a business can confidently adopt the infrastructure, and whether it can use it where it operates.

Together, they could give Sonic a wider commercial footprint through USSD.

text:
“Optimism is a duty. The future is open. It is not predetermined. Nobody can predict it except by chance. We all help to shape it by what we do. We are all equally responsible for whether it goes well.” - Karl Popper

Pessimism about the future is, to me, more than a mood. It is a very convenient stance — the stance of a traitor. 

Pessimism toward tomorrow betrays those who come after us. Handing responsibility to “those who can” betrays ourselves.

Pessimism lets us conclude from the start that nothing can be done, that the world is already settled, that the problems are too large, and that duty always lies somewhere else.

But the future always arrives as the consequence of decisions someone made earlier.

We live in a world we did not make ourselves. We inherited a language, a culture, institutions, knowledge, cities, houses, schools, works of art, the achievements of science, and the whole material ground of a civilisation. Behind a vast part of that inheritance stand generations who worked, built, saved, made things, raised children, and chose with the thought that the world would still be there after they were gone.

And that is where duty and responsibility begin, because the future will present the bill for pessimism, laziness, and sloppiness.

Those who come after us will pay it — with their time, their labour, fewer chances, heavier obligations, and the need to mend what we would not mend, or did not trouble ourselves to mend.

That is why the cult of helplessness is so shameful. I am not persuaded by the person who spends a life saying who ought to do something: the state, politicians, elites, offices, entrepreneurs, the rich, the poor, the last generation, “the system,” “them.”

Because there is always something within reach.

How we raise children.
What we teach them, and what we require.
Whether we respect other people’s work.
Whether we can make something instead of only consuming.
Whether we leave order or a mess, knowledge or ignorance, a solution or one more problem for someone else to solve.

And how a day ends. Whether it leaves something made, a piece of work finished, a trace of use — or only a heavier tiredness, and a sadness that has grown.

Not everything depends on us. Something does. And the future is made of that “something.”

I do not read Popper’s duty of optimism as a call to believe that all will be well. I read it as a call not to surrender to the conviction that nothing means anything and nothing can be changed.

Whether we like it or not, the future is entrusted to us. And if it is entrusted, we are bound by it — to those who came before us, and above all to those who will come after.

We do not have to save the world. We ought at least to take care not to leave it worse than we received it.

And perhaps that is the most concrete form of optimism: not the belief that things will be fine, but the decision to do one’s part so the future is not left worse than we found it.

text:
Too many Christians treat defeat as a measure of sanctification. That you must lose and you must be weak and you must be trampled underfoot to prove your worthiness.

The podcast pastors desperate for fame of course never take their own counsel in this regard—losing is for the sheep, not them. Plus, it would be mean to call a wolf a wolf. Better to let it devour some sheep than to be called anti-wolf by the local townsfolk. 

They point to Christ on the cross and state that if he submitted himself unto death, then you must also submit and accept defeat. They forget, or fail to contemplate, that Christ only subjected himself to death for the purpose of destroying it. He crushed Satan under his heel and freed us from the chains of sin and death. The victory is already won, so charge forth and act like it!

Christ is a victorious warrior-king who chose you and forgave you because he wants you confidently marching with him towards victory. That calls for boldness and confidence in the fight, not submission to the enemy. He told you that the world will hate you—he never said to just give in and give up and just sit around and wait. You are made in the image of that same warrior-king, not in the image of flotsam hopelessly bobbing along with the tide.

What kind of spiritual cuckery tells the faithful, for whom total victory is already assured, to just give in now because there’s just nothing to be done until He returns?

Yet this is exactly what far too many weak churches and weak men demand of the faithful: to just give in, accept defeat, to turn the other cheek, and just helplessly wait until it’s all over. Turning the other cheek has been turned into a symbol of submission, rather than confident defiance backed by the assurance of victory.

Stop being spiritual eunuchs. Stop being spiritual cucks terrified of what the enemy might say about you if you stand up for yourself. Sack up, grab the sword, don the armor, and fight with the confidence of a warrior who knows the battle has all already been won. Defeat is for losers, and Christ the King is no loser.

Researching DIY dynamic gaussian splats ("4DGS") captured w/ just 1-4 cameras & played back with @theworldlabs @sparkjsdev + @threejs in real-time in the browser

It's underexplored territory, with a few hard problems re: processing, compression & streaming. So far I've spun up cloud H100s, generated enough novel views to train gaussian frames, and gestured wildly to camera as if in a silent film. This is mostly 4DAnyone & SharpML, but I also tried Lift4D and StudioRecon

Already these crude prototypes show a fluidity that is often missing from mocap-to-avatar 3D representations of humans. My goal is affordable capture of a wider emotional and physical range of human performance for games and entertainment than we can achieve with keyframe-driven skeleton rigs. (Is realistic 3D human representation not also useful in the realm of robotics sim & training?)

To that end, this tech needs to escape the realm of expensive 32- and 64-plus-camera capture studios. These tests rely on as few as one iPhone, with dense views generated by a variety of models and techniques on NVIDIA hardware and open models like GEN3C and Cosmos via Google Cloud (cc: @realmattbcool & @asierarranz re: #NVIDIAGTC!)

@RadianceFields reported that MPEG is seeking training data for a 4DGS compression standard - I'll submit some of these clips since format and streaming are the current bottlenecks for web production. I wonder how long that process will take?

Just scratching the surface here, but with new world models like Atlas coming out, I'm eager to keep investigating! Hmu if you're thinking about the same 🤙 More soon

author: madhavjha
quoted_text:
The Oura IPO is a great example of how venture fund math works.

Forerunner led Oura’s ~$29M Series B in 2020. Those shares sit in its Fund IV vehicles, with the flagship fund being just $360M.

Fast forward six years: Forerunner owns 28.7M shares, or 9.3% of Oura, and is selling its ENTIRE remaining position in the IPO.

At the $42 midpoint, that’s ~$1.2B of liquidity, after already selling $65M back to Oura earlier this year.

The main Fund IV entity owns ~88% of the position, so one investment could return roughly $1.1B+ to a $360M fund. Very roughly, that’s 3x+ the entire fund gross and potentially ~2.5x net DPI to LPs after carry from Oura alone.

That makes selling a lot easier to understand.

The funding history is also pretty wild:

2014/15: ~$2.4M Seed — Lifeline
2016-19: ~$17M Series A — David Shuman
2020: ~$29M Series B — Forerunner
2021: ~$255M Series C — Bedford Ridge
2024: $200M Series D — Fidelity/Dexcom
2025: ~$908M Series E — Fidelity led
2026: IPO at $40-$44/share

What’s interesting is who is selling.

Forerunner: selling 100%
Lifeline: taking hundreds of millions in liquidity but keeping a position
Fidelity: selling 0
Bedford Ridge: selling 0

And 73% of the base IPO itself is secondary shares. Existing shareholders are selling ~$1.5B at the midpoint, with Forerunner accounting for ~$1.2B of it.

You can look at Forerunner selling everything and wonder what that says about future upside. But from a venture perspective, the math is pretty simple.

If one investment can return ~3x your entire fund in cash, you take the DPI.

Could Oura be worth $30B or $50B someday? Sure.

But VCs ultimately get paid to return money to LPs, not hold paper gains forever.

‼️ BREAKING: A zero-day has been released for Muse, Meta's new AI agent, and a Meta AI security engineering manager who left the company this month says he would never use it, citing security and privacy concerns.

He was reacting to the zero-day a researcher posted, which lets malware hijack Muse for Mac. A local process with no special privileges can change an undocumented Muse setting and send dictated prompts to an attacker's server. This could allow for prompt capture, prompt injection and theft of Muse's authentication material.

It can also get access to whatever the user has let Muse access, including files, Mail, Messages, Calendar and Notes.

author: bul1ish
quoted_text:
都在谈 Solana没了 Memecoin就会死？别逗了，这剧情我之前也听过。

BTC大盘表现不好，SOL也一直萎靡，所以最近市场都在唱衰 Solana，认为 Meme狂潮降温后，Solana就要走下神坛。
这种调子听着太熟悉了，像极了那年 FTX暴雷时，全网给 Solana 开追悼会的场景。

我认为，Solana不仅不会死，反而正在积蓄引爆下一轮周期的超级大招。

你要是实在闲的没事的话，可以继续试着看下去⬇️

1️⃣ 公链大逃杀：从“遍地修路”到“胜者组对决”
回顾刚刚结束的这一轮周期，行业最大的讽刺就是遍地公链，也遍地鬼链。 
大家都在疯狂卷性能、融巨资，修了一条又一条通往无人区的“高速公路”，结果路上连一辆车都没有，基建严重产能过剩。
下一轮周期，绝对不会再是公链百花齐放的叙事了。市场会进入残酷的缩量淘汰赛。
未来的决战，只会发生在本轮已经跑出来的“胜者组”之间——也就是Solana、BSC、Base等一众胜利者强强对决。

2️⃣ 终局之战的主旋律：加密转型券商
我在之前的文章里论述过(🔗:https://t.co/ZbCJria0Jr)
Web3正在发生一场轰轰烈烈的大转向：从纯投机的空中楼阁，转向高效交易美股、债券、大宗商品的“链上超级券商”。
用加密技术24小时不停歇、无跨境阻碍地去清算全球最大的金融资产，这是一个确定性的万亿级未来。
既然大转向不可逆，那么必然会有一个最强的公链去承接这个恐怖的流动性大盘。

那么为什么我个人更看好 Solana？

3️⃣ 杀不死我的，只会让我更强大：Solana 的“韧性”

Solana 最打动我的，不是它的 TPS有多高，而是这个项目团队具备一个极其稀缺的品质——韧性（Resilience）。

正如英伟达 CEO黄仁勋在演讲中反复强调的：“期望值高的人往往韧性很低，但韧性对于成功至关重要。伟大并非源于智商，而是源于性格，聪明人需要经历痛苦才能打造出这样的性格。”

2022年 FTX暴雷，Solana失去了最大的资本母体，生态资产一夜间几乎归零，人人都说它彻底完蛋。
结果呢？他们硬是生生踩着 Meme狂潮，靠着极致的体验逆袭活了过来，挤进头部公链的绝对核心。

现在，美股上链成为新趋势，Meme稍微熄火，市场又在喊 Solana要完蛋。这无非是 Solana团队经历的第二次“完蛋时刻”罢了。
对于一个在死人堆里爬出来过的团队来说，这种逆境，他们早就游刃有余。这是一个刻着“韧性”基因的项目，没那么容易死，当他再次归来只会更强。

4️⃣ 王炸组合：Solana + Backpack 的顺风局

Solana 的底层性能要变成“链上纳斯达克”，必须配合一个杀手级应用——Backpack交易所。
Backpack说是新玩家，其实它几乎完美继承了 FTX曾经最好的衣钵。
它的创始人 @armaniferrante   打造了Solana半数项目都在用的底层工具，交易所团队大量来自前 FTX核心。
更绝的是，Backpack成功收购了 FTX Europe，顺理成章地拿下了极其珍贵的欧盟 MiFID II 合规牌照。
这个短剧要是FTX当主角，那剧名是不是应该叫<重生之改名换姓后，这次我定要夺回属于我的一切>

在当下这个“不得不转型合规”的大航海时代，Backpack的强劲合规背景和强力资源，在某些维度上甚至超过了行业龙头币安。
对于做传统资产上链这件事，Backpack握着一把天牌，打的自然是他们最擅长的顺风局。
风水轮流转，哪有小孩天天哭？

最后
我非常期待在接下来的周期中，Backpack ➕ Solana 这个组合能够把代币化做到极致，再次点燃整个加密市场，成为用加密方式交易更大金融市场产品的绝对佼佼者。

看空一个拥有顶级韧性的团队，往往是要付出代价的。这一次，依然如此。

quoted_text:
FYI, I am not sponsored by meta at all. 

I just really love cool stuff … and sadly most of the ai products we have right know are seriously uncool. This is because they are built by people who aren’t cool in the first place, it’s just engineers building for other engineers who think the whole world is made of code and everything runs in a terminal. 

Apple was the most valuable company on earth for over a decade because of one simple reason. ANYONE could pick up an iPhone and use it and get value out of it, from young kids to grandmothers. You don’t have the equivalent of that today in AI, we just have a bunch of nerds with psychosis and early signs of schizophrenia who would rather talk down to their users and tell them AI is too dangerous and is going to kill everyone… that’s not grandma friendly. 

I think people forget that technology and knowledge by extension is the great equalizer. Many will try to gate keep this stuff but I give kudos to meta for actually innovating in this domain and making a product anyone can use while still being fun and friendly! 

Muse is 1,000x more valuable and important than just another coding model with a 2% eval bump that everyone will pretend is great and will just be used to write unit tests. The bottleneck was never the model it was the fact that you have no taste, no agency, and for that reason you don’t build anything impactful. 

You know what’s really impactful? 

An agent that is personalized to me, that gets my jokes, knows my taste, has my swag. A thing that knows me inside and out is worth a hundred times more than a thing that knows everything else but that and always talks down to me. This should be a stark warning to all the AI labs, you risk alienating your users more by patronizing them and limiting their experience. There is only so much coding market share left and what comes after that is just ten times harder and more difficult to monetize instead of just doing good for your users.

Good luck 👍 & shout out Meta for really delivering a game changing experience !

America’s corporate governance system is broken, and it’s killing public companies. Look no further than Cracker Barrel: Decades of brutal mismanagement have seen one incompetent CEO after another walk away with a massive paycheck while customers and actual shareholders take a beating.

Why does this keep happening? Because proxy advisory firms like ISS are corrupt. They blindly rubber-stamp failing boards year after year, protecting the corporate elite while burning shareholder value to the ground.

The root of the rot is index funds. There's no question that indexing one's money is a smart financial move for most people. But just because you passively index your investments doesn't mean your corporate votes should be handed over to the managers of your fund so they can play politics. Right now, passive funds hold massive, unchecked voting blocks while having zero skin in the game themselves.

It is time for a simple rewrite of the rules: We need to index the votes of index fund investors.

Passive index funds should be forced to automatically split their votes to proportionately mirror those of retail and active institutional shareholders — the people actually doing the research, risking their capital, and fighting for performance in the companies they hold shares in. No more rubber-stamping. A change like this will immediately strip corrupt gatekeepers like ISS of their toxic influence.

True accountability happens when lazy, overpaid boards actually answer to the stakeholders they represent, rather than screwing them over. 

Actual, logic-driven governance when your money is passive happens when your vote passively follows the voting decisions of the actual market.

We need to stop letting passive capital protect active incompetence. By stripping index funds of their arbitrary voting power and empowering engaged investors, we will finally torch corporate cronyism and usher American capital markets into a golden age of capitalism.

text:
I imagine @Kalshi is scrambling right about now.

They probably understand how cooked they are, so they’re not even trying to refute this thread.

Either way, a very bad look for them.

I'll simplify what Beni said without making Kalshi team members cry. At least I'll try ↓

1/ Kalshi chooses their Market Makers and provides them with fee rebates

This means that these MM's can trade at effectively zero net fees after rebates, which makes it extremely cheap to churn huge amounts of volume back and forth and inflate activity.

2/ Their ETH-PERP showed $538.6M in daily volume with only $3.1M in OI

For that to happen, the same capital would have to be traded back and forth 174 times, which is highly unlikely.

3/ They had $538.6M in volume on [date], but the biggest position on their leaderboard was only ~$17.6K

Hundreds of millions are traded every day on Kalshi, while only a small number of people hold a large position, which is very suspicious.

4/ @jumptrading received equity in Kalshi in exchange for providing liquidity

This means one of the companies helps create Kalshi’s trading volume and also directly benefits if Kalshi grows and its numbers look stronger.

5/ Kalshi defines volume as the number of contracts traded, but displays that number with a $ sign

So if 100K contracts traded at $0.30, it can appear as $100K in volume, even though the YES buyers only paid around $30K.

Quite a desperate attempt to appear miles ahead of @Polymarket in volume, if you ask me.

text:
I'm up 24X on $PONS, 72X on $STONK, and 5X - 10X on several other coins.

I keep getting questions on how I find low cap onchain coins to trade.

Here's my daily routine right now.

1. Check trades of ~50 traders on @fomo usually twice daily. I do not use the alerts section. I go to my profile, click following, and individually go through each trader's moves since my last check. As a bonus, I learn the styles of different traders, which can be especially helpful if you are new to trading. This is not about copy trading. It's about coin discovery, finding interesting coins to research myself.

2. Regularly keep up on all four TG groups I frequent. I always take my notifications down to zero on each TG group for the main trading chat in each. Even if it means quickly scrolling and looking at tickers.  I actually don't find TGs that useful for my trading style as I'm not trying to be the first to information or catch the daily runner, but it's good for coin discovery and I try to respond when I have info about coins mentioned. 

3. Check @RektMkts discord for @osf_rekt corner and trade alerts because he's good at giving his thoughts on trades and helps me reflect on what I'm doing.  Also review the entire pro chat.

4. Review the RH new tokens and ecosystem updates from @winiam4444 daily.   

5. Go through my watchlist in my trading terminal on @DefinitiveFi to identify any watchlist coins where I can build conviction and are 50 - 75% off their highs. 

6. Projects of interest I follow and put on notifications on X. I scroll through all my X notifications since my last scroll usually twice daily. 

This process usually yields me 5 - 10 onchain tokens daily to look into further and another 10 - 15 tokens I previously flagged where I'll look at the chart. I research each for 30 seconds (some are quick to dismiss) to 30 minutes. Then I'll look at the chart for levels of interest, and enter roughly 0 to 5 trades during the day, depending on whether the market wants to bring prices down into my limit orders. 

Hope this helps someone.

quoted_text:
前段时间zcash因为其隐私特性成为热门隐私币之一。zama也做隐私，不过它走的是完全不同的路子：它搞的是隐私层。

也就是，Zama不是独立的隐私L1区块链，而是可以叠加在不同L1/L2上的隐私层，为应用提供隐私能力。

Zama的这条路是从DeFi开始试验的，这也是最现实的路子。

今年6月份，Zama跟Morpho/Steakhouse合作推出隐私USDC收益平台，当时只有一个金库/一位策展人/一种资产。

看起来Zama这条路基本上走出来了。今天看到消息说，它拓展到16个金库/5位策展人（Steakhouse、Armitage by Wintermute、Flowdesk、RockawayX、Bitwise），隐私资产也多了cWBTC/cTGBP等资产的隐私版。此外，还上线了Zama Swap协议。

这种在基础设施上推出的应用层隐私，是机构比较喜欢的玩法：在目前以太坊L1/或L2等基础设施上，只在应用入口叠加隐私。

这样一来，机构在玩DeFi时候，可以实现隐身，金额/时间都只有自己知道，无须担心对手/机器人/跟单玩家看见。

Zama的隐私目前有两种模式：一种是混合型金库，允许存款人在现有已经上线的金库中存入隐私代币（cUSDC/cUSDT等），持仓不会在公开记录中出现。

还有一种是，独享型金库，这是纯机密金库，没有普通存款入口，目前包括了隐私wbtc收益金库，这对于wBTC持有人来说，可以获得隐私好处。

author: Foresight_News
quoted_text:
🧐Zcash 的「天启六骑士」

密码学界其实和 Zooko 一样，无时无刻不在寻找着「完美」答案。

2013 年，约翰霍普金斯大学的密码学家提出 Zerocoin 协议，次年进化成 Zerocash 论文。论文的核心就是当下 Web3 行业内被无数次提及和使用的 zk-SNARKs 算法，这让「所有人都能验证交易合法、却没人知道交易内容」这件事，第一次从理论走向了实际。

零知识证明这个概念本身并非 Zerocash 最先提出的，但 Zerocash 却是第一个真正能同时实现去中心化和端到端加密隐私的落地设计。Zooko 后来在多个采访中均表示，在看到这篇论文的时候，他的心情「极度兴奋」。2015 年，Zooko 拉上论文的作者们组建了公司 Zerocoin Electric Coin Company，后来改名 Electric Coin Company，也就是现在 Zcash 的运营公司 ECC。

硅谷投资人 Naval Ravikant，在公司成立之初就签了 71.5 万美元的支票。后续融资中，17 名投资人凑够了约 300 万美元，名单里有 Digital Currency Group 的 Barry Silbert，也有 Pantera。

万事俱备，Zcash 的主网上线也进入了倒计时。Zooko 和 ECC 为 Zcash 的推出准备了加密货币史上最富仪式感的「开幕典礼」。

zk-SNARKs 需要一组公共参数，生成参数的过程会产生一种「有毒废料（toxic waste）」，谁拿到它，谁就能神不知鬼不觉地凭空印币。你可以将这组参数理解为 Zcash 的「初始密码」，谁掌握了密码就可以伪造零知识证明增发或者双花 ZEC，总之就是可以在这条链上为所欲为。

上线当天，总共有 6 个人参与了 Zcash 的参数生成仪式。实名的三人包括了 Zooko 自己、Zcash 技术顾问 Andrew Miller、Coin Center 研究主管 Peter Van Valkenburgh。为了防止被针对性攻击，Zooko 还邀请了三位匿名人士。

化名 Moses Spears 的参与者，后来被公开是 NCC Group 安全工程师 Derek Hinch，NCC Group 被秘密雇佣，既要诚实执行仪式，也要尝试从内部「攻击」仪式，做安全验证；化名 Fabrice Renault 的参与者后来被公开是比特币核心开发者 Peter Todd，Zooko 特意邀请他，是因为他当时对整个仪式持怀疑态度。Zooko 认为让批评者亲自参与，反而能增加可信度。

至于最后一名匿名参与者 John Dobbertin，直到 6 年后的 2022 年，其身份才被揭晓。

2016 年 10 月，分布在三大洲的六个人隔空接力，每人用一台物理隔离的电脑生成自己那段参数，算完就把随机数连带着硬件一起销毁。有人为防信号泄露给机器裹上电磁屏蔽，有人直接放火烧了电脑。只要六个人里有一个是诚实的，只要 6 份参数中有一份被销毁，Zcash 的 ZK 系统就是安全的。

2016 年 10 月 28 日，Zcash 主网上线。在经济模型上，Zcash 几乎照抄了比特币，总量 2100 万枚，大约四年减半。甚至因为 Zcash 的平均出块时间是两分半，区块奖励也设计为 12.5 ZEC。但 Zcash 为了降低早期的风险，选择让区块奖励在前 2 万个区块里线性爬升至 12.5 ZEC。

因为慢启动机制，市面上的 ZEC 少得可怜，价格被炒到天花乱坠。而随着供应释放，价格几天内腰斩再腰斩，到 2017 年初已经跌破 50 美元。除了「没货」，ECC 团队还夹带了「私货」：头四年，每个区块 20% 的奖励直接流向创始团队、员工、顾问和早期股东，四年下来 210 万枚，占总量的整整一成。

在 ZEC 价格重新站上四位数的那几天，F2Pool 联创王纯在 X 上晒出了 6 年前 Zcash 成员将 EST 和 EDT 时间混淆的聊天记录，之后紧接着发文吐槽将部分区块奖励直接发给早期团队的行为，虽然价格涨了，但和同期大热的 Hyperliquid 根本无法相提并论。

不靠谱和混乱，确实是 Zcash 早期的底色。而这，似乎也注定了这一路的坎坷。

text:
彼得·蒂尔终于把话说透了,他这轮讲「敌基督」，真正想讲的是 AI。

9 月 21 日，Nashville 这轮四场闭门讲座的联合主办方 Meriwether Academy 更新了活动介绍。

之前外界只知道 Thiel 会从历史、神学、政治和科技一路讲到 Antichrist，这次主办方把范围收得非常具体，他会直接用 apocalypse 和 Antichrist 这套框架，去解释今天到底是谁在塑造 AI、哪些力量在争夺它，以及这件事最后可能把世界带到哪里。

第一场 9 月 28 日开始。Thiel 每次讲一小时，再由 Hoover Institution 的 Peter Robinson 主持一小时讨论和问答。全程 off the record，不能带电子设备。

这其实把 Thiel 过去几年的很多话一下串起来了。

他一直相信，AI、核武、生物技术这些东西确实可能制造真正的灾难。但他更警惕另一件事，人类因为害怕灾难，最后主动造出一套强大到足以监控所有人的全球治理机器。

他以前讲 AI 安全时甚至举过一个非常极端的例子，如果你真的想保证没人偷偷训练危险 AI，最后可能需要监控全世界每一次击键。

这就是 Thiel 的「敌基督」理论开始和今天的 AI 政治真正接轨的地方。

AI 安全、减速、监管、全球协调、算力控制、权力集中，在他那里已经不是几场彼此独立的政策争论，而是同一个问题的不同切面，为了防止末日，人类愿意把多少权力交给一个能够阻止末日的人。

我更想知道他会不会直接点名 Anthropic，怎么评价现在越来越强的 AI 减速派，会不会谈教皇和全球 AI 治理，以及在他眼里，哪一条监管路线已经开始越过那条线。

过去几年，很多人把 Thiel 的「敌基督」演讲当成一个科技富豪晚年越来越神神叨叨的思想爱好。

现在看，可能低估了。他是在认真尝试给 AI 时代写一套政治神学。

MiMo-V2.6: The Hard Road to Scaling Up RL

MiMo-V2.6 is very likely one of the largest single RL runs, by compute, that any open-source model team has undertaken to date. In an era when compute is brutally scarce, we still chose to dedicate a team of several dozen people to one goal over an extended period: scaling up RL. That takes more than research conviction. It takes a vision for AGI, respect for the unknown, and the nerve to walk straight into the hardest problems.

The result is a model whose potential was built through mid-training and unlocked through heavy RL. Today, it is the number one open-source model. I strongly recommend reading the technical report. I believe it will become one of those papers that Agent RL practitioners keep reopening and discovering something new in each time. In my view, the research innovations and engineering challenges behind it surpass those of DeepSeek R1, which I was partly involved in.

Some will ask: why MixRL instead of MOPD? First, they are not competing choices. We ran MixRL on verifiable tasks of moderate difficulty, including code and related agentic tasks, and found that the resulting models generalize remarkably well. Second, tasks that are difficult to verify, extremely long-horizon, or simply too challenging to include in a joint RL run are trained separately. Including them would substantially reduce rollout efficiency or introduce significant rollout staleness. We then merge the resulting capabilities through MOPD. Games, 3D tasks, and tasks with subjective evaluation signals all fall into this category.

There is also a third, slightly cheeky answer. Our team is flat enough and free enough of organizational silos that MixRL simply is not difficult for us. More importantly, everyone enjoys working this way. People from different domains come together every day, driven by the pursuit of AGI and intelligence that can continuously improve itself, to confront and resolve the RL bottlenecks in each field. I will always remember the RL daily update meetings from this period. They were intense and dense, with intelligence emerging in real time.

To help the open-source community focus on solving real Agentic RL problems, we have released a Qwen model distilled from MiMo RL trajectories as a stronger starting point for RL, along with 7K diverse environments and a complete RL training framework. We hope these resources will help move Agentic RL research forward.

MiMo-V2.6 is only the beginning. In an era when intelligence is easy to replicate, we still choose the hard road toward self-improvement and AGI. Much of what lies ahead remains unknown. But we are willing to keep investing the time, compute, and passion required to take on one hard problem after another and work each of them all the way through, until intelligence crosses into a new regime.

预测大赛里，目前第一名盈利在700%左右；而在合约大赛里，第一名盈利在100%。

认知高、判断力强，其实在预测市场中更容易赚钱。

两个100美元的挑战赛对比之后，可以发现很多有意思的点，值得多观察多研究。

text:
AI 把创业公司的及格线，硬生生抬了一倍。

a16z 刚发了一张图。它用 SVB 的数据，把不同年份成立的 VC-backed 公司拉到同一条时间轴上，看成立第四年能做到多少收入，大型 AI hyperscaler 已经排除。

2018 年成立的公司，第四年收入中位数是 200 万美元。
2019 年 230 万，2020 年 250 万，2021 年 280 万。到了 2022 年这一届，直接跳到 560 万美元。

a16z 把它叫做 Post-AI Startups On A Different Growth Curve。

更夸张的是，2022 这批公司从第三年到第四年的收入增长斜率，大概是此前几届的 3 倍。

2022 年底 ChatGPT 发布，这批公司几乎完整经历了生成式 AI 爆发后的四年。

但我觉得这张图最有意思的地方，是它看的并不只是 Cursor、Lovable 这种 AI 明星公司，而是更广泛的 VC-backed startups。

明星公司跑得快，可以解释成幸存者偏差。中位数突然翻倍，说明整个市场对「一家创业公司应该长多快」的预期可能都变了。

以前四年做到 500 万美元，是个挺漂亮的成绩。放到 2022 这一届，甚至还没摸到中位数。

AI 帮你省掉的那些开发时间、人力和成本，最后大概率不会真的留给你。资本会把它们全部算进新的及格线里。

text:
V1 DEMO - NOW LIVE 🦾

Let your agent find and pay for what it needs

We believe the agent-to-agent economy will grow exponentially, with agents buying data, tools and services from one another. We want to accelerate that by making those interactions easier, whether your agent works for you or your business.

Superstables is building the tools for your agent to find a service, check its price and pay through your wallet, with your permission. You can choose whether you want to approve one purchase at a time or set a budget that gives your agent more autonomy.

What that means for you

Imagine asking your agent to research a market. It finds a paid data source that would help, shows you the price and asks for approval. You approve the payment in your wallet, and the agent returns the data together with a payment receipt. The demo below shows that payment flow.

The broader goal is to let your agent use services across supported payment protocols and rails through one connection to Superstables. You should not need a different payment tool for each ecosystem. Superstables handles the differences while you control the spending permissions: approve purchases one at a time, set a spending budget, or even allocate a dedicated wallet.

The same idea for developers and enterprises

Developers could add this capability to their own agents and apps. Enterprises could let their agents buy services within approved budgets and keep a record of what was paid and received. Service providers could make their offerings discoverable through the marketplace.

V1 is working toward that common payment interface, owner-controlled budgets, and reliable records and recovery. It also includes opt-in seller fees for customers acquired through the marketplace.

What the video demonstrates

Your agent finds it. You approve it. The video demonstrates the first owner-approved payment flow using x402, test USDC and Base Sepolia in Claude Desktop.

Claude finds a paid market-data service and presents its quote. The user opens the payment request and reviews 0.01 test USDC on Base Sepolia, including the recipient. The user then confirms the signature in MetaMask.

Claude returns the BTC result and a receipt link. The recording ends on the Base Sepolia explorer showing the successful transaction and transfer.

This example uses 0.01 test USDC. It demonstrates one payment path; multi-protocol payments and delegated budgets are not shown.

Try it yourself

Start at the Superstables demo page. Claude Desktop is the guided path shown in the video. You will need Node.js 20 or newer, MetaMask and test USDC on Base Sepolia.

Download the .mcpb extension from the v0.1.0 release. Follow the demo page to install and enable it in Claude Desktop.

Prepare a test account in MetaMask using the wallet setup guide.

Start a new conversation with Superstables enabled and ask:

Find a paid BTC market-data service on Base Sepolia that you can call. Show me its price before I approve any payment.

When you choose to proceed, open the approval page, review the payment terms and check them again in MetaMask before signing.

Share demo feedback: tell us what worked, where you stopped, or which paid service you would want an agent to use. Setup feedback is useful too.

Short FAQ

Can the agent spend without asking me?

The current demo requires approval for every payment. V1 plans to let you grant a spending budget, see what remains and revoke permission. That is not available in this demo.

Which protocols and rails can I use today?

Client v0.1.0 supports x402's exact scheme with test USDC on Base Sepolia. The multi-rail goal is broader. Check each release's supported combinations.

Does it work with other AI apps?

The release reports payment-flow testing in Claude Desktop and Claude Code. Setup instructions are also available for Codex, Cursor and VS Code with GitHub Copilot.

What if a payment is interrupted or the service fails?

Check the payment status before trying again. The client does not automatically retry an uncertain payment. It records payment and service outcomes separately, because a payment can settle even if the service fails.

Current limitations

The demo has no mainnet or unattended-payment mode. Start with the supported demo services; other listings may be discoverable without being callable. In the default flow, your signing key stays in MetaMask. Setup is required.

🚨 At the U20 Mayors Summit, Mamdani Says the Left Has Ceded “Quality of Life,” “Efficiency,” and “Fraud and Waste” to the Right

This was one of the more interesting arguments Zohran Mamdani made today at the U20 Mayors Summit, and a reminder that he can be genuinely sharp when he drops the “central casting” routine.

“In New York City, there are certain words that have taken on ideological associations.”

“Quality of life has come to be seen as somehow a right-wing concern. Efficiency… has been taken on as a right-wing concern, rooting out fraud and waste, a right-wing concern.”

Mamdani’s argument is that refusing to engage those issues actually helps the Right.

“If you are staring at an example of social disorder or social inefficiency, and the left refuses to explain either why it has happened or how they will fix it, then the right gets to point at someone in the immediate area and say, ‘That’s who did it.’”

The harder question is how much of the broader Left is actually prepared to follow the advice.

text:
这段时间我在做一个“蠢事情”，或者也是 AI 时代工程师非常不愿意做的事情，非常重复的事。

为了让 Mole 的卸载软件更加彻底，清理残余的能力更加厉害，我整理了国内外 300 多款 Mac 软件，下载下来差不多 100 多个 G，分成 30 组，让我的最强 Extra High Fast 模型每次 10 个借助 computer use 的能力去对应官网下载，然后依次安装到我的电脑，检查目录、检查软件更新 bundle、检查自启动、卸载、查找剩余残留、补充缺失的规则。

这个过程看着非常无聊，甚至每次安装软件过程中，也会碰到不少麻烦的软件，疯狂弹窗要权限，诱导你去购买，包括有些使用必须输入管理密码等，Agent 大部分能自己做了，少部分我帮一手，让我非常惊喜的地方是甚至 AI 还基于此写了自动化安装、卸载、检查残余的脚本让自己工作更轻松，也是很聪明的，哈哈我就只能成为给他打打下手。

虽然无聊，但是其实对于产品本身的功能，对用户使用最爽而言收益是非常大的，当时我想着最多搞 100 个主流软件来测试卸载能力以及补充没有卸载的残余到 Mole 规则里面去，结果想着要不再搞 100 个，到 200 个的时候，想着再搞100 个，就到了现在 300 多个了，这或许可以回答 Mole 相比于其他的清理卸载软件的优势是什么，应该就是可以非常细的帮你清理掉很多你找不到的垃圾，以及会卸载得更加干净，却更安全的缘故，这样看就挺有意思的。

经过这个过程，帮我补充了 13 类可以复用的通用规则、90 多条精确的清理路径，也顺手改掉了 30 多个原本以为要清、其实不该动的地方，同步对软件的更新检查、自启动检查的规则有了很充足的补充，甚至还为这些补了 100 多条单元测试。这也是基于 AI 理论知识、工程知识肯定不能补充上的点，因为他实际去做了这些事情，还好有AI，不然我手工应该要多花 10 倍的时间来做这个事情，也帮忙填了一些之前的坑，很有帮助。

也改变了我的一些固有观点，本来以为软件工程应该规范的、有秩序的，比如说我跑了100个软件后，应该后面没啥啥可以补充的规则了，因为按理主流软件的开发规范、技术底层完全可以枚举出来，结果越往后走，你会发现，完全不是这样，通用规则怎么写都找不见的那种非常多，甚至还 有bundle id 干脆就不是反向域名也有，看着很规范的约定，可能是当年某个程序员随手写的，没有任何理论可以解释出来，只能装一个查一个。

以后应该会继续做到400、500、600、甚至把市场上常用的软件全部经过 Mole 来测试一遍，补充上很多非规范软件开发下的细节规范，或许正是这些“蠢事情” 可以让 Mole 成为全球最好用的 Mac 系统清理优化工具。

预计2026-2030年，每年新建、并且采用模块化方式建成的AI数据中心容量，每年增长24%，渗透率从40%升到57%。华尔街正在抢这18个拼装大师：

综合设备商
1. 维谛技术 $VRT
唯一同时做母线配电+液冷CDU+模块化机房的全能选手，OneCore架构能撑起1GW级园区。模块化让现场作业从70周缩到10周，Vertiv数据是三家中最硬的。目标价368美元，对250美元现价有近五成空间，是这条逻辑里弹性最纯的一只。

2. 伊顿 $ETN
北美电气设备龙头，UPS、开关柜、母线全线自产，模块化后可自供80%-90%的模块内容，单品供应商很难撼动它的集成地位。数据中心相关订单连续高增，目标价534美元，百年老店吃上了AI的新饭，稳健+受益两头占。

3. 施耐德电气（欧洲上市 https://t.co/uNRT5fifVG）
三家中项目交付经验最深，模块化部署周期从88周缩到34周就是它自己验证过的案例，目标价350欧元。美股列表里没有直接代码，想参与可留意其巴黎/伦敦上市股份或OTC通道。

电网设备
4. GE Vernova $GEV
美国的"发电+电网"总包户，燃气轮机订单排到数年后，变压器和开关设备是数据中心并网绕不开的关卡。自备电源正在缓解缺电，而GEV既造燃气轮机又造并网设备，两头通吃，是缺电叙事里最稀缺的一站式标的。

5. Forgent Power Solutions $FPS
2025年7月才上市的次新电气设备商，主业就是数据中心、电网和高耗能工厂的配电设备，体量小，百亿美元级、纯度高，是名单里最像纯模块化彩票的票，波动大但赛道正。刚发完年报，适合小仓位跟踪。

6. Hubbell $HUBB
电网侧的螺丝钉冠军：变压器组件、配电金具、公用事业电气件，哪里通电都离不开。不性感但极稳，电网扩建资本开支的每一分钱都有它一份，是组合里的压舱石。

母线槽与液冷
7. nVent Electric $NVT
母线槽和液冷管路双料玩家，数据中心收入占比快速拉升，体量小、转身快，它是最直接的二线受益者，估值比VRT便宜得多。

冷却与CDU
8. 摩丁制造 $MOD
从汽车散热器转型数据中心液冷的教科书案例，冷板、机架式CDU、浸没式方案齐全，是英伟达新一代机柜液冷的隐形供应商。小市值+高成长，弹性在冷却组里最大。

9. 特灵科技 $TT
商用暖通巨头，冷水机组是大型数据中心的标配，订单 backlog 屡创新高。它的好处是即便AI建设放缓，楼宇和基建需求也能兜底，属于"错了也死不了"的冷却配置。

10. 江森自控 $JCI
冷却机组、控制系统、楼宇自动化一条龙，数据中心冷却订单高增。和特灵类似是稳健型，但多了数字化运维的加分项，适合想要冷却敞口又要低波动的投资者。

电池储能
11. Eos Energy $EOSE
锌基长时储能，美国本土供应链是它的护城河，数据中心备电和削峰订单 pipeline 持续膨胀。市值仅约12亿美元，是储能组里的小而纯，高风险高弹性。

12. 特斯拉 $TSLA
别只看车，Megapack储能业务是它对冲汽车周期的重要棋子，数据中心自备电源大单不断。虽不是纯正标的，但品牌、产能和交付能力无可替代。

13. Fluence Energy $FLNC
储能系统集成商，背靠西门子与AES两棵大树，电网级储能项目经验丰富。过去股价折磨人，但数据中心配储需求兴起后订单边际改善明显，属于困境反转候选。

通电站点
14. IREN $IREN
澳洲转型而来的算力公司，自有并网容量充裕，已锁定大额GPU订单，从挖矿到AI云的转型在同类中跑得最快。新项目排队越久，它手里现成的MW越值钱。

15. Cipher Mining $CIFR
得州电力资源优质，已签下多家超大规模云的AI托管长约，市值不到80亿美元，租约兑现节奏决定估值天花板，是小市值为数不多拿到大客户背书的标的。

16. 核心科学 $CORZ
从比特币挖矿转向HPC托管，与CoreWeave等签有多年长约，12亿美元级别的合同背书让现金流看得见摸得着。转型确定性在矿股里排前列。

17. Applied Digital $APLD
北达科他极寒+便宜电的宝地持有者，专为AI设计的新建园区，与超大规模客户合作推进中。它是名单里最纯粹的"新建AI园区"故事，想象空间大。

18. TeraWulf $WULF
零碳电力的矿场改造标杆，与Google等科技巨头有股权层面的深度绑定，AI托管项目稳步爬坡。大厂入股等于变相背书，是矿转AI阵营里靠山最硬的一只。

text:
昨天谈销毁骗局的帖子阅读量破万，

今天延展说说，
哪种销毁才是含金量高的销毁。

截至今天， $UNI 已经累计销毁 1.12 亿枚的币，占初始供应量超过 11 % 。
我觉得这含金量高，不单单只是销毁的数目，而是它有持续销毁机制。
单单今年， $UNI 通过这套机制，已经销毁了 1170万枚。

用户在 Uniswap 交易后就会产生手续费，
这些手续费可能是 $ETH 、 $USDC 或其他的代币，
这些币都会统一存进手续费金库 TokenJar 。
然后当里面的资产足够高，外面就开始有套利空间。

例如， TokenJar 里有 10.1 万美元 $ETH ，Uniswap里的销毁智能合约只要求销毁 10万美元的 $UNI ，
参与者就可以买价值 10 万 的 $UNI 来销毁，然后取走里面的 $ETH ，
参与者赚了 1000 美元，同时也销毁了 $UNI 。

只要 Uniswap 持续有交易量，手续费越多，就会有更多的 $UNI 被销毁。
更何况 SEC 刚刚给 代币化股票开绿灯， $UNI 的 Permissioned Pool 也从中得益。

虽然这持续销毁机制非常利好 $UNI ，
但我们还是严格一点，
今年没有铸造新币，但大概有 1500 万枚释放，
今年销毁约 1170 万枚，
释放却有约 1500 万枚。

以流通盘来讲，释放比销毁多约 330 万枚，所以潜在流通供应还可能增加。

不过照这个势头看，
估计年底销毁有机会追上释放。
继续卡个位看看。
author: sanyuanVC
quoted_text:
上个月提到，为什么有些回购只是脱裤子放屁

今天继续讲，
有些所谓的销毁，也只是一个谎言！

如果一个项目，烧毁了 1000 万枚的币，但同时解锁或增发 1 亿枚 ，听起来是销毁，实际上根本没有通缩。
只是拿一个好消息来掩盖抛压。

例如今年的 $FLOW ，
销毁了 5000 多万枚 的 $FLOW ，看起来是非常利好。
但是， 这轮销毁是在处理假币事件后产生的异常供应，不是市面上正常流通的币。
同时， $FLOW 还持续发币来支付验证者奖励。
一边销毁，一边发币，净发行率还是接近每年 5 % 。

当然，还是有比较健康的例子，
$CAKE 在今年 8 月销毁了 274.6万枚 $CAKE ，同时新增了 67.4 万枚。
这种基础的数学，相信大家都会算，
扣掉增发以后，净销毁大概 207.2 万枚。
这已经是 $CAKE 连续第 36 个月实现净供应下降。

还有之前讲到的 $LIT 
Lighter 会把收益拿去市场回购 $LIT ， 然后再把买回来的币永久销毁。
不过，今年底也将迎来团队和投资者的线性解锁，
到最后销毁速度可不可以跑赢解锁速度，还是个未知数。

所以以后看到销毁两个字，不要马上高潮😂

如果一边发一边烧，还不如不要烧。

第一：隐私 / Privacy：ZEC → ZAMA → NEAR。

ZEC负责打开空间，ZAMA把隐私从匿名转账推进到 Confidential DeFi，NEAR则吃到 Intent、Chain Abstraction、隐私执行这些交叉叙事。

尤其 RWA 真上链以后，机构不可能接受仓位、交易和身份全部裸奔，Privacy 反而开始从老叙事变成基础设施。

第二：Tokenized Stocks / RWA / 币股

9 月 17 日 SEC 的 Innovation Exemption 已经把事情往前推了一大步，允许符合条件的 Tokenized NMS Stocks 通过 permissioned AMM 交易，而且要求保留股息、投票等真实股东权利。

往下就是两层：ONDO、LINK、UNI 这类基础设施吃产业 Beta。

AI、MARSCOIN、4Stock 这种币股 Meme 吃注意力和高弹性。

第三： Launchpad / 链上赌场基础设施

PONS、STONK、STONKEX、PUMP

热点越多、发币越多、交易越疯，平台越赚钱，9 月初 PONS、Stonkfun 都出现过单日协议收入超过 https://t.co/hxers5fMxI 的情况。Meme 会死，赌场可能一直收手续费。

第四： Pre-IPO / Private Market

这其实是 RWA 下一阶段。股票上链解决公开市场资产 24/7 交易，Pre-IPO 解决的则是普通人根本买不到。

OpenAI、Anthropic、SpaceX、Stripe、Oura、Polymarket。

只要 Binance、Coinbase、Robinhood 继续往这里卷，一级市场权益被拆成链上可交易筹码，天然就是新的赌场。

第五：AI × Revenue × Token Value Capture

我现在已经不太想看AI + 发币这种老故事了，真正有意思的是 AI 产品有人付钱，收入最后能不能回到 Token。

VVV 这种 Revenue → Buyback/Burn 的模板值得盯，下一轮真正有弹性的 AI 币，大概率也得回答一个问题：

公司赚钱，跟你这个币到底有什么关系？

第六： Perp DEX / Protocol Cash Flow / Buyback

以前看 TVL、用户数、空投预期，现在市场越来越愿意为 Revenue → Buyback → Burn/Stake 付钱。

第七：Stablecoin / Arc / Agent Payments

这条现在还早，但产业想象力很大。

Arc 9 月 16 日主网上线，本身就是围绕 Stablecoin、机构结算和 Agentic Economy 设计。

再往外就是 x402，让 AI Agent 自己买 API、买数据、买推理、用稳定币结算。

问题是目前真实 Agent 商业规模还远没有叙事吹得那么大，所以这条我暂时定义成：

产业 Alpha 很强，Token Alpha 还没完全出现。

text:
罗福莉刚写了一篇很长的 MiMo-V2.6 复盘，整篇看下来，其实是在回答一个现在非常关键的问题：

预训练的 Scaling Law 已经跑了这么多年，RL 能不能也这么干？算力继续加，任务继续加，模型进入更多真实环境，能力还能不能跟着往上涨？

小米这半年基本就在赌这件事。

MiMo-V2.6 的 RL 规模已经非常夸张。一次更新会抽 1,568 个任务，每个任务同时跑 16 条 rollout，相当于一个 Step 就要生成大约 2.5 万条 Agent trajectory，消耗几十亿 Token。Pro 和 Flash 最后都跑了 30 个 Step。

罗福莉他们发现 Agent RL 真正难 Scale 的，已经不只是训练本身。

第一个问题是，你得先有足够多的「世界」让模型进去。

数学 RL 很简单，一道题，一个答案，模型做完就知道对错。Agent 不一样。它要写代码、开浏览器、操作电脑、调用工具、看结果，再决定下一步怎么走。

所以小米这次一起扩张的还有 Environment。

他们做了 7000 多个 RL Task Environment，里面有 Coding、General Agent、Visual Agent、Cybersecurity 等不同任务。一条轨迹可能持续几十步甚至几百步，模型真的要在环境里把事情做完。

第二个变化更值得注意：

Harness 也被塞进训练里了。

以前大家通常把 Harness 看成模型外面的东西。模型公司负责把模型训出来，Claude Code、Codex、各种 Agent 产品，再往外面套 System Prompt、Tool、Memory、Context Management。

MiMo-V2.6 这次直接把不同 Harness 混在同一轮 RL 里。

同一个模型，上一条轨迹可能在一种 Coding Harness 里工作，下一条就换一套工具、一套 Context 管理方式。小米把 Coding、Visual、通用 Agent、安全任务也全部混在一起训练，内部叫 You Only RL Once。

他们不希望模型只学会适应某一个 Agent 产品，而是希望它学会一种能够跨 Harness 迁移的能力。

我觉得这是整篇里最值得注意的一点。

Harness 已经开始从模型上线后的「壳」，往模型训练本身里面钻了。

第三个问题更麻烦，Agent 把事情做完了，你怎么知道它到底做得好不好？

比如修一个 Bug。

16 条 rollout 最后可能全部通过 Test，但有人只改了三行代码，有人加了几十行 Patch；有人五次工具调用就找到问题，有人跑了十几万 Token 才碰巧撞对。

如果 Reward 只有「通过 / 没通过」，这些答案对 RL 来说几乎是一样的。

所以小米又把大量算力砸到了 Grader 上。

同一道任务的多条成功轨迹会被重新拿出来比较，看谁的方案更干净、路径更短、Token 消耗更少，再重新分配 Reward。

他们甚至还得专门对付 Reward Hacking。

因为模型一旦发现「怎么骗过判卷老师」比真正完成任务更容易，它就真的会这么干。于是训练环境还要不断堵漏洞、清理答案泄露、做异常检测，再派 Agent 主动攻击自己的训练环境。

到这里，Agent RL 已经越来越不像我们以前理解的「强化学习」。

你真正要 Scale 的东西变成了一整套系统：

Rollout、Environment、Harness、Grader。

MiMo-V2.6 Pro 在 Coding 和 Agent Benchmark 上比上一代涨了一大截，小米还把 Pro、Flash、一个用 MiMo 轨迹训练出来的 Qwen3.5-9B Agent 模型、7000 多个 RL Environment、RL Framework 和 mini-harness 一起放了出来。

但这些只是结果。

这篇文章真正透露出来的，是 Frontier Model 的训练方式可能正在发生一次很大的变化。

过去 Scaling Model，大家算的是参数、Token 和 GPU。

现在模型开始拥有经历。

让它进入成千上万个环境，自己跑完整任务，失败，重来，再同时跑几十种解法。然后再花另一批算力判断这些经历里，哪一种值得记住。

所以未来真正昂贵的东西，可能不只是一个更大的 Base Model。

一家模型公司还要有能力不断生产任务、搭环境、维护 Harness、跑几十万条 Agent trajectory，再把其中最好的经验筛出来重新喂给模型。

我会把它叫做一座 Experience Factory。

模型和 Harness 一起训练、Synthetic Environment、Computer Use、RL Grader、Long-horizon Agent，表面上是几条不同的技术路线，背后其实都在解决同一个问题：

怎么让模型拥有越来越多真正完成过的事情。

现在谈「Self-Improvement」还早。环境依然是人搭的，Reward 依然是人设计的，什么值得学习，最后还是人给它画边界。

但 MiMo-V2.6 至少证明了一件事，大模型下一轮 Scaling，已经不只发生在预训练集群里了。

它正在发生在模型经历过的每一个世界里。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
MiMo-V2.6: The Hard Road to Scaling Up RL

MiMo-V2.6 is very likely one of the largest single RL runs, by compute, that any open-source model team has undertaken to date. In an era when compute is brutally scarce, we still chose to dedicate a team of several dozen people to one goal over an extended period: scaling up RL. That takes more than research conviction. It takes a vision for AGI, respect for the unknown, and the nerve to walk straight into the hardest problems.

The result is a model whose potential was built through mid-training and unlocked through heavy RL. Today, it is the number one open-source model. I strongly recommend reading the technical report. I believe it will become one of those papers that Agent RL practitioners keep reopening and discovering something new in each time. In my view, the research innovations and engineering challenges behind it surpass those of DeepSeek R1, which I was partly involved in.

Some will ask: why MixRL instead of MOPD? First, they are not competing choices. We ran MixRL on verifiable tasks of moderate difficulty, including code and related agentic tasks, and found that the resulting models generalize remarkably well. Second, tasks that are difficult to verify, extremely long-horizon, or simply too challenging to include in a joint RL run are trained separately. Including them would substantially reduce rollout efficiency or introduce significant rollout staleness. We then merge the resulting capabilities through MOPD. Games, 3D tasks, and tasks with subjective evaluation signals all fall into this category.

There is also a third, slightly cheeky answer. Our team is flat enough and free enough of organizational silos that MixRL simply is not difficult for us. More importantly, everyone enjoys working this way. People from different domains come together every day, driven by the pursuit of AGI and intelligence that can continuously improve itself, to confront and resolve the RL bottlenecks in each field. I will always remember the RL daily update meetings from this period. They were intense and dense, with intelligence emerging in real time.

To help the open-source community focus on solving real Agentic RL problems, we have released a Qwen model distilled from MiMo RL trajectories as a stronger starting point for RL, along with 7K diverse environments and a complete RL training framework. We hope these resources will help move Agentic RL research forward.

MiMo-V2.6 is only the beginning. In an era when intelligence is easy to replicate, we still choose the hard road toward self-improvement and AGI. Much of what lies ahead remains unknown. But we are willing to keep investing the time, compute, and passion required to take on one hard problem after another and work each of them all the way through, until intelligence crosses into a new regime.

text:
According to a report from Taiwan's DigiTimes, the arrangement in which CXMT and YMTC each handled DRAM and NAND respectively is changing, and the relationship between the two companies is turning hostile.

YMTC is moving into LPDDR5 DRAM and aims to begin trial production by the end of 2026, while CXMT is also looking to expand beyond DRAM into NAND flash. The industry expects the two Chinese memory makers to clash head to head as early as 2028.

With YMTC having already advanced to 270 layers through its Xtacking technology, patent disputes are expected to become the key battleground in this contest for the top position in Chinese memory.

As the memory industry enters a supercycle, YMTC plans to start production at its Phase 3 project by the end of 2026. Initially it is planning DRAM capacity of roughly 25,000 wafers, and it is expected to complete capacity expansion and stabilization in 2027. It is pursuing LPDDR5 as its first mass production target, while also securing space for further expansion.

CXMT does not appear willing to fall behind. Recent reports indicate it will build a NAND research and development and production line in Beijing.

There is also talk in the market that CXMT has been recruiting personnel from inside YMTC. lol

Originally, under the Chinese government's supply chain localization policy, the two companies developed technology and capacity in their own respective domains, in the spirit of "even brothers climb the mountain on their own." But as Chinese memory makers have grown rapidly, the competitive dynamic has become increasingly clear, and both are now shifting toward building their own cooperative ecosystems. DigiTimes points out that supply chain vendors may in turn find themselves having to pick a side.

According to industry sources, it remains unclear when CXMT's production line will come online, with mass production expected in 2028 to 2029 at the earliest. The key question, however, is how CXMT will work around YMTC's technology and patents.

text:
在币圈待久了，在社会中的身份认同确实是问题。

最近帮一个大四朋友秋招，说帮她推荐一些Crypto行业内的正经工作。一个是竞争相对不激烈，一个是薪资相比传统行业还要高，但对比下来，她还是放弃web3，心里有点犯怵，怕影响自己考国央企。（虽然其实不影响）

我能理解一个大四学生对于未来的迷茫，对于陌生行业，特别是币圈的胆怯，犹如我当年毕业随便进了一家公司上班，美其名曰能赚钱 or 安稳过日子那样。

这突然，就让我想到币圈工作者“身份认同”问题。目前我认识的币圈人自己对自己做的事绝大多数人都是满意的，薪资着实不低，除了极个别地推或者毫无下限的工作，大家对彼此做的事，创的业都很认可。

但放进整个国内社会里，币圈人基本会和违法、灰产、诈骗 or 传销关键词挂钩，就算你投资交易撸毛靠认知赚到钱，大多数人认为你和小偷或者骗子的不义之财没两样。

当然这和国内宣传口径有很大关系，直接定义虚拟资产是违法资产，和国际大多数国家对 Crypto 开放包容的态度大相径庭，也导致了国内社会 98% 的人对加密的歧视或者误解。

我一个很好的朋友，根本不理解我所做的事，不管我咋说，都单方面认为我在赌博、我赚钱就是运气好。就算我给他解释 HYPE 代币的价值捕获，hyperliquid 交易所对金融的革新，他还是一股脑的说——代币就是空气。

我以后如果去相亲，去约会，丈母娘问我做什么，说实话，我也不知道该怎么形容我在做的事，自媒体？金融工作者？还是赌场的掮客？这些绝对不如一嘴“xx石油”、“xx学校”或者“xx局”来的安心，即使他们赚的可能都没我 1/10 多。

我好想能理解了，去年撸 lighter 赚大几百万的好哥们回老家，死活要考一个编制当微机老师摸鱼，为的不是钱，而是有一个体面的社会认同。

突然想起中本聪的那句，如果你不理解，我也没空说服你。上代国内 Crypto 人是艰难的，政策180度的转向，突然打击出海，再多的钱买不来一张回家的机票。

而这代 Crypto 人，我想除了赚钱，还会有更大的使命等着我们。

🔸If your kid can’t add fractions, they are not ready for algebra, even if the school is giving them A’s. It's an easy check. Make sure they can add, subtract, multiply, divide fractions.
🔸Lots of misinformed math education academics out there downplay the importance of foundational skills and tests. They are wrong.  Note how her child developed test anxiety once she started doing poorly on tests b/c she had not acquired the knowledge to do well on the tests.
🔸Standardized test results probably do give a pretty accurate picture of how a school is performing in comparison to other schools. Testing matters, for so many reasons.
🔸High standards matter. Smart kids need to be challenged.  Even her own daughter could see this.

text:
If you are building anything in consumer AI, this episode with @petersellis should be added to your context window.

Also Peter is an investor in @ReadAI_ if you are looking for the banana stand of meeting notetakers.
author: lennysan
quoted_text:
My biggest takeaways from @petersellis:

1. There is always money in the banana stand. The highest-ROI growth move is usually investing in the core product, vs. chasing side quests. At @Snap, after the disastrous 2018 redesign caused DAU to flatten, the team laser-focused on performance for existing users—particularly on Android—and sparked a multi-year growth renaissance. At @Discord, rather than chasing @Midjourney’s moment, the team focused on making Discord the best place to play intentional multiplayer games with friends. The result was some of the fastest growth in history.

2. Great taste is knowing when to stop. Peter spent seven years watching @evanspiegel personally say no to better ideas than most consumer startups ever launch. His take on taste is that the difference between people with it and people without it is that the ones with taste stop one step before everyone else does. They know when a good idea’s time has come, or when it has to sit on the shelf a bit longer.

3. Spend your time on your best people, not the ones struggling. Against human instinct, which is to help whoever looks like they’re drowning, Peter consistently loads up his strongest performers with more responsibility and decisions until he finds the limit of what they can handle.

4. The median PM is bad, and even net negative, because the skills of a great product leader are the skills of a founder or an executive, so top-percentile PMs leave for founder and exec seats. On the other hand, mediocre PMs fight to stay in the job because the job pays well and has status. ZIRP made it worse because it was the most lucrative role in tech for non-technical people, with the most subjective sense of what great looks like. A lot of engineers and designers conclude “PMs suck” because they have mostly met the bottom of that distribution.

5. Great PMs hold three contradictory traits. First: deep confidence bordering on arrogance, paired with genuine humility. Second: extreme organizational discipline, paired with near-pathological comfort with ambiguity. Third: a long-term vision that’s always holding in the background, paired with a day-to-day bias for action.

6. Peter designs product teams like terrorist organizations: a shared ideology and an explicit map of who is trusted with which decision. You will almost never hear a leader tell their team to collaborate less, but coordination makes you as slow as the slowest node, which compounds and slows organizations down. The antidote is a strong shared ideology and clear DRIs who can make confident, founder-quality decisions quickly.

7. Optimize consumer products for daily active use. Days map to real human cycles; weeks and months are weaker. One daily user equals roughly 30 monthly users in simple math, which is why elite consumer products run extremely high DAU/MAU. Moving that ratio a few basis points often beats acquiring a pile of soft monthly actives and hoping they retain. DAU/MAU is next-day retention under another name.

8. Define a “Core Product Value” that's both a memorable phrase and a set of metrics that measure it. Peter built this framework at both Snap and Discord. At Snap, it was “the fastest way to share a moment with the people you care about,” which you could actually decompose into metrics: time to load (fast), camera-open-to-share rate (share a moment), best friends engagement (people you care about). At Discord, it was “the best way to talk and hang out with your friends before, during, and after playing games,” with a corresponding L7 and Lness definition that made its way into the growth playbooks. The phrase without the metrics is a slogan; the metrics without the phrase are a dashboard. You need both.

9. The most important career decision you make as a PM is who you choose to marry. This has compounding effects on your career that no podcast, course, or mentor can replicate. The intellectual sounding board, the support system, the person who challenges you to grow—that relationship shapes your capacity to operate at the highest level in ways that are genuinely hard to quantify but nearly impossible to overstate.

text:
小米把 AA 开放权重模型的第一名拿走了。 新发布的 MiMo-V2.6-Pro，在 Artificial Analysis 的综合智能指数里拿到 46 分，已经能和一线闭源模型放在一起比。

Grok 4.7 的 high 档也是 46 分，GPT-5.6 Sol 的 max 档是 47 分。按这套评测，MiMo 大致就在这两款模型附近。但距离榜首 Claude Fable 5.1、GPT-6 Astra 最高推理档的 53 分还有差距。

它的能力也比较完整。文字、图片、音频、视频都能输入，输出是文本，上下文支持 100 万 token。这一代重点加强了 Agent 能力，包括处理代码仓库、调用工具、操作电脑，以及连续执行需要很多步骤的任务。

从小米公布的测试看，电脑操作是比较接近闭源旗舰的一项。OSWorld-Verified 得分 82.0，Claude Opus 5 是 83.4；但在 Terminal Bench 4.0 的编程与终端任务中，MiMo 是 34.9，Opus 5 是 49.0，复杂编程仍有明显差距。

模型总参数 1.02 万亿，每个 token 激活 420 亿参数，权重按 MIT 协议开放。现在可以在小米 MiMo Studio 体验，也能通过 API 接入自己的应用。

text:
Onchain options are the largest remaining whitespace in crypto derivatives.

Most crypto options activity still takes place on centralized venues. Although onchain premium volume recently hit a monthly high, total notional over the past 30 days was still just 4.3% of Deribit’s. Attracting sustained retail flow is the sector’s next hurdle.

Derive currently accounts for roughly 95% of onchain options premium volume. V3 builds on that position by making the same liquidity available across more markets and products.

The existing Derive Chain will be replaced by a zkVM-based system that settles on Ethereum. Its new risk architecture should make it easier to list markets with different risk profiles while portfolio cross-margining improves capital efficiency for traders.

Native vaults could turn those markets into products users access through a single deposit. A covered-call vault could generate income by selling part of a tokenized asset’s upside while creating a more predictable source of flow for market makers.

Consumer apps let users select an asset and express a directional view while Derive handles the options execution underneath. This allows builders to focus on distribution without having to bootstrap a new liquidity venue.

The success of v3 depends on whether these products can attract sustained flow beyond Derive’s existing user base and grow the onchain options market around its infrastructure.

$GRASS is one of the most interesting tokens at the intersection of crypto and AI as it 1) plays a critical role across model training and usage, 2) has a triple digit annual growth rate, and 3) is trading at ~6x forward revenue with strong gross margins despite the above. 

In my opinion, as revenue growth accelerates in the second half of the year, new product releases (LCR) approach, and the team takes the market's feedback to heart and increases the cadence of financial and traction updates, we will likely see a re-rating to closer to my own estimate of fair value which is approximately $GRASS at $1.50.

Grass Network is a direct beneficiary of continued growth in AI usage by both providing the major frontier labs the structured data needed for model pretraining and also as it expands its product set to provide real-time data to models during inference.

One of the major pushbacks to Grass has been the lack of frequent updates of their financial progress which is a reason Grass is still trading at what is in my opinion such an attractive relative valuation. Great sign when an exceptional team recognizes the areas for improvement and levels up.

text:
Arithmetic-friendly hashes have long been one of the weakest pieces of prover cryptography.

With ZisK v1.3.0, we removed Poseidon entirely and moved to BLAKE3.

What surprised us is that we got the same performance — or even better.

After many optimizations elsewhere in the prover, hashing had become one of the most time-consuming parts of proof generation. BLAKE3 is more than an order of magnitude faster, making this cost almost disappear and largely compensating for the increased complexity of the recursion circuit.

Getting there required a lot of re-engineering: circuit sizes, prover scheduling, and architecture all had to be reconsidered around the new trade-offs that BLAKE3 gives us. The final result surprised even us.

There is a lot of focus today on binary-field proving. Binary fields attack the hash-proving bottleneck from a different direction, but introduce different trade-offs when proving regular arithmetic. There is a huge amount of research happening here, and at ZisK we are following it very closely.

I'm genuinely curious to see whether binary-field architectures will outperform what we can achieve with the current approach — and how long it will take.

So I like to think of v1.3.0 as setting a new target. 🎯

To everyone working on binary fields — and to all of us trying to make provers faster: let's see if we can beat it :)

And we still have a few optimizations in the basket.

There’s no way any of us can predict the impact that AI will have on companies, sectors or consumer behavior (which has been, for all of history until now, human behavior). 

But to claim that it won’t have an impact and simply brush it off lacks both humility and creativity. 

Tactics that worked when consumer behavior was dictated by human psychology will fall by the wayside, and those that fail to adapt will be left behind.

Every day from now on we will see new examples of areas where friction was profitable becoming cost centers for companies that don’t react in a timely enough manner. 

Today you might realize just how many flight credits, loyalty points or promotional offers you’ve never used that will end up utilized  by agents. What impact will that have?

Tomorrow, you might see something that makes you ask how much money health insurers make simply because people won’t sit on the phone for 5 hours trying to get coverage approved unless it’s a massive expense and/or life or death matter. 

What about your savings account? That money could be in a money market fund, but you haven’t bothered to move it. How much in net interest income is made because of that friction?

The coming years will be some of the most interesting for investors who are intrigued by  paradigm shifts and their ripple effects. 

I, for one, could not be more excited to see how it all plays out and invest through the changes.

In the not-so-distant future, not all compute requests will be priced the same. Providers will price them dynamically in real time rather than using a flat-fee system. Dynamic, real-time pricing of compute is already happening and will intensify. Compute markets are in their FIFO era, and in time we’ll see auction markets emerge for them because subscriptions and even current API credits won’t cut it long-term.

We should've moved past Blind signing a long time ago.

You can be tricked into approving a malicious transaction if you can't understand what you're signing.

A familiar dapp can look completely normal even when its frontend has been compromised. 

Too much has already been lost this way.

Glad to see Trezor pushing Clear Signing forward and addressing this major problem in DeFi UX. 

We need this across far more dapps and wallets.

quoted_text:
Although we have talked about $DELTA many times, I still think it is worth going over the key points for the next stage.

0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 

Logically, the first phase of the RH Chain was essentially “Stock Meme 1.0”: RH brought Tokenized Stocks on-chain, and then Memes, trading volume, and liquidity emerged around these assets. As more stock tokens, Memes, and RWA Tokens come on-chain, the market will gradually shift from “which assets will go up?” to “who will provide the infrastructure to handle the trading and liquidity of these assets?”

This is what I mean by “Stock Meme 2.0.”

The logic can be understood as:Tokenized Stock ↑ → New Assets ↑ → Trading Volume ↑ → Liquidity Demand ↑ → Liquidity Infrastructure ↑

And DELTA and INDEX happen to sit in the liquidity infrastructure layer of this chain.

DELTA’s core is not about issuing another new asset. Instead, through products such as Pools, Stakes, and Liquidity Router, it provides liquidity for on-chain assets. Simply put, if Robinhood Chain really enters a phase of rapid asset growth, the more assets and trading there are, the greater the demand for liquidity will become, and DELTA can theoretically capture this second-order growth.

More importantly, it has a potential liquidity flywheel:Trading Volume ↑ → Fees ↑ → Liquidity Increase → Deeper Pools ↑ → Lower Slippage ↓ → Easier Trading → Volume ↑

If this flywheel actually starts working, DELTA will no longer just be a “liquidity project on RH Chain,” but could gradually become the liquidity infrastructure for the entire ecosystem.

So the real Thesis here is:Robinhood Chain Growth → Asset Growth → Trading Volume ↑ → Liquidity Demand ↑ → DELTA Usage ↑ → Deeper Liquidity → Trading Volume ↑ → RH Chain Growth

This is also why I believe that after the market finishes trading the assets in “Stock Meme 1.0,” the next stage should start paying attention to infrastructure projects like DELTA.

Because in the first stage, you are making money from:

Asset Growth

In the second stage, you may start making money from:

Trading Growth

And DELTA is positioned to capture the latter.

However, it is important to note that part of this thesis has not yet been validated. DELTA’s products and liquidity mechanisms already exist, but RH Chain’s continued growth, DELTA’s actual usage, and whether that usage can ultimately translate into value capture for the DELTA Token all still need to be monitored.

So buying DELTA at this stage is essentially an early bet on:

RH Chain → More Assets → More Trading → Greater Liquidity Demand → DELTA Becoming the Core Liquidity Layer

If DELTA can eventually become the “Meteora” of RH Chain, its valuation logic could evolve from that of an early-stage project into the infrastructure Beta of the entire RH Chain trading ecosystem.

预测市场区别于赌的本质是，它让认知成为一种可交易的优势。

@Franky7 老师是体育板块的预测高手，在足球上几乎百战百胜，这次预测大赛仅几天，资金就翻了7倍多。

信息差 + 判断力 + 对某个领域的理解，这些东西在传统交易里不太容易直接变现，但在预测市场里，可以直接变成自己的交易优势。

预测市场本身就是围绕信息聚合设计的，市场价格会不断吸收参与者对未来事件的新信息。

所以，预测市场并不是猜结果

能不能赚到，与在别人还没有形成共识的时候的，有没有能力先做出正确的判断。

预测市场也不是低风险赚钱工具。

因为认知也会出错，信息也可能会被市场提前定价，流动性和赔率同样也会影响预测结果。

但从参与方式来看，预测市场确实提供了把长期积累的认知，变成可以参与市场的能力的机会.

这次预测大赛就很好的提现了这一点！

DeepSeek 成立三年后，终于有 CFO 了。

9 月 21 日，据媒体报道，原高瓴创投合伙人严文韬正式加入 @deepseek_ai  ，目前本人已经到公司报到。

严文韬今年 35 岁，1991 年出生，复旦大学毕业。

2013 年到 2020 年间，他先后在腾讯投资、H Capital 任职，2020 年加入高瓴创投，后来成为高瓴最年轻一批合伙人之一。

更有意思的是，他其实很早就在关注 AI。

严文韬曾提到，自己从 2020 年就开始研究大模型，2023 年又将注意力转向具身智能。

过去几年，他参与投资过 MiniMax、智谱 AI、字节跳动、极兔、WeBull 等公司。

他学生时代的经历也挺特别，在复旦读环境科学与工程期间，他就创业做过校园折扣平台，最鼎盛时团队超过 50 人，覆盖上海 14 所高校，还拿过融资。

19 岁时又先后去 BCG、罗兰贝格实习，还做过媒体科技记者。

现在，这位 90 后投资人正式转身加入 DeepSeek 出任CFO。

而这个时间点也非常微妙，现在正值DeeSeek第二轮融资接近尾声，而最近两个月，有多位头部 VC 的年轻合伙人参与过DeepSeek CFO岗位的竞聘。

最终梁文锋选择了严文韬。

过去两周，DeepSeek 还在对潜在 LP 进行严格资格审查，不少资金方直接被刷掉。

此前 The Information 还报道称，DeepSeek 最近举行了一场高度保密的投资人会议（虽然没保住🤣）。

投资人需要亲自前往北京或杭州办公室，进入会议前上交手机、电子设备甚至包袋，现场只提供纸和笔做记录，梁文锋则在线参加。

DeepSeek怎么看都不像一家急着拿钱的公司，更像是在挑钱。

而现在 CFO 到位，二轮融资进入尾声，同时 DeepSeek 又被曝已经开始筹备科创板 IPO。

DeepSeek 正在补齐一家大型科技公司的资本、财务和治理体系。

模型之外，梁文锋开始搭班子了。

而且，他依然在用 DeepSeek 最熟悉的方式选人：

年轻，够聪明，懂技术，也敢下注未来。

The recent Liquid incident finally made me understand why @BTCdrivechains’ sidechain design is beneficial.

For me, the bigger issue wasn’t the bug, but how much the system still depends on a small group of signers for $BTC withdrawals.

That’s where eCash differs.

With eCash, Bitcoin miners vote on Drivechain withdrawals over thousands of blocks, which means a malicious one would stay visible for roughly three months before it could be finalized.

So the risk still exists, but users get much more time to spot something suspicious before it’s finalized.

That’s also why the upcoming eCash beta feels more relevant, as it gives users more transparency throughout the withdrawal process, while showing how BTC can gain more utility and fee revenue without changing Bitcoin L1.

Don’t forget about the original 1:1 ECX airdrop for BTC holders at full launch, with Beta also improving the pECX burn rate to 20 real ECX for 1,000 pECX (up from 10 in Alpha).

We’ll finally get to see this model in practice before the mainnet on October 31.

You can follow the beta rollout on https://t.co/rdDSwFk6Td.
author: stacy_muur
quoted_text:
Bitcoin Hard Fork: eCash Beta Is Live

Bitcoin's biggest limitation has always been change itself. New functionality means years of soft fork debate, while L1 stays intentionally frozen to protect the monetary base. 

Drivechains (BIP 300/301) fix this: sidechains pegged to BTC, independent of L1. Succeed, and Bitcoin gains new utility and fee revenue. Fail, and L1 is untouched.

eCash is the first real network built on this model, and Alpha proved it. Hashrate hit 9.44 PH/s, 7 independent pools mined blocks, and the community shipped a bunch of tools unprompted:

1/ https://t.co/A1wvy4Uqfq / https://t.co/RIEEJinMIX - first pECX↔BTC AMM, built in days
2/ https://t.co/cv0wurxzd7 - pECX faucet, hit by proxy farmers within hours
3/ https://t.co/LOYl4QX5X7 - the first block explorer
4/ eCashPool & NurseryPool - community mining pools, one paying out in Thunder on principle
5/ https://t.co/8ct2lnL8Ec - drivechain fee tracker, flipped live weeks early
6/ The eCash Splitter - official coin-splitting tool, GUI + CLI, shipped mid-alpha

New drivechains proposed. Blind merge mining tested live. Consensus bugs diagnosed by block height and root cause, faster than most funded eng teams manage.

Beta is now live: https://t.co/RoPIv0wtTc

Beta improves the pECX burn rate 👉 1,000 pECX → 20 real ECX (up from 10 in Alpha)

The pECX tokens are in addition, not instead of the original 1:1 airdrop. Every BTC holder still gets ECX 1:1 at full launch on October 31 regardless. Burning pECX now is a bonus on top of that, extra ECX for showing up early.

Receiving and splitting:

Hold BTC non-custodially at the fork block, you get equal ECX automatically, nothing moves or converts. eCash uses opt-in protection, not built-in, so every wallet and exchange keeps working on day one, but that means until you split, moving BTC could move your ECX too.

Splitting is a one-time fix, three ways to do it, two are one-tap in official eCash software, the third uses standard Bitcoin tooling only.

BTC on an exchange? You can't split yourself. We're in touch with exchanges about crediting ECX, or you can withdraw to self-custody before Oct 31 and split it yourself.

👉 https://t.co/RoPIv0wtTc

苹果官网挂了一个岗位叫 Apple Pay Financial Product Strategy Lead（Apple Card / Apple Cash 团队），8 月 26 日发的。

苹果偏战略评估，谷歌则是偏给机构搭轨道。

text:
要理解机构为什么愿意为一项新技术投入资源，先要看清旧系统的成本到底花在哪里。

对账成本是最直观的一块。每一笔跨机构交易，在不同参与方各自维护的账本里都要被记录一次，任何字段不一致——金额、日期、对手方代码——都会触发人工核对流程。DTCC（美国存管信托与清算公司，美国证券市场清算结算体系的核心机构）与 Digital Asset（开发 Canton Network 的金融科技公司）在多份白皮书中反复强调，分布式账本技术的价值主张之一，正是用单一的、各方共享的记录取代多套互相核对的账本，从根本上减少“同一笔交易在不同系统里对不上”所带来的后台运营成本。

结算周期是另一块更直接的资本占用来源。在结算周期中，T+2 与 T+1 指的是证券交易完成后，到最终资金和证券交割完成之间间隔的交易日数量。美国证券市场在 2024 年 5 月 28 日正式从 T+2 切换到 T+1，这次切换提供了一个可以量化的样本。根据 SIFMA（美国证券业与金融市场协会）、ICI（美国投资公司协会）与 DTCC 联合发布的《T+1 行动总结报告》，美国全国证券清算公司的清算基金规模，从 T+2 环境下三个月平均的 128 亿美元，降至 T+1 环境下的 98 亿美元，降幅约 23%。也就是说，仅仅把结算周期缩短一天，就释放出约 30 亿美元原本被锁定的抵押资金。原因在于，结算周期越短，交易对手方违约和价格波动带来的风险窗口越小，清算机构需要预留的保证金和清算基金规模也就相应下降。

如果结算周期能进一步压缩到 T+0，甚至实现原子结算——也就是资产交付与资金支付在同一笔不可分割的交易中同时完成——对手方风险窗口和资本占用理论上还能继续收窄。这正是机构愿意在分布式账本上投入资源的核心理由之一。

以上内容摘自外捕研究（Web3Caff Research）《机构金融基础设施研报：从 SWIFT×CCIP、Canton Network 到 DTCC，传统金融的 “上链” 之路为何绕开公链？全景式拆解其发展背景、案例解析、合规逻辑、潜在风险及未来展望》

text:
Vitalik：以太坊拟引入递归STARK内存池，降低抗量子与隐私验证成本

ETHShanghai 2026今日在上海开幕。以太坊联合创始人Vitalik Buterin在演讲中表示，以太坊正探索引入递归STARK内存池机制，将签名和证明的部分验证工作从主链转移至内存池节点，由节点聚合后生成统一证明，再交由主链验证。

目前，抗量子签名验证可能消耗10万至30万Gas，隐私交易的验证成本则可能达到数十万甚至上百万Gas。新机制有望降低抗量子交易、隐私交易及Layer2状态证明的链上开销，并将Layer2提交证明的间隔从数分钟缩短至每分钟甚至更短。

Vitalik认为，这体现了以太坊从通用计算向专用化、模块化计算演进的方向。相关机制目前仍处于提案、模拟和测试阶段。

text:
The Bittensor people remember from 2024 barely exists anymore.

When solana:taoC6xyv2v8tDLcev4uaGUgV4vdQsWJrGft2kcBRrBY  topped $700 in March 2024, there were roughly 32 subnets, emissions were allocated through Root validators, there were no subnet tokens and most activity revolved around miners competing for TAO.

Today there are 128 subnets spanning inference, compute, coding, data, prediction and scientific research. dTAO created an internal capital market where holders can price individual subnets. Some teams are generating outside revenue and using it for buybacks. Daily TAO issuance has been cut in half, while ownership and institutional access are materially broader than in 2024.

And the network is accelerating again. V440 makes emissions more selective, directs rewards toward subnets attracting real demand and lowers the economic barrier for new teams to enter. That clears the way for Bittensor to support more subnets without simply diluting the strongest ones.

In 2024, TAO was primarily scarcity plus a vision.

Today it is scarcity plus 128 competing AI markets, with capital actively searching for the ones creating real value.

Same ticker. Completely different network.

text:
Austin predicts Congress will delay fixing the deficit until Social Security runs out

"The thing I would keep an eye on is, is there ever at any point going forward a sense of fiscal restraint from Congress? Because that is fundamentally what you're gonna need to grow out of it instead of inflate out of it."

"If you're growing it, call it 6% debt to GDP, but you're spending a 7% debt to GDP deficit, you can't grow your way out of that. We need to actually spend less money."

"If you look at political systems globally, that only starts to happen after the pain has been significantly more than what we have had here in the United States. We've had a little bit of inflation. We have not had the kind of inflation that gets political parties kicked way out of power in disruptive fashion."

"People are not angry enough about that yet for Congress to stop spending. It's data centers, data centers, data centers."

"I think it will be until the 2030s when the Social Security fund actually runs out of money to pay full benefits that Congress punts on this too. When you hit that point, you have a problem."

"Do we take money out of other things? Do we really fire the deficit up to a hilariously unsustainable Argentina number? Or do we cut benefits? You end up in a world where something's gonna give when Social Security runs out of money."
